7th Legion:
The 7th Legion is an elite special operations regiment composed of the Alliance's most seasoned veteran fighters. Initially serving behind the scenes, the Legion became the face of the Alliance military during the Fourth War, leading Alliance incursions into Zandalar. Before this campaign as well as after, they have participated in almost every major offensive and engagement the Alliance has been involved in. They fulfill a similar role to the Horde's Kor'kron Guard; the two have frequently crossed blades during the various conflicts between the Alliance and Horde, including in Northrend and Pandaria.
Their troops are equipped with the best technology the Alliance can provide. They are often seen using gunships, submarines, guns, cannons, ground support weapons such as chain guns and harpoon guns, and more recently, they employed warframes, bombers and siege tanks on the battlefield. The 7th Fleet is one of the Alliance navy's fleets belonging to the 7th Legion.
7th Legion Base Camp:
7th Legion Base Camp is a dwarven base of operations in Silverpine Forest, headed by General Marstone. Dwarven Infantry patrol the area.
Lord Godfrey will have Horde heroes come here to assassinate Marstone in the quest  [5-30] Sowing Discord in order to slow the advance of the Alliance forces in the resultant confusion. Meanwhile Lord Walden wants some recon data in  [5-30] 7th Legion Battle Plans. Heroes wandering into the area should be advised that the mobs are elites due to the presence of three friendly NPCs during the associated quests.
A'dal: A'dal is the naaru leader of the Sha'tar and ruler of Shattrath City. It shimmers like a chained sun, and if unleashed, its power might destroy cities or topple mountains.
Aalgen Point: Aalgen Point is a Valarjar camp south of the Lost Temple.
Abandoned Burrows:
The Abandoned Burrows was the former main vulpera settlement in northeastern Vol'dun, recently destroyed by a force of Faithless sethrak led by Fangcaller Sraka. To the southwest lies the Brine Basin, while heading north out of the burrows takes one to the Whispering Crag.
After crashing into the Brine Basin, the Horde adventurer was captured by the Faithless and awakened in the Shrouded Hollow in the southeastern part of the burrows before being rescued by Nisha. The two subsequently fought their way through the sethrak, retrieved Nisha's map from Sraka, and escaped to the Vulpera Hideaway.
By the year 42 ADP, the vulpera had regained control of the Abandoned Burrows. First Arcanist Thalyssra noted that while the vulpera take care to post sentinels, they don't try to hide their presence in their regained home. Lita was eager to show the nightborne all the new construction that had taken place.
Abandoned Camp:
The Abandoned Camp is located in the Storm Peaks. Once host to the dwarven archaeologist Brann Bronzebeard, the tent was ransacked and destroyed during his quest for Norgannon's keystone. What remains of the encampment stands, whipped by the arctic winds, on the northeastern side of a collapsed bridge that once spanned Bor's Breath. 
Archaeologist Andorin assigned adventurers to ascertain who had pillaged the site with the help of a Frosthound, eventually leading them to the iron dwarf Tracker Thulin.
Abandoned Kirin Tor Camp:
Located in the craggy hills just to the west of Karazhan, on the border with Duskwood, the Abandoned Kirin Tor Camp is, as the name suggests, a Kirin Tor camp that has been abandoned. Arcane Hunters and Excited Mana Scavengers roam around. An old circle of power is still there.
The camp was used an unknown number of years prior to the First War by Arrexis, a member of the Council of Tirisfal who was researching Karazhan. Arrexis found a way to stop the warping of space caused by the tower from happening within special wards, but while bringing the wards up reality was weakened. Medivh, who was possessed by Sargeras and secretly killing members of the Council of Tirisfal in "accidents", encouraged Arrexis to try his ritual on demonic realms. Arrexis caught the attention of the eredar Balaadur. The catastrophe ended with Arrexis and all of his apprentices dead, Balaadur taking  [Ebonchill], Daio exiled from the Kirin Tor for his part in it, and all records of Arrexis stripped from Kirin Tor records so that no one would repeat his mistakes.
Merina was among the apprentices to come here with Arrexis.
Aberrus, the Shadowed Crucible: Aberrus, the Shadowed Crucible is the second raid in Dragonflight, added in patch 10.1.0. Hidden beneath the Obsidian Citadel, it is a massive laboratory in Zaralek Cavern where Neltharion's most horrid creations were made, including the dracthyr.
Abyssion's Lair: Abyssion's Lair is located in the upper shelf of Deepholm, directly southwest of Lower Silvermarsh and southeast of the Temple of Earth. This is where the twilight dragon, Abyssion, hides one of the World Pillar fragments.
Acherus: The Ebon Hold: Acherus: The Ebon Hold (/ˈæk.əɹ.əs/ ACK-ə-rus) is a former Scourge necropolis originally floating above Light's Hope Chapel in the Eastern Plaguelands. It is now located above the easternmost part of the Broken Shore of the Broken Isles, though as of We Ride Forth, Acherus has canonically moved to Icecrown Citadel in Northrend. It is the headquarters of the Knights of the Ebon Blade and the starting area for all death knights of the Alliance and the Horde. As such, the Ebon Hold has been designated as a sanctuary, and can be reached by death knights through the  [Death Gate] ability.
Addle's Stead: Addle's Stead is located in southwestern Duskwood, south of Raven Hill and west of the Vul'Gol Ogre Mound. It is one of the many abandoned farmsteads, presumably left behind when the darkness crept into Duskwood. The farm is inhabited by Forlorn Spirits, presumably, spirits of dead Defias Brotherhood members who used to occupy the abandoned farm.
Admiral Taylor's Garrison:
Admiral Taylor's Garrison was a forward camp established by Admiral Taylor in the Spires of Arak, but fell to mutiny when the necromancer Ephial led an uprising. The ghosts of its deceased inhabitants remain, some of them seeking to bring the traitors to justice.
The garrison is made up of a town hall, barracks, a Dwarven Bunker and several farms, as well as an inn named the Briny Barnacle.
Aegis Wall:
The Aegis Wall  is a dawntower location and fortified front against the nerubians coming up from Azj-Kahet in southeastern Hallowfall. When players first get there in  [75-78] Where the Light Touches, early in the Hallowfall storyline, the fortification is being overrun by the Dreadstrike nerubians.
The area is bordered by Dunelle's Kindness to the north, the Ragged Front to the east and south, and the Sanguine Grasps (and Skittering Breach delve) to the west.
Aerie Peak: Aerie Peak (or the Aerie (s)) is the capital of the Wildhammer clan of dwarves affiliated with the Alliance. It is located in the Hinterlands in a mountainside to the northwest, and it has a range of different services including a gryphon master or a leatherworking trainer.
Afterlives: Afterlives is a series of animated shorts serving as a prelude to World of Warcraft: Shadowlands. Each episode focuses on one of the four Covenants that rule over the zones of the Shadowlands. The series was announced on August 24, 2020 and the first episode premiered during gamescom's Opening Night Live on August 27, with subsequent episodes being released on September 3, September 10, and September 17.
Agamand Mills: The Agamand Mills is a vast windmill network in the highlands of northern Tirisfal Glades. Once owned by the wealthy Agamand family, the area was taken over by the undead and is now probably the largest Scourge outpost in Tirisfal. It can be accessed from the west by a road leading up from Calston Estate, and from the east by a road from Garren's Haunt.
Ageless Shards: Ageless Shards is an area in Zereth Mortis.
Agmar's Hammer:
Agmar's Hammer is the main Horde base in the Dragonblight region of Northrend. It is a well-fortified stronghold for the Kor'kron led by Overlord Agmar, and demonstrates the new, more aggressive architecture of the Horde. Its barracks serve as the local inn. It also has an orphanage.
During the war against the Lich King, one of the reasons the Horde was there to rescue Roanauk Icemist, High Chieftain of the taunka, was because they built their base right on the doorstep of Icemist Village. At some point, the death knight Koltira Deathweaver decided to join the ranks of Horde, and enlisted to Overlord Agmar here, which allowed to stay in a room of the fortress.
Following the war against the Jailer, the brothers Bronzebeard reported that the stronghold is still active under the lead of Overlord Agmar.
Agol'watha:
Agol'watha is a forest troll ruin in the north-central Hinterlands that was overrun by animated sludges. It was once a temple of the late Amani Empire, and later the Vilebranch trolls whose broodguards tended the eggs of Shadra's brood.
The eye of Shadra was guarded in Agol'watha until it was recovered by adventurers.
A version of the ruins also exists within the Emerald Dream. Here, Nightmare-corrupted dragonkin can be found under the command of Florius, some of them protecting dragon eggs.
Agurak's Fall: Agurak's Fall is a subzone consisting of a colossal skeleton in southeastern Frostfire Ridge. It is accessible from the Bones of Agurak.
Ahn'Qiraj: Ahn'Qiraj (/ˈɑːn.kiˌɹɑːʒ/ AHN kee-RAHZH), or the qiraji empire, is the city-state of the qiraji found in the southern part of Silithus. It was originally a titan research station which housed the old god C'Thun before being commandeered by the aqir, who would become the qiraji led by the Twin Emperors: Vek'nilash and Vek'lor. Following the War of the Shifting Sands, the kingdom was contained from the rest of the world by the Scarab Wall, until it was opened again recently.
Akama:
Akama is the elder sage and leader of both the Ashtongue tribe and the elite of said tribe, the Ashtongue Deathsworn, a faction of Broken in Outland. Prior to the destruction of Draenor and the genocide of the draenei, Akama was chosen by Prophet Velen to join the Council of Exarchs as the leader of the Vindicators, the warriors of the Light and defenders of the draenei people. Years after he was infected by the red pox and mutated into a Broken, Akama was offered a chance at revenge against the orcs who decimated his people. He allied himself with Illidan Stormrage to overthrow Magtheridon in the aftermath of the Third War, only to later find that the new Lord of Outland was no better than the pit lord. To all outward appearances, Akama remained a loyal servant of Illidan and led his Ashtongue Deathsworn in his service — but away from his prying eyes, Akama sought to end Illidan's reign.
Allying with Maiev Shadowsong during the course of the invasion of Outland, whom he had been charged with keeping imprisoned, Akama rallied a group of adventurers to enter the Black Temple, leading up to the final battle with Illidan himself — the battle that ended the Betrayer's life. With Illidan gone, Akama hoped that the Holy Light would fill the dismal halls of the temple once more.
Akarek's Tears: The Akarek's Tears is the crash site and runoff of the necropolis Nurakkir that continue down to the Sepulcher of Knowledge. The House of Constructs is seen taking from the wreckage.
Alcaz Island:
Alcaz Island is a large island off the northeast coast of Dustwallow Marsh. Unlike the rest of the zone, it features tropical vegetation similar to the nearby Echo Isles. It is inhabited mostly by gnomes raised into undeath, and technological inventions led by Doctor Weavil. The island was once under the control of the Strashaz naga.
After the Theramore's Fall scenario, Alcaz Island becomes deserted, and can be accessed again by speaking to Zidormi.
It is a no-fly zone and nearing it on a flying mount automatically dismounts the character, alongside the message "You are hit with anti-aircraft gunfire!"
Aldor:
The Aldor are an ancient order of draenei priests once run by Prophet Velen, and currently led by High Priestess Ishanah. They are servants of the naaru in Shattrath City known as the Sha'tar, and assisted them in their battle against Illidan Stormrage and the Burning Legion in Outland. They are also at odds with the Scryers, and compete with them for power within Shattrath and for the naaru A'dal's favor.
By the time of the war in Draenor, the Aldor still answered to the naaru first and foremost.
Aldrassil: Aldrassil is the giant tree and village in the center of Shadowglen, which is located in the northeastern corner of Teldrassil. The leader of Shadowglen, Tenaron Stormgrip, makes his home inside the very top of Aldrassil.
Alexston Farmstead:
Alexston Farmstead is one of the many farms in northern and central Westfall that have once been taken over by the Defias Brotherhood. Since the fall of the organization, only the deadly mechanical Harvest Watchers roam the fields. Baros Alexston, an architect at the service of Stormwind City, hailed his humble origin from this very land, where he worked as a young boy.

 This section concerns content related to Cataclysm.
Following the Cataclysm, the farmstead was partially devoured by the Raging Chasm, as was the nearby Gold Coast Quarry.

 This section concerns content related to Legion.
During the Burning Legion's invasion, the area fell under the Burning Legion's control. Its residents were enslaved by nathrezim and were later killed by the defenders.
Alexstrasza:
Alexstrasza the Life-Binder is one of the six Dragon Aspects and the leader of the red dragonflight, having been one of the original five dragons chosen by the Pantheon of Order to be imbued with a portion of their power. Each aspect was given a specific charge, Eonar The Life-Binder granted Alexstrasza power over life, and so she became the guardian of all living things throughout Azeroth. She was also appointed as queen of all dragons and their ancient kingdom. Her visage is that of a high elf.
During the Nexus War, Alexstrasza resided at the top of the Wyrmrest Temple in Dragonblight, a place considered a holy ground for all dragonflights. No longer content to simply watch over the mortal races, she took direct action in bringing dragonkin together to battle the blue dragonflight and its crazed Aspect, Malygos. She also played a role throughout the war against the Lich King, including the Battle of Angrathar the Wrathgate, where she had inadvertently led to the reanimation of Bolvar Fordragon.
During the Cataclysm, she played a pivotal role through the War against Deathwing, having committed her dragonflight towards combating their corrupted brethren within the black dragonflight. This culminated in her directly confronting Deathwing within the Twilight Highlands, though it ended in both aspects being greatly wounded. Alongside Thrall, Alexstrasza and the other Dragon Aspects were able to utilize the Demon Soul in order to vanquish Deathwing during a fateful encounter at the Maelstrom. The aspects had given up the power granted to them by the Pantheon in order to defeat Deathwing, and so Alexstrasza passed on her legacy to the mortals of the world.
Later, she returned to the Dragon Isles upon their awakening to assist against the threat of the Primal Incarnates. Following the blooming of Amirdrassil, she and the Dragon Aspects were once again empowered, this time by Azeroth herself.
Algaz Station: Algaz Station is a dwarven outpost in Loch Modan where many dwarven mountaineers are stationed. It is located just east of the North Gate Pass, and south of Dun Algaz, from which it takes its name. Mountaineer Stormpike can be found here, as well as an armorer named Gothor Brumn.
Algeth'ar Academy: The Algeth'ar Academy is a legendary place of higher learning for all dragons, where they share their history and knowledge. Though it fell dormant with the rest of the Dragon Isles, it has recently reopened and is back under the guidance of Headteacher Doragosa. In a series of exciting, new changes, the Academy is currently seeking new students from all walks of life, not just dragons, as well as volunteers, to help get it back to the bustling halls of education it once was. Those who walk the Academy grounds are sure to learn something new.
Alleria Windrunner:
Alleria Windrunner (/əˈlɪɹiə/ ə-LEER-ee-ə or /əˈlɛɹ.i.ə/ ə-LAIR-ee-ə) is the leader of the void elves, a hero of the Alliance, and the oldest of the Windrunner sisters. Once a ranger-captain of Silvermoon, who led her rangers under the Alliance of Lordaeron against the Old Horde during the Second War, she was also the head scout of the Alliance Expedition during the Invasion of Draenor. Leaving their son Arator behind, Alleria and her lover Turalyon eventually disappeared after the Dark Portal was destroyed since the orcish homeworld was falling apart due to Ner'zhul's failed ritual and threatened to drag Azeroth into its fall. Unlike the Sons of Lothar who regrouped on the now decrepit Outland, Alleria and Turalyon disappeared after passing through a rift into the Twisting Nether and were not heard from again for decades.
They resurfaced during the final war against the Burning Legion on Argus, having been members of the Army of the Light for a thousand years from their perspective inside the Nether. After learning how to use the Void with the help of Locus-Walker, Alleria absorbed the power of the dark naaru L'ura in the ruins of Eredath and became the first void elf. Following the end of the Burning Crusade, she met Magister Umbric and his void elves at Telogrus Rift, and since then, Alleria became their leader in the service of the Alliance and taught them how to control their powers and not succumb to the whispers.
After Dalaran was destroyed by Xal'atath, Alleria led the hunt for her throughout Khaz Algar, while also resisting her whispers to succumb to the void. This culminated in a tenuous alliance with the Harbinger, when Locus-Walker sought their aid in stopping the return of Dimensius. Alleria grew increasingly disillusioned with Locus-Walker as she learned more about his role in the destruction of K'aresh. Though they managed to defeat the Void Lord, Xal'atath betrayed them and killed Locus-Walker. Alleria swore an oath to hunt Xal'atath down and avenge her teacher.
Her hunt led her to the Voidstorm, where she eventually reunited her son Arator and Turalyon. She joined them on an assault against Xal'atath's citadel, the Voidspire, but was captured and lost control to the Void. Xal'atath tore L'ura from her body to corrupt the Sunwell into the Darkwell, and she and Turalyon were lost to the Void.
Alleria was one of the main protagonists in Tides of Darkness, Beyond the Dark Portal, Legion, The War Within, and Midnight.
Allerian Post: Allerian Post is a small Alliance camp in eastern Terokkar Forest, just south of Firewing Point. It is seemingly named after Alleria Windrunner.
Allerian Stronghold: Allerian Stronghold is an Alliance hold in Terokkar Forest. It is named after Alleria Windrunner and has a large number of high elves. An elven mage tower, a town hall, and a blacksmith can be find here.
Alliance:
The Alliance (also called the Grand Alliance) is one of two major political factions of the mortal races in Azeroth, its counterpart being the Horde which the Alliance has traditionally been at war with. Driven by tradition, the Alliance consists of powerful cultures and groups bound not by desperation or necessity, but by their deep commitments to abstract concepts like nobility, honor, faith, justice, and sacrifice. Striving to represent these high ideals, its many different peoples all contribute their technical, arcane, and spiritual wisdom toward the shared goal of preserving order on Azeroth and creating a peaceful and just world. It is an evolution of the original Alliance of Lordaeron. Following its fall in the Third War, the memories of its allegiances and idealism served as the ultimate inspiration for the new Alliance of the present day. The modern faction has the bulk of its forces across the Eastern Kingdoms, but also in Northern Kalimdor, Northrend, Pandaria, and even in Outland.
The Alliance has remained throughout the Warcraft story the only force that can match up to the Horde. These two factions have warred several times with their predecessors, respectively as the Alliance of Lordaeron and Old Horde, having clashed together in the First, Second, and Third Wars. During the Fourth War, the controversial actions of Warchief Sylvanas Windrunner eventually caused a Horde rebellion, leading High King Anduin Wrynn to accept a temporary unity between the two factions to end both the reign of Sylvanas and the enmity between their factions. Following the battle at the Gates of Orgrimmar, ending the conflict, many argue that efforts at peace likely will not last, or cannot forgive the atrocities of the past. Currently the Horde and Alliance are in an "uneasy armistice."
The Alliance is one of the two factions that player characters belong to―along with the Horde―as determined by a given character's race (with the exception of pandaren, dracthyr and earthen which can be either). Besides race, being a member of one or the other affects gameplay through what settlements, NPCs, quests, reputation factions and in some cases items and encounters the player may access. Faction mechanics also prevent players from talking with each other or making groups together, and most PvP gameplay involves Horde players fighting against Alliance players. The divide between both factions—in regard to gameplay mechanics, story elements, and sometimes in social aspects like faction pride—acts as the core element of the World of Warcraft experience.
Alliance Beachhead: Alliance Beachhead is the beach on which the Alliance landed on the Lost Isles. It's from here they carry out orders from Stormwind. Off shore is three Alliance ships, one of which holds the "precious cargo" the Horde seeks.
Alliance Embassy: The Alliance Embassy is located at the Coreway in Dornogal.
Alliance Vanguard:
The Alliance Vanguard is a coalition overseeing the Alliance forces established throughout Northrend. Spearheaded by the Valiance Expedition, it consists of the following factions:

Valiance Expedition - The main army of the Alliance in Northrend, unified under King Varian Wrynn's command.
Explorers' League - An organization dedicated to researching the origin of the dwarven race.
The Frostborn - Having recently befriended the Explorers' League, the frost dwarves have agreed to join the Alliance.
The Silver Covenant - A militant faction of the Kirin Tor, these high elves have recently teamed up with the Vanguard.
Their Horde counterpart is the Horde Expedition.
Alliance of Lordaeron:
The Alliance of Lordaeron (also known as the Lordaeron Alliance, Great Alliance, Grand Alliance, Human Alliance, or the Alliance) was the union of the seven human kingdoms, along with the dwarves of Khaz Modan and Aerie Peak, the gnomes of Gnomeregan, the high elves of Quel'Thalas, and others with major political influence including the Church of the Holy Light. This coalition formed as a response to the threat of the Orcish Horde during the Second War, unifying its forces under the command of Supreme Commander Anduin Lothar.
Following the defeat of the orcs and the destruction of the Dark Portal by the Sons of Lothar during the Invasion of Draenor, the Alliance of Lordaeron experienced its share of internal political conflicts. It eventually began to collapse with the departure of the kingdoms of Gilneas, Stromgarde, and Quel'Thalas, which decided to withdraw for their own interests following the liberation of the internment camps by the New Horde. Nevertheless, the other kingdoms remained steadfast in their commitment and reaffirmed their support for the cause of King Terenas Menethil II.
The faction was ultimately disbanded during the Third War, as a result of the spread of the Plague of Undeath across Lordaeron and the corruption of Prince Arthas Menethil, who became the champion of the Lich King and killed his father during the Scourging of Lordaeron. At the head of the Undead Scourge, the prince brought ruin to the mightiest nations of the Eastern Kingdoms, paving the way for the Burning Legion's second invasion. In the aftermath of the Battle of Mount Hyjal, the memories of the Alliance of Lordaeron's allegiances and idealism served as the ultimate inspiration for the new Alliance of the present day.
Alliance resistance: The Alliance resistance (normally referred to as simply the Alliance) was a force that operated in the aftermath of the Third War and consisted of humans, Kirin Tor, blood elves and dwarves (under both Bronzebeard and Wildhammer) led by Grand Marshal Garithos and Prince Kael'thas Sunstrider.
Alluvium Hollow: The Alluvium Hollow is a cave within the Bony Spindles that has the rare Sister Chelicerae. There is a another cave full of corpselice in the Forgotten Wounds that shares the same name. They do not connect.
Altar of Har'koa:
The Altar of Har'koa is a temple dedicated to worshipping Har'koa, the leopard goddess. It's located northeast of Kolramas in Zul'Drak.
When the Drakkari began the sacrifices of their loa, in order to fight against the invading Scourge, it was here that Har'koa's prophet tried to hold her captive instead of sacrificing her like the other prophets with their loa.
Later, a Zandalari troll named Witch Doctor Khufu sent adventurers to free Har'koa.
Altar of Sha'tar:
Altar of Sha'tar is an Aldor-controlled temple in the northern area of the Shadowmoon Valley. It is the staging grounds for the warriors of the Aldor of Shattrath City to face the forces of Illidan. The city of Elodor once surrounded it.
Like its counterpart Sanctum of the Stars to the south, the neutral attitude of the Aldor in Shattrath City is not exhibited here in the Shadowmoon Valley. Those aligned with the forces of the Scryers will be attacked on sight by any Aldor in this area. It has several vendors and quest givers, as well as an innkeeper.
Altar of Zul: The Altar of Zul is a Vilebranch forest troll altar in the Hinterlands. Qiaga the Keeper can be found on top of the altar. Before the Cataclysm Morta'gya the Keeper could also be found here and the  [Sacred Mallet] used to create the  [Mallet of Zul'Farrak] dropped off Qiaga.
Alterac (kingdom):
The Kingdom of Alterac was one of the seven human nations, and was situated in the foothills and mountains of the land known as the Alterac Mountains. Originally an Arathorian city-state founded after the Troll Wars, it became an independent kingdom after the empire split apart. Lastly ruled by King Aiden Perenolde, Alterac was the weakest kingdom to join the Alliance of Lordaeron during the Second War, and was a relatively small contributor of soldiers and supplies. As the war raged, King Perenolde lost hope of victory for humanity and betrayed his allies, forming an alliance with the Old Horde. In exchange for their protection, the orcs could pass through their lands without resistance. When the betrayal was revealed, Alterac was besieged by the Alliance and put under martial law by King Terenas Menethil II.
Following the Alterac crisis and the death of King Perenolde, the Alteraci people are now scattered, and many of them are affiliated with the Syndicate; a criminal organization created by Lord Aliden Perenolde and led by villainous nobles of Alterac. The masks worn by the Syndicate members are orange, just like the national color of the fallen kingdom.
Alther's Mill:
Alther's Mill is an abandoned lumber mill located northeast of Lakeshire in the Redridge Mountains region of Stormwind.
This relatively backwater area was once overrun by spiders, buzzards and the occasional stray orc. Most folks passed through on the way to Stonewatch Keep. It has since been taken over by Blackrock clan of orcs who have a very large worg kennel here. Overseen by Homurk and Murdunk, this is where the captured human Messner was held.
At the conclusion of the Redridge Mountains storyline the area is cleared of all enemy NPCs.
Alturus' Sanctum: Alturus' Sanctum is the sanctum of Archmage Alturus, a member of the Violet Eye, the group of Kirin Tor agents who were spying on Medivh and Karazhan. When Khadgar was an apprentice to Medivh, he would sometimes come here to work with Alturus on a piece of the  [Archmage's Prismatic Disc] entrusted to him by Archmage Antonidas. The portal to it is located in the Master's Cellar in Deadwind Pass.
Amaki tribe:
The Amaki tribe is a tribe of blood trolls located at Zal'amak in Nazmir. They are led by Warmother Nagla, who drove her forces with a brutality and strength the Zandalari trolls did not expect.

 This section concerns content related to Battle for Azeroth.
During the Fourth War in 33 ADP, they were worshippers of the Old God G'huun. They kept their men as slaves while bloodsingers drain male "volunteers" for blood to use to turn Krag'wa's tadpoles into crawgs. Cyrus Crestfall and Rokhan eventually tasked the Alliance and Horde heroes to destroyed Zal'amak and its inhabitants.

 This section concerns content related to the Warcraft novels, novellas, or short stories.
By the Year 42 ADP, the blood trolls had been cleared from Nazmir, and the current whereabouts of the Amaki tribe are unknown.
Amani Empire: The Amani Empire (also called the Amani Empire of Zul'Aman) is a forest troll empire located in northern Lordaeron. Established long before the Great Sundering, it took its name from the strongest tribe of forest trolls and the founders of the empire at that time, the Amani. Their empire was crushed in the Troll Wars, thought to never be able to rise again. Although a shadow of its former self, the empire still endures from its capital, the temple city Zul'Aman.
Amani tribe:
The Amani tribe is a tribe of forest trolls who founded the Amani Empire in the northeastern side of ancient Kalimdor, with Zul'Aman as their capital. In modern times, their empire is a shadow of its former self, with most of their territory stretching only as far as the borders of Zul'Aman itself in Quel'Thalas.
Akil'zon is the main loa of the Amani tribe as a whole and of the Amani ruling family in particular.
Amani'Zar Village: Amani'Zar Village is the capital of the Amani tribe and Amani Empire.
Amani'shi:
The Amani'shi is a group within the Amani. They are located mostly within Zul'Aman. Some Amani'shi can be found within the Throne of Thunder, allied to Zul and his Zandalari.
Several units ride Amani Bear Mount‎s and Amani Warbears.
Amber Ledge:
Amber Ledge is a cliff with a mage tower overlooking the Westrift in west-central Borean Tundra, next to the ruined bridge across the rift. During the Nexus War, the Kirin Tor and their red dragonflight allies, led by Librarian Donathan and Lord Surristrasz respectively, used the area as a staging ground to investigate the mage hunters' abduction of magi at Beryl Point, just to the south.
After the war against the Jailer, the Bronzebeard brothers wrote that Surristrasz is still located at Amber Ledge and keeping the younger red dragons that work with the Kirin Tor in line. Muradin Bronzebeard doesn't know who originally built the tower at the ledge.
Amberleaf: The Amberleaf forest sprites are found on the Wandering Isle. They interrupted a meditation of Aysa Cloudsinger in the Cave of Meditation and overturned a supply cart in Dawning Valley on its way to the training grounds.
Ambermill: Ambermill (or Amber Mill) was a human town located slightly southwest of Lordamere Lake in Silverpine Forest. It is made up of a town hall, a stables, several mills, and a lumber mill. It was originally part of kingdom of Gilneas. Following the Third War, the town was occupied by the forces of the Kirin Tor from the Magocracy of Dalaran, who were friendly with the Alliance. However, the town was eventually conquered by the Forsaken at the time of the invasion of Gilneas. Following the final battle of the Silverpine Forest campaign, the area is inhabited by servitors once more, though the shield is gone.
Amberpine Lodge: Amberpine Lodge is the primary Alliance outpost in the western area of the Grizzly Hills. It was nominally always an Alliance outpost, even before the war against the Lich King; Alliance-affiliated woodsmen built it to serve as a meeting hall. During the war, Valiance Expedition forces led by Lieutenant Dumont commandeered it for military use. Since the end of the war, the lodge has slowly gone back to more peaceful uses.
Ammen Vale: Ammen Vale is a small island off the coast of Azuremyst Isle, separated by the Crystalbrook River, and serving as the starting area for the draenei players.
Amphitheater of Annihilation:
Amphitheater of Annihilation is a sub-zone in northwestern Ashran, on Draenor. 
A watery zone home to sporelings, podlings, sporebats and fungal giants. Flytraps and Slippery Slimes can be found here to augment the powers of opportunistic adventurers. The inhabitants of this area are known as "the Shapers".
An'daroth: An'daroth is a ley-line nexus located in the northwestern Ghostlands, found east of Goldenmist Village and west of Elrendar Crossing. It was once used by the high elves of Quel'Thalas prior to the Scourge invasion. By the time the blood elves joined the Horde, a night elven camp of Sentinel spies and their leader made this area their base of operations.
An'owyn: An'owyn is a camp of the Sentinel spies in the southeastern Ghostlands. The night elves are using moonstones and ley lines to spy on the activities of the blood elves in Silvermoon.
An'telas: An'telas is a camp found east of Sanctum of the Sun in central Ghostlands. This camp was originally inhabited by the Sentinel spies, who were eventually ambushed and killed by the blood elf forces from nearby Tranquillien. It is now occupied by Magister Sylastor and guarded by two Tranquillien Scouts.
Anchorite Ahuurn:
Anchorite Ahuurn is a draenei located at Telredor in Zangarmarsh. Originally, the resident priests seldom received visitors, but when the orcs started to attack draenei settlements, refugees began to arrive in larger numbers. Anchorite Ahuurn and the others transformed Telredor from a shrine into a safe haven. He continued to work on his goal to maintain Telredor as a safe haven for all of his allies during the invasion of Outland.
When he heard reports and confirmation of the Feralfen Lost Ones taking over the Boha'mu Ruins, he wanted to approach them. First, he wanted to study their beliefs and asked the adventurer to obtain their idols. When he saw them it looked like they were worshiping arakkoa. Therefore, he planned to use an arakkoa disguise. When the adventurer delivered him the required reagents, Ahuurn mixed a potion and sent the adventure back to the temple and speak with Elder Kuruti with a message for the Lost Ones to return to the draenei people. Kuruti, however, saw through the illusion and refused. On the other hand, Ikuti at the Orebor Harborage accepted the aid sent by Ahuurn.

 This section concerns content related to Dragonflight.
Ahuurn invited every Lost One tribe on Outland that he could find to the Tishamaat in the Exodar. He wasn't asked to do it, but felt it was important. He was once afraid of the Lost Ones and Broken, but eventually came to realize that they were all one people even if they lead different lives. Standing next to Kuruti, he was seen speaking with Alchemist Funen and Arechron in the Trader's Tier.
Andorhal: Andorhal is a destroyed human city located in the Western Plaguelands, formerly known as the western Eastweald, Lordaeron's breadbasket. One of the largest cities in northern Lordaeron, Andorhal was the main agricultural distribution point in the region. It is from here that the plague of undeath started to spread at the beginning of the Third War. Following the Scourging of Lordaeron, the undead Scourge took control of the ruined city for years, until the Alliance and the Forsaken expelled them and fought each other in the Battle for Andorhal. The waters around Andorhal are still contaminated by the plague.
Angerfang: The Angerfang are a sub-group of the Dragonmaw clan that largely operates out of the Wetlands. The Angerfang were long time supporters of both Nekros Skullcrusher and Nek'rosh Skullcrusher; a decision regretted by their leader, Gorfax Angerfang.
Angerfang Encampment:
The Angerfang Encampment, located in central Wetlands, is the largest Dragonmaw orc camp in the region, belonging to the Angerfang.

 This section concerns content related to the original World of Warcraft.
Formerly led by Nek'rosh Skullcrusher, son of Nekros Skullcrusher, their plan was to use the encampment as a rallying point to attack Menethil Harbor with catapults. The Alliance finally sent agents to deal with Nek'rosh, thus ending the Dragonmaw threat to Menethil. Captain Stoutfist had also adventurers bring him war banners from the defeated Angerfangs.

 This section concerns content related to Cataclysm.
In the years surrounding the Cataclysm, leadership of the clan fell back to Gorfax Angerfang. He was eventually attacked by Alliance adventurers sent by Prospector Whelgar to ensure that the Dragonmaw do not attack them at Whelgar's Retreat.
Anglepoint Wharf:
Anglepoint Wharf is a fishing village in western Tiragarde Sound. A debilitating sickness is running through the town from tainted shipments. The villagers are being watched over by tidesages led by Brother Therold and Hera Copeland. Brannon Stormsong hasn't visited the village in some time.
It is close to the seagate and its wall, and as such needs to be protected. The great kraken Viq'Goth and the Horde both tried to attack Kul Tiras through it during the Fourth War, but both attacks were defeated by the Outriggers.
Anglers: The Anglers are a faction of fishermen active in Pandaria who have banded together by a desire to explore all the secrets of the deep ocean and catch some big fish. Their main base is the Anglers Wharf in Krasarang Wilds.
Anglers Wharf:
Anglers Wharf can be found off the southern coast of the Krasarang Wilds, south of the Incursion and immediately to the southwest of the Narsong Trench nestled between the Narsong Spires. It is home to the faction The Anglers.
It would be the southernmost port of Pandaria, if it weren't for Marista's Bait & Brew just a bit southwest across the water. The Anglers Wharf is a lot older than Marista, though.
Ango'rosh Stronghold: Ango'rosh Stronghold is a floating island fortress, held by the Ango'rosh  tribe, located in the northwestern area of Zangarmarsh. On land it can be accessed by crossing a huge mushroom that has fallen to the island, making a bridge toward the ogre mound.
Ango'rosh tribe:
What ecology means? Me smash you! - The Big Chopper
The Ango'rosh tribe is a tribe of ogres, found primarily in the northwestern area of Zangarmarsh. Overlord Gorefist is their leader and their base is located northwest of Zangarmarsh across a bridge made from a fallen mushroom.
Angor Fortress: Angor Fortress is the main site of operations of the Dark Iron dwarves in the Badlands. Here, they organize their exploration for exploiting Uldaman. An agent of Ragnaros, Ambassador Infernus, also resides in this keep.
Anguish Fortress: Anguish Fortress (or the Fortress of Anguish) is a fortress of the Shadowmoon clan on Draenor. It is the location of the Shadowmoon Burial Grounds. It is here where draenei prisoners are taken to be sacrificed in order to summon void monsters. Ancestors are also being desecrated here. The inside the fortress is locked to outsiders and only with a  [Fragment of Anguish] can one enter.
Ankhaten Harbor: Ankhaten Harbor is a harbor built along the southwestern shore of Uldum. It was formerly known as Schnottz's Landing until the Wastewanders took control of it.
Antecedent Isle: Antecedent Isle is a small island floating off the northern edge of Zereth Mortis, accessable either by a translocator beacon (available after completing chapter 3 of the Zereth Mortis campaign) or by flight. The world boss Antros is fought there.
Antorus, the Burning Throne: Antorus, the Burning Throne is a raid on Argus, in the Antoran Wastes. It is entered from a crack below the artillery platform near Felfire Armory, not the main gate, which kills all who walk near it. The main gates are never visited.
Anub'ar: The Anub'ar are a Scourge faction consisting of undead nerubians and living cultists, located around Icemist Village and within Azjol-Nerub.
Anvilmar: Anvilmar (also known as building A3) is the first settlement of significance encountered by starting dwarves. It lies to the north in Coldridge Valley and has a set of trainers and some quest givers, as well as a few vendors. The central structure of Anvilmar houses a large forge, although there are no tradeskill trainers present.
Anyport: Anyport (also referred to as the Cove) is a smugglers cove located in western Drustvar. The Lowtide Tavern is located below the broken night elf ship, and the Drunk Tank is in the water, north of Anyport.
Apothecarium:
The Apothecarium lies in the southwest corner of the Undercity. It is the home of the Royal Apothecary Society, a large-scale organization of undead led by Master Apothecary Faranell and dedicated to eradicating the "infestation of humanity" from Lordaeron. This is where the Forsaken work to brew their newest plagues and poisons, as well as creating more powerful abominations to serve in their armies. It is the center for alchemy training for the Forsaken. Forsaken medics such as Vellcinda Benton also studied here to learn the science of tissue and organ transplants.
During the Battle for the Undercity, the Alliance led by Varian Wrynn entered the Apothecarium and killed Putress here. The king was horrified when he saw the laboratory.
After the Cataclysm, Koltira Deathweaver was captured by Sylvanas Windrunner. During the Burning Legion's third invasion, it was revealed that Koltira was held captive in the Apothecarium. Thassarian and the Deathlord of the Ebon Blade infiltrated the Apothecarium only to find it abandoned. They killed Gurgoth and freed Koltira.
Apothecary Camp: The Apothecary Camp is a Royal Apothecary Society camp on a cliff overlooking the Chillmere Coast west of Steel Gate in Howling Fjord.
Ara'lon: Ara'lon was a sylvar member of the Wild Hunt. He joined the Hunt after the death of his grove, Tirna Noch. He appears as a recurring quest giver in the Ardenweald storyline and the Night Fae Campaign.
Arakkoa:
The arakkoa ("heirs of Arak" in Ravenspeech)  are a bipedal, keenly intelligent avian race, native to Draenor (now Outland), which they call Rakshar ("the Sunstone"). They have an affinity for arcane magic and secrecy. Most are aggressive to both Alliance and Horde, although there are friendly members of the arakkoa to be found.
The winged arakkoa or high arakkoa, were the proud descendants of the once-grand Apexis civilization, a glorious empire of the sun that ruled vast territories alongside the ogre empire centuries ago. While many of the great works of their forebears remain a mystery, the arakkoa in the time of Draenor's final days—proud, hateful and defiant—mastered their own form of sun magic. From atop the Spires of Arak, they gazed down on Draenor with scorn and sought to restore their people to the heights of their power.
A second group of arakkoa, called the Arakkoa Outcasts, were born from the treachery of their kin. Transformed into hunched shadows of their former selves by the Curse of Sethe and gifted with a mastery over shadow magic by the raven god Anzu, in Draenor's final days they desperately sought to survive the genocidal efforts of those who had betrayed them. Without champions, and without hope, the Outcasts ultimately heeded the influence of an Old God and were lost to the darkness in which they'd once taken refuge.
Arathi Empire:
The Arathi Empire (/əˈræθi/ ə-RATH-ee or /əˈrɑːθi/  ə-RAHTH-ee) (sometimes called Arathor) is a major civilization located on an unspecified Azerothian landmass beyond the Storming Sea. Its people, the Arathi, are mixed-race descendants of humans from the ancient Empire of Arathor and high elves from Quel'Thalas. The Empire worships the Holy Light in the form of the Sacred Flame and is ruled by a divine emperor, who interprets the Flame's prophetic visions.
More than a decade before the war in Khaz Algar, the Hallowfall Expedition left the Empire in pursuit of a prophetic vision seen by the current emperor. The expedition became stranded in Hallowfall, an underground region in Khaz Algar. Although cut off from the mainland, they remain loyal to the Empire.
Arathor:
Arathor (variously called the Empire of Arathor, the Arathor Empire, the Arathorian Empire, Arathi, the Arathi Empire, or old Arathor) was the first great human civilization, which ruled over much of the northern Eastern Kingdoms between its founding circa 2,800 BDP and its disintegration circa 1,200 BDP. Its capital was the city of Strom (now Stromgarde) in the Arathi Highlands.
The empire was established through the unification of the warring human tribes under the Arathi tribe and their king, Thoradin, in response to increased aggression from the Amani forest trolls. During the Troll Wars, Arathor allied with the high elves of Quel'Thalas and helped them defeat the Amani Empire, with the high elves teaching the humans arcane magic in exchange for their military aid. In the centuries that followed, Arathor expanded across large portions of the northern Eastern Kingdoms through the founding of multiple city-states. These city-states grew increasingly autonomous over time, until eventually the Empire of Arathor split apart into the Seven Kingdoms of the modern day: Stromgarde, Dalaran, Gilneas, Alterac, Kul Tiras, Lordaeron, and Stormwind. Another successor state called the Arathi Empire arose across the sea, having been founded by descendants of the original empire.
The demonym for something from Arathor is "Arathi" (which can also refer specifically to the Arathi tribe as well as to the contemporary Arathi Empire) or, less ambiguously, "Arathorian".
Arbiter:
The Arbiter was an Eternal One who dwelled in the Crucible in the city of Oribos and was responsible for judging all mortal souls that entered the Shadowlands and sending them to appropriate afterlives. Originally created by the other Eternal Ones in the ancient past to replace Zovaal, the original judge of souls, the Arbiter carried out her duty for most of known history. Nameless and voiceless, she was served by the attendants, with Tal-Inara serving as her Honored Voice to speak on her behalf.
At the end of the third invasion of the Burning Legion, the Arbiter was struck dormant by the corrupted soul of Argus, causing all new souls to flow past her into the Maw. She was later destroyed for good by Zovaal, who consumed her essence in order to regain his full power. The kyrian Pelagos later took her place to become the new Arbiter, restoring balance to the Shadowlands.
Arcforged:
The Arcforged were the mechagnomes that followed King Mechagon and his ideas of "reversing" the Curse of Flesh.
King Mechagon's soldiers were all fully mechanized, most of them sadly forced into it. Worse, their limbs were sometimes replaced with tools unfitting for normal function. After such operation, subjects had to deserve their new robotic upgrades, piece by piece, as a status symbol. The Rustbolt Resistance was fighting them, trying to overthrow Prince Erazmin's father in order to not let him accomplish his dream, but also for the freedom and autonomy to install mechanical upgrades out of their own will and choice.
A few of King Mechagon's residual creations kept wandering after the end of the rebellion, refusing to accept his dethroning. As a way to thank the mechagnomes for their help with resuscitating Gelbin Mekkatorque, Alliance forces cleared up the remaining Arcforged loyalists from Mechagon City, and as such, led to the reunification of gnomekind.
Archive:
The Archive  is the nexus of earthen civilization in Khaz Algar. There, memories are cycled, catalogued, and stored at the end of an earthen's scheduled rotation. A task that is done by the Archivists. It is located on the western edge of the Coreway in southwestern Dornogal.
Ten thousand years ago, the Great Sundering damaged the great machines of the earthen, including the Archive, eventually leading to its shutdown. While their memory gems could still be stored within it, the earthen lost the ability to access the memories held in the gems. Eventually High Speaker Eirich sent Speaker Brinthe away to Dornogal to serve on the Council of Dornogal in his stead and preside over the restoration of the Archive, though that was a just a pretense to exile her from the Ringing Deeps.
When the earthen in the Isle of Dorn split into the Unbound and the Oathsworn, the Unbound lost access to the Archive and could no longer store their memory gems within it.
When Magni Bronzebeard repaired the Awakening Machine, he also restored the other inactive titan machines in Khaz Algar, including the Archive. Following the arrival of the Alliance and Horde fleets on the Isle of Dorn, High Speaker Brinthe and Dagran Thaurissan II accessed the ancient transporter in the Archive, which sent them to the Vault of Memory. There, they eventually uncovered several personal logs left behind by Archaedas which spoke of the Manifold, worldsoul crystals like Beledar, and the titan's efforts to keep the earthen from rebelling by having them store their memories into the Archive every few thousand years.
Archivist Roh-Suir: Archivist Roh-Suir is an attendant located in the Reliquary of Remembrance of Keeper's Respite in Korthia. He was previously known as Scholar Roh-Suir until the events of the "Archivists of Korthia" storyline played out in the Chains of Domination campaign. He serves as the quartermaster of the Archivists' Codex faction.
Archivists' Codex:
The Archivists' Codex is a reputation faction in Korthia, unlocked in the "Archivists of Korthia" chain during the Chains of Domination campaign.
Players must gather  [Relic Fragment] items and turn them in to Archivist Roh-Suir for both  [Cataloged Research] (in a one-to-one ratio), and standing with this faction (in a two-to-one ratio).
Area 52:
Area 52 is a neutral goblin-run town found on the southwesternmost island of Netherstorm. It is a settlement structured much like Gadgetzan and Everlook, with a short wall surrounding a small hovel of buildings. The goblins are seen building a rocket ship, named the X-52 Nether-Rocket, to journey into the Twisting Nether.
Area 52 provided bombs to the troops fighting the Burning Legion in Hellfire Peninsula.
Argent Crusade:
The Argent Crusade is an order of holy warriors formed from the union of the remains of the Order of the Silver Hand in Lordaeron with the Argent Dawn. As a world-wide organization maintaining a status of neutrality, the Argent Crusade is not a political body, nor do their members ever wish to become one. Their cause is to fight swiftly and mercilessly against any element of evil that surfaces in Azeroth. To that end, they call both the Alliance and the Horde allies in the cause of stamping out evil, and therefore recruit from all races without distinction.
Founded by Highlord Tirion Fordring after the Battle for Light's Hope Chapel, the Argent Crusade was a major contributor to the successful campaign in Northrend, where they temporarily allied with the Knights of the Ebon Blade to form the Ashen Verdict and topple the Lich King at the Frozen Throne. Since the Cataclysm, they worked to restore the Plaguelands of northern Lordaeron.
At the beginning of the third invasion of the Burning Legion, the Argent Crusade was decimated during the disastrous Battle for Broken Shore. Under the lead of Lord Maxwell Tyrosus, who succeeded the late Tirion, the remaining forces of the Crusade allied with all the paladin orders of Azeroth to reform the Order of the Silver Hand at the Sanctum of Light, beneath Light's Hope Chapel. Following the Fourth War, the Argent Crusade managed to reform its ranks and faced the resurgence of the Scourge alongside the Alliance and the Horde. Since the defeat of Zovaal the Jailer, the crusaders hold their positions in Northrend to prevent the masterless undead from threatening the rest of the world.
Argent Dawn:
The Argent Dawn (referred to as the knightly order of the Argent Dawn, or simply the Dawn) was an organization focused on protecting Azeroth from agencies that seek to destroy it, such as the Burning Legion and the Scourge. As a worldwide organization maintaining a status of neutrality, the Argent Dawn was not a political body, nor did their members ever wish to become one. Their cause was to fight swiftly and mercilessly against any element of evil that surfaced in Azeroth. To that end, they called both the Alliance and the Horde allies in the cause of stamping out evil and therefore recruited from all races without distinction. Their base camps could be found across all the Plaguelands as well as in Tirisfal Glades, while their agents were also present in Stormwind City, Darnassus, and Everlook.
Following the Battle for Light's Hope Chapel, Highlord Tirion Fordring assumed leadership over the Argent Dawn and merged them with the Knights of the Silver Hand in Lordaeron, founding the Argent Crusade. In the aftermath of the fall of the Lich King and the Cataclysm, the Crusade took over the now-defunct Argent Dawn's outposts in the Plaguelands.
Argent Stand:
The Argent Stand is the main base of the Argent Crusade in Zul'Drak, and was built in a Drakkari structure which once might have been some sort of open air market. The central area of the Argent Stand functions as an inn and provides rest.
During the war against the Lich King, it was initially chosen by the Argent Crusade as a defensive position to keep the Scourge from taking the second tier of Zul'Drak. However, that effort failed, but the crusade hasn't given up.
Following the war against the Jailer, the brothers Bronzebeard reported that this heavily fortified area still hosts quite the population of crusaders fighting the Scourge. They described it as a safe enough place, where they were able to sleep, though surrounded by the sounds of battle as the undead threw themselves against the fortifications.
Argent Tournament Grounds:
The Argent Tournament Grounds is the location of the base for the Argent Crusade's tournament, located north of Sindragosa's Fall, in the northeast area of Icecrown. It is a sanctuary and a full-featured quest hub with flight masters, profession trainers, and vendors. Built during the war against the Lich King, the Argent Crusade put time and effort into building a sturdy stone arena and a tilting ground as a way to search out the elite warriors they thought had the best chance of taking a run at Icecrown Citadel, since throwing a whole army against the undead would only have increased the number of troops in the armies of the Lich King.
To start the quest-chain of the area, Justicar Mariel Trueheart is present inside the Argent Pavilion just to the west of the Crusaders' Coliseum, while the northern part of the building serves as a chapel of the Light led by Argent Confessor Paletress. The Alliance and the Horde are respectively represented by the Silver Covenant in the Silver Covenant Pavilion and the Sunreavers in the Sunreaver Pavilion. In patch 3.3.0, the Tournament Grounds' defenses were reinforced with three guard towers - one between the Coliseum and Deathspeaker's Watch, one near the Silver Covenant Pavilion, and one near the Sunreaver Pavilion.
Argent Vanguard: The Argent Vanguard is the main forward base of the Argent Crusade and is located in the Valley of Echoes in Icecrown.
Argus Wastes: The Argus Wastes are the edges of Krokuun. They contain areas that have little Legion presence, although the wyrmtongues know how to find the wealth the area contains.
Argussian Reach:
The Argussian Reach, also known as the Krokul or the Darkfallen, is a faction associated to the Broken of Argus based in Krokul Hovel.
The krokul of the Argussian Reach have a division of wranglers led by Jerek.
The Sacred Stone at the Krokul Hovel let them hear the whispers of the planet, which steadies their hearts.
Ariden's Camp:
Ariden's Camp is a deserted campsite found just north of the main road passing through Deadwind Pass from Duskwood to the Swamp of Sorrows. Ariden was the leader of the Dark Riders, and this was the camp he set up before being cursed, from which he attempted to sell Medivh's fake artifacts.
In Season of Discovery, a Dalaran Agent of the Violet Eye traveled here to investigate after several powerful artifacts disappeared from the Kirin Tor's vaults in Dalaran. Unable to feel the presence of the Dark Riders of Karazhan in Deadwind Pass, she tasked adventurers to bring her any of the stolen artifacts they found during their travels.
Armies of Legionfall:
The Armies of Legionfall are a coalition of all orders united to defeat the Burning Legion at the Tomb of Sargeras. Their base of operations, Deliverance Point, is located south-west of the island of Thal'dranath.
In addition to the orders, the Armies of Legionfall are also allied with the Court of Farondis, the Azurewing, the Nightfallen, the Highmountain Tribe, and the Wardens, as evidenced by their assistance to the Legionfall Commander.
Following the end of the third invasion of the Burning Legion and the Argus Campaign, it is unknown if the Armies of Legionfall remains active, however, it is most probably that they dissolved after reaching their goals.
Army of the Light:
The Grand Army of the Light (also called the Golden Army, the Army of Light, the Light's Army, or the Lightforged) is a faction of enlightened races led by the naaru who rose against the Burning Legion. After the fall of Argus to Sargeras, the draenei's finest warriors followed the prime naaru Xe'ra across the cosmos in an eternal war to bring about the Legion's end. Since then, other survivors of the Burning Crusade have joined the ranks of the Lightforged.  Once they have been found worthy to become eternal protectors of creation, their soldiers are empowered by the Holy Light and become immortal.
After finally achieving victory on Argus, High Exarch Turalyon believed that it was time to take up arms alongside their brothers and sisters of the Alliance and pledged their forces to High King Anduin Wrynn.
The Lightbound of alternate Draenor are similar to the Army of the Light.
Arom's Stand: Arom's Stand is a Kul Tiran town located in central Drustvar, named after Arom Waycrest, the first lord of Drustvar. It serves as the headquarters of the Order of Embers.
Arrangement Index: Arrangement Index is an area in Zereth Mortis.
Artisan's Market: The Artisan's Market (or Marketplace) is a located in Valdrakken.
Aruuna:
Aruuna is a draenei town in eastern Talador that has been attacked and burned by the Adherents of Rukhmar, a sect of flying arakkoa who resided high in the Spires of Arak, in search of artifacts found by the draenei.
Survivors headed south to Anchorite's Sojourn.
Ascendant's Rise:
Ascendant's Rise (also called Ascendant's Circle) is a Twilight's Hammer outpost on a ledge overlooking the Throne of Flame and close to Sulfuron Spire in Mount Hyjal. It is here the most highly trained Twilight's Hammer devotees have achieved a partial elemental state. 
A wagon with a  [Pure Twilight Egg] can be found in this area as well. This egg reveals that for the first time the Twilight dragons have a matriarch, Desperiona, capable of being a broodmother.
Ashen Verdict:
The Ashen Verdict is the name of the alliance struck between the Argent Crusade, led by Highlord Tirion Fordring, and the Knights of the Ebon Blade, led by Highlord Darion Mograine. Much like the Shattered Sun Offensive against Kael'thas Sunstrider, the Ashen Verdict is a combination of separate orders for a common purpose: the final assault against the Scourge in Icecrown Citadel and the eventual fall of the Lich King.
The strongest combatants of this coalition, along with the champions of the Alliance and Horde, will lead the charge against the citadel.
During the Fourth War, the Ashen Verdict is shown disbanded as Light's Hammer is now a deserted area with geists looting stuff belonging to the former alliance and abominations guarding the entrance.
Ashmaul: The Ashmaul is an ogre group who appear to have made their home in Brute's Rise on Ashran, in alternate Draenor. They also control the Ring of Conquest in western Ashran.Hostile to both Alliance and Horde in the region, they are notable for their pyromancers, flamespeakers, and magma casters, summoning fire elementals and hurling flame at enemies.
Ashmaul Burial Grounds:
Ashmaul Burial Grounds is a sub-zone in southwestern Ashran, on Draenor. 
The zone is home to the Gor'vosh ogres and the spirits and risen dead produced by their dark magics. Web-wrapped Soldiers can be found here, and freed to aid the player in battle.
The zone represents the southwestern segment of the main island, set low and close to the water. To the north Kings' Rest connects the zone to the other western areas, with the Ring of Conquest visible but not directly reachable across the waters north of the zone. To the east the land runs up to Archmage Overwatch, where the Alliance make their last stand against the constant onslaught of the Horde.
Ashvane Trading Company:
The Ashvane Trading Company (or simply Ashvane Company and later Ashvane Loyalists) is a Kul Tiran shipping and manufacturing company based out of the city of Boralus and owned by House Ashvane. The company involves itself in a large number of ventures, including weapons manufacturing, shipping, security, smuggling, and piracy, among others. Characterized by its ruthless business practices and disregard for moral and lawful conduct, the Ashvane Company sits atop a vast criminal empire, hoarding power and profit on a grand scale.
The beginning of the Fourth War and the appearance of Azerite have both presented major opportunities for the organization. Under the leadership of Lady Priscilla Ashvane, the company allied with the Irontide Raiders and other pirates, while secretly plotting a coup against House Proudmoore. This would culminate in the Siege of Boralus, which saw the company and its allies defeated. Despite these setbacks, the Ashvane Company retains numerous holdings across Kul Tiras and beyond.
Aspirant's Crucible: Aspirant's Crucible located in southernmost Bastion. Here, kyrian aspirants begin their training, culminating in the final rite within the Chamber of First Reflection, called the First Cleansing.
Aspirant's Rest: Aspirant's Rest located in southern Bastion, between Vestibule of Eternity and Aspirant's Crucible.
Astral Glory: Astral Glory is gathered with Herbalism on Argus.
Astranaar:
Astranaar is a night elven town located in central Ashenvale. It is the largest settlement in the region. It lies on an island within a lake, straddling the main road through Ashenvale, connected to the mainland with only a pair of bridges.
Astranaar offers a wide range of services, as well as a flight master, to Alliance players. It also has an unnamed inn and a graveyard.
Atal'Aman: Atal'Aman is an area located in Zul'Aman. Known as the temple city, it contains shrines to Nalorakk, Akil'zon, Jan'alai, and Halazzi.
Atal'Dazar:
Atal'Dazar (/ˌɑː.tɑːlˈdə.zɑɹ/ AH-tahl-DƏ-ZAHR) is a series of royal and ancient pyramids secluded high atop Mount Mugamba. It is named after King Dazar, the first king of the trolls. For millennia, the Zandalari kings and queens were laid to rest within the tombs of Atal'Dazar. These pyramids grew more elaborate with each passing ruler, as new rooms were constructed to house the deceased's vast wealth. Now, these once pristine halls have been corrupted by the Prophet Zul and his trusted lieutenant, Yazma, who seek to twist the power of these ancient kings for their own dark machinations.
It is the location of two dungeons in World of Warcraft, the Atal'Dazar and the Kings' Rest instances.
King Rastakhan led the Warpack and the Horde adventurer to the pyramid to deal with the traitors. After Rezan's death and subsequent revival, the sacred tombs became a battlefield between the fanatical Dazar'ai keepers and the invading Atal'zul.
Allured by all the gold of the city, Jastor Gallywix and his Bilgewater thieves later appeared in the southern wing to loot it. They used Gallywix's Personal Teleporter to get there. Magister Umbric and an adventurer used a Void Portal to chase him down.
Princess Talanji allowed the Darkspear tribe to place the  [Urn of Vol'jin] here. When the Speaker of the Horde did that, Bwonsamdi appeared and took it away.
Atal'ai tribe:
The Atal'ai tribe (or the Atal'ai), an extremist faction of the Hakkari, are worshipers of the Blood God Hakkar and are based within Temple of Atal'Hakkar. They are green or white skinned with green, purple, or white hair.
The Atal'ai trolls are a tribe of dark casters, known for practicing forbidden magic, including necromancy which was taught to them by Hakkar for their unwavering loyalty. The Atal'ai was a once-great troll civilization that was destroyed, its buried artifacts can be found beneath the Pool of Tears.
The term "atal'ai" means Devoted Ones in Zandali, the language of the trolls.
Atal'zul:
The Atal'zul are an extremist faction of Zandalari trolls, led by the Dark Prophet Zul. Seeing Rastakhan as a weak king, Zul leads a coup against him. Zul and his lieutenant, Yazma, have corrupted the once pristine tombs of Atal'Dazar on Mount Mugamba. They seek to twist the power of the ancient kings buried there for their own dark machinations, and revive Dazar, first king of the Zandalari. Zul had also witnessed the Drakkari tribe draining their loa for power in Zul'Drak, and sought to do the same to the loa of Zandalar. They were considered heretics.
The Kao-Tien mogu led by Warlord Kao and Vilnak'dor attacked the Zandalari at Warport Rastari in Zuldazar. In truth, it was a distraction, so that Zul could begin his coup against Rastakhan. At the Temple of the Prophet and the Temple of Rezan, more mogu appeared to aid Zul after his rebellion became public.
It is unknown what happens or remains of them after the death of their leader, however, those who were exiled from the Zandalari due to being sympathetic with Zul's coup were welcomed into the Widow's Bite.
Atul'Aman: Atul'Aman is a titan pyramid in central Vol'dun.
Auberdine Refugee Camp:
The Auberdine Refugee Camp is located just outside the Ruins of Auberdine in Darkshore. It houses some of the original Auberdine inhabitants, as well as other NPCs. Archaeologist Hollee also reaches the camp after  [5-30] The Last Refugee.

 This section concerns content related to Battle for Azeroth.
In the Battle for Darkshore, the camp was lit on fire.
Auchenai:
The Auchenai (/ˈɑː.kɪn.aɪ/ OCK-ə-nai) are the guardians of the draenei grave-city of Auchindoun in Terokkar Forest. For over two hundred years, it was the duty of their "death priests" and "soulpriests" to take care of the spirits and dead of Auchindoun using the Light. However, the genocide of the draenei orchestrated by the Old Horde pushed Exarch Maladaar to madness, leading him to ordain his death priests to practice necromancy and bring back the dead to serve them. During the invasion of Outland, Maladaar and his followers were eventually defeated by the adventurers.
Years later, now a spirit freed from madness, Exarch Maladaar returned to lead the Auchenai and form a new generation of death priests to take care for the souls of their kin in Auchindoun.
Auchindoun:
Auchindoun (/ˈɒ.kɪnˌduːn/ OCK-in-doon) is a mausoleum, a "city of the dead", a former draenei holy site where the dead were laid to rest, placed in the ground. It is located in the middle of the Bone Wastes in the Terokkar Forest within Outland.
By the time of the invasion of Outland, Auchindoun had been overrun by multiple factions, including Nexus-Prince Shaffar's ethereals within the Mana-Tombs, the Burning Legion in the Auchenai Crypts, a renegade clan of arakkoa within the Sethekk Halls, and the Shadow Council in the secure Shadow Labyrinth.
In recent years, Auchindoun had been reclaimed by the Auchenai draenei, who have since resumed their former role of caring for the souls of their dead.
August Celestial:
"Celestials" redirects here. For the world boss encounters, see Chi-Ji (tactics), Niuzao (tactics), Xuen (tactics), and Yu'lon (tactics). For the in-game faction, see August Celestials.

The August Celestials (also known as the August Ones or simply the celestials) are four powerful Wild Gods who dwell in and watch over Pandaria. They consist of Chi-Ji the Red Crane, Niuzao the Black Ox, Xuen the White Tiger, and Yu'lon the Jade Serpent.
August Celestials (faction): The August Celestials are four Wild Gods who defend the temples of Pandaria from the evils of the sha and mogu. This faction includes the four celestials and their respective servants.
Axefall: Axefall is a Horde settlement in the Spires of Arak. The only major building in this outpost is decided by the commander, which is either the Smuggler's Den or the Hearthfire Tavern. Before a choice is made, the space is occupied by Axefall Worksite.
Axxarien: Axxarien is a satyr outpost located in northern Bloodmyst Isle, home of the sect with the same name.
Azeroth:
Azeroth (/ˈæz.əˌɹɒθ/ AZ-ə-roth) is the name of the world in which the majority of the Warcraft series is set. At its core dwells a slumbering worldsoul, the nascent spirit of a titan. Floating within the infinite reaches of the Great Dark Beyond, Azeroth once fell to the corruption of the Old Gods and their Black Empire, until the Pantheon of Order defeated them and began the Ordering of the planet. It has since been populated by a multitude of different races and creatures, some native to the planet, others from different worlds; all carving out territories for themselves. However, Azeroth also became the target of enemies from beyond, including the chaotic armies of the Burning Legion and the voracious forces of the Void. Those responsible for the world's safety are not a united group; Azeroth's history is filled with wars and conflicts, and in modern times, the Alliance and the Horde are the major political factions of the mortal races. Each represents the unification of various racial, cultural, and philosophical civilizations. Despite their incessant conflicts and bloodshed, both factions treasured Azeroth, believing it should be cared for and protected, and in times of grave danger, they are willing to work together in the face of a common foe.
Although unnamed and numerous, it is thanks to the brave adventurers that Azeroth, and the universe itself, have been saved on numerous occasions. There are also many organizations dedicated to the protection of the world, which maintain an independent position during global conflicts, such as the Cenarion Circle, Earthen Ring, Kirin Tor, Argent Crusade, and Kingdom of dragons among many others.
Azj-Kahet:
Azj-Kahet (/ˈɑːʒ.kəˌhɛt/ AHZH kə-HET) is a subterranean zone located in the deepest part of Khaz Algar, south and below Hallowfall and the Ringing Deeps. The high capital of nerubian society, Azj-Kahet is home to the last kingdom of living nerubians. Unlike Azjol-Nerub, which was consumed by the Scourge, Azj-Kahet represents nerubian society as it once was—deadly survivors of mythic wars that have played out time and again over millennia. The zone is dominated by the sprawling City of Threads, which has been built on top of itself over and over as its districts decay, with the highest locations reserved for the wealthy and those who have the favor of Queen Ansurek. Azj-Kahet also features areas of dark and beautiful wilds, inhabited by other creatures who have found ways to live alongside the nerubians.
With the Black Empire destroyed and the Old Gods dead, Xal'atath, the Harbinger of the Void, has traveled to Azj-Kahet to conscript its inhabitants into a new army to bring Azeroth to its knees. She has entered into a bargain with Ansurek, offering her people the opportunity to rise from their isolation and become a powerful kingdom once again, and in return for their loyalty has provided a way to evolve chosen nerubians into a new kind of powerful soldiers. The nerubians now harvest the Black Blood of the Old Gods within Nerub-ar Palace and are engaged in a continuous assault against the Arathi of neighboring Hallowfall. However, not all nerubians agree with Ansurek, and they have begun to maneuver against her and Xal'atath's plans.
Azj-Kahet (kingdom): The Kingdom of Azj-Kahet is the last nation of living nerubian on Azeroth, which is found in Azj-Kahet, an underground region located in the deepest part of Khaz Algar. Unlike the Empire of Azjol-Nerub, which was consumed by the Scourge, Azj-Kahet represents nerubian society as it once was—deadly survivors of mythic wars that have played out time and again over millennia.
Azure Archives:
The Azure Archives  are the personal library of Sindragosa, prime consort of the blue dragonflight, located in the Azure Span in the Dragon Isles. It is where the Azure Oathstone is located, as well as the entrance to the Azure Vault.
The Conjured Biscuit Inn serves as a rest area here.
The Archival Assault delve, while accessed from K'aresh, takes place within the vaults as the Shadowguard attempt to plunder them.
Azure Front:
The Azure Front is located south east of the Violet Stand in southern Crystalsong Forest. Many artifacts belonging to the blue dragonflight can be seen in the area. The blue dragonflight seems to be drawing power from the largest crystal tree with a chain of three surge needles. There is a fourth surge needle with a different crystal on it between this area and the Violet Stand.
During the Nexus War, it was where the blue dragonflight established their front against Dalaran and the Kirin Tor.
Years later, following the war against the Jailer, the brothers Bronzebeard mentioned in their report that there were still surge needles floating in the air, but they didn't seem to be in active use since the end of the Nexus War. They also mentioned that there were also still blue dragonkin around, though a fraction of what was once an invading force.
Azure Watch: Azure Watch is a draenei settlement and Hand of Argus forward outpost located on Azuremyst Isle. It serves as an intermediary town between Ammen Vale and the Exodar.
Azurewing: The Azurewing (or the Brood of Senegos) are a brood of blue dragons of the blue dragonflight originally led by Senegos, based in Azurewing Repose in Azsuna on the Broken Isles. By the time of the third invasion of the Burning Legion, Stellagosa commanded the Scalewardens, and following the return of the Dragon Isles, she succeeded her late grandfather as the new leader of the brood.
Azurewing Repose:
Azurewing Repose is an area in Azsuna held by the Azurewing brood of the blue dragonflight. It is a dragon pool with ley energy.
Following the war against the Primalists, the area was no longer the home of the Azurewing, since the dragons had been called to the Dragon Isles, but it still remained in their control, with young drakes, whelplings, and their wardens present here. When Thalyssra passed by it, she described it as a vacation point.
Badlands:
The Badlands is an arid and desolate region in Khaz Modan accessed via the Searing Gorge to the west and Loch Modan to the north. Only the hardiest of creatures can survive in the arid wastes, such as coyotes, cougars, and buzzards. The black dragonflight have a pronounced presence in the Lethlor Ravine and Dustbowl. Scattered across the Badlands are also camps of the Dustbelcher ogres.
The region is often mistaken for being an Alliance territory. It is an extreme environment, it is imperative to have an excellent map of the ruins and surroundings to survive, the sandstorms sweeping the region can confuse the landmarks. It is advisable to travel at night, to sleep during the day, to protect your face from sand and winds, and to provide plenty of water, or a mage.
Despite its position between Stormwind and Dun Morogh, the Badlands have traditionally been Horde territory, though the Alliance have recently established Dragon's Mouth in the western part of the region. To the north of the encampment lies the Horde stronghold of New Kargath, built after its predecessor was buried by an avalanche during the Cataclysm. In the east is the goblin town of Fuselight and its sister port town, Fuselight-by-the-Sea, both controlled by the neutral Steamwheedle Cartel. In the west, a massive, charred ravine called the Scar of the Worldbreaker was formed when Deathwing passed through the area.
In the northeast, near the border with Loch Modan, lie the ruins of a titan-forged fortress known as Uldaman, home to titan-forged earthen, savage troggs, and much information about the origins of the dwarven race, while the smaller Tomb of the Watchers has recently been unearthed in the center of the region. As a result, the Alliance-affiliated Explorers' League, the dwarven Dark Iron clan, and the blood elven Reliquary are fighting for control over the ruins and any titan artifacts that may lie within.
Bael Modan:
Bael Modan is a dwarven base in the Southern Barrens consisting of a fortress with a giant cannon and an excavation site for digging. Before the dwarves came, the area was home to the Stonespire tauren. There is an ancient titan complex and research facility under Bael Modan. It seems likely that there are many relics and much knowledge to be discovered deep beneath the surface.
The Bael Modan digsite and the nearby mighty Bael'dun Keep are led by General Twinbraid, Heggin Stonewhisker, Prospector Khazgorm, Malgin Barleybrew, Captain Gerogg Hammertoe, and Lord Cyrik Blackforge. A number of dwarves from Bael Modan traveled west to Mulgore and set up another digsite known as the Bael'dun Digsite.
Baine Bloodhoof:
Baine Bloodhoof is the High Chieftain of the united tauren tribes of Mulgore and leader of Thunder Bluff. He is the son of the late tauren leader, Cairne Bloodhoof, whom he looked up to as a role model. While Baine has formidable skill on the battlefield, his true talents lie in the arena of diplomacy. He is a strong force for moderation, calm wisdom, and unity within the Horde, especially in their dealings with the Alliance.
Following Cairne's death in a duel with Warchief Garrosh Hellscream, Baine fled his home in Bloodhoof Village when the tauren matriarch Magatha Grimtotem's agents attacked and seized Thunder Bluff. Although still pained by the loss of his father, Baine staged a counterattack on Magatha and her forces, ultimately retaking the tauren capital and defeating the treacherous matriarch. Cairne's honorable son spared Magatha's life, banishing the matriarch and her traitorous allies to the harsh Stonetalon Mountains. Since then Baine has assumed the role of high chieftain of Mulgore's courageous tauren.
While bitterness might still linger over Cairne's demise, Baine had remained loyal to the Horde and its Warchief for the good of the tauren race. He eventually supported the Darkspear Rebellion in ousting Garrosh and pledged his support to his successor, Vol'jin. With Vol'jin's passing shortly after the disastrous Battle for Broken Shore, Baine remained loyal to Sylvanas Windrunner after Vol'jin chose her with his dying breath.
