It contains profession and class trainers so players will not need to run back and forth between here and Brill. The estate is owned by the lonely Sedrick Calston.
From here the Forsaken launch attacks on the Solliden Farmstead, perform experiments along the Tirisfal coast, etc. Many pre-Cataclysm quests have been reused, but reorganized in such a way as to fit the current storyline and involve far less running around.

 This section concerns content related to Battle for Azeroth.
Following the Fourth War, Lilian Voss arranged a meeting of dark rangers led by Delaryn Summermoon and Kitala Starshadow with Calia Menethil and Derek Proudmoore at the estate, leading to the latter two joining the Horde in an effort to bring comfort and guidance to them and the other Forsaken. Some Scarlet Crusade propaganda pamphlets were distributed near the estate, accusing Anduin of conspiring with his secret lover Sylvanas at the Gathering of the Arathi Highlands in order to kill Calia Menethil and make secure his claims to the kingdom, and further claiming to have Calia's surviving son as the last remaining heir to the Menethil dynasty, with whom the Brotherhood intended to one day end Anduin's "puppet reign".
Camp Antonidas:
Camp Antonidas  is a Kirin Tor camp in central Azure Span. Mage's Rest serves as the inn of the camp. It is named in honor of the former Grand Magus of the Kirin Tor, Antonidas.
The area on the main east-west road of the span, and is surrounded by the Upper Frostlands to the north, east, and south, and Khuri's Fishing Spot is to the northwest. Further out, the Cobalt Assembly is to the north, Camp Nowhere is to the southeast, and the Azure Archives are to the southwest.
By the Year 42 ADP, Camp Antonidas had been ceded back in the snows, with the Kirin Tor who remain within the Azure Span taking up residence at the Azure Vault, the Cobalt Assembly, or even Vakthros.
Camp Aparaje:
Camp Aparaje was a tauren village in eastern Stonetalon Mountains that was attacked by Grimtotem forces from Grimtotem Post led by Grundig Darkcloud. Makaba Flathoof used to live there with his daughter Kaya.

 This section concerns content related to Cataclysm.
Following the Cataclysm, as the Alliance and Horde fought for control of the Stonetalon Mountains, Warchief Garrosh Hellscream ordered his forces to burn Camp Aparaje to the ground and all Grimtotem in the area incinerated.
Camp Ataya:
Camp Ataya is a small tauren settlement located in the shade of the Twin Colossals in Feralas.

 This section concerns content related to the Warcraft novels, novellas, or short stories.
After the Fourth War, Camp Ataya came under constant raids from the Woodpaw gnolls and Gordunni ogres. As a response, the Horde Council sent Belgrom Rockmaul for aid.
Camp Boff: Camp Boff is, together with Camp Cagg, Kosh, and Wurg, the home of some of the Dustbelcher ogres. It is the southeastern camp, only guarded by three Dustbelcher ogres.  One exception though was their leader, Boss Tho'grun, who patrolled the Badlands between the four ogre bases.
Camp Cagg: Camp Cagg is, together with Camp Boff, Kosh and Wurg, the home of some of the Dustbelcher ogres. One exception though was their leader, Boss Tho'grun, who patrolled the Badlands between the four ogre bases.
Camp Everstill: Camp Everstill is a very small Alliance camp on the shores of Lake Everstill in Redridge Mountains.
Camp Kosh:
Camp Kosh is, together with Camp Boff, Cagg and Wurg, the home of some of the Dustbelcher ogres. It is the northernmost camp. There the ogres prey on supply caravans that must traverse the barren Badlands headed to Kargath or into the Searing Gorge.
When Sigrun Ironhew and his men left the Uldaman excavation site, they were forced to abandon many wagons and crates of supplies along the way. The ogres from Camp Kosh plundered their abandoned equipment, which consisted of all their weapons and food. He later tasked Alliance adventurers to recover theirs supplies.
Camp Lastwind:
Camp Lastwind is a recently-established vulpera camp directly northeast of the Port of Zem'lan and southwest of the Exiles' Enclave in Vol'dun. Seemingly led by Norah, the vulpera at the camp plan to be the first to succesfully steal treasure from the Port of Zem'lan.
After escaping from Zem'lan with a Horde adventurer, First Mate Jamboya and his skeletal pirates take up residence with the vulpera at the camp.
Camp Mojache:
Camp Mojache is a tauren village in eastern Feralas overlooking the scenic Wildwind Lake. The camp straddles a swift-flowing stream that feeds the lake. Tauren refugees have started flooding into the village from Thousand Needles, mostly from Freewind Post, due to the destruction.
The camp is known for its thick hides and courageous braves offering travelers protection against the dangers of Feralas.
Camp Murroch: Camp Murroch  is a quest hub in south-central Ringing Deeps. The camp is nestled between the Living Grotto to the west, Taelloch to the east, the Rumbling Wastes to the north, and the Ancient Falls to the south.
Camp Narache:
Camp Narache is the starting town for the tauren, which is located in southern Mulgore at the northern edge of the Red Cloud Mesa. Camp Narache is the main village of the Hawkwind Tribe, and its Chief gives the first quest for tauren. It has five buildings: the main tent (where several wounded braves rest), a spirit lounge, a bakery tent, an armory tent and a simple trader's tent. The class trainers are gathered in a circle around the center of the village, paying respect to the fallen matriarch Greatmother Hawkwind.
Shortly before the shattering of the world, the camp was attacked by a fire and a centaur. Muln and his shaman could do nothing but retreat. However, Shotoa took care of it.
Camp Nooka Nooka: Camp Nooka Nooka is a hozen village in northwest Jade Forest, right next to Lake Kittitata. The small village is led by Tooki Tooki, under the great Chief Kah Kah.
Camp Nowhere:
Camp Nowhere  is a Dragonscale Expedition camp in southeastern Azure Span. Dealing with the fallout of Imbu to the southwest and the Rustpine Den to the north, the expedition is also interested in exploring the Ruins of Karnthar.
Mulsted's Marquee serves as the inn of the camp.
The area is bordered to the north by the Rustpine Den, to the southeast by the Ruins of Karnthar, to the southwest by the elite area Imbu, and to the west by the Timbertooth Trail.
Camp Oneqwah:
Camp Oneqwah is an area in central-eastern Grizzly Hills between Grizzlemaw and the coast. Tormak the Scarred and his taunka reside here. The camp is rather close to Solstice Village, so they might be fighting them. The taunka from villages across Northrend are planning to evacuate here.
Following the war against the Jailer, the Bronzebeard brothers reported that the camp had greatly expanded on account of the refugees who made the village their new home. They later visited Solstice Village, and Muradin Bronzebeard speculated that the trappers there may come into conflict with Camp Oneqwah at some point, a conflict he'd place money on the taunka winning.
Camp Stonewash: Camp Stonewash is an area located in Zul'Aman.
Camp Sungraze: Camp Sungraze is a small Horde camp and quest hub in Mulgore located northeast of Thunder Bluff.
Camp Thornscar:
Camp Thornscar is a base of the Shattered Hand clan in Shadowglade in the Spires of Arak. From there, the orcs hunt and capture arakkoa to kill and torture them. They also raise ravagers as mounts.
Thornscar is a recent establishment, as the Shattered Hand seeks to expand their domain.
Camp Tunka'lo:
Camp Tunka'lo is a small taunka village located on top of the mountains in eastern Storm Peaks, which rests high above Dun Niffelem on one side and the Plain of Echoes, with the ruined and destroyed titan Temple of Life, on the other. The village has been safe from the Scourge attacks that destroyed so many other taunka villages, thanks to its remote location.
Following the war against the Jailer, the brothers Bronzebeard visited the village. Their sentries were wary of them when they greeted them from a safe distance, but then recognized they weren't earthen or iron dwarves and were polite after, if still a bit cagey. The dwarves chose not to overstay that small amount of welcome, however.
Camp Una'fe:
Camp Una'fe (or the Camp of Refuge) is a Horde tauren camp in the Overgrowth of the Southern Barrens. When the camp was first set up, it was at the edge of the jungle, but the jungle has since grown beyond it. Lane Tallgrass thinks the camp's name, Una'fe, which means "Refuge", no longer fits.
The camp is useful as a place to run to in the event that a fight nearby starts to get overwhelming; the Tauren guards will help defend you. In addition, Gahroot (the butcher) provides great support for hunters who need food for their pets, to help them to recover between combat. Murhane can fix your gear if it happens that the wildlife has gotten the better of you. 
Several quests around level 30 are available in the camp.
Camp Winterhoof:
Camp Winterhoof is a taunka village located at the northern edge of Howling Fjord, west of Fort Wildervar, and which sits on the edge of the mountain Gjalerhorn's eastern slope. It is where Chieftain Ashtotem and his taunka reside.
The camp has bright totem poles and rounded houses—good for shedding snow—built around hot springs that bubble up from the mountain. They planned on evacuating during the events of the war against the Lich King, though whether they did or did not is unknown; as they were still actively living in the same spot years later.
After the war against the Jailer, the brothers Bronzebeards came to their gates to make an offer of friendship, and while they weren't hostile, they didn't appear overly motivated to invite the dwarves in either; as they remain loyal to the Horde.
Camp Wurg:
Camp Wurg is, together with Camp Cagg, Boff and Kosh, the homes of some of the Dustbelcher ogres. One exception though was their leader, Boss Tho'grun, who patrolled the Badlands between the four ogre bases.
During the Cataclysm, Camp Wurg was destroyed by Deathwing as it lies directly in the path of destruction that makes up the Scar of the Worldbreaker.
Cartel: A cartel refers to a large group of traders in goblin and broker society.
Cartels of Undermine:
The Cartels of Undermine is the fifth Major Faction of The War Within.
It has four sub-factions, based on favor gained with Monte Gazlowe (Bilgewater Cartel), Baron Revilgaz (Blackwater Cartel), Marin Noggenfogger (Steamwheedle Cartel), and Grimla Fizzlecrank (Venture Company). A fifth sub-faction (Gallagio Loyalty Rewards Club) is associated with the Liberation of Undermine raid. There's also Darkfuse Solutions, which unlocks after the first Chrome King Gallywix kill.
Carver's Harbor:
Carver's Harbor is a Kul Tiran slaughterhouse located on the eastern coast of Drustvar. It is a meat market, with a dock by the sea, and employed some of the greatest butchers of the region. The two buildings here are named the Hog's End Butchery and Gibb's Boat Restoration.
During the Fourth War in 33 ADP, Griffith Shelvey in Fallhaven couldn't send his latest butchery shipment to the harbor, as the witch Helena Gentle had cursed his swine with dark magic, making them unusually aggressive and difficult to corral for transport. Before being cursed, Shelvey was writing a letter to Foreman Thomas Staughton, promising that he would attempt another shipment by week's end.
At the same time, a witch of the Heartsbane Coven planted a Pig Effigy in the harbor, which turned all the workers into pigs. The area was subsequently taken over by hexed howlers and their prized butcher, Roland Hacksaw, was subsequently enslaved by the Coven. Foreman Thomas was the only one to escape and sought desperately to save his co-workers from becoming minced meat. The delay in meat delivery eventually forced vendors like Elijah Eggleton in Fallhaven to sent Alliance adventurers to investigate. After they defeated the corrupted beasts, Staughton burned down the effigy they recovered, saving the workers from the curse. As things turned back to normal, Staughton mentioned that Elijah would soon get his sausages delivery.
In Year 34 ADP, Carver's Harbor was occasionally attacked by Darktide naga who amassed prisoners to sacrifice to their dark master, until they were repelled by the adventurers.
Carving Winds:
The Carving Winds is located in southeastern Ohn'ahran Plains.
During, Fyrakk Assaults, the area is besieged and turns into  [70EWQ] Suffusion Camp: Cinderwind.
Castle Nathria: Castle Nathria is a raid in World of Warcraft: Shadowlands. It is a Gothic castle located in Revendreth, a winged raid starting with 2 wings with 3 bosses each. The raid has 10 bosses in total. The raid opened on December 8, 2020.
Catalyst Gardens: Catalyst Gardens is an area in Zereth Mortis.
Catalyst Wards: The Catalyst Wards are found just north of the Catalyst Gardens in Zereth Mortis. Entry is granted from using the Catalyst Wards Lock. The Wards and its automa are covered with overgrown flora, and it also houses the Undulating Foliage treasure.
Cataract River:
The Cataract River runs from the Waterworks at  south to the Living Grotto at  along the central western wall of the Ringing Deeps. The headwaters are at Shimmermist Falls and the river drains through the Living Grotto into Azj-Kahet.
From north to south, the river's eastern side borders Pillarstone Spire, the Rumbling Wastes, and Taelloch.
The Cataract River Cruise skyriding race starts at  just south of Pillarstone Spire.
Cauldron:
The Cauldron is an enormous excavation site in the center of the Searing Gorge. It was fortified some time after Ragnaros was summoned by the Dark Iron dwarves. It is rimmed by the giant excavation machines of the Dark Iron clan. In the burning depths of the Cauldron, fire and magma elementals traverse the fiery crevices.
Many Slave Workers captured by the Dark Irons toil away endlessly inside the Cauldron. Driven mad by their masters, the grueling work, and the constant oppressive heat, they will attack anyone interfering with their work in the Cauldron — even potential liberators.
Cavern of Lost Spirits:
The Cavern of Lost Spirits  lies beneath the Ordon Sanctuary northeast of the Celestial Court near the center of the Timeless Isle. Zarhym can frequently be found inside and starts the "Zarhym Altogether" event, a timed, phased loot-grabbing run.
The odd blue flames found within the Cavern of Lost Spirits have led many unwary adventurers to their doom.
Caverns of Contemplation:
The Caverns of Contemplation  are a cave system located underneath Keeper's Respite in northeastern Korthia. The mouth of the cave is located in the Scholar's Den.

An Anima Conduit to the Vault of Secrets is in the back of the cave.
Caverns of Time:
The Caverns of Time (or simply the Caverns) are home to the Dragon Aspect Nozdormu and his bronze dragonflight, as well as the Timewalkers. Located in the eastern part of Tanaris, it contain various portals to different key historical periods and events in Warcraft history. The caverns act as a crossroads for the various timeways, branching from the one true timeline, and through them one can travel back and forth along the ebb and flow of time.
Since the world was young, the bronze dragonflight has safeguarded the winding labyrinth, monitoring the shifting timeways to ensure that the delicate balance of time is upheld. It is the bronze dragons' sacred mission, one which was charged to them by the titans, to guard the caverns against the intrusion of mortals, whose interference would assuredly disrupt the flow of time. In recent years, a mysterious force called the infinite dragonflight meddled with time, leading the flight to recruit adventurers to make sure that the events that took place in the past remain as they were.
The hourglass at the center of the caverns are a perfect replica of the Sacred Hourglass found at the Temporal Conflux in Thaldraszus. In a similar reflection, the temple structures on the Dragon Isles lend many unique features to the anomalous lair in southern Kalimdor.
Celestial Court:
The Celestial Court  is the home of the Celestial challenges. Located in the center of the Timeless Isle, the courtyard is surrounded clockwise from the north by the Three-Breeze Terrace, the Cavern of Lost Spirits, Red Stone Run, Mossgreen Lake, Old Pi'jiu, Tushui Landing, Timeless Shore, Huojin Landing, and the Misty Strand.
By 40 ADP, there were still groups of adventurers who participated in the challenges. When they take place, it becomes a lively and noisy place. Brewmasters and street cooks sell their wares, and fireworks and kites fill the sky.
Cenarion Circle:
The Cenarion Circle (or simply the Circle) is a harmonious order that guides and keeps watch over the world's druids and their practices. The organization mostly consists of members of the tauren, jungle troll, night elf, and worgen races, but also receives help from primal manifestations of Life such as the Wild Gods and the Children of Cenarius. The Cenarion Circle are the guardians of nature, the preservers of balance, and the protectors of all life; striving to maintain the fragile balance within the world. Furthermore, their members act as keepers of ancient lore and pay particular attention to the traditional ways of the druids. The organization was blessed and named after the Lord of the Forest Cenarius, one of the most powerful and influential demigods of Azeroth.
The Cenarion Circle operates outside of the kaldorei government's authority, and is currently co-led by Cenarius, along with several Archdruids including Malfurion Stormrage, Hamuul Runetotem, and the leaders of various druid organizations. The Circle has many posts across Azeroth and even in Outland, but their main home is the town of Nighthaven in the Moonglade. Their other major presence was once the Cenarion Hold, from where they fought against the Qiraji Empire in Silithus. Years later, they used the Dreamgrove as their base in Val'sharah to repel the third invasion of the Burning Legion.
Cenarion Enclave:
The Cenarion Enclave is a major district and a grove in the night elven capital of Darnassus, where the city's druids reside and meet. Archdruid Fandral Staghelm formerly led his followers and kin from the boughs of the Enclave, until Malfurion Stormrage returned from the Emerald Dream during the War Against the Nightmare. The area remains a hub for druid trainers.
Below-ground, a secretive rogue guild can be found if one knows where to look within the westernmost bough. Darnassus's hunters also come to the Cenarion Enclave to train in the easternmost tree, while the skill and means to ride nightsabers can also be obtained at the foot of the Enclave tree.
The Cenarion Enclave is located in the northwest of the city, accessible from the Temple Gardens to the south, Craftsmen's Terrace to the east, and the Howling Oak to the north. Tall trees — oaks and ashes especially — lined the enclave. Each tree bore mystic runes shaped from the very bark. Within the circular grove, a handful of unique structures molded both from living wood and carefully-shaped stones represent the usual gathering place for convocations. The largest of these structures served as the residence of Fandral Staghelm.
Cenarion Expedition:
The Cenarion Expedition is a faction of night elves and tauren based in Zangarmarsh and led by Ysiel Windsinger. The Expedition was sent by the Cenarion Circle to Outland shortly after the Dark Portal was reopened in order to study the surviving life forms of that uncharted world. Although it began as a small organization directly controlled by the Circle, the Expedition has grown to become an autonomous organization, independent of the Circle's leadership on Azeroth. In fact, Circle reputation (regardless of how good or bad) bears no weight with the Expedition, and all characters begin at neutral with them.
The primary base of operations for the Cenarion Expedition is Cenarion Refuge in eastern Zangarmarsh. Additional Expedition outposts are located in Hellfire Peninsula, Terokkar Forest and Blade's Edge Mountains.
The Druid organization D.E.H.T.A. in Northrend is also aligned with the Cenarion Expedition, and their quests give reputation with this faction.
At some point, the Cenarion Expedition requested help from the Omenai at the Temple of Telhamat, in order to study what happened in the region and help reverse any damage possible. Amaan the Wise accepted and later sent the adventurers in support.
Cenarion Hold:
Cenarion Hold was a location of utmost strategic importance in Silithus and one of the biggest druid settlements in Kalimdor — almost as big as Moonglade itself. The Cenarion Circle took over the duty of defending the ancient night elven settlement against the increasingly hostile and aggressive silithid and other forces that had set foot in the troubled region, establishing the Fort, after the War of the Shifting Sands to guard the imprisoned Old God C'Thun and its armies.
The settlement was reached on foot by following the well-worn track through the Un'Goro Crater northwest from the Mossy Pile. The path climbs steeply up the cliff, and switches back on itself to enter Silithus. The merchants of Cenarion Hold gladly sold their goods to any adventurer who passed through, since business was hard to come by.

 This section concerns content related to Legion.
The hold was destroyed along with the rest of Silithus when Sargeras tried to destroy Azeroth at the end of the third invasion of the Burning Legion. Malfurion Stormrage reported that everyone in the hold was killed instantly. During a ceremony in Thunder Bluff, Hamuul Runetotem advocated recreating the Cenarion Hold, and some in Orgrimmar are wondering whether Cenarion Hold is needed now that C'Thun and his aqir are defeated.
Cenarion Post: Cenarion Post is a small camp located on the northern part of the Sha'naari Wastes in western Hellfire Peninsula. It's neutral to both Alliance and Horde, and is the first encounter Outland adventurers get with the Cenarion Expedition faction. Several quests are offered here by agents of the Cenarion Expedition.
Cenarion Refuge:
Cenarion Refuge is a neutral faction town in Zangarmarsh. The town was originally founded by the Cenarion Circle, who came to Outland to study the local flora and fauna. Their presence became so large in outland, that the Cenarion Expedition was formed as Outland's sub-faction of the Cenarion Circle.
The city is fully functional, with a mailbox, an inn, a general goods vendor, trade goods vendor, armor repair, cooking and fishing trainers, as well as many quests. However, Cenarion Refuge does NOT have a flight master; Alliance players can fly to nearby Telredor and Horde players to Swamprat Post instead. Players start out at neutral with the Expedition, but reputation gains are very generous. There is a repeatable turn-in quest to help players progress from neutral through honored by turning in  [Unidentified Plant Parts] to Lauranna Thar'well.
Cenarion Thicket:
Cenarion Thicket is a Cenarion Expedition encampment overrun by vicious moths and dangerous gases. All the druids here are dead, except three.
Only one druid in the Cenarion Thicket survived, Warden Treelos. He went mad, though, and is found talking about tea time and how it's watching him. Earthbinder Tavgren, a Cenarion tauren druid returning from a scouting mission, found the Thicket devastated and with all the druids, but Treelos, dead. Tavgren starts a line of quests which lets the player find out that:

Except for all the druid corpses, there is one single Broken corpse with a strange black box next to it, which later is discovered to be a prototype of a mana bomb.
After asking Empoor, a traveling Broken merchant, he says the black boxes came from an ethereal merchant in Shattrath City, nearby.
After talking to Wind Trader Lathrai, and after having done his errands, he says that there might be more black boxes in the nearby city of Tuurem.
There is one. After touching it, broken ambushers and a Firewing Courier attack you. The Firewings are blood elves allied to Kael'thas and Illidan, and have allied with the broken and Lost Ones from Tuurem.
After killing a lot of Blood elves and their leader at Firewing Point, the blood elf base, it's discovered they are creating the so-called "Mana Bomb" and are making the project at Firewing Point.
Then the players kill Sharth Voldoun, the overseer of the project, and made the mana bomb explode within the blood elf base.
The only one who knows exactly what happened in Cenarion Thicket is Warden Treelos, and although he tries to tell players, his madness has gone too far to tell players exactly.
To summarize: The Wrekt sent a messenger to suicide-bomb the Thicket, as vengeance for the druids destroying the colossi. The bomb was devised by the blood elves allied to Kael'thas. The ingredients of the bomb were delivered by them via Empoor, who got it from a dimension-traveling ethereal. The Thicket is now overrun with mutated moths and only three druids survived: Warden Treelos, Earthbinder Tavgren and Isla Starmane.
Cenarius:
Cenarius (/səˈnɑː.ɹi.əs/ sə-NAH-ree-əs), Lord of the Forest and patron of many druids, is one of the most powerful and influential demigods of Azeroth. Worshipped by the night elves since their early history, the Son of Malorne taught the elves to be druids and embrace nature, as opposed to the arcane-inclined Highborne and the religiously-inclined Sisterhood of Elune. He served as a commander of the forces of Kalimdor in the War of the Ancients after the death of his father. He continued serving as a teacher and protector of the elves and their forests for 10,000 years until he was killed by the demonically corrupted orcs led by Grom Hellscream.
Several years later, he was brought back into the world with the awakened Ysera through the Gates of Sothann to aid in defending Hyjal from Ragnaros and the resurgent Twilight's Hammer. He now serves as a leader of the Cenarion Circle.
Centaur:
The centaur (sometimes pluralized as centaurs) are a warlike humanoid race with human-like upper bodies and the lower bodies of horses. Two discrete centaur civilizations exist. The first, the Maruuk Centaur, date back to before the War of the Ancients and rule the Ohn'ahran Plains on the Dragon Isles, where they worship the wind god Ohn'ahra and hunt the wild game of the region. Although split into many different clans ruled by various khans, they share a single culture. The Maruuk's ancestors forged a pact with the green dragonflight, but were cut off from the rest of the world when the Dragon Isles were hidden after the Great Sundering.
Millennia later, a separate, more cruel and primitive centaur civilization was born on Kalimdor from the union of Zaetar and Theradras. These centaur roam the plains of Central Kalimdor (primarily Desolace and the Barrens) and are the mortal enemies of the tauren, whom they hunted for centuries until the arrival of the Horde. Although their clans have historically warred among themselves, Horde and Alliance efforts to unite the tribes against common foes have met with some success.
Chained Precipice: The Chained Precipice is a fragment of Zereth Mortis pulled onto the northeastern side of the Crown of Gorgoa in the upper Sanctum of Domination by the Jailer's chains, which are anchored in the Loom of Fates on the floor above. The Guardian of the First Ones resides here, protecting its masters' cyphers from the Mawsworn.
Chamber of the Sigil: The Chamber of the Sigil  is found when a portal is open in the Vault of Secrets in southern Korthia. The sigil of the Primus was placed here after he entrusted it to Korthia's vaults. Players may only access the chamber while on the quest  [60] Into the Vault.
Champions of Azeroth: Champions of Azeroth is a faction located in the Wound and the Chamber of Heart in Silithus. Their goal is to heal Azeroth from the damage caused by Sargeras with his sword. They are primarily helped in this task by shaman of the Earthen Ring and druids from the Cenarion Circle.
Chi-Ji: Chi-Ji the Red Crane is a Wild God and one of the four August Celestials who watch over Pandaria. He watches over the Valley of the Four Winds and Krasarang Wilds and is sometimes referred to as the Southern Celestial or the Spirit of Hope. As such, he is served by the monks and priests of the Crane Wing order at the Temple of the Red Crane. Chi-Ji also takes the guise of Fat Long-Fat.
Chillwind Camp: Chillwind Camp is an Alliance encampment in the Western Plaguelands. It is located in the south, at the entrance to the Plaguelands from Chillwind Point in the Alterac Mountains.
Chip Off the Block: Chip Off the Block is located in the Forgegrounds in Dornogal.
Chiselgrip: Chiselgrip is a neutral Thorium Brotherhood camp located southwest of the Ruins of Thaurissan in the Burning Steppes.  It serves as a quest hub from which adventurers strike undercover at the Blackrock clan, after making the necessary preparations at Flamestar Post. Despite not being listed as one, Hoddruc Bladebender is a repair vendor. It has a flight path and two forges located near Stebben Oreknuckle.
Chittering Den:
The Chittering Den  is a kobold- and undercrawler- filled area in the Ringing Deeps. Located on the mid-eastern wall, the area is bordered by the Obsidian Hollow to the southwest, the Fetid Grotto, Shadowvein Point and the Shadowvein Extraction Site to the west, and the Warrens to the northwest. The lower part is home to friendly kobold grubtenders who raise domesticated jawcrawlers, but the area has been infested by undercrawlers that prey on both the kobolds and their grubs. The upper parts have been taken over by the Glumtooth Gang, cronies of the Candle King who are building an army of captured bugs for war with the Machine Speakers.
The Dread Pit delve instance line is at  in a small cave on the eastern wall, and the Chittering Concourse skyriding race is at  on the northern wall near the Warrens.
Church of the Holy Light:
The Church of Light (full name the Church of the Holy Light or simply the Church) is the religious institution at the head of the predominant human religion, the worship of the Holy Light. Founded around 1,200 BDP in Lordaeron, the Church's precepts were codified from the different Light-based traditions and belief systems used by a religious movement under the Empire of Arathor, which was formed by the priestess Mereldar and her companions after they received mysterious visions from holy beings. For centuries, the Church spread its faith through the Seven Kingdoms, building temples, shrines, and churches throughout the far-flung human lands as places of worship, with a hierarchy of religious leaders to oversee its devoted followers.
By embodying the tenets of their religion, the Church's skilled clergy can wield holy magic. Believing that the Light dwells on each and every being, its members are dedicated to creating a world of honor and justice, striving to aid others and be good in all actions, they also seek to be the best of oneself. Among their ranks, the priests heal and restore in times of peace, and protect their allies in times of war. The paladins of the Order of the Silver Hand act as the Church's martial branch, enforcing its laws, protecting the weak, and vanquishing the evil across Azeroth.
By the time of the Second War, the Church's followers included most of the people from all the human kingdoms combined. Archbishop Alonsus Faol later offered its support to the Alliance of Lordaeron against the Orcish Horde. During the Third War, the Church concentrated its efforts to contain the Plague of Undeath and cure the sick, but was ultimately wiped out when Lordaeron fell to the Scourge. Eventually, the institution was reformed by Archbishop Benedictus and his bishops at the Cathedral of Light of Stormwind City. They have been dedicated to the cause of the Alliance ever since.
Cinderside Hall: The Cinderside Hall is located in the Corridors in Dornogal.
Cinderwold:
The Cinderwold (once known as the Cindercreg) is an elite area in the eastern part of the Isle of Dorn. This ironwood forest is primarily inhabited by cinderbees, though storm wolves can be found here as well. The Ironwold lies to the west and the Cinderbrew Meadery lies to the east.
The world quest  [80WQ] Special Assignment: Cinderbee Surge takes place here.
Circle of Ancients:
The Circle of Ancients is a group of Ancients who meet at the Grove of the Ancients in Darkshore. They at least have enough authority to make large decisions, such as pooling their powers to help Archdruid Fandral Staghelm and his druids in growing the new World Tree of Teldrassil. Sentinel Tysha Moonblade was sent to explore the ruins of Ameth'Aran and, after discovering information on Ameth'Aran's fall, delivered a report on her findings to the Circle.
At some point, Velinde Starsong asked the Circle for help with the worgen that she had unleashed in Ashenvale, but they weren't able to help her.
City Center: The City Center is an area of Eredath located near Azurelight Square and the Ruins of Oronaar.  It is a travel hub, consisting of a small draenei structure hosting a Lightforged Beacon defended by Lightforged Bulwarks.
City of Threads: The City of Threads is the capital of the nerubian kingdom of Azj-Kahet, taking up the southernmost third of the Azj-Kahet zone. A sprawling, decaying city that falls away into the depths, the capital has been built on top of itself many times over. As old districts (such as Ara-Kara) crumble, new ones are built on their ruins, resulting in a city that climbs ever higher. Citizens possessing enormous wealth or the favor of Queen Ansurek live in hanging nests and huge palaces over the swarming masses of the many other districts.
Clan Aylaag: Clan Aylaag is a Maruuk Centaur clan. Nomads, their caravan makes its way across the Ohn'aran Plains.
Clan Kaighan:
Clan Kaighan is one of the lesser maruuk centaur clans, located within the Ohn'ahran Plains. The clan plays relatively no role in the story, only serving as the captors of Initiate Radiya when she wanders too close to their camp. They appear to have allied with Clan Nokhud, as the clan is notably hostile to adventurers, and several Storm Extractors can be found within a cave in the clan's home. They are draining the power from a thunder lizard named Lizi; who is a friend of Radiya's. She asks adventurers to free them and bring them back to Ohn'iri Springs.
Kaighan centaur are also capable of dropping  [Tempest Armaments]; confirming their loyalty.
Clan Nokhud: Clan Nokhud is one of the four major Maruuk centaur clans of the Ohn'ahran Plains. They are the newest clan to rise to power and maintains the largest standing military force. Led by Balakar Khan, the Nokhud have allied with the Primalists and turned against the rest of the Maruuk. Their seat of power is Nokhudon Hold.
Clan Ohn'ir: Clan Ohn'ir is one of the four major Maruuk centaur clans of the Ohn'ahran Plains. It consists of mystics who feel a special connection their god, Ohn'ahra, and serve as spiritual advisors to the other clans. Their khan is Tigari Khan and their main seat of power is the Ohn'iri Springs.
Clan Shikaar: Clan Shikaar is one of the four major Maruuk centaur clans of the Ohn'ahran Plains. They specialize in honing their skills and hunting game across the plains, and are led by Sansok Khan.
Clan Teerai: Clan Teerai is one of the four major Maruuk centaur clans of the Ohn'ahran Plains. They are responsible for upholding the traditions of the ancestors and guiding the Maruuk according to their ways. The Teerai are not led by a normal khan but instead by the Khanam Matra (currently Khanam Matra Sarest), who acts as the cultural khan of all Maruuk. Their seat of power is Teerakai.
Clan Toghus:
Clan Toghus is one of the minor Maruuk centaur clans of the Ohn'ahran Plains. It was formerly one of the four major centaur clans, before they were usurped by Clan Nokhud.
Holding major power in the plains, they were an extremely resourceful people, consisting of skilled gatherers, trackers, and animal trainers. The raw materials they gathered were highly desired by crafters from the other clans, and their animals helped them in many endeavors. They were also known for their food. They were based out of Toghusuq Village.
One generation before the awakening of the Dragon Isles, Jhakan Khan of Clan Nokhud raised a mighty army and defeated the Toghus, taking over their territory and their position as one of the four strongest Maruuk clans. The Toghus were not fighters, and their last khan, Faraqseng, incorrectly assumed that their prestige would be enough to protect them from Jhakan's ambitions. He hoped that the remaining Toghus would settle into new lives.
Some of the Toghus survived and went on to form the village of Daruukhan, a village of craftsmen; though this village too was destroyed when the Nokhud allied with the Primalists. The surviving members of the clan were aided by an adventurer and the kind bakar Taivan; retreating back to Maruukai.
Clan Ukhel:
Clan Ukhel is one of the lesser maruuk centaur clans, located within the Ohn'ahran Plains. In dramatically stark contrast to the other centaur clans, the Ukhel practice necromancy; using the magic to raise the spirits of many bakar and ohuna in The Eternal Kurgans. They have allied with Clan Nokhud, and ultimately commit greater sacrilege by using their dark magic to raise the spirits of long deceased ancestors and khans to fight against the other Centaurs during the Nokhud Offensive.
The clan's leader, Gravelord Monkh, attempts to desecrate the spirits of Teera and Maruuk; succeeding in awakening them but not enthralling them. They are soon after killed by the awakened centaur spirits, who are outraged at the idea that their legacy has been besmirched by some of their kindred defiling graves.
Cliff's Edge: Cliff's Edge is a small tauren outpost found on the cliffs Highmountain. It overlooks the Witchwood as well.
Cliffwalker Post:
Cliffwalker Post is a small tauren village on a rise in northern Stonetalon Mountains. It is home to the Cliffwalker family. The village was burned by orders from Overlord Krom'gar after his army's general was killed by the tauren leaders.

 This section concerns content related to the Warcraft novels, novellas, or short stories.
Its rising path is dotted by tauren totems. When Aramar Thorne and Taryndrella passed by Cliffwalker Post, Aram could see figures moving among the trees at the top of the rise. A heavily armed tauren brave emerged down the path that led to the post, but he did not notice them and returned. A few minutes later, Galena Stormspear‎ went by it and several tauren braves noticed her and charged at her. Aram and Drella, now with a subdued ram named Blossom, joined with Galena and managed to flee.
Cobalt Assembly:
The Cobalt Assembly  is the home of the Cobalt Assembly faction of blue dragons in north-central Azure Span. The area has been taken over by the Sundered Flame, and the blues of the area are asking for adventurers to help restore their cache of arcana.
Atop the central tower, a group of young dracthyr are using the area as a library.
Outside of the quest hub, the surrounding areas are an elite area and are best tackled with a group of well-geared adventurers.
The Training Grounds at the eastern end of the Assembly are a free-for-all PvP area, and a world quest from Malicia ( [70WQ] Wild Arcana) asks players to kill other players or destroy Unstable Arcana fairly frequently. To the northeast, the Forge of Arcanum is held by the Spellforged Destroyer.
The assembly is bordered to the east and southeast by the Upper Frostlands, to the southwest by Camp Antonidas, and north by the Dragonsprings Summit of the Ohn'ahran Plains.
The flight master, Kruthix, has connections to Theron's Watch, Rhonin's Shield, Camp Antonidas, and Three-Falls Lookout in the Azure Span; Forkriver Crossing and Pinewood Post in the Ohn'ahran Plains; and Garden Shrine in Thaldraszus.
Coilfang Reservoir:
Coilfang Reservoir is a large artificial cavern located in Zangarmarsh. Under Serpent Lake is a subterranean pumping station, operated by Lady Vashj and the sinister naga. The dungeons are found in this underground area, and consist of gigantic caverns with huge pipes descending from the ceiling powered by titanic crystal capacitors. While the entrance to the reservoir is underwater, the instances themselves are only partially submerged, similar to Blackfathom Deeps.
Four instances comprise Coilfang Reservoir: three 5-man dungeons and one 25-man raid. Similar to Hellfire Citadel where the dungeons are designed for differing levels, The Slave Pens is designed for levels 61 to 64 and the Underbog is designed for levels 62 to 65, while both the 5-man The Steamvault and the 25-man Serpentshrine Cavern raid are designed for level 70 players.
Cold Hearth Manor:
Cold Hearth Manor is a farmstead in central Tirisfal Glades, formerly known for its warm atmosphere and bountiful crops. After the Plague of Undeath claimed the lives of everyone who lived or worked here, the fields have grown barren and become infested with mindless Scourge zombies.
The Forsaken managed to claim the farmhouse for themselves. They now offer trade opportunities to travelers passing on the main road nearby.

 This section concerns content related to Shadowlands.
After the Forsaken reclaimed Brill, Tirisfal Farmers took control of the manor, and Scarlet Warriors patroled the road in front of it.
Colossal's Fall:
Colossal's Fall is a Thunderlord settlement in northern Frostfire Ridge, north of the Cracking Plains. Much like the capital, Grom'gar, Colossal's Fall is built in the corpse of an earth giant.
The Thunderlord regard Colossal's Fall as a sacred location, claiming it was their clan who felled this colossal many decades ago.
Commons:
The Commons is the main thoroughfare for trade in the city of Ironforge. It contains the bank, Auction House and inn, as well as a few shops. The Commons is always the busiest and most crowded portion of the city.
To get to the Commons, you can head northeast from the Gates of Ironforge, southwest from the Great Forge, west from the Military Ward, or south from the Mystic Ward.
Ironforge was the home of the original Alliance auction house, and before expansions pulled away the top level population, this area was infamous for its lag.
Conquest Hold:
Conquest Hold is the main Horde stronghold in the Grizzly Hills. The fortress walls are built around a deep fighting pit. During the war against the Lich King, the hold was run by an orc named Conqueror Krenna, who was aggressive and ill-tempered even for the Horde, and ruled over the forces stationed there.
At some point, she ended up challenged in her own pit and was killed by her sister Gorgonna, who became the new leader of the Conquest Hold.
Barracks serves as the local inn.
Conservatory of the Arcane:
The Conservatory of the Arcane is a location in Eredath. It was the greatest school of magic on Argus. The Augari, Consulate, and Wakeners orders were based here and led by Archimonde, who was himself an alumnus.
The eredar once stored great quantities of energy throughout power conduits here. Several native species were drawn to the area because of its latent energies, including panthara and marsuul.
Quoram was once the keeper of the Conservatory's keys, custodian to all of its locks and gates.
Based on the quotes of lingering spirits in the Conservatory, it seems they didn’t fled with Velen and the Draenei and died when the Legion came upon them.
It is divided into the Hall of Enlightenment, the Praetorium, and the Wakener's Enclave.
Consortium:
The Consortium is a loosely affiliated cartel of ethereal smugglers, traders, and thieves that have come to Outland to benefit from its riches. Led by Nexus-Prince Haramad, their main base of operations is the Stormspire in Netherstorm, but they can also be found in Midrealm Post, at Aeris Landing in Nagrand, within the Mana-Tombs of Auchindoun, and various other places across the broken world. The Consortium is also known to do business in the Hara'samid Sector, on Heraazi, Sodaraami, and the Xarodi Sector.
According to their recruiters, the Consortium is looking for resourceful individuals with loyalty, dedication, and a reasonable amount of moral flexibility. They are well known for taking good care of their friends, who receive gems as payment for their services each month, and whose quality depends on how loyal they've been to the cartel.
They are allied with another ethereal faction, the Protectorate, which was formed in reaction to the obsessive search for vengeance of the Ethereum ruling class against Dimensius the All-Devouring.
Coreway:
The Coreway is an immense tunnel extending from Dornogal on the surface deep into Azeroth. It was built by the titan-forged so that the titans could study Azeroth's worldsoul without harming it. At one point, the Coreway extended all the way to the core of Azeroth; at present it terminates in the Ringing Deeps.
The Coreway is found in the southwest corner of Dornogal. After fending off a nerubian invasion in  [68-70] They Come from Below, part of the Isle of Dorn storyline, the Coreway serves as the passage into the continent down to the Ringing Deeps. The Archive is on the western edge of its entrance, the Forgegrounds lie to the west, and a passage leads north to Keepers Terrace and Foundation Hall.
Corin's Crossing: Corin's Crossing is a ruined town in south-central Eastern Plaguelands, located on a crossroads between Andorhal, Darrowshire, Stratholme, and Tyr's Hand and nestled between the shores of the Infectis Scar and Lake Mereldar. Light's Shield Tower is located just to the north. The town, which has a town hall and blacksmith, is filled to the brim with Scourge. Even rogues using  [Stealth] are advised not to attempt to sneak through the town, as the invisible Unseen Servants can see through stealth.
Corlain:
Corlain is the regional capital and largest city of Drustvar, serving as the seat of power for House Waycrest. The settlement itself is divided into an upper and lower section, with Waycrest Manor dominating the northern portion of town. The Waycrest Guard are responsible for keeping order within Corlain. It is surrounded by numerous outlying fixtures, including an armory to the south, aviary to the north, Bleak Hills Mine to the east, and Whitegrove Chapel to the west. The city has its own access to the sea via Chandlery Wharf, and is further protected by the Watchman's Rise outpost covering the eastern approach.
During the Fourth War, Corlain fell under the control of the Heartsbane Coven, along with much of Drustvar. Led by Lady Meredith Waycrest herself, the witches occupied the city, corrupted the guards, and used its citizens in horrifying rituals. Those who survived the disaster had fled to Arom's Stand seeking refuge, until the Order of Embers waged a war to drive the Coven from the city. After the Alliance adventurers defeated Gorak Tul, the city was cleansed of the corruption and was reinvested by its citizens, while Lady Lucille Waycrest succeeded her parents as ruler of Corlain.
Council of Dornogal: The Council of Dornogal is the ruling council of the earthen of Khaz Algar.
Council of Oracles:
The Council of Oracles was a group of elite K'areshi Oracles who constituted the ruling authority of K'aresh prior to its destruction, and its members guided the K'areshi people through all facets of life. At the onset of the Devouring War it was lead by the High Priest of the Untamed, Salhadaar, but during the war he renounced his position as High Priest and its leadership fell to his confidante the Soul-Scribe.
The Council of Oracles' customary gathering place for meetings was in Tazavesh, though its members could request for it to meet elsewhere with the High Priest's approval.
After the destruction of K'aresh and the Oracles' loss of connection to their Worldsoul, members of the Council of Oracles formed the Ethereum under the leadership of the former High Priest and now Nexus-King Salhadaar and became the Nexus-Princes, while the Soul-Scribe formed the Wastelanders.
Council of Six: The Council of Six, also known as the Six, the high council, the Dalaran Council, or the Ruling Council, was the name given to the Kirin Tor high council of Dalaran. These six individuals were the leaders of both the city and all territories under the control of Dalaran. The Six were usually the most senior, but not necessarily the most gifted. They were chosen by several means, magic but one of them.
Council of Three Hammers:
The Council of Three Hammers is a council of the dwarven people, established to ensure fair and even representation in the City of Ironforge. Formed in the wake of Moira Thaurissan's ill-fated coup of the city following her father, King Magni Bronzebeard, being crystalized in Old Ironforge, the council represents all three types of dwarf from Khaz Modan. A seat is reserved for a representative of the Bronzebeard clan, Dark Iron clan, and Wildhammer clan. As the name suggests, its members are referred to as the Three Hammers.
The council also provincially rules over Ironforge until its heir presumptive, Dagran Thaurissan II, son of Moira, reaches the age of majority. When that day comes, this arrangement will come to an end. The council itself does not seem to be set to be dismissed upon this occasion, as pointed out by both Moira and Falstad following Magni's re-awakening.
Court of Farondis:
The Court of Farondis are a group of night elven ghosts cursed by the destruction of the Tidestone of Golganneth in Azsuna.
They are one of the factions heroes can acquire reputation for in order to purchase certain toys and gear in Legion.
Court of Harvesters:
The Court of Harvesters are a reputation faction in Revendreth comprised of venthyr and their servants. The court is made up of the eponymous Harvesters; venthyr that were created or chosen from former mortals by Denathrius to represent certain sins to be used in the name of Revendreth. These seven harvesters were gifted with special medallions that gave them tremendous powers. After Denathrius' turn to the Jailer, elements of the court rose up in defiance. By the end of the  [Venthyr Campaign], only the faction that rose against Denathrius survives, and more and more venthyr are binding themselves to the court instead of the Master and his tyrants. 
If one joins the Venthyr Covenant, one is accepting the gift of the Court of Harvesters.
The Court of Harvesters collectively replaced Denathrius as rulers of Revendreth.
Court of Night: The Court of Night is the court of the Winter Queen of Ardenweald. It is composed primarily of the droman of each the Celestial trees, the leaders of the Wild Hunt, and a few other members. Meetings are held in the Heart of the Forest.
Crane Wing Refuge: Crane Wing Refuge is a camp of refugees found near the Krasarang River, in the Deepwild of north-central Krasarang Wilds.
Crane Wing order: The Crane Wing order is an order of monks and priests serving the August Celestial Chi-Ji in the Krasarang Wilds. They traditionally wear red armor and robes.
Crapopolis:
Crapopolis is a goblin town located on the southern shore of Kezan. It was used by Mogul Razdunk and his Venture Company to mine Azerite. The Horde and Alliance eventually defeated him and ended his operation. Not much later, Jastor Gallywix bought the town, making it a part of his Bilgewater Cartel. Hobart Grapplehammer had a workshop in the area where he had been working on the X-52 Personnel Armor. Goblin adventurers later came here to help Hobart defeat Gallywix, who wanted to steal the invention.
It is unknown if the town continued under the cartel following Gallywix's abandonment of them, as it was repeatedly noted that he had personally purchased the area for his own seat of power. Following Gallywix's death during the Liberation of Undermine, the fate of the town still remains unknown.
Crash Site:
The Crash Site is where a large piece of the Exodar crash-landed in Ammen Vale. The area offers vendors, quest givers, and trainers for young draenei adventurers.
In Year 26 ADP, when the Exodar crashed on the Azuremyst Isles, one of its sections fell in the vale upon impact. Using the area as refuge, the draenei began to heal the survivors of the accident, and had to use the nearby vale moths' blood to replenish their stock of healing crystals. The pandaren Mojo Stormstout was cataloging the local wildlife when the Exodar crashed, and later came to help the survivors at the Crash Site.
When the adventurers reached Azure Watch outside the vale, Technician Dyvuun promised them he would soon send aid and supplies to the Crash Site.
Crestfall Rise: Crestfall Rise is a subzone of Ashran, the physical tower found in the Archmage Overwatch zone. The tower appears to be named for its inhabitant the Alliance Tower Guardian Rylai Crestfall, who can be found here surveying the battle below, and smiting any enemies within range with her frost and ice magic. The tower itself is cloaked in a constant snowstorm, no doubt thanks to the mage's magics.
Crimson Watch:
Crimson Watch is a small blood elf base that oversees the Path of Conquest in southern Shadowmoon Valley. The elves are part of a group known as the Crimson Sigil, and are the elite blood elf guards of Lord Illidan.
Marcus Auralion, High General of the Sha'tar, is kept imprisoned in a crystal here. Upon retrieving the journal of Val'zareq the Conqueror and taking it to him, the Battle of the Crimson Watch begins.
Croaking Hollow:
The Croaking Hollow  is the southeastern beach of Timeless Isle. Bordered by the Red Stone Run to the north, and the Firewalker Ruins and the Firewalkers' Path high above on the cliffs, the hollow is home to poisonous frogs! The frogs also guard one of the four Sturdy Chests on the isle.
Offshore is a pirate ship, which has a Gleaming Treasure Satchel hanging from a boom.
An unnamed cave below the water contains a Grim Campfire, serving as a portal to Gorgrond.
Crossroads:
The Crossroads is the largest Horde town in the Northern Barrens, aptly named for the crossing of the main north-south road (from the Gold Road) and the road from Ratchet in the east all the way to the Stonetalon Mountains in the west. Combined with its central location and the wyvern flight routes, the Crossroads offers access to nearly all Horde outposts in Kalimdor. As such, this small crossing is usually the first place you will see large gatherings of players outside of Orgrimmar or Thunder Bluff.
The Crossroads graveyard is considered the default graveyard for Horde players, much like the Sentinel Hill graveyard for Alliance players.
Despite having only few lodgings, the Crossroads is a busy bustling trade center. Traders enjoy shouting their wares and interests. Just past the settlement, there is a burial area that the Horde members visit to pay their respects to the dead.
Crown Guard Tower:
Crown Guard Tower is a scout tower located in the Eastern Plaguelands. During the Scourge invasion of Lordaeron, Crown Guard Tower was destroyed and left in ruins. Later it became a battleground as it was one of the fallen towers that the Alliance and Horde fought over for in order to fortify themselves in Lordaeron. The Crown Guard Tower, along with all the other towers of the Eastern Plaguelands, have since been rebuilt by the Argent Crusade and is being used as an outpost for the region. Like the nearby Light's Hope Chapel, there are signs of life around the tower, and there is also a neutral flight master. 
To the right of Argus Highbeacon, there is a Argent Parachutes chest which applies a 5 second Parachute debuff. One can only presume that Blizzard understands the players' affinity for exiting a tower by jumping over the ledge.
Crucible of the Damned:
The Crucible of the Damned  is the southwestern portion of the Maw mainland. Players notably first land here in  [10-60] Through the Shattered Sky, part of the Shadowlands intro experience. It is bordered by Calcis to the north and Gorgoa: River of Souls to the east and south.
A Chaotic Riftstone to the Tremaculum is available once players unlock it with the  [Encased Riftwalker Essence].
Crusader Forward Camp: Crusader Forward Camp is a small camp near the Dead Fields in Zul'Drak. It was established by a group of Argent Crusaders, but soon after fell under Scourge attack and their steam tank destroyed. Engineer Reed is currently attempting to repair it so they can stand a chance against the hoards of zombies.
Crusaders' Pinnacle: Crusaders' Pinnacle (or Crusaders' Spire) is a small mountain plateau northwest of Argent Vanguard and north of Dalaran in Icecrown. Once controlled by the Scourge, it was taken over by the Argent Crusade, who built Justice Keep there. Since then, the area is supporting a mailbox, vendor, and a flight master, as well as several quests. While there's no innkeeper the inside does act as an inn.
Crushblow:
Crushblow is a Horde outpost in the Twilight Highlands. It was established by the warriors of the Axebite alongside the Dragonmaw clan and Kor'kron under Zaela, and the Forsaken sent by Sylvanas Windrunner under Lady Cozwynn. This combined force assailed the Twilight Gate, seeking to accomplish their mission of stemming the tide of the Twilight's Hammer.

 This section concerns content related to Battle for Azeroth.
Following the Fourth War, Commander Dresh was overseeing construction in Crushblow when the peons of the region disappeared. Seeking to prove the vulpera's usefulness in the Horde, an adventurer and Kiro set out for the outpost to find out what happened to the peons. Heading out to the area, they found the peons hid away in the old Dunwald Holdout; now renamed Peon Hideout. Within, they found that the peons had revolted under Foreman Magrok. Finding that the peons of Crushblow felt undervalued, Kiro and the adventurer set about breaking apart the revolt. They went about this by gathering supplies for a party, giving promotions, and repairing their tools; culminating in a feast in Crushblow. With this all done, the adventurer then challenged Foreman Magrok and defeated him in a duel; thus ensuring the peons returned to work and the foreman resumed his duties.
Crushridge: The Crushridge are a group of ogres residing in the Alterac Mountains.
Cryo-Core:
The Cryo-Core is a cryogenic core from the Exodar that had crash-landed on Bloodmyst Isle. It served as a pod holding area like the one in Ammen Vale.
In Year 26 ADP, after Vindicator Boros received rapports of the Cryo-Core's location, Vindicator Kuros sent draenei adventurers to search for supplies and survivors, however, they found only Sunhawk blood elves scavenging the area. At the request of Morae, the heroes looked for her missing husband, Galaen, who worked as a technician in the Cryo-Core. They eventually found Galaen's corpse within the ruins, where his ghost told them he survived the crash, only to be killed by the sin'dorei infiltrators, and that his last thoughts were for his wife.
Galaen's Journal later revealed that Vindicator Saruan, a leader of the Hand of Argus, had been captured and taken to the Cryo-Core, where he was tortured and killed at the hands of Matis the Cruel.
Cult of the Damned:
The Cult of the Damned is an order of living beings who served the Lich King. It was formed years prior to the Third War, as the predecessor and creator of the Scourge, in order to establish a foothold on Lordaeron for the Burning Legion's return. The Lich King Ner'zhul, trapped within the Frozen Throne, reached out telepathically any dark soul lusted for power that would hear his call - most notably the then-Archmage Kel'Thuzad who would become an Archlich and the creator and leader of the Cult of the Damned. The cult is notorious for concocting grandiose plans that in the end, rarely succeed.
Although its members aspire to become undead, they remain alive because undeath is considered an honor that must be earned; they are also valuable to the Lich King for infiltrating Horde and Alliance settlements, as well as recruiting powerful individuals into either the Cult or the Scourge. The Cult ranks consists mostly of humans, but orcs, high elves, and other races are also present.
Following the rise of Bolvar Fordragon as the new Lich King, the Cult of the Damned began operating independently, leading the remaining Scourge strongholds across Azeroth. After the destruction of the Helm of Domination, the organization re-emerged across the world, answering the call of the Jailer's herald, who preached that the "Banished One" would claim the soul of Azeroth and that all would serve him.
D.E.H.T.A. Encampment: The D.E.H.T.A. Encampment is a D.E.H.T.A. camp located in central Borean Tundra, just southeast of Lake Kum'uya. In the middle of the encampment is a bonfire dwarf, which symbolizes their hate for Hemet Nesingwary.
Da'kani: The Da'kani are a tribe of intelligent gorillas in Gorilla Gorge in Zuldazar. They became enlightened due to exposure to kaja'mite, which wasn't always there.
Dabyrie's Farmstead:
Dabyrie's Farmstead is a farm located in the northern reaches of the Arathi Highlands. It is the home of the Dabyrie family—Kenata Dabyrie and her children Fardel and Marcel—citizens of the kingdom of Stromgarde and members of the Alliance. The farmstead is protected by the Dabyrie Militia.
The rare wasp Boros is found in the hills directly northwest of the farm.
Daggerfen Village: Daggerfen Village is the village of the Daggerfen Lost One tribe. It is in northwestern Zangarmarsh.
Daggerfen tribe: The Daggerfen tribe is one of three Lost One tribes in Zangarmarsh. They are led by Chieftain Mummaki and are highly specialized in assassination.
Daggerspine: The Daggerspine naga can be found in Eastern Strand (Hillsbrad Foothills), and Drowned Reef (Arathi Highlands), and Daggerspine Landing (Eversong Woods).
Daggerspine Point:
Daggerspine Point is an island on the western shore of Eversong Woods that has been claimed by the Daggerspine naga. It was formerly named Shalandis Isle.
This area, including Daggerspine Landing, is one of the Ritual Sites.
Dai-Lo Farmstead:
The Dai-Lo Farmstead is a large farm in the southeastern area of the Wandering Isle. The local virmen have been stealing the farmstead's crops as of late.
The farmers have been growing carrots, pumpkins, turnips, berries and another unidentified crop. The farmers here take their breaks seriously, and as such they have a Break Gong.
Dalaran:
Dalaran (/ˈdɑːləˌrɔːn/ DAHL-ə-RAWN), also City of Dalaran and Dalaran City, was the capital of the magocratic nation of the same name. Founded as a city-state by magi of the Arathorian Empire after the Troll Wars, it was ruled by the Kirin Tor, an elite cadre of the most powerful wizards in the known world, under the leadership of the Council of Six. Originally located near the southern coast of Lordamere Lake in Lordaeron, Dalaran was magically lifted and moved to Northrend at the time of the Nexus War and the war against the Lich King, until it was teleported to the Broken Isles during the third invasion of the Burning Legion. The Violet Citadel, the city's inner fortress described as a sanctum and haven for mages, served as the focal point for magi and the study of the arcane throughout human history. The city of Dalaran had the greatest concentration of magic in the world, other than the lands of Quel'Thalas, and was defended by some of the most powerful magi in Azeroth. The Kirin Tor Guardians patrolled and protected the surface of Dalaran, while the Underbelly Guard were the guardians of the Underbelly, the sewer system beneath the capital.
By the time of the Third War, Dalaran was home to many of the greatest sorcerers of the time, while most contemporary human and high elven mages of Quel'Thalas bowed to both the sovereignty of the Kirin Tor. However, the Siege of Dalaran by the Scourge forced the Dalaranian people to flee their kingdom, while the Kirin Tor's leadership and its surviving members were scattered after Archimonde destroyed the city. In the aftermath of the Third War, the survivors returned to rebuild the ruins of Dalaran and created a vast, magical dome around the heart of their city. After Dalaran was restored to its former glory, the Kirin Tor magically floated the city so that no ground assault by the undead could ever reach them again. The nation since became one of the foremost forces standing against the threats posed to Azeroth's survival, with Dalaran serving as a neutral ground where the heroes of every kingdom could join together against their mutual foe; a place where all were welcome, so long as they behaved themselves.
After Dalaran was teleported above the Isle of Dorn in Khaz Algar, Xal'atath unleashed the nerubians of Azj-Kahet upon the city. The Harbinger of the Void then siphoned Dalaran's power into the Dark Heart from the Violet Citadel and ultimately used the artifact to destroy the city in an explosion. Its remains can be found across the shores of the Tranquil Strand on the Isle of Dorn.
Dalaran (kingdom):
For the city in-game and everything gameplay related, see Dalaran.

Dalaran, officially the Magocracy of Dalaran, is one of the seven human nations in the Eastern Kingdoms. It is a small, magocratic nation originally founded as a city-state by magi of the Arathorian Empire. It is ruled by the Kirin Tor, an elite cadre of the most powerful wizards in the known world, under the leadership of the Council of Six. Originally located near the southern coast of Lordamere Lake in Lordaeron, its capital, also called Dalaran, was magically lifted and moved to Northrend during the war against the Lich King, until it was teleported to the Broken Isles during the third invasion of the Burning Legion. The city of Dalaran had the greatest concentration of magic in the world, other than the lands of Quel'Thalas, and was defended by some of the most powerful magi in Azeroth.
For over two thousand years, Dalaran maintained a friendship with the elven kingdom of Quel'Thalas. However, this alliance would be strained by their differing loyalties, and was broken as a result of the Purge of Dalaran. During the Second War, the mage-state was a strong supporter of the Alliance of Lordaeron and devoted their knowledge as well as the power of their awesome magiks against the Old Horde. By the time of the Third War, Dalaran was home to many of the greatest sorcerers of the time, while most contemporary human and high elven mages bowed to the sovereignty of the Kirin Tor. However, the Siege of Dalaran by the Scourge forced the Dalaranian people to flee their kingdom, while the Kirin Tor's leadership and its surviving members were scattered after Archimonde destroyed the city.
In the aftermath of the Third War, the survivors returned to rebuild the ruins of Dalaran and created a vast, magical dome around the heart of their city. After Dalaran was restored to its former glory, the Kirin Tor magically floated the city so that no ground assault by the undead could ever reach them again. The nation has since become one of the foremost forces standing against the threats posed to Azeroth's survival, with Dalaran serving as a neutral ground where the heroes of every kingdom could join together against their mutual foe; a place where all were welcome, so long as they behaved themselves.
After Dalaran was teleported above Khaz Algar, Xal'atath unleashed the nerubians of Azj-Kahet upon the magical city. The Harbinger then siphoned Dalaran's power into the Dark Heart, using it to destroy the city in an explosion. Its remains can be found across the shores of the Isle of Dorn, while the survivors were evacuated to the earthen city of Dornogal.
Dalaran Crater: Dalaran Crater is an area in the Hillsbrad Foothills located at the west end, on the shores of Lordamere Lake. It is north of Brazie Farmstead, the former Lordamere Internment Camp, and just east of Silverpine. It is a massive crater where the city of Dalaran once stood, which was destroyed during the Third War. The region was once patrolled by Dalaran wizards and their rock elemental minions, who were leveled in their mid-thirties. The NPCs that remain around the crater are friendly to the Alliance and hostile to the Horde. The camp was led by Archmage Ansirem Runeweaver.
Dalson's Farm: With the Scourge having been expunged from Dalson's Tears, it has been rebuilt as Dalson's Farm in the middle of the Western Plaguelands. Formerly known as Dalson's Orchard, the farm appears to be abandoned but is presently growing a variety of vegetables including pumpkins. The nearby neutral quest hub of the Menders' Stead is nearby, run by the Cenarion Circle.
Dandred's Fold:
Dandred's Fold is a small farm and manor on the westernmost side of the Uplands, in northwestern Alterac Mountains. Since it has a harbor on Lordamere Lake, it is also on the Misty Shore. Prior to the Cataclysm, Lord Aliden Perenolde, the last known leader of the Syndicate, his mistress Elysa, as well as some Syndicate members, and even the Argus Wake orc Nagaz, could be found here.
Horde adventurers were sent here to retrieve the necklace that had once belonged to Taretha Foxton, and end Aliden's life. After killing him, Aliden's mistress Elysa gave them the necklace, which she was wearing, in fear they would also harm her.
Alliance adventurers were sent here by Magistrate Henry Maleb to kill the Argus Wake member Nagaz, which was allied with the Syndicate and could have been a potential threat.
After Cataclysm, no quests take place here anymore and this area no longer serves any purpose.
Dark Horde: The Dark Horde, also referred to as the "true Horde", was a renegade group of orcs, trolls, ogres, and goblins who dwelled in Blackrock Spire, which consisted largely of the remnants of the Blackrock clan and Dragonmaw clan in the aftermath of the Second War. They were marshaled by Nefarian of the black dragonflight and ruled by the self-styled Warchief Rend Blackhand. Unlike the orcs of Thrall's New Horde, they remained steadfast to the ideals of the Orcish Horde and embraced the demonic bloodlust.
Dark Iron clan:
The Dark Iron clan or Dark Iron Nation (also capitalized Dark Iron nation), also known as the kingdom of Thaurissan or simply as the Dark Iron kingdom, is the primary faction of the Dark Iron dwarves. These dark-skinned dwarves were formerly ruled by Sorcerer-thane Thaurissan and vied for control of Ironforge with the Bronzebeard clan and the Wildhammer clan during the War of the Three Hammers. The accidental summoning of Ragnaros eventually ended the dwarven civil war, with the Dark Iron dwarves finding themselves enslaved under the Firelord's command.
Now ruled by Queen-Regent Moira Thaurissan, widow of the late Emperor Dagran Thaurissan and daughter of King Magni Bronzebeard, the Dark Iron clan seek to forge a new future for themselves independent of the tyranny of Ragnaros and his minions, which has long been imposed upon them in their home of Blackrock Mountain. Under Moira's guidance as a member of the Council of Three Hammers, the Dark Iron clan reintegrated Ironforge alongside the Bronzebeard and Wildhammer clans, and by the time of the Fourth War, they officially joined the ranks of the Alliance.
Dark Riders: The Dark Riders (also called the Black Riders) were once a group of traveling merchants who crossed the sorcerer Medivh, who cursed them to an eternity of hunting artifacts for him. They were led by Ariden and are a major cause of danger in Duskwood and Deadwind Pass. They are infamous for being a merciless group of relic hunters. They are the focus of the graphic novel Dark Riders.
Dark Talons: The Dark Talons is a dracthyr weyrn. Where the enemies of the Earth-Warder tread, the Dark Talons shall harrow their skies, crush their will, and topple their leaders, denying the black dragonflight's enemies solace in walls and borders. For every talon in their ranks, they strike down ten of their foes from behind. This weyrn, currently under the authority of the Scalecommander Cindrethresh, trained to be the elite force that shall be feared by all enemies of the black dragonflight. While the leader of the Dark Talons sees the Horde as little more than a collection of undisciplined misfits and outcasts, Scalecommander Cindretresh can't help but admire their honor and desire to be better people, gladly fighting alongside them.
Darkcloud Pinnacle:
East of the Great Lift, atop three small mesas (and several smaller, not inhabited mesas), is Darkcloud Pinnacle, a settlement that the Grimtotem tauren call home. These mesas are connected by rope bridges and have only two access points: a natural slope up a fourth mesa followed by a trip across a bridge, or another bridge from Razorfen Downs in Thousand Needles. Both entrances are well guarded.
It is here that a secret correspondence between Grimtotem leaders and an unknown dark power takes place. The leaders of the Grimtotems here are Arnak Grimtotem and Harb Foulmountain. The entry path from the base begins at .
Aramar Thorne described its location as being located on one of the largest mesa in the area.
Darkfall Ridge: Darkfall Ridge is a large subzone in Krokuun. The area was once inhabited by the peaceful eredar, but had been taken over by the foul creatures of the Legion. Siegemaster Voraan is the leader of the army here. This is where heroes of Azeroth first land during their quest to invade Argus. They eventually win the fight, and claim the area. There are lost artifacts.
Darkfuse Solutions:
Darkfuse Solutions (or Darkfuse Cartel) is a goblin cartel that has operated in numerous theatres across Azeroth and beyond. Originally known as the Blackfuse Company, it was led by the eponymous Siegecrafter Helix Blackfuse and provided advanced weaponry for the True Horde under the direct order of Warchief Garrosh Hellscream, such as the Iron Juggernaut. Their technology, most notably the Iron Star, paved the way for the weaponry used by the Iron Horde; whom they later also aligned with on alternate Draenor.
The company rebranded following the events of the war in Draenor, showing up again as Darkfuse Enforcement in Khaz Algar and Undermine as Jastor Gallywix's private army. After Gallywix's death, they rebranded, yet again, to Darkfuse Solutions -- seeking to be on the winning side for a change by exploring new business opportunities.
Darkheart Thicket: Darkheart Thicket is a dungeon located in Val'sharah at the base of the World Tree. It is the heart of the Nightmare corruption that is spreading throughout the zone. A version exists fully built underneath Shaladrassil, but players enter it at Shala'nir, far from the start of the road in the instance. Entering that version causes the player character to fall asleep and wake up outside the entrance.
Darkshire:
Darkshire (formerly known as Grand Hamlet) is a once-quaint little woodland village located in Duskwood, but it has fallen on literally dark times. The surrounding forests have been corrupted after the death of Medivh, cloaking the land in constant darkness for decades. The walking dead choke the graveyards, and foul creatures known as worgen have overrun many of the outlying farmsteads. Even worse, the political instability orchestrated by Lady Katrana Prestor in Stormwind City caused the abandonment of the town and its surrounding areas by the authorities and the Stormwind Army. This has left the stubborn people of Duskwood little choice but to defend themselves. Besides its town hall, the village also has a blacksmith and an inn.
Prior to the third invasion of the Burning Legion and their adherence to the Veiled Hand cult, Lord Ello Ebonlocke and the Council of Darkshire ruled the town while Althea Ebonlocke led the Night Watch, a local militia that works to keep the roads free and the creeping darkness that plagues the land back for as long as possible. Following the Fourth War, Sarah Ladimore succeeded the late Althea as the commander of the organization. The people of Duskwood are a jumpy and suspicious lot, but they are desperate for any aid they can get against the evil that now surrounds their homes.
Before their treason, the Council of Darkshire was responsible for enforcing justice, such as ordering death sentences for those who sold bodies from Duskwood cemeteries. In the town hall, Clerk Daltry keeps records on the people that live and pass through the town, although some of his records are a little outdated. Tobias Mistmantle had to hide his "true self" from the citizens who react poorly to worgen.
Darkshore:
Darkshore is a long strip of coast on the northwestern part of Kalimdor. It is known for its characteristically shadowed woods and rocky beaches, littered with ancient ruins and mountainside caves. It was the only Alliance zone on the mainland of Kalimdor, with the village of Lor'danel serving as a friendly trading post, before it became contested during the War of the Thorns. Old night elf ruins stand crumbling on the cliffs, infested with naga, satyrs, grell, and haunting ghosts. Even the seas are unsafe, as bloodthirsty frenzies, gigantic threshadons, and hostile murlocs lurk beneath the waves.
During the Fourth War, the Horde managed to conquer most of Darkshore after the Burning of Teldrassil, until the Army of the Black Moon returned to reclaim their lands from the Forsaken and the goblins occupying them. Under Maiev Shadowsong's leadership, and with the assistance of the kingdom of Gilneas, the kaldorei ultimately won the Battle for Darkshore. Following the armistice, they eventually abandoned Bashal'Aran, allowing the settlement to return to ruins, while Tyrande Whisperwind and her Sentinels began largely focusing their wrath against the Horde elsewhere.
Darkspear Isle: Darkspear Isle (or the Echo Isle) is the largest island of the Echo Isles.
Darkspear tribe:
The Darkspear tribe are a tribe (or a clan) of jungle trolls (occasionally called island trolls) part of the Horde. During Warchief Thrall's exodus from Lordaeron in the Third War, the Horde rescued the Darkspears from the mysterious naga sea witch Zar'jira. The Darkspear tribe owed Thrall and the orcs a great debt and allied themselves with the Horde in gratitude.
Led by Sen'jin and then later his son, Vol'jin, the Darkspear tribe became integral to the Horde, with Vol'jin acting as one of the most trusted advisers to the leaders of the faction. This culminated with the troll himself becoming Warchief in the aftermath of the Siege of Orgrimmar, though he would later be slain defending Azeroth during the third invasion of the Burning Legion. With his passing, the tribe went leaderless for a time, before Rokhan was approached to take up the mantle as the new chieftain and representative of the Darkspear tribe in the Horde Council.
The trolls worship many loa in the Darkspear tribe, but the three main loa of the Darkspear tribe are Bwonsamdi, Lukou, and Kevo ya Siti, who are referred to as the soul, heart, and head of the tribe.
Darkspear's Edge: Darkspear's Edge is a Horde camp in Frostfire Ridge. The forces stationed here watch over the Cracking Plains, Colossal's Fall and Iceblister Den for threats.
Darktide:
The Darktide are naga attacking seaside settlements in Kul Tiras, in order to amass prisoners to sacrifice to their dark master.
They also appear on the Siren Isle.
Darktide Roost: Darktide Roost is a large island located south of Shadowmoon Valley, separated from the mainland by the Darktide Strait.
