It is a large breeding ground for rylaks, one which the Iron Horde has been exploiting under Grommash's orders, hoping to achieve aerial supremacy in Shadowmoon Valley. To this end, Blackfuse Company agents have set up shop along the coast of the island, using their Darktide Rylakinator-3000 shredders to subdue the beasts, and then experimenting on them with mind-altering devices. Meanwhile, their Iron Horde allies have docked on the island and are hard at work stockpiling weaponry, constructing siege weapons, and deforesting the island. In the main timeline, it probably became Netherwing Ledge.
Darktooth Pond: Darktooth Pond is an area located in the Azure Span.
Darnassus:
Darnassus (aka Darnassus City), now known as Remains of Darnassus, was the capital city of the night elves of the Alliance, found in western Teldrassil. The High Priestess, Tyrande Whisperwind, resided in the Temple of the Moon, surrounded by other sisters of Elune and her mate, the Archdruid Malfurion Stormrage.
Darnassus was the greatest city of the night elves, housing the leaders of both the druids and the faithful of Elune. It was carefully guarded by Sentinels, ancient protectors, and ancients of war. It was destroyed during the Burning of Teldrassil.
Darnassus (faction): Darnassus is the faction associated with the playable night elves of the Alliance. Their capital was once Darnassus at the top of Teldrassil. It has since been replaced by Bel'ameth on the Dragon Isles.
Darnassus (nation): Darnassus is the nation of the night elves and a member state of the Grand Alliance. Named after their former capital city, Darnassus, it is the cultural descendant of the ancient Kaldorei Empire. Led by High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind throughout the Long Vigil, the nation arose after the Battle of Mount Hyjal and the creation of Teldrassil by Archdruid Fandral Staghelm. Following the Burning of Teldrassil and the blooming of Amirdrassil, the night elves built their new capital of Bel'ameth on the Dragon Isles, with High General Shandris Feathermoon succeeding as the leader of their people.
Darrowshire:
Darrowshire is a village located in the southern part of what is now the Eastern Plaguelands. During the Third War, Darrowshire came under attack by a Scourge force led by the ghoul lord Horgus the Ravager and the death knight Marduk Blackpool. Though the defenders of Darrowshire made headway at first, the defenders were eventually slaughtered.
Today, Darrowshire is silent, and remains in ruins, a place where only ghosts and memories remain. Those defenders who fell now litter the Plaguelands as ghouls in the service of the Scourge, their spirits trapped in their rotting corpses. Very rarely in Darrowshire an event can be seen where the Battle of Darrowshire is re-enacted by ghosts and undead.
Darsok's Outpost: Darsok's Outpost is an orc burrow located near the Dry Hills in the Northern Barrens.
Dawn: Dawn was the first earthen to awaken from the Hall of Awakening after it was restored by Magni Bronzebeard. She now serves as a guide for newly awakened earthen, alongside Foreman Uzjax, helping them navigate the process of awakening and preparing them for the outside world.
Dawn's Blossom:
Dawn's Blossom is a small town and the heart of pandaren life in the Jade Forest. It is an important stop for travelers and has not taken a side in the Alliance / Horde conflict. Though largely peaceful, the local breweries of Wanderbrew and Goldendraft hold a grudge against each other, leading to tensions between the two families. There is a third major family, the Windfur, of which the mayor Master Windfur is a member.
The inn, run by Peiji Goldendraft, is the Drunken Hozen. Business with nearby settlements is helped along by the social Toya.
Dawn's Reach: Dawn's Reach is a tiny Argent Crusade camp in the southeastern Dragonblight, just south of the Carrion Fields and north of the Forgotten Shore. Orik Trueheart, Tilda Darathan, and a small group of Argent Crusade Riflemen were sent here to quell the Scourge attempting to escape the Carrion Fields. The camp consists only of a tent, a campfire, a wagon, and three graves, along with an unusual combined Argent Crusade-Argent Dawn banner.
Dawnchaser tribe: The Dawnchaser tribe is a tribe of Horde tauren introduced in World of Warcraft: Mists of Pandaria. They have two outposts in the Krasarang Wilds, one is Thunder Cleft and the other is Dawnchaser Retreat. Members of the tribe, particularly their Chief, Sunwalker Dezco, are occasionally encountered elsewhere.
Dawnrise Expedition: Dawnrise Expedition is a small blood elf camp established by the Reliquary in the western area of the Valley of the Watchers in southern Tanaris. It has an Alliance equivalent, Gunstan's Dig.
Dawnseeker Promontory:
The Dawnseeker Promontory is the Sunreaver Onslaught toehold on a small island off the northwestern coast of the Isle of Thunder. After claiming Zeb'tula (and phasing in the Dawnseeker Promontory), adventurers of the Horde wishing to help the Sunreaver Onslaught claim the rest of the isle can teleport here from the Horde camp at  southeast of the Shado-Pan Garrison in Townlong Steppes. Surrounded by the Bay of Echoes, the Wildvine Marsh and Diremoor are to the east, and the Court of Bones is to the south. Following its establishment, completion of daily quests will contribute to the promontory's continued construction.
The promontory is presumably named for the Thalassian hero, Thalorien Dawnseeker.
Dawnstar Spire:
Dawnstar Spire is the former residence of Dar'Khan Drathir before he turned to the Scourge. He spent his childhood here. He also used the Spire to conduct Void research. It is located on the eastern shore of Lake Elrendar in the northeastern Ghostlands, south of Zeb'Sora and northeast of the Farstrider Enclave, and is now guarded by his Arcane Reavers.
In the year 25, Dar'Khan used the place to lure the Blood Knights into a trap. A plan that ultimately failed when Lor'themar Theron arrived and killed him.
Years later, Magister Umbric found Dar'Khan's research and left notes at the top of the Spire. Alleria Windrunner later arrived to the top of the Spire and opened a portal to Telogrus Rift.
Dawnstar Village: Dawnstar Village is a blood elven village located on the Isle of Quel'Danas.
Dazar'alor: Dazar'alor refers to the urban center of Zuldazar. It is named after the royal palace, the pyramid of Dazar'alor. Two of the palace's floors, centered around the Great Seal in the palace's interior chamber, serves as the Horde's embassy on Zandalar and includes some portals to each major city, profession trainers, bank and guild banks, transmogrifier and a mission table. The current ruler of the city is Queen Talanji.
Dead Acre:
The Dead Acre was once one of many farms in southeast Westfall, close to the bridge leading into Duskwood. However, when the Defias Brotherhood took control of Westfall, they burned the farm that had once stood there, as well as the fields. Now, only the smoking ruins remain with mechanical Harvest Watchers roaming the smoldering fields.

 This section concerns content related to Legion.
During the Burning Legion's invasion, the area fell under the Burning Legion's control. Its residents were enslaved by nathrezim and were later killed by the defenders.
Deadgrin:
Deadgrin was a village and home to the Laughing Skull clan in southwestern Gorgrond. The skull of one of the earth giants looms above it. The goren, led by Skothwa and Tog the Earthrender, overtook the village, killing many villagers, and ultimately causing the orcs to abandon their home. The surviving villagers moved to the northeast where Broken Horn Village was built.

 This section concerns content related to Battle for Azeroth.
When the Horde adventurer and Eitrigg returned to Draenor, decades in the future, the area could be visited. While the layout of the village was different, and the giant skull was no longer present, the village itself was roughly in the same location. Here, Grand Anchorite Almonen gave a sermon to several Mag'har, who, following the draenei's lecture, willingly converted to the Lightbound. Outside of these five inhabitants, the village was otherwise abandoned. Unlike Beastwatch, Deadgrin has not been revamped into the architecture of the Iron Horde.
Deadmines: The Deadmines are expansive, winding tunnels dug out under Westfall and part of northwestern Stranglethorn Vale. It is the lowest-level Alliance instance and is populated by members of the Defias Brotherhood. Its entrance can be accessed in the town of Moonbrook in southwestern Westfall, while its exit is located in the western part of the Dagger Hills near the ocean.
Deadwash:
Deadwash is the name of a town between the Drowned Lands and the Briny Flats in western Stormsong Valley. The surrounding area is a project where a bay was drained of water to create more farmland in Stormsong Valley, with the seawall at Fort Daelin holding back the ocean, but the town is more concerned with revealed treasure from a formerly sunken Second War ship than anything else. As such, the greedy Irontide Raiders pirates are attacking it.
There are about two hundred and fourteen treasure hunters and workers here.
Deadwind ogres: The Deadwind are a group of ogres found in Deadwind Pass. The ogres live in an area called the Vice. They can be seen fighting against Deadwind Widows here for unknown reasons.
Deadwood Village: Deadwood Village is a furbolg village of the Deadwood tribe in southern Felwood. Like most of their kin, the Deadwood furbolgs have been corrupted and are hostile. After the Cataclysm, Deadwood Village was slightly expanded and more fortified. A wooden fence comprised of thick timbers encloses much of the village and there are more sturdy structures inside.
Death Cultist Base Camp:
The Death Cultist Base Camp is a Scourge-controlled subzone of the Eastern Plaguelands. It's located west of Tyr's Hand and has its own plague cauldron, which Betina Bigglezink wanted disturbed with her mixture.
Prior to the Cataclysm, it was the site of the Scarlet Base Camp.
Death Rising:
Death Rising was a world event in patch 9.0.1 available from 10 November until the launch of Shadowlands on 23/24 November 2020 that heralded the launch of World of Warcraft: Shadowlands. It was similar in scope to the Scourge Invasion events.
The event dealt with the immediate repercussions of Sylvanas Windrunner shattering the Helm of Domination, freeing the Scourge from Bolvar Fordragon's command and handing its control to the Jailer's forces, and kidnapping leaders of the Alliance and Horde. Many cities in Azeroth were attacked by the rampaging undead, including Lakeshire, which lore-wise lost many of its citizens.
Death knight:
Death knights are melee fighters that wield dark magic and runeforged weapons. Death knights engage their foes up close, supplementing swings of their weapons with dark magic that renders enemies vulnerable or damages them with unholy power. They drag foes into one-on-one conflicts, compelling them to focus their attacks away from weaker companions. To prevent their enemies from fleeing their grasp, death knights must remain mindful of the power they call forth from runes and pace their attacks appropriately. To protect themselves and their fellows from death in battle, death knights gird themselves in heavy armor and parry attacks with their blades. They have a personal connection with their blades, and can forge runes onto them in order to increase their power. These runeblades are empowered with dark magic, and they can expend the power of their runes for vicious attacks.
Primary death knight attributes are strength and stamina. Most important secondary attributes are usually Haste and Critical Strike, though certain specializations and rotations may favor Mastery. Their talents can bolster their defensive abilities by focusing on their ability to heal themselves, increase their damage and spell attacks, or summon forth minions and diseases by making use of their runes:

Blood death knights are dark guardians who manipulate and corrupt life energy to sustain themself in the face of an enemy onslaught.
Frost death knights are harbingers of doom, channeling runic power and delivering vicious weapon strikes.
Unholy death knights are masters of death and decay, spreading infection and controlling undead minions to do their bidding.
Death knights were first introduced in Warcraft II, then as a hero unit in Warcraft III. The death knight was the first hero class of World of Warcraft, introduced in the Wrath of the Lich King expansion. Each death knight of the game's original 8 races begins at level 8 and has a unique starting experience in Plaguelands: The Scarlet Enclave. However, the more recent death knights risen by Bolvar Fordragon in the Shadowlands expansion, instead, start at level 10 and are sent directly to their faction's capital city.
Death's Advance: Death's Advance is a reputation faction in Korthia, representing the combined might of the four covenants and their assault on the Maw.
Death's Advance Supplies: Death's Advance Supplies is the paragon reward from the  [60] Supplies from Death's Advance quest at Keeper's Respite in Korthia.
Death's Head tribe:
The Death's Head tribe (also known simply as Death's Head) is a group and cult of undead quilboars found in Razorfen Downs in Kalimdor. They are controlled by the Scourge, led by the lich Amnennar the Coldbringer, and were the first major Scourge outpost on Kalimdor. They are allied with the Razorfen tribe.
Preachers of Agamaggan and the Death's Head are known as speakers and prophets. Some notable elite members include Death Speaker Jargba, Aggem Thorncurse. The Crone Charlga Razorflank was said to be leading it before her death, though Amnennar was the official leader. According to Shagtusk, Chugara Razorflank surrendered Razorfen Downs to the Death's Head.
After Amnennar's initial defeat, Death Speaker Blackthorn took control of the cult, with plans to raise Amnennar once again.
The Death's Head also house a giant boar, Agathelos the Raging, within Razorfen Kraul. Already a powerful creature, Agathelos had been fed Kraul bat guano, which produces a maddening effect, resulting in increased stamina and strength. The Death's Head planned to utilize Agathelos as a powerful weapon to crush all who oppose them.
Death's Stand: Death's Stand is an encampment of the Valiance Expedition located near the Wailing Ziggurat in Borean Tundra. It was here that Thassarian, the first of the Alliance death knights, led "Unit S" in a suicide mission to claim the ziggurat, possibly as a base for an attack on Naxxanar and the Temple City of En'kilah. Dusk, Thassarian's demon deathcharger, can be found here as well.
Death's Watch Waystation:
Death's Watch Waystation was a small camp just southeast of Brill in the Tirisfal Glades. It was a Deathguard waystation.
During the events of the Battle for Lordaeron, the waystation had been already destroyed and there was no trace of it.
When the Forsaken reclaimed Brill, they used the area of the Waystation as a staging ground for the deployment of the Plague Eater against the remaining blight in Tirisfal.
Deathforge Tower: Deathforge Tower is a small spire that overlooks the Deathforge in central Shadowmoon Valley. This tower holds two Wildhammer dwarves who give out quests for Alliance players. Slag Watch, a similar structure for Horde, stands just north of here.
Deathknell:
Deathknell is a small Forsaken village nestled in a well-guarded valley just north of Silverpine Forest in Tirisfal Glades which serves as the starting area for the Forsaken. One of the greatest struggles for the citizens of Deathknell is obtaining the natural resources they need to survive, particularly gold. The gold mine to the northwest has been overrun by spiders, and the people of Deathknell frequently attempt to clear it out, so that they may begin mining its precious metals. In the meantime, they do what they must to survive in the face of the Scourge and the Scarlet Crusade.
Lore-wise, Deathknell is unique among Forsaken sites due to its name. While other communities inhabited by the rebel undead of the Banshee Queen retained their names from their days as centers of human civilization, Deathknell was obviously renamed to its current appellation for reasons unknown. The valley itself is guarded by a number of Deathguard Elites.
Deatholme:
Deatholme was a Scourge citadel located in southwestern Ghostlands, marking the beginning of the Dead Scar. It served as the major Scourge outpost in Quel'Thalas, with several ziggurats, slaughterhouses, and the Tower of the Damned at its center. Dar'Khan Drathir resided here along with his undead lieutenants: Mirdoran the Fallen, Borgoth the Bloodletter, Jurion the Deceiver, and Masophet the Black.
By the time of the War of Light and Shadow, Deatholme had been reduced to ruins.
Deatholme cult: The Deatholme cult was an organization of mortal necromancers led by Dar'Khan Drathir, the commander of the Scourge forces in Quel'Thalas.
Deathspeaker's Watch:
Deathspeaker's Watch is a new camp infested with the Cult of the Damned, on a plateau northwest of the Argent Tournament Grounds in Icecrown.
Players are directed to the watch in the quest chain starting with  [25-30] The Black Knight's Curse.
Deeprun Tram: The Deeprun Tram (or simply the Tram) is a long, fully enclosed, underground (and partially underwater) set of double tracks upon which rolls two sets of three wagons, all credited to the gnomes' technical engineering. The service is fast and smooth, and is provided free of charge to travelers between the Alliance-aligned cities of Ironforge and Stormwind City. To keep the tram running smoothly and safely, there are gnomes that work on it daily. As such, any problems with it can be quickly addressed. The underwater section of the tram is, in fact, a subterranean lake.
Defias Brotherhood:
The Defias Brotherhood (or the Defias Gang, Defias Thieves, or simply The Brotherhood) is an order of bandits founded by Edwin VanCleef, and made up of former stonemasons, assassins, thieves, brigands and pirates that once sought to overthrow the Kingdom of Stormwind, defying the corrupt nobility by wearing red bandanas in order to symbolize the blood shed by the oppressed.
Once based in the Deadmines of Westfall, an area deeply impoverished and not easily protected by the Stormwind Army, they began to prepare their revenge with the construction of a massive Juggernaught to destroy Stormwind, while acting and scheming in the shadows. However, they were defeated by adventurers sent by Gryan Stoutmantle before they could accomplish their goals.
Years after Edwin's death, at the time of the Cataclysm, Vanessa VanCleef succeeded him as the Kingpin of the Brotherhood and intended to continue her father's plan until her defeat by adventurers and the Westfall Brigade. She faked her death and reappeared to join the Uncrowned during the third invasion of the Burning Legion, pledging the allegiance of the Brotherhood to the rogue order.
In the wake of the Legion's defeat, Vanessa struggled to keep the organization focused on aiding the people of Westfall rather than simple thieving and banditry, especially of innocents. She eventually realized that all of the principled Defias had either died or retired after receiving the royal pardon and reparations from King Anduin Wrynn, leaving only the thugs and bullies. After they were manipulated into attacking Northshire Abbey by a disgraced noble, Vanessa helped Mathias Shaw defeat her former compatriots before determining to find her own legacy. During the battle, the bandit Duncon Ratsbon announced that the Defias were now answering to him and fled before being defeated, stating that the organization could not lose its new leader. Some eventually left to join the ranks of the Red Dawn in the Arathi Highlands.
Defilers:
The Forsaken Defilers seek to foil the League of Arathor in Arathi Basin and claim it for the Horde. They not only try to secure the Arathi Basin food and supplies for the Forsaken forces, but to weaken the Alliance forces there as well. They seem to show no true loyalty to the Horde forces in Hammerfall, who are more interested in eliminating the Ogre and Witherbark tribes, but to the Forsaken, who wish to destroy the remaining humans in Lordaeron.
Some of the Defilers are former Stromgarde citizens.
Deliverance Point:
Deliverance Point is the main base of the Armies of Legionfall in the Broken Shore. It consists of an upper tier with the Mage Tower and Command Center, a middle tier with large tents and representatives from most class orders and a bottom tier where the Nether Disruptor and members of the Cenarion Circle are located. There are two entrances to the base, a southern path leading to the shore where the Nameless Mystic can be found, and a northern path that leads down the Infernal Causeway to the center of the island. The base can also be entered through Grapple Points added by the Valarjar and via a flight path operated by Illidari Calia.
In year 42 ADP, Thalyssra reported that the old base of Deliverance Point still remained and its buildings were repurposed.
Den (Harandar): The Den is an area located in Harandar.
Den of Flame: The Den of Flame is an area in Dustwallow Marsh, just west of the Stonemaul Ruins that has been completely overrun by dragonkin of the black dragonflight, presumably under the orders of the great black dragon Onyxia, who resides nearby. The structure was built by the Stonemaul ogres to be their ogre mound, as the architecture in the area corroborates, and as such it still contains the  [Stonemaul Banner] required by  [15-30] Banner of the Stonemaul.
Den of Haal'esh:
The Den of Haal'esh is a deep chasm located in southwestern Hellfire Peninsula, beyond Dustquill Ravine. It is heavily populated by aggressive arakkoa and their kaliri.
By the time of the Cataclysm on Azeroth, it appears that the den was transformed into a Burning Legion citadel.
Den of Nalorakk:
The Den of Nalorakk is a dungeon in Midnight. It will have adventurers prove themselves to earn Nalorakk's favor.
The dungeon is unlocked by reaching level 88 or completing the quest  [83-88] Den of Nalorakk: A Taste of Vengeance in chapter 3 of the Zul'Aman storyline.
Desmotaeron: Desmotaeron  is the eastern portion of the Beastwarrens island in the Maw. The area was taken over by the forces of Helya and Vyraz in patch 9.1. The interior of the area has the appellation Helgarde Keep, home to three rare-elite enemies and the Instance portal to the Sanctum of Domination raid.
Desolate Council: The Desolate Council is the governing body of the Forsaken.
Desolation Hold:
Desolation Hold is a Horde fortress in Southern Barrens located on the western side of the Battlescar, with the Alliance outpost Fort Triumph on the eastern side. Warlord Gar'dul had Desolation Hold constructed over a Silithid colony, known as the Field of Giants, over Crawgol's objections.
Warlord Gar'dul, who was in charge of the Horde in the region, failed to live up to the expectations of Warchief Garrosh, because of this he has sent Warlord Bloodhilt to investigate the situation and solve the problem. Warlord Bloodhilt, having solved the issue, took command of the fortress until he joined the war effort in Pandaria and relocated to Domination Point, where he met his end.
By the time of the Fourth War, command of Desolation Hold belonged to Warlord Crawgol. The hold came under attack by Alliance forces that were sent to attack in order to reestablish Fort Triumph.
Destiny Point: Destiny Point is a small camp that serves as a base for the Army of the Light assault on Nath'raxas Hold.
Devoted: The Devoted are a faction of sethrak led by Vorrik that are still loyal to the deceased serpent loa Sethraliss, unlike Emperor Korthek and his Faithless.
Dhar Kazhad: Dhar Kazhad  is found in northern Isle of Dorn. With War Mode enabled, the area is a Free For All and  [80WQ] Along for the Ride is sometimes available.
Dire Maul:
Dire Maul is a three-wing instance found in north-central Feralas. It was once a proud Highborne city called Eldre'Thalas (or Eldre'thalas), but now lies in ruins, overrun by ogres, satyrs, and undead. Only a tiny remnant of the original Highborne population remains in the form of a murderous sect called the Shen'dralar. It is comprised of three instances: the Warpwood Quarter, the Capital Gardens, and the Gordok Commons.
The sub-region of Dire Maul plays host to two night elf archaeology dig sites: the Broken Commons Digsite and the Dire Maul Digsite.
The ruins stand strong because of an ancient crafting technique that bound arcane energy within the stone.
Direhorn Post:
Direhorn Post is a camp full of hostile Grimtotem tauren, north of Tabetha's Farm in the Quagmire of Dustwallow Marsh.
Apothecary Cylla drops a  [Sealed Letter] which starts  [38] The Apothecary's Letter or  [38] Signs of Treachery?.
Dolanaar:
Dolanaar was a night elven village located in the central-eastern part of Teldrassil. Found just southwest of Shadowglen, its central location made it involved in much of Teldrassil's regional affairs and the first major town usually encountered by aspiring night elf adventurers after leaving Shadowglen. Class trainers for all night elven classes, as well as profession training, were also available here.
Koroleth and Kelestra used to live in the village.

 This section concerns content related to the Warcraft novels, novellas, or short stories.
During the Burning of Teldrassil, the conflagration spread to Dolanaar.
Dominance Offensive:
The Dominance Offensive is the major Horde force for the Pandaria campaign of the Alliance-Horde war. Its Alliance counterpart is Operation: Shieldwall.
This is likely the invasion fleet mentioned in  [10-35] The Art of War.
Domination Point:
Domination Point is the western island located in the Southern Isles of Krasarang Wilds where Domination Keep, a Horde fortress, was built. The fortress contains a barracks, burrows and cannon towers.

 This section concerns content related to the Warcraft novels, novellas, or short stories.
Following the awakening of the Dragon Isles, Chen Stormstout, Li Li Stormstout, and Catelyn the Blade visited Domination Point, which was then considered a friendly place "for a fortress". The gates were guarded, but open, and the guards were happy to gossip with them. When Chen mentioned that they were looking for a good place to eat, the trio was advised to visit their goblin allies at Bilgewater Beach.
Dooker Dome:
The Dooker Dome is home to the Ookin tribe of hozen, near the western end of the Burlap Trail in central Kun-Lai Summit. Across the trail to the south is the Broketooth Outpost, and the Burlap Waystation is between the two hozen camps, just to the east.
The Dooker Dome camp gets it's name from the giant dome holding Chomp Chomp at the camp's northern end.
Doom's Vigil:
Doom's Vigil is a Twilight's Hammer camp within the Darkwhisper Gorge of Mount Hyjal. It is here failed recruits are sent to be disposed of; should they dispose of the disposer, they will have earned their second chance.
It is also here that the new initiates arrive after completing their trials and tasks waiting to be inspired by the head of the class.
Dor'Danil Barrow Den: The Dor'Danil Barrow Den is located in Ashenvale, south of Splintertree Post, and southwest of Felfire Hill. Although it has traditionally been the site of rest for night elven druids, the incursion of the Horde put the barrow den behind enemy lines. Although the orcs had little interest in a bunch of sleeping elves, the Forsaken who later joined the faction were not so disinterested. Experimenting with severing the sleeping druids from their spirits, they drove the night elves insane. The barrow den is now filled with skulking Forsaken assassins, the enraged souls of the severed druids, and three particularly powerful spirits — those of Uthil Mooncall, Mavoris Cloudsbreak, and Taneel Darkwood.
Dornogal:
Dornogal  (/ˈdɔːrnəɡɔːl/ DORN-ə-gawl) is the capital city of the earthen dwarves of Khaz Algar and serves as the player capital of The War Within. It is located in the center of the Isle of Dorn.
The city was named in honor of the titanic watchers Dornic and Galan. It was originally built to be the fortress for the Coreway. After Adelgonn and the Stonebound abandoned the Edicts, the city fell into disrepair. Dornogal has been isolated within Khaz Algar for a long while, which resulted in the city's earthen developing their own manners and customs. The city is surprisingly verdant and was apparently carved from the land.
In the year 42 ADP, Xal'atath unleashed the nerubians of Azj-Kahet upon Dalaran and destroyed the magical city. The resulting crash lured Stormward Baelgrim and his Stormriders away from Dornogal, allowing the nerubians to damage the Coreway. The survivors of Dalaran were welcomed into the city by Councilward Merrix for their part in defending the earthen.
To help repair the Coreway, Merrix ordered Baelgrim to enlist the aid of Adelgonn and the Unbound. After a tense reunion, Baelgrim and Adelgonn reconciled after he apologized for failing to protect the Unbound. They were officially allowed to return to the city and began repairs to the Coreway.
After the Horde and Alliance armies sailed to the Isle of Dorn to aid in the war against Xal'atath, they established embassies within Dornogal.
Dornogal (nation): Dornogal is a nation of earthen located on the continent of Khaz Algar. Under the leadership of the Council of Dornogal, the Algari earthen society has been isolated for thousands of years, gradually developing their own behaviors, language, and demeanor with many similarities to other former earthen groups. Their capital is the fortress city of Dornogal, located at the heart of the Isle of Dorn.
Draenei:
The draenei (/ˈdɹænɑɪ/ DRAN-eye) (meaning Exiled Ones in their own tongue) are a faction of uncorrupted eredar who fled their homeworld of Argus to escape the corruption of the demonic Burning Legion. Led by the Prophet Velen and guided by the divine naaru, they traveled throughout the Great Dark Beyond for millennia, settling on numerous worlds they had to flee each time the demons found them. They eventually landed on a planet they would come to call Draenor, or "Exiles' Refuge", where they lived for centuries in relative peace with the native orcs. When agents of the Legion found them, however, the orcs were corrupted by the blood-curse of Mannoroth and formed the original Orcish Horde, which slaughtered the draenei en masse and driven into hiding to escape the wrath of Kil'jaeden.
Decades later, the survivors escaped the ravaged world now known as the Outland aboard the Exodar, a vessel of the naaru fortress Tempest Keep, but crashed upon the world of Azeroth; more specifically, on the Azuremyst Isles off the western coast of Kalimdor. Inspired by tales of the heroic Alliance that stood against the might of the Legion during the Third War, the draenei pledged their allegiance and led the charge during the invasion of Outland. Following the defeat of Kil'jaeden at the Sunwell Plateau, some draenei were sent back to revitalize their former civilization on Outland. However, the majority vowed to stay and uphold their sacred commitment to the Alliance, as Velen predicted a great war between the Darkness and the Light was fast approaching, and that Azeroth would be its principal battleground.
In the wake of the Legion's defeat on Argus, marking the end of the Burning Crusade and its third invasion of Azeroth, the draenei now seek a new destiny in the blessed Light. Years later, Velen organized the first Tishamaat since their escape from Argus, and declared his intention for the draenei to build a new city for themselves on Azeroth so that they would no longer be scattered exiles.
The draenei, as they are known today, were first introduced with The Burning Crusade, though corrupted draenei — later identified as Lost Ones and Broken — were seen as early as Warcraft III: The Frozen Throne. The draenei of alternate Draenor also play a significant role in the Warlords of Draenor expansion.
Dragon's Mouth:
Dragon's Mouth is an Alliance camp in the southwestern Badlands. It is situated northeast of Camp Cagg and southeast of New Kargath, at the southwest end of the Scar of the Worldbreaker. It has flight paths connecting to Fuselight, Dustwind Dig, and Morgan's Vigil, a functioning mailbox, repair and trade goods vendor, and a tiny inn consisting of a tent. Dragon's Mouth was established during the Cataclysm to give the Alliance their first real foothold in the Badlands, which had previously traditionally been Horde territory.
During the Cataclysm, Terrance Storm sent men keep the black dragonflight forces at nearby New Kargath at bay, which left the camp vulnerable to a potential attack from the Dustbelcher ogres at nearby Camp Cagg. Terrance sent Alliance adventurers to preemptively thin the ogres' ranks. The black dragons' ravaging of the camp's would-be hunting grounds left Dragon's Mouth short on supplies, so Victoria Dolen sent adventurers to obtain food and crafting supplies from the ogres.
Dragonbane Keep:
Dragonbane Keep is a keep located just directly south of the Obsidian Citadel. The area was originally a djaradin holding; though appears to have been abandoned when the djaradin entered their hibernation with the departure of the dragons. In the time of their disappearance, the keep became the home of the Obsidian Outcasts, a group of black dragonkin, until the return of the Qalashi tribe djaradin; who forcibly ejected the Outcasts from the keep. The keep is a rotating major community objective, with the Obsidian Outcasts launching a massive siege of the area to re-establish their holding over the area and eject the Djaradin from their home. Players can lend their aid to this objective every few hours, allowing them to re-establish the keep as a safe area and receive leveled-loot from the chest at the end of the siege.
While the Keep is under Djaradin control, it can be very dangerous to traverse the area; as the Qalashi will man the wingshredders upon the walls, placing a rapidly stacking debuff on any player that flies over it. If the debuff reaches 10, the player will be dismounted; sometimes to fatal results. While the keep is under Outcasts control, these wingshredders are disabled and it is safe to fly over the area. While the area is reclaimed, the members of the Outcasts will take up various positions across the keep until the Djaradin take it over again. Narsysix and a Blacktalon Schemer (as well as their goat) can also be found here while the keep is reclaimed, thanking the player for helping the Outcasts.
Dragonmaw Base Camp:
The Dragonmaw Base Camp is a fortified area of southwestern Netherwing Ledge in southeastern Shadowmoon Valley. It is densely populated with Dragonmaw fel orcs, and is where questers are sent to infiltrate the Illidari.
NPCs in this area are only friendly to players who have completed  [25-30] Blood Oath of the Netherwing. Even so, avoid the Dragonmaw Ascendants and Dragonmaw Skybreakers, as they are the only ones who can see through players' fel orc disguises.
Dragonmaw Fortress:
Dragonmaw Fortress is a large fortress located in the southeastern area of Shadowmoon Valley. 
When the Dark Portal was reopened, the fortress was attacked by Ragnok Bloodreaver in order to get an army. While Zuluhed and some orcs escaped, most of the Dragonmaws were forced to join the death knight.
It is full of Dragonmaw fel orcs who have enslaved the nether drakes from the nearby Netherwing Fields as mounts. Zuluhed the Whacked resides here.
Dragonmaw Port:
Dragonmaw Port is the naval base of the Dragonmaw clan in the Twilight Highlands. While entering the Highlands, a fleet of Horde zeppelins is attacked by Twilight Dragons, causing them to crash off the coast of Dragonmaw Port. Subsequent events see the orcs of the Dragonmaw clan freeing themselves from their Fel Orc masters and Zaela becoming the leader of the clan and the port itself. After getting supplies to bolster the defenses of the port and dealing with the traitor Sauranok the Mystic, due to phasing, Dragonmaw Port will resemble the Horde bases in Northrend, including its barracks. The Port will also gain a Zeppelin Tower.
Several blade throwers and demolishers are protecting the port.
Dragonmaw clan:
The Dragonmaw clan (or Nelghor-shomash, "Cry of the Beasts" in Orcish) is an orcish clan dating back to ancient Draenor. Under the command of the shaman Zuluhed the Whacked, the Dragonmaw swore fealty to Warchief Blackhand and accompanied the Old Horde to Azeroth during the First War. After Blackhand's death, the Dragonmaw maintained their fealty to the late Warchief by pledging themselves to Blackhand's two sons and their Black Tooth Grin clan. The Dragonmaw were later empowered by the Aspect Deathwing to enslave the red dragonflight, including the Dragonqueen Alexstrasza herself, forcing the noble dragons to fight for the Horde throughout the Second War. During this time, the clan was based out of the ancient stronghold of Grim Batol, which housed the prison of Alexstrasza.
The Dragonmaw retained their dominance over the red flight even after the Horde's defeat and the destruction of the Dark Portal but lost control over their winged captives during the Battle of Grim Batol. The cursed city was destroyed by the vengeful dragons, forcing the clan to flee into the Wetlands and the Twilight Highlands, where they remained relatively dormant for years and clashed with the Wildhammer dwarves. Part of the clan, including their chieftain Zuluhed, remained on Outland and instead pledged their service to Illidan Stormrage, enslaving the nether dragons of Shadowmoon Valley for the Illidari. The Azerothian Dragonmaw were eventually recruited into the New Horde by Garrosh Hellscream in the wake of the Cataclysm.
Under the leadership of Warlord Zaela, the Dragonmaws remained fiercely loyal to Garrosh during the Siege of Orgrimmar, later allying with the Ironmarch forces in Blackrock Spire during the Iron Horde Incursion. On both occasions, they had traded out the black dragons they used for proto-dragons. It is noted that they also breed these dragons in the Twilight Highlands, forming bonds with them without having to break them.
Gorfax Angerfang became chieftain of the clan after the downfall of Zaela. He and his Dragonmaw have had a tumultuous relationship with the Horde in the aftermath of the True Horde; though this was ultimately resolved as their clan was welcomed to Azeroth's first Kosh'harg festival. Gorfax is resolute in the idea of redeeming the Dragonmaw's tainted legacy, or to have the clan die trying.
Dragonscale Basecamp:
Dragonscale Basecamp  is the headquarters of the Dragonscale Expedition.
Located at the base of a waterfall near the border of the Ohn'ahran Plains, the area is bordered by the Obsidian Bulwark to the north, the Flashfrost Assault to the east, the Rubyscale Outpost to the south, and the Wild Preserve to the west.
Dragonscale Camp:
Dragonscale Camp  is, as suggested by the name, a small Dragonscale Expedition camp in southeastern Zaralek Cavern.
Sharpbeak, the flight master, has connections to Loamm and Obsidian Rest.
The Crystal Circuit dragonriding race is not far to the northwest at .
Also present are the Camp Anvil for repairs, Chef Butterfingers, Earthmender Narvra from the Earthen Ring, and Tellywin Sharpfizzle.
Dragonscale Expedition: The Dragonscale Expedition is the name of the joint Alliance and Horde expedition to the Dragon Isles. Explicitly not a military expedition, it set up outposts throughout the Isles as it continued to explore them. Despite their shared mission, rivalries between the Explorers' League and Reliquary endured.
Dragonshrine:
The Dragonshrines are places dotting the wasteland of the Dragonblight where dragons come to when their life is at an end. There is one for each dragonflight, including the Ruby Dragonshrine, Azure Dragonshrine, Emerald Dragonshrine, Bronze Dragonshrine, and Obsidian Dragonshrine.
During the war against the Lich King in 27 ADP, in addition to the problems facing the individual dragonshrines, the dragons had to contend with Arthas Menethil and the Scourge, who took the bones of dead dragons and used them to create frost wyrms.
Following the war against the Jailer in 36 ADP, the Bronzebeard brothers reported that as the dragons have dispersed now on their own business; all the dragonshrines stand empty.
Dragonskull Island:
Dragonskull Island  is a fairly large island off the northeastern shore of the Forbidden Reach. So named by the shape of the rock formation on the southeastern side of the island, Dragonskull is hollowed out by a large cave. The island is bordered by the Stormsunder Mountain and Stormsunder Crater to the south, the Hornswog Grounds to the southeast, Froststone Peak to the west, and Warder's Solace to the northwest.
While the island is initially inhabited by Earthshatter Elementals and Fracturing Rumblers, during the return, they've been replaced by Earth Elementals and Primal Boulders.
Herbalists may find some  [Dormant Lifebloom Seeds] from any herb node in the Forbidden Reach. Take them to the Awakened Soil at  above the cave. Plant the seeds to spawn the rare Kangalo! Defeat it for some herbs. The summoner is granted bonus loot: 5x  [Artisan's Mettle], and an  [Undigested Hochenblume Petal].
A Dragon Glyph is hidden behind the peak near some trees.
Drak'Sotra: Drak'Sotra is an area east of Drak'Agal and west of Kolramas in Zul'Drak. This area was once held by the Argent Crusade but was lost soon after the Scourge arrived. What remaining troll residents of this land can now be found at the Drak'Sotra Fields.
Drak'Tharon Keep:
Drak'Tharon Keep is an old ice troll fortress located between the northwestern border of the Grizzly Hills, and the southwestern border of Zul'Drak. It contains one scaled instance for level 62 - 80 players. On heroic, it awards approximately 2000 reputation.
Drak'Tharon Keep is located in the icy northlands of Northrend, it is a massive Drakkari fortress that sits on the border of Zul'Drak and Grizzly Hills; it's an impressive collection of spires and beautifully carved walls.
Drakkari Empire:
The Drakkari Empire, or the Empire of Zul'Drak, was among the largest troll nations ever to have existed, made of the ice trolls of Ancient Kalimdor and led by the Drakkari tribe. The empire was formed at a time when troll dominance on Azeroth was unhindered. From the capital temple city of Gundrak in Zul'Drak, the Drakkari and their subordinate tribes, including the Winterax and Frostmane, laid claim to much of the frigid north of the continent, bordering the Amani Empire to the southeast.
The Drakkari were known to be particularly cunning fighters, which they would prove to great effect during the Aqir and Troll War, and were strong enough to challenge the Zandalari, Amani, and Gurubashi trolls. As with the rest of their kind, the Drakkari Empire was fiercely devoted to loa worship, erecting temple cities and other structures in their honor.
For millennia, the Drakkari Empire continued to thrive without incident. The Great Sundering, which shattered the old continent of Kalimdor, would prove disastrous for the Drakkari. Their empire was weakened, with the tribes dispersed to different continents. The Drakkari themselves, now living on Northrend, would continue to maintain the empire, though it was a shadow of their former glory. In time, it too would eventually fall at the hands of the Undead Scourge, marking the end of an era.
Drakkari tribe: The Drakkari tribe was a tribe of ice trolls that founded the Drakkari Empire in Northrend, with Zul'Drak as their capital. They seemed to be a hardy people, persisting through hostilities from the empire of Azjol-Nerub and the Scourge. The tribe suffered massive losses in the war against the Lich King. The raid on the Throne of Thunder marked the last time the Drakkari were seen fighting as a unified tribe. The remaining Drakkari are now scattered across Azeroth.
Dranosh'ar Blockade:
The Dranosh'ar Blockade is a massive system of fortifications outside the Gates of Orgrimmar, stretching east-west in front of the northern mountains of Durotar. It reaches from Skull Rock to the east to Rocktusk Farm to the west. It is presumably named in honor of Dranosh Saurfang, who fell at the Battle of Angrathar the Wrathgate during the war against the Lich King.
At the front of it, several siege weapons stand ready for defense. Behind these, archers of the Horde train for battle, while laborers build machinery and transport goods. The blockade has built around Jaggedswine Farm and uses the hut there for storage. The hut just to the west of the front gate contains Gor the Enforcer and Shin Stonepillar, who have differing views on the leadership of the Horde.
Dreadlord Insurgents: The Dreadlord Insurgents were one of the Scourge forces loyal to the Burning Legion during the power struggle in Lordaeron following the Legions's defeat at the Battle of Mount Hyjal. The Dreadlords Insurgents were commanded by Balnazzar, Detheroc and Varimathras.
Dreadmaul: The Dreadmaul ogres are found in the Blasted Lands claiming the territory of Dreadmaul Hold and an area further south, Dreadmaul Post.
Dreadmaul Post: Dreadmaul Post is an ogre mound of the Dreadmaul ogre Clan in the Blasted Lands.  Dreadmaul Ogres remained close to the Dark Portal after coming to Azeroth from Draenor.  They continue to maintain a strong presence in the area.  An occasional lost draenei can also be found wandering the nearby territory.
Dreadmaul Rock:
Dreadmaul Rock, also known as Dreadmaul Peak, is the base of operations for the Firegut ogres. It is a large structure, with paths leading to the top and a complicated cave system of ogre mounds within.
Around the time of the Cataclysm, the ogres allied with the Blackrock clan. Dreadmaul Rock is now being used as a major base of operations for attacks by the clan aimed towards Redridge Mountains to the south.
Dreadmist Camp:
Dreadmist Camp  is a Horde encampment located at the foot of Dreadmist Peak, north of the Crossroads along the Gold Road. It is an important stop for Horde caravans traveling through the Northern Barrens.
It is run by Nagala Whipshank.
During the Legion Invasions, the camp was overrun, with several kodo, guards and peons killed.
Dreadwake's Landing:
Dreadwake's Landing is a Forsaken landing area on Ashil's Bay in Stormheim. The Oblivion is moored offshore here.
The Gilneans are trying to assault this area, turning the nearby shore (Greymane's Offensive) into a battlefield.
Dreadwatch Outpost: Dreadwatch Outpost was a Forsaken outpost watching over Gilneas City, in the Northern Headlands of the Ruins of Gilneas. Prior to the invasion of Gilneas, it appeared to be a chicken farm.
Dreamer's Rest:
Dreamer's Rest is a small camp located south of Oneiros, on the eastern side of the Twin Colossals in Feralas. Overseen by the Druids of the Talon, it offers many facilities for an outpost of its size.

 This section concerns content related to the Warcraft novels, novellas, or short stories.
Thrall was briefly sent here by Ysera after the Cataclysm to help its druids against the elements. The disrupted memories of its ancients was what caused Thrall to subsequently journey to the Caverns of Time in order to find out exactly who or what was interfering with history.
Dreamgrove:
The Dreamgrove is the order hall of the druids of the Dreamweavers and Cenarion Circle. Located in Val'sharah, the Dreamgrove is directly linked to the Emerald Dreamway, a section of the Emerald Dream connecting several locations powerful in Nature magic across Azeroth, such as the Grizzly Hills and Twilight Grove.
When asked what the Dreamgrove meant to them, the Archdruid replied among the followings:

Balance - Like the turn of every season, so do they change, adapt, survive, and endure. They ensure the promise of the Dreamgrove: that all things return to balance.
Life - The Dreamgrove is the warm light by which death's shadow is cast. That is worth protecting.
Nature - They are the vast and varied nature of all living things. The freedom of the world that was, that is, and that will ever be. Good and evil may wax and wane, but nature is eternal.
Dreamweavers:
The Dreamweavers (or the Druids of Val'sharah) are one of the factions that heroes can acquire reputation with for toys and gear in Legion. Powerful druids in Val'sharah, they grew under Cenarius's tutelage before and after the Great Sundering. Their knowledge of druidism is ancient and unparalleled.
According to Khadgar, mighty Shaladrassil was grown from a sprout taken from G'Hanir in a time before the Sundering. The tree is noted as so ancient, it stood at the center of Val'sharah and druidic culture since the very first night elves reached for the Emerald Dream. From this, the Dreamweavers were formed, an order so ancient they beheld as Shaladrassil bound itself to the Emerald Dream and towered over the land for eons. This, coupled with Rensar Greathoof's commentary, means that the Dreamweavers were the first druidic order on Azeroth and some of its first druids.
During the Legion Assaults, they lend their hippogryphs to assist the adventurers.
Drekirjar: The Drekirjar (or the Dragon-Riders) are a group of dragon-taming vrykul located in southeastern Stormheim, in the city of Hrydshal. A part of the Tideskorn, the Drekirjar have famously maintained a pact with the local Thorignir storm drakes for ages, granting them an unprecedented command of the skies. In recent times, however, the rise of God-King Skovald has seen the Drekirjar betray this alliance, with disastrous consequences.
Drogbar: The drogbar (/ˈdɹɔɡ.bɑɹ/ DRAWG-bar) are a shamanistic humanoid species that dwell underground, mainly found in the infinite caverns deep within Highmountain on the Broken Isles and in Zaralek Cavern on the Dragon Isles. Their brutish appearance can hide their cleverness. Having once been the slaves of Deathwing himself, the drogbar have long lived in relative peace with the Highmountain tauren, but shortly after the Burning Legion's return the drogbar leader, Dargrul, stole the ancient Hammer of Khaz'goroth, initiating a war between the two races.
Drottinn Hrothgar:
Drottinn Hrothgar is a kvaldir raider who has claimed Hrothgar's Landing from the local tuskarr. Adventurers are tasked to kill him in the <Crusader>-level daily quest  [25-30 Daily] Drottinn Hrothgar.
According to the quest, "Drottinn" is Hrothgar's title, not part of his name.
Druid:
The druid (occasionally druidess for females) is a shapeshifting hybrid class available to the night elf, worgen, tauren (including Highmountain), troll (including Zandalari), and Kul Tiran races. Druids are able to perform each of the three group roles (tanking, healing, and dealing damage) by utilizing their shapeshift forms. While a druid is most effective in the role determined by their active specialization and equipment, they can also use their shapeshifting abilities to temporarily switch to a different role in combat. In addition to combat forms, druids can shapeshift into forms that increase movement speed while running, swimming, or flying. The ability to switch roles out of combat - and temporarily perform a different role in combat - makes the druid class one of the most versatile in World of Warcraft.
Druids have as many faces to them as nature itself: destruction, animal fury, transformation, healing. Everything about them is rooted in cycles and transience, and the Emerald Dream of what Azeroth would have been with nature unfettered. Although nature magic serves as the druid's source of power, they can also call upon Elune's moonlight, as well as the solar magic emitted by the suns and the god An'she.
Druids for the Ethical and Humane Treatm:
Druids for the Ethical and Humane Treatment of Animals (D.E.H.T.A.) is an organization based primarily in Northrend and is a radical portion of the Cenarion Expedition. The organization was created in direct opposition to master hunter Hemet Nesingwary. They are opposed to the decimation of wildlife caused by Nesingwary and his hunters, and they also give players the chance to battle Hemet's hunters.
If a player kills any animal in the Borean Tundra, including hostile ones, the debuff  [Animal Blood] is applied. The debuff causes D.E.H.T.A.-associated NPCs to become hostile and attack on sight, chasing and screaming insults until it wears off. This debuff is easily cured by jumping into a body of water.
During the third invasion of the Burning Legion, D.E.H.T.A. came to Highmountain to oppose the Pinerock Hunters that threatened the wildlife in the area.
Drust:
The Drust were a population of vrykul who inhabited the island of Kul Tiras before the first humans arrived there. They wielded powerful death magic and mainly lived in Drustvar, but also resided in several areas of Tiragarde Sound and to lesser extent Stormsong Valley; to this day, their ruins and ancient roads can be seen throughout the island. When human sailors from Gilneas arrived in Kul Tiras around 2,700 years ago, the Drust king Gorak Tul led his people into war against the human settlers. However, not all Drust agreed with the war, and the druidic Thornspeakers left Drust society to side with the humans.
Gorak Tul eventually lost the conflict, and his Drust were almost all slain by the human invaders. However, Gorak Tul called upon the dark powers of Thros, the Blighted Lands, where the Drust's spirits found refuge. Since then, they have slowly been trying to make their way back to the mortal world. During the Fourth War, they made a pact with Lady Waycrest, helping her save her dying husband in exchange for assisting them. On the Drust's part, all they desired was vengeance against her people. Following this pact, Waycrest began wielding Drust magic and formed the Heartsbane Coven, an order of witches who began terrorizing the people of Drustvar and worked to summon Gorak Tul back into the realm of the living.
Gorak Tul's efforts on Kul Tiras were eventually thwarted, but the Drust have reappeared in large numbers in the Shadowlands, where they are attempting to invade the realm of Ardenweald from Thros, led by nightscreamer Gorak Zhar.
Drywhisker: The Drywhiskers are a group of kobolds found in the Arathi Highlands.
Dubra'Jin: Dubra'Jin is a small Zandalari outpost that is located west of Gundrak in Zul'Drak. It is also the name of the forgotten god, represented by the nearby statue. By sacrificing raptor eggs to the god, he, in turn, protects the few trolls there from being overrun by the Drakkari.
Dun Algaz: Dun Algaz (/ˈduːn ˈɑlɡɑz/ DOON AHL-GAHZ) (or Algaz Gate) is the tunneled mountain pass area between Loch Modan and the Wetlands, as well as the name of a stronghold located in the pass. It is bordered by Algaz Station in Loch Modan and Slabchisel's Survey in the Wetlands.
Dun Argol:
Dun Argol is an iron dwarf city located in the Grizzly Hills of Northrend. The iron dwarves here are led by Iron Thane Furyhammer. Dun Argol became the capital of the iron dwarves after the fall of Thor Modan and its continued destruction by the stone giants.
Explorers' League prospectors Gann, Torgan and Varana were sent to Dun Argol by Raegar Breakbrow to search for artifacts and information about the history of the settlement, however, they never expected Dun Argol to be this heavily populated and they were all taken captive by the iron dwarves. They were later rescued by adventurers.
The brothers Bronzebeard made note of Dun Argol, stating that the city resembles the Northrend titanic style, with runes inscribed on nearly every surface.
Dun Garok:
Dun Garok was a dwarven keep nestled into the southeastern hills of the Hillsbrad Foothills. Led by Captain Ironhill, the dwarves helped protect the humans of Hillsbrad as well as the Azurelode Mine. The Forsaken loathed the presence of these dwarves and once offered several quests for Horde adventurers to infiltrate Dun Garok and kill the dwarves within.
The Forsaken, outnumbering the dwarves ten-to-one, assaulted them with all their might. The dwarves fought until the bitter end, but every last one of them died in defense of Dun Garok.

 This section concerns content related to Cataclysm.
The dwarves who fell in battle rose again as Dun Garok Spirits and now haunt the land, refusing to yield it even in death. The Forsaken eventually gave up on trying to inhabit the fortress and let the dead spirits keep their land.
The ghost of Captain Ironhill has remained in Dun Garok, not for vengeance, but out of sadness for his people that have remained. He tasks Horde adventurers to release their spirits from the place. Additionally, the ghost of Tamra Stormpike can occasionally be found in the main quarters, seething with hatred.

 This section concerns content related to Battle for Azeroth.
Some time later, the Forsaken finally took over Dun Garok by controlling the ghosts. Meanwhile, troops from Ironforge marched to purge the Forsaken and the ghosts, and to retake the fortress. Jezelle Pruitt and Brandur Ironhammer‎ were encountered here, by the Alliance and Horde respectively.
Dun Mandarr: Dun Mandarr is a small base nearby an icy cavern in south-eastern Winterspring. The camp is overrun by ferocious moonkin and was set up by Jaron Stoneshaper, its dwarven origin obvious from the linguistic qualities of the cave's name. Jaron had discovered a  [Blue-Feathered Amulet], which enraged the wildkin and caused them to chase Jaron off and destroy his camp.
Dun Modr:
Dun Modr (/ˈduːn ˈmoʊdrə/ DOON MOHD-rə) is a fortified middle-sized dwarven city that sits along the road just south of Thandol Span, in the north of the Wetlands. It was occupied by Dark Iron dwarves, which claimed the fallen city as their own. It was eventually recaptured by Thargas Anvilmar of Ironforge following the Cataclysm.
The city contains a blacksmith shop and an inn-brewery.
Dun Niffelem: Dun Niffelem is a fortress of massive spikes of ice and iron chains, spreading out to block off an entire section of the Valley of Ancient Winters, in the eastern of Storm Peaks. It is home to the Sons of Hodir, a clan of frost giants, and their ruler King Jokkum.
Dunelle's Kindness:
Dunelle's Kindness  is a town with a dawntower, located in the eastern extent of the zone. Players are directed here in the first quest of the Hallowfall storyline,  [75-78] The Hallowed Path.
The town is bordered by Lothar's Landing to the east, Shadowmire to the southeast, The Aegis Wall to the south, Rumshackle to the west, and Growling Hollow to the north.
The Dunelle's Detour skyriding race is started northeast of town.
Dunemaul Compound:
Dunemaul Compound is the ogre mound of the Dunemaul ogres of Tanaris. Their leader, Sandscraper, resides here in his cave. Megs Dreadshredder, located just east at the Dunemaul Recruitment Camp, tries to "recruit" these ogres into the Horde.
During the Burning Legion's invasion, the camp falls under the Legion's control. Its residents are enslaved by nathrezim and are later killed by the defenders.
Dunemaul Recruitment Camp:
Dunemaul Recruitment Camp is a small Horde camp just east of the Dunemaul Compound in Tanaris. Megs Dreadshredder believes it is a waste for this ogres to just be sitting around here doing nothing, when they could be working for the Horde, but directly under the Bilgewater Cartel as cheap local labor. She eventually recruits the Dunemaul Ogres with the help of an ogre "Ambassador" and an adventurer.

 This section concerns content related to Legion.
During the Legion Invasions, the camp was defended by Bilgewater Muscles.
Dunemaul clan:
The Dunemaul clan is a large clan (also referred to as a band or tribe) of nomadic ogres who have taken over a large area of Tanaris and formed a compound to the south. The leader of this clan was Gor'marok the Ravager but was replaced by Sandscraper at some point. The Dunemaul clan eats the bits of the Centipaar silithid.
Following the Cataclysm the Dunemaul clan was brought into the Horde by Megs Dreadshredder and the Dunemaul "Emissary", who are stationed at the Dunemaul Recruitment Camp, through means of force and threats. After they were "recruited", Megs has them caged up and sent to other locations to work for the Horde, leaving only sand where they once were.
During the Burning Legion's invasion, their compound was assaulted. All remaining residents were enslaved by nathrezim. Some of them could be rescued by the adventurers.
Durnholde Keep:
Durnholde Keep is a ruined stronghold located east of the town of Tarren Mill in the Hillsbrad Foothills. It used to be an internment camp and prison for the orcs.
Along with its inner barracks, Durnholde also had a mage tower and an arena.
The small village that encircled Durnholde was inhabited by those who made their living off tending to the needs of the fortress's inhabitants.
Durotar (nation): The nation of Durotar (or kingdom) is an orcish nation and a member state of the Horde. Following the Third War, the clans under Warchief Thrall's leadership founded the nation of Durotar and the great city of Orgrimmar.
Duskhaven: Duskhaven was a town located along the southwestern coast of Gilneas, with Gwen Armstead as its mayor. It was the location that the evacuees from Gilneas City fled to as the worgen overran the capital.
Dustbelch Grotto: Dustbelch Grotto is a large ogre mound in southwestern Badlands. It is home to the Dustbelcher ogres.
Dustbelcher: The Dustbelcher ogres live in the Badlands, mostly found in Dustbelch Grotto.
Dustwind Dig:
Dustwind Dig is situated in the hills above Hammertoe's Digsite in the Badlands and is the expanded Alliance camp of Sigrun Ironhew.  It contains a flight path.
Following the Fourth War, the Explorers' League is still present and active on the digsite in the region.
Earthen Ring: The Earthen Ring is a neutral faction of shaman dedicated to preserving the balance between the elements. This gathering of the most powerful shaman of Azeroth seeks to maintain the balance between the world's elemental forces, unlike its sinister adversary, the Twilight's Hammer cult. Led by the Council of Elders, it includes shaman from both the Alliance and the Horde, who put aside old rivalries for the good of the world. As the true masters of the elements, they wield the power of the elemental forces between which they maintain balance. Those who assist the Earthen Ring find themselves rewarded with items that reflect the wisdom and primal power of the elements. During the Cataclysm, they healed the world and the elements wherever they could. They also fought the Burning Legion alongside the other class orders during the demons' third invasion.
Earthenworks:
The Earthenworks  is located in north-central Ringing Deeps. The area is bordered by the Stonevault Exterior to the north, Nibelgaz Mine to the east, Gundargaz to the south, Ironhaul Station and Hallowfall Gate to the southwest, and Candleslag Quarry to the west.
The instance line to the Stonevault is at  in the Stonevault Exterior, and the Hall of Awakening is just to the west at .
East Spire: The East Spire is a destructible building in northeastern Tol Barad. It can be destroyed with the two Abandoned Siege Engines that spawn nearby at the entrance to Cursed Depths for more time.
Eastvale Logging Camp: Eastvale Logging Camp (also known as the Eastvale Lumber Camp or just Eastvale Camp) is a series of Stormwindian lumber mill camps with living areas in between, located in eastern of Elwynn Forest. Orders for lumber are constantly streaming in from various buyers, and the lumberjacks work against strict deadlines. There is also stables where adventurers can purchase horses mounts.
Eastwall Tower: Eastwall Tower is a scout tower located in the Eastern Plaguelands.  During the Scourge invasion of Lordaeron, Eastwall Tower was destroyed and left in ruins.  Later it became a battleground as it was one of the fallen towers that the Alliance and Horde fought over for in order to fortify themselves in Lordaeron. The Eastwall Tower, along with all the other towers of the Eastern Plaguelands, have been rebuilt by the Argent Crusade and are currently being used as outposts throughout the region. Like the nearby Light's Hope Chapel, there are signs of life around the tower, and there is also a neutral flight master. The PvP component has been removed.
Eastwind Rest:
Eastwind Rest can be found northwest of the Kun-Lai Pass in the Yaungol Advance of southeastern Kun-Lai Summit. The pandaren of Eastwind have chosen to ally with the Horde forces under the command of General Nazgrim. Eastwind's Alliance counterpart is Westwind Rest, found opposite Mogujia and the Chow Farmstead, due north of the Gate of the August Celestials to the Vale of Eternal Blossoms.

 This section concerns content related to Battle for Azeroth.
By the time of the rise of N'Zoth, Eastwind Rest has been destroyed by the rampaging mogu forces, as with Westwind Rest.
During the events of the war against the Primalists on the Dragon Isles, Li Li Stormstout reported that there was little sign left of Eastwind Rest.
Ebon Scales:
The Ebon Scales are a dracthyr weyrn originally charged with bringing destruction to the enemies of the black dragonflight, raining down fire and unleashing spellcraft upon those who would stand against the Earth-Warder. After awakening from their confinement like the rest of the dracthyr, they felt betrayed by their former Aspect and decided to cut off ties with the dragonflights, renaming themselves the Sundered Flame. Led by Scalecommander Sarkareth, the weyrn went on a quest to reclaim their legacy and obtain the secrets of Neltharion for themselves, entering into open conflict with the inhabitants of the Dragon Isles or anyone who would stand in their way, including their former kin.
Following Sarkareth's death in Aberrus, Scalecommander Emberthal and Winglord Dezran embraced the lost, surviving members of the weyrn and reformed it under its original name, the Ebon Scales.
Ebon Watch:
Ebon Watch is a minor encampment of the Knights of the Ebon Blade in Zul'Drak.
During the war against the Lich King, the Ebon Blade established Ebon Watch as a small outpost in Zul'Drak, and from there conducted their own operations — and some in cooperation with the Argent Crusade.
Following the war against the Jailer, the brothers Bronzebeard reported that while most of the death knights have moved on to fight in other wars, Ebon Watch remained out of an abundance of caution for years. That caution turned out to be rather prescient when Sylvanas Windrunner destroyed the Helm of Domination and the Scourge ran amok once more.
Ebyssian:
Ebyssian the Earth-Warder is one of the six Dragon Aspects and leader of the black dragonflight, having ascended to the role following the reawakening of the Dragon Isles. Prior to Sabellian's return from Outland, he was one of the few black dragons on Azeroth uncorrupted by the Old Gods. 10,000 years ago, his egg was purified prior to his birth by Huln Highmountain within Neltharion's former lair. For generations to follow, Ebyssian watched over Huln's descendants in Highmountain as a tauren spiritwalker named Ebonhorn; a name given to him by Huln while "Ebyssian" is the draconic name he later took on.
During the third invasion of the Burning Legion, Ebyssian was essential in the fight against the drogbar, and used his role as a spiritwalker to help Mayla Highmountain ascend to the role of High Chieftain. Prior to the Highmountain tauren joining the Horde, it was discovered that Ebyssian inadvertently risked the Old Gods corrupting him whenever he leaves Highmountain, which manifested during a feast in Thunder Bluff following the Argus Campaign. It occurred a second time during the Fourth War when he traveled to the Chamber of Heart, though he is now able to travel freely following the defeat of N'zoth.
During the war against the Primalists, Ebyssian was initially present alongside Wrathion on the Forbidden Reach to assist the dracthyr following their awakening from stasis against the Primalists, eventually leading the Dark Talons to Orgrimmar in order to work alongside the Horde. He was later present within the city to offer Horde adventurers the invitation of the Dragon Aspects to visit the Dragon Isles, which led to the formation of the Dragonscale Expedition. He later played a role in assisting Scalecommander Emberthal with securing the Forbidden Reach.
After the Primal Incarnates opened the way to Zaralek Cavern, Ebyssian joined Sabellian and Wrathion at the behest of Alexstrasza. Initially allying with the Loamm Niffen to deal with Fyrakk, Ebyssian later assisted in dealing with the Sundered Flame. Throughout their time in the Cavern, Ebyssian frequently served as a mediator between Wrathion and Sabellian, who both sought to reclaim Neltharion's legacy. After they both realized the truth behind that legacy throughout Aberrus, the Shadowed Crucible, they stepped aside, pledging themselves to Ebyssian as the new Earth-Warder. Following Fyrakk's defeat in the Emerald Dream, Ebyssian finally gained his Aspectral power once each of the Aspects had been blessed by Azeroth for their defense of Amirdrassil.
Eco-Dome Al'dani: Eco-Dome Al'dani is a dungeon in The War Within, added in patch 11.2.0. According to Ve'nari, it is one of the most important Eco-Domes. It was built upon the former site of the K'areshi's most sacred grounds, the High Temple of K'aresh.
Edj:
Edj is a large port town controlled by the Blackwater Raiders. This much smaller cousin to Bilgewater Port is located on the opposite side of the island, in Kezan's northeastern coast.
Despite the fact that they are pirates, the Blackwater Raiders are not really that much of bad guys. They are less interested in plunder and more interested in securing mercantile deals and widening the circle of ports with which they can trade. A goblin known as Baron Revilgaz, based in Booty Bay in Stranglethorn Vale, rules the Blackwater Raiders, and thus is technically in charge of Edj. The Trade Coalition has little inﬂuence over Revilgaz, and indeed the Raiders attempt to go under, above, or around the coalition's head.
Edj has a secluded port that primarily serves the Raiders and their allies. It is largely for goods the pirates don't want the coalition to know about: contraband and especially pricey stuff, like magic items and political prisoners. For normal trade items, they go through Bilgewater Port like everyone else.
Ekka's Hideaway: Ekka's Hideaway is found in the south western parts of the Nar'anan ruins in Nazjatar.
Elder Rise:
Elder Rise is directly east of the central bluff and is the home of the Cenarion Circle in Thunder Bluff. Many tauren druids and priests reside here and provide training. The Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem resides here. Before her exile, the leader of the Grimtotem tribe, Magatha Grimtotem, used to inhabit the hut between the two bridges. Elder Rise connects to high rise and middle rise by separate rope bridges.
Elder Rise holds the governing Council of Elders and also members of the Cenarion Circle.
During Saurfang's rebellion, Elder Rise was defended by Highmountain tauren led by Mayla Highmountain as well as Huojin and Tushui pandaren led by Ji Firepaw and Aysa Cloudsinger respectively.
After the Fourth War, Rexxar and Zekhan visited the rise and met with the trainers. They were happy to hear that the Horde Council wished them health and safety, and the elders stated few needs from their people, in addition of healing.
Elodor: Elodor is a draenei city located to the northwest of Karabor, and is the breadbasket of Shadowmoon Valley. It is the home of the Council of Exarchs, the five draenei leaders under Prophet Velen. The city is separated into sections, the main town, Altar of Sha'tar, Elodor Dig, Elodor Fields, Exarch's Rise, Fey Landing, Rangari Enclave and The Silken Pillow. During the course of the Draenor campaign, Exarch Hataaru is murdered by Soulbinder Nyami under the order of Exarch Othaar. After much bickering, Othaar is exposed and flees to Shattrath City.
Elysian Hold:
Elysian Hold is the Sanctum of the Kyrian Covenant, located in the northeastern part of Bastion, and is part of the larger Spires of Ascension and serves as the entrance to the Spires. The Hold was originally created by the Archon herself to serve as a base of operations from which the Ascended can stand guard over the region. The rest of the Spires of Ascension were created by the First Forgelite.
It is the meeting place of the Archon and Paragons of Bastion, and serves as the location of many powerful facilities and tools, such as the Crest of Ascension used to elevate new ascended. Wards that protect each of the five temples of Bastion are also found in the Hold in the southern wing of the hold. The bell named Echo of Aeons in the central upper platform can summon the Paragons to the Archon while the northern wing holds the Bell of Recall to summon the ascended kyrians back to the hold.
Embaari Village:
Embaari Village is a draenei settlement located in the central part of Shadowmoon Valley, west of Karabor and south of Elodor. Embaari is a center of trade, and its ranchers also domesticate talbuks and elekks for use in Shattrath City and other draenei settlements. The village also supports the practical needs of Teluuna Observatory's researchers.
The merchant town is known for its delicious food and exotic wares.
Embaari is eventually attacked by the Shadowmoon clan, with the goal of taking enough prisoners to Anguish Fortress, but the attack was repelled.
Emberfall Watch: Emberfall Watch is a subzone of Ashran, the physical tower found in the Emberfall Tower subzone. It is from the Emberfall Watch that the Horde Tower Guardian Jeron Emberfall surveys the battle below, guarded by two Lava Furies.
Emberstone Village: Emberstone Village is a village along the Northgate River in northeastern Gilneas.
Emberwatch: Emberwatch is a Dragonscale Expedition camp within some dragon ruins located near the Sundapple Copse in northern Ohn'ahran Plains.
Emerald Circle: The Emerald Circle are a largely autonomous branch of the Cenarion Circle working specifically to undo the corruption in Felwood. They are stationed at the Emerald Sanctuary in southern Felwood.
Emerald Nightmare:
The Emerald Nightmare (or the Nightmare for short) is the name given to the Old God corruption of the Emerald Dream. When the Nightmare spreads, it consumes the life force of all it touches. The more it spreads, the weaker druid magic becomes. It is a realm of death, decay, and nightmare.
During the War Against the Nightmare, it was revealed that the Emerald Nightmare was under the rule of a figure known as the Nightmare Lord, who in fact was really Malfurion Stormrage's old nemesis, the satyr Xavius. However, it was also revealed that Xavius himself was a minion of a powerful yet ancient evil, residing in the Rift of Aln, and possibly also beneath Azeroth's oceans. Despite the defeat of Xavius and the removal of much of the nightmare through the course of Stormrage, the noting of a still-corrupted area indicated that the Nightmare was still a threat. Its influence was slowly overtaking the forests of Val'sharah through the World Tree Shaladrassil during the events of Legion.
The Nightmare acts like a heavy shroud, warping reality, altering the perception of all living things, and bending the boundary between reality and dream. None are immune to the Nightmare's corruption, and it has been known to take hold of former Dragon Aspects, demigods and even demons. When a mortal has become corrupted by the nightmare, there is no return. Only death will set them free, although Elune's power in Tyrande Whisperwind's presence has seemingly cleansed or resisted its corruption to varying degrees on several occasions, such as with Eranikus, Elothir and Ysera. Once cursed, the nightmare will begin consuming the victim's thoughts and filling their head with the voices of other corrupted beings, even the nearby flora. The curse itself, however, is known to make the victims very, very powerful, rivaling even that of ancients.
Emerald Sanctuary: Emerald Sanctuary is a camp of the Emerald Circle in southeastern Felwood. The druids stationed here give quests to adventurers about investigating demonic corruption at Jaedenar and snuffing it out.
Emperor Shaohao (faction): Emperor Shaohao is a reputation earned by helping Emperor Shaohao. His spirit now oversees the war against the Ordon yaungol, chaotic barbarians who threaten Pandaria while the bulk of the Alliance and Horde participate in the Siege of Orgrimmar.
Empire of Zul:
The Empire of Zul was a powerful coalition of troll tribes formed during the Aqir and Troll War, around 16,000 BDP. United by the most powerful and influential troll tribe on Ancient Kalimdor, the Zandalari, the empire sought to halt the relentless advance of the insectoid aqir, who had begun to swarm across the breadth of the continent. The alliance was one of necessity, with each faction of trolls facing extinction.
Working together and employing new tactics, the empire succeeded in repelling the aqiri invasion, significantly preventing the fall of the strategic Zandalar Mountains. The united troll tribes then launched several brutal and concurrent campaigns to not only destroy the aqir threat permanently, but also to expand their borders to new and untouched lands. In the aftermath, the Empire of Zul remained intact and continued to flourish. While uncontested in its domination of all of Kalimdor for thousands of years, however, its relevance and effectiveness waned as the various troll nations began to become more independent and isolated.
The empire survived at least until the rise of the Kaldorei Empire, at whose hands the trolls were soundly and repeatedly defeated. At this point, their power had been greatly reduced on the continent, with the night elves becoming the new dominant race. It is assumed that, with the Great Sundering, the last vestiges of the once-mighty Empire of Zul were eradicated, as Kalimdor was torn apart and the troll race scattered.
It is unknown exactly how the Empire of Zul was led and governed. Although referred to as an empire, it was composed of largely independent tribes which maintained a majority of autonomy even during the war with the aqir. It is likely that meetings were held among representatives from each tribe to discuss and govern major aspects of the empire (as has been known to occur with other examples of unified troll tribes).
Enclave: The Enclave  is the southwestern quadrant of the Ring of Fates in Oribos. Here, representatives of the four covenants are found, alongside Tal-Inara, Honored Voice of the Arbiter, and Bolvar Fordragon. The enclave serves as the quest hub of the expansion - campaign-level storylines begin and end here. Additionally, the PvP vendor and questgivers, and the reputation quartermasters can all be found in the area. The map table, depicting Oribos and the four zones of the Shadowlands, was created by the First Ones and is able to connect to the mortal plane via an object tied to it, and the adventurer does so by using a fragment of the Helm of Domination.
Eredath:
Eredath, called the Jewel of Argus, was one of the most illustrious cities of Argus, the pinnacle of eredar civilization, and the most sacred of all cities. Following the destruction that befell Argus, the city of Eredath now floats above the planet, in a relatively pristine state.
