Eredath serves as one of three zones on Argus and hosts the Seat of the Triumvirate dungeon.
Estuary of Awakening: The Estuary of Awakening  lies between the Windswept Aerie to the south and Hope's Ascent to the north in southwestern Korthia. The area has been overrun by devourers, feasting on both the anima and the razorwings.
Eternal Palace:
The Eternal Palace is the royal seat of Queen Azshara and the Nazjatar Empire. It was built after the Sundering alongside the rest of Nazjatar. After opening the waters around the naga homeland, Azshara invited the Alliance and Horde forces wrecked there to her palace, where she tried to fulfill her mischievous plans.
In Rise of Azshara, the Eternal Palace serves as a raid in the zone of Nazjatar, with Queen Azshara herself as the final boss. It is entered through the whirlpool in the Gate of the Queen, in which a water current will transport the player in-front of the raid entrance. To return, the Displacement Pedestal near the stairs is used to teleport you back to the Tidal Conflux.
Ethereum:
The Ethereum are a faction of ethereals who once served as the ruling class of K'aresh, the ethereals' homeworld. They swore vengeance upon Dimensius the All-Devouring after the void lord consumed their world. Since then, they have grown dark and twisted, with vengeance becoming their only recourse they have become ruthless. Several of the Nexus-Princes of the Ethereum council abandoned the Ethereum to form other groups and factions with different goals, such as the Consortium and the Protectorate who believe that the Ethereum have become as great a threat as Dimensius.
During the invasion of Outland, they sought to use the manaforges of the Netherstorm to "become void", but their efforts were thwarted by the Protectorate and the adventurers. They later allied with the blue dragonflight in Northrend during the Nexus War. During the Burning Legion's third invasion, they assaulted the Nexus to access the blue dragonflight's treasures within.
Ethereum members glow with red or shadowy energies rather than blue.
Evergrove: Evergrove is a Cenarion Expedition outpost located in Ruuan Weald in the Blade's Edge Mountains. Unlike the other outposts belonging to the Cenarion expedition in Outland, this outpost is manned almost entirely by night elves. All available services, including a flight point (Located at ), are offered to both Horde and Alliance.
Everlook: Everlook is a trading post run by the goblins of the Steamwheedle Cartel. It lies at the crossroads of Winterspring's main trade routes and contains a goblin laboratory.
Evermorn Hold:
Evermorn Hold is a Mag'har outpost based in Gorgrond from the alternate Draenor's future. It is built upon where Evermorn Springs once were. During the war between the Lightbound and the Mag'har, Evermorn Hold was attacked by the Lightbound led by Exarch Orelis. From here, the Exarch launched an attack against Beastwatch. However, the Mag'har repelled the assault and launched their own assault on Evermorn Hold. During the assault, Exarch Orelis was personally killed by Overlord Geya'rah, Eitrigg, and a Horde champion.
Following the Mag'har exodus to Azeroth, the state of the Evermorn Hold is unknown.
Evermorn Springs: Evermorn Springs is a botani base near Deeproot in Gorgrond.
Exile's Rise: Exile's Rise (or Palemoon Village) is a settlement located on Mount Kra'gor. The Shadowmoon Exiles led by Rulkan have made this village their home after splitting from Ner'zhul and his followers. The Shadowmoon's broken Ancestral Totem is located below the village; carved upon it was the name of every member of the Shadowmoon clan since its founding. Ner'zhul broke the stone when he agreed to join the Iron Horde, forswearing all loyalty to his ancestors.
Exodar:
The Exodar (pronounced EX-o-dar) is the draenei's enchanted capital city located on Azuremyst Isle. It is a dimensional ship satellite structure of the dimensional fortress known as Tempest Keep that crashed on Azeroth. Like other dimensional ships, the Exodar was able to transcend dimensions and warp time itself, but now acts solely as home of the draenei on Azeroth.
The Exodar contains a large amount of technological wonders, such as tall pillars of lavender lightning in the city districts are part of a system that courses threads of arcane power through the Exodar.
Exodar (nation): Exodar is a nation of draenei and a member state of the Alliance. Following the ill-fated landing of the Exodar, the dimensional ship they used to escape Outland, the draenei have worked feverishly to use its remains as their capital city on the Azuremyst Isles. Having suffered a long and arduous history of exile, the draenei are now resolved to give their lives in defense of the Light and Azeroth itself. In the wake of the Burning Legion's defeat on Argus, ending the Burning Crusade, Prophet Velen revealed his intention for the draenei to build a new city for themselves on Azeroth so that they would no longer be scattered exiles.
Expedition Armory:
The Expedition Armory is a ruined Sons of Lothar base on the edge of south-central Hellfire Peninsula. It was destroyed by Horde forces consisting of orcs and death knights near the end of the Invasion of Draenor. The death knights cursed the armory's defenders and turned them into the Unyielding, vengeful ghosts who haunt the ruins and remain trapped in an eternal battle against the Fel Horde. Most of the Sons of Lothar are unwilling to speak of or go near the ruins due to the painful memories involved.
The armory contains several ruined buildings, including Nightwatch Inn and the Lordaeron Armory.
Expedition Point:
Expedition Point is an outpost of Honor Hold in eastern Hellfire Peninsula. It is strategically placed near both Zeth'Gor and the Legion Front, and requires aid in fighting both fel orcs and demons. 
The camp is situated around the remains of a fel reaver; Alliance soldiers can be found mining the metal of the fel reaver.
Explorers' League:
The Explorers' League, also known as Explorers' Guild, Explorer's League or simply the League, is an organization dedicated to researching the origin of the dwarven race. They have many archaeological dig-sites in all corners of Azeroth, but also on Outland and alternate Draenor. The League's main base of operations is located in the Hall of Explorers in Ironforge. While Brann Bronzebeard is the current leader of the League, his brothers King Magni and Brann were founding members of the organization.
While predominantly a dwarven organization, the League also has members of other races among its ranks. Clopper Wizbang was, according to himself and Prospector Nachlan, the first gnome to become a member of the Explorers' League. The League also has an excellent, and unofficial, relationship with SI:7 that few people are familiar with. The two organizations traveling through Azeroth sometimes hold and share information by codes and secret means.
Explorers' League Digsite:
The Explorers' League Digsite is a small Alliance quest hub located near Mistvale Valley in the Cape of Stranglethorn.
Following the Fourth War, the league is still present and active on the digsite.
Explorers' League Outpost: Explorers' League Outpost is an Alliance quest hub located in the southeast area of the Howling Fjord, east of Nifflevar and Daggercap Bay, and just west of Baelgun's Excavation Site and Stonewall Lift.
Exploring Azeroth: Kalimdor: Exploring Azeroth: Kalimdor is an official Warcraft book by Sean Copeland presenting information on Kalimdor. It is the second book of the Exploring Azeroth series, released on 7 December, 2021.
Eye of Ysera:
The Eye of Ysera, often just shortened to "the Eye", is a place within the Emerald Dream. It is the green dragonflight's main base where Ysera and her brood watches over both the Dream and Azeroth from. It was created 20,000 years ago, just before the War of the Scaleborn broke out, and named by the green dragonflight in honor of Ysera.
The Eye is where Ysera and her flight most often congregate in the Dream. It's said to be the most idyllic place in the Dream and it's a valley nestled among great, encircling hills. The land is lush and filled with grass and flowers, but the name comes from the magnificent golden dome in the center, where Ysera herself dwells.
Faerin's Advance: Faerin's Advance is found in Azj-Kahet. It is a camp established by Faerin Lothar after the Reckoning's crash. Survivors of Dalaran went here to rest after escaping from Rak-Zakaz.
Fairbreeze Village: Fairbreeze Village is a blood elf village in southern Eversong Woods just west of the Dead Scar and close to the Sunsail Anchorage. Fairbreeze is the place where many young adventurers learn their trades, before venturing forth into the Ghostlands and Tranquillien.
Faithless: The Faithless, also known as the Faithless empire or the sethrak empire, (sometimes capitalized as the Sethrak Empire) are a force of militant sethrak led by Emperor Korthek. Having turned away from the sethrak's loa Sethraliss, the Faithless and their emperor seek to conquer all of Zandalar and will not stop until they have conquered the world. They have allied themselves with the forces of  General Jakra'zet of the Zanchuli Council with the shared goal of breaking the seal on the great pyramid of Atul'Aman and unleashing the monstrosity within in order to conquer Zuldazar.
Falanaar: Falanaar (or the Ruins of Falanaar) is a small ruined town behind Ambervale in Suramar that was heavily damaged in the Sundering, the destruction of the  [Tidestone of Golganneth], the loss of the first Arcan'dor, or some combination thereof. Based on the wall around the town, it does not appear to be a former part of Suramar City. The ruined Temple of Fal'adora, dedicated to Elune, is located here. Part of the town has collapsed into the Falanaar Tunnels where the Fal'dorei reside. Between the tunnels and the temple is the Shattered Locus, a failed arcan'dor. Moonshade Sanctum is nearby.
Falcon Watch: Falcon Watch is a Horde-aligned blood elf settlement in the western area of the Hellfire Peninsula. Its current leader is Ranger Captain Venn'ren. There are several quest givers and vendors here, as well as a flight master and an innkeeper.
Falconhurst: Falconhurst is a Kul Tiran town located in southwestern Drustvar, cut off from other settlements by the Crimson Forest.
Faldir's Cove:
Faldir's Cove is a small natural harbor on the southern shores of Arathi Highlands, near Stromgarde Keep and the Drowned Reef.
The cove is named after Faldir, apparently marking the spot where he and his followers began their voyage across the sea to create the kingdom of Stormwind.
Fallhaven: Fallhaven is a Kul Tiran farming village in eastern Drustvar. Its mayor, Cyril White, is a longtime friend of the Proudmoores. During the Fourth War, the villagers were cursed by the witch Helena Gentle, who used the Heartsbane Coven's dark magic to make them unable to move or respond. The village was eventually saved by Alliance adventurers sent to investigate the mysterious disappearances in the region.
Fallow Sanctuary: The Fallow Sanctuary is the village of a tribe of Lost Ones simply called the "Lost Ones", who live in the Swamp of Sorrows. All the Lost Ones here have been driven mad with homesickness and turned completely feral.
Fallsong Village: Fallsong Village is a jinyu village on the Krasarang River just to the south of the Krasari Falls in northwest Krasarang Wilds. The lore object Origins is located in a small temple at the center of the village, Cournith Waterstrider often appears here as well. The village is bordered by the Sentinel Basecamp and the Field of Korja. Dawnchaser Retreat can be found due south.
Fallsong tribe:
The Fallsong are a tribe of jinyu based at Fallsong Village in Krasarang Wilds. Their leader is presumably the waterspeaker Tired Shushen.

 This section concerns content related to Mists of Pandaria.
During the Alliance-Horde war in Pandaria, the village was pillaged by a band of saurok led by Slovan, without provocation or warning. The Temple of the Red Crane usually came to their aid when he attacked, but this time they found themselves outmatched and outmaneuvered. During the attack, the saurok stole the clothes off their dead, the trinkets out of their homes, and the ingots out of their forge. Their waterspeaker, Tired Shushen, later tasked adventurers to recover their stolen supplies and kill Slovan.
East of the village, the adventurers encountered Cournith Waterstrider, a pandarian champion, after they disrupted his meditations.

 This section concerns content related to Battle for Azeroth.
By the time of the Fourth War, the tribe found some Azerite washed ashore near their village, which Tired Shushen gave to adventurers who brought them the  [Razorfin Hunting Spear].
Fang'rila:
Fang'rila is the capital of the Blackfang tribe of saberon, located in southeastern Tanaan Jungle.
The Blackfang Challenge Arena, where the greatest champions of the Blackfang saberon can be summoned, is found in the southern part of the village. At the eastern edge of the village, there is a small lake filled with groupers and with an uninhabited island in its middle. On the northern edge of the lake, corrupted and twisted stone spires jut out of the ground, surrounding a pool of fel lava.
Far Watch Post:
Far Watch Post is a small Horde outpost located just west of the bridge between Durotar and the Northern Barrens. It contains a watch tower, an orc burrow and a few catapults. A riding wolf pen watched over by a pair of peons is located directly south.
Although not an accommodating spot, the outpost is vital for the protection of supply caravans, as well as keeping Durotar safe from Alliance and quilboar threats.
During the Burning Legion's invasions, the outpost fell under the Legion's control. Several of its residents were enslaved by nathrezim and were either killed or rescued by the defenders.
Farraki tribe: The Farraki tribe or the Sandfury tribe (sometimes spelled Sand Fury), originally known as the Razorbranch tribe, is a tribe (sometimes called an empire) of sand trolls, located in the deserts of Southern Kalimdor.
Farshire:
Farshire is a small town located outside of Valiance Keep in the Borean Tundra. At the start of the Valiance Expedition, the farmers of Farshire cut their fields into the rich, black soil of the tundra and their mine into the nearby hills. They supplied the keep with food and much-needed ore. Since the undead attacks, the only intact buildings are the town hall and lighthouse.
During the war against the Lich King, the town was consumed by the Scourge when infiltrators from the Cult of the Damned dropped their plague on the town and burned the place as the remaining townsfolk fought back. In the mine, Captain Jacobs and his Scourged Footmen controlled access to the last load of ore; while in the farmlands, ghouls fought against the Farshire Militia. Later, Alliance adventurers were sent to discover how the cultists infected the town, and to provide aid to the militia in keeping the Scourge at bay.
Years later, after the war against the Jailer, the Bronzebeard brothers reported that the farmers left are resourceful, stubborn folk, still trying to fight back the Scourge to regain their home. Muradin Bronzebeard also mentioned that he heard the farmers even figured out how to repurpose their mechanical harvest collectors to attack invading ghouls.
Farstrider Enclave:
Farstrider Enclave is a Farstrider base in the Ghostlands. It is located on the southern shore of Lake Elrendar, isolated from most of the rest of the friendly population of the Ghostlands. It is surrounded by ghosts on the lake, trolls of the Shadowpine tribe to the east and south, and lynxes on the land.
The enclave was renovated in year 25. Halduron Brightwing and his Farstriders were present here when they noticed some strange happenings at Dawnstar Spire. They immediately rushed there only to find the Blood Knights and Lor'themar Theron fighting against Dar'Khan Drathir and his undead minions.
Lor'themar and Halduron later held a summit with Warchief Thrall, Cairne Bloodhoof, Vol'jin, and Sylvanas Windrunner at the enclave, in which they formalized their kingdom's entry into the Horde.
Farstrider Lodge: The Farstrider Lodge (or Farstrider's Lodge) is a hunters' lodge located in southeastern Loch Modan. It houses several merchants and quest givers, as well as a hunter trainer and a pet trainer. Judging by its architecture, it is of high elven make, although there is only one known high elf residing there now — its other inhabitants being humans and dwarves.
Farwatcher's Glen:
Farwatcher's Glen is an Alliance town located southwest of Thal'darah Grove and Thal'darah Overlook in Stonetalon Mountains. While using night elf architecture, it features many different Alliance races, most prominently worgen. It holds flight paths to Thal'darah Overlook, Mirkfallon Post, Windshear Hold, and Nijel's Point.
In addition to Alliance NPCs, a significant number of ravens can be found here.
Fatescribe Roh-Tahl: Fatescribe Roh-Tahl is an attendant located in Oribos.
Fe-Feng Village: Fe-Feng Village is a Fe-Feng hozen village found just to the northwest of Morning Breeze Village on the Wandering Isle. Ruk-Ruk leads the hozen on this isle.
Fe-Feng tribe: The Fe-Feng are a tribe of hozen located on the Wandering Isle.
Feathermoon Stronghold: Feathermoon Stronghold, also known as New Feathermoon, is a kaldorei port located on the Forgotten Coast in Feralas. It was built after the Shattering as a replacement for the original, now destroyed stronghold located on Sardor Isle, which has been renamed the Ruins of Feathermoon. The fortress has a moonwell within and is under the command of General Shandris Feathermoon.
Fel Core: The Fel Core is the area below the Antoran Wastes. It displays if a player falls off the map, shortly before the player's horrific demise.
Fel Horde:
The Fel Horde is the army of fel orcs who first served the pit lord Magtheridon and then the Illidari. They are headquartered in Hellfire Citadel and the Black Temple. The Fel Horde is primarily made up of fel orcs, though they have some ogres and demons within their ranks.
It is revealed by Caza'rez that the Horde is researching a method to restore the fel orcs to their original state. Tagar Spinebreaker appears to be the only remaining leader of the Fel Horde following The Burning Crusade, as there are no quests or objectives to kill him; instead he wanders aimlessly near Hellfire Citadel.
Fel-Encrusted Herb: Fel-Encrusted Herbs are found on the Broken Shore and in Krokuun and Antoran Wastes.
Felpaw Village: Felpaw Village is a furbolg settlement that lies in the very north of Felwood, near the entrance of Timbermaw Hold. The village belongs to the Deadwood, a tribe of furbolgs that have been corrupted.
Felrock: The Felrocks, formerly Needlerocks, are a group of stone troggs located in Needlerock Chasm and Needlerock Slag in the Deepholm. They were led by Bouldergut until his death by the hands of the adventurers of the Alliance and Horde during the Cataclysm era.
Felsoul Hold:
Felsoul Hold is the name of a base of operations of the Burning Legion in the southwestern region of Suramar. The demon Azoran was leading the operations there and planned to use the Legion ship stationed there, the Lightbreaker, to destroy Dalaran. A soul engine was used to power the ship.
At one point, the Order of the Silver Hand sent here their troops to dispose of the giant infernals and felbats who attacked any who come near, and to collect the blood of the demons for their own use. The Valarjar forces also investigated to steal a Legion gateway and eventually encountered Doomlord Vrazzik and his demons. The portal was ultimately not suitable for their plans.
After he was captured and impersonated by Detheroc, Mathias Shaw was held captive at the hold. When the Uncrowned found him, they called on Marin Noggenfogger to create an explosive diversion for the Last Shadow and Taoshi to save the spymaster from his demonic jailer, Vaultwarden Umbra.
Years later, Felsoul Hold was in the process of being restored by druids. While mostly still barren rock, patches of plantlife have started to return. Deep inside Felsoul Hold was a still-working soul engine where Legion holdouts led by Sarothar remained active and were trying to begin another invasion.
It is presumably named after Varedis Felsoul.
Felstone Field:
Felstone Field is located in northwestern Western Plaguelands. Originally, the area had been a life-sustaining farm, but it was overrun by the vile Scourge. In their quest to destroy the living, they placed a large cauldron in the middle of the field which constantly spewed disease-filled vapors into the air. The cauldron itself was protected by Cauldron Lord Bilemaw, Skeletal Sorcerers, Skeletal Flayers and Slavering Ghouls.
A Scarlet Crusader party was also detected in Felstone and would destroy both players and Scourge with equal vengeance.
Inside the house in the northeastern corner of the field was a friendly NPC, Janice Felstone, who offered a quest.
Feltotem:
Feltotem is a village found on the Rockaway Coast in western Highmountain, serving as headquarters for the Feltotem tribe. The Lair of the Devout is inside.
Navarrogg led an attack on Feltotem with adventurers to kill the corruptors creating fel totems. They also found Tugar Bloodtotem and a Fel Infused Worm.
After the Feltotem kidnapped some of their allies, the champions of the Unseen Path attacked Dreadhoof and his forces to teach them a lesson.
During Legion Assaults, the corrupted tribe imprisoned Highmountain tauren and Norgabbon of Stonedark, seeking to conscript them into their ranks.
Felwood:
Felwood is a corrupted forest filled with tainted creatures of the woods, demonic satyr and infernals, and rotting treants and ancients. It is located in Northern Kalimdor, north of Ashenvale, east of Darkshore, and west of Mount Hyjal and Winterspring.
Once a serene forest and a part of northern Ashenvale, it was corrupted by the dreadlord Tichondrius and the Skull of Gul'dan during the Third War, and its healing has been very slow over the recent years. The Emerald Circle, a sub-section of the Cenarion Circle druids, have been working to heal the land and defeat the remaining demons that corrupt it, specifically the remaining Shadow Council forces led by Lord Banehollow. It is also home to one of the two tribes of pure furbolgs left in the world — the Timbermaw tribe. There are no dungeons or battlegrounds of any kind in this area.
Fenris Keep:
The gloomy Fenris Keep lays at the center of Lordamere Lake in Silverpine Forest upon the Fenris Isle. The keep had strategic significance, and was home to a sizable portion of Lordaeron's military. During the Fourth War, after the Battle for Lordaeron, it was contested between the Alliance and the Horde, but the Bloodfang Pack managed to reclaim it from the Forsaken.
The Scarlet Crusade during the events of Dragonflight managed to take control of the isle and its keep, but they were swiftly driven out by the Forsaken.
Feral Scar:
The Feral Scar is a tribe of yetis living in Feralas. Their leader is also named Feral Scar.
In the past, several Feral Scar yetis fought against Varian Wrynn in Dire Maul.
Since the Cataclysm, the Feral Scar yetis flourished and their hide was thought to have become stronger compared to several years ago.
Feralfen Village: Feralfen Village is the village of the Feralfen Lost One tribe in southern Zangarmarsh and built around the Boha'mu Ruins. It is located south of the Twin Spire Ruins. The Lost Ones have turned to the worship of animal spirits and are primarily hostile. A series of quests from Telredor has adventurers, under the guise of an arakkoa, try to convert them back to the Holy Light. Despite their superstitious and primitive nature, they are not stupid, so these efforts may fail.
Fire Camp Bataar:
Fire Camp Bataar can be found in the Yaungol Advance of south-central Kun-Lai Summit, in between Westwind Rest, Eastwind Rest, and the Chow Farmstead, just to the northeast of the great gate to the Vale of Eternal Blossoms.
After two months, Garrosh retook the camp and made a Horde camp there.

 This section concerns content related to Battle for Azeroth.
During the rise of N'Zoth, abandoned ale kegs were found here. They were recovered and delivered to Chen Stormstout.
Fire Camp Ordo:
Fire Camp Ordo can be found between the Kota Basecamp, Firebough Nook, and Westwind Rest in the northwestern reaches of the Yaungol Advance in south-central Kun-Lai Summit. The Ordo tribe of yaungol is led by the Ordo Warbringer who is protected by a shield cast by a blazecaster, embercaller, firespeaker, and a pyromancer. Once the fourth fire yaungol is dead, the warbringer's shield drops and can be attacked.
Like in several other yaungol fire camps, mobile oil derricks can be found there.
Fire Camp Osul:
Fire Camp Osul is home to the Osul tribe of yaungol. Found just southwest of the Ox Gate bordering Kun-Lai Summit, Jung Duk leads the Osul. Lin Silentstrike was captured back during  [20-35] Finish This! and can be found here as well. The Shado-Pan have claimed Longying Outpost, which is just to the southeast. Like in several other yaungol fire camps, mobile oil derricks can be found there.
The totem Dominance, one of the objectives of the Pandaria exploration achievement  [The Song of the Yaungol], is found in the upper part of the mesa, not far from Battat and Urang.
The Fire Camp Osul Digsite here actually covers Fire Camp Osul and Fire Camp Gai-Cho.  It is a Mogu archaeology site.
Fire Camp Ruqin: Fire Camp Ruqin is home to the Ruqin tribe of yaungol in east-central Kun-Lai Summit. Immediately to the north is the Grummle Bazaar and the eastern end of the Burlap Trail, just southwest is Mogujia, Muskpaw Ranch is to the southeast, and Fire Camp Yongqi is the closest settlement to the east. Like in several other yaungol fire camps, mobile oil derricks can be found there.
Fire Camp Yongqi: Fire Camp Yongqi is the Yongqi tribe of yaungol settlement immediately to the south of the Temple of the White Tiger in eastern Kun-Lai Summit. What's left of Yinying Village is sandwiched between Yongqi and the temple, the Auburn Bluffs are to the east, and Lao & Son's Yakwash and Muskpaw Ranch are to the south. Like in several other yaungol fire camps, mobile oil derricks can be found there.
Fire Plume Ridge:
Fire Plume Ridge is the volcano in the center of Un'Goro Crater. Lava flows down the sides of the mountain, where fire elementals can be found. The strongest of all fire elementals in Un'Goro, Blazerunner, lives within a cave at its peak.
The fiery mountain forms a natural border where the jungle meets the earth, scorched from lava flows. Shallow veins of magma flow beneath the bowl of the crater, heating the steam pools and geysers around Un'Goro.
The hottest place in the ridge is apparently 428,000 degrees Kraklenheit.
Ringo came to the ridge to explore and ended up getting lost and now suffers from heat exhaustion, he can be found in the southern cave.
After the Fourth War, Zekhan reported that the volcano continues to teem with elementals and wildlife. The spirits of fire told him that they have been burning here for centuries, petering out and reigniting over and over again. Zekhan would like to take Queen Talanji here one day if she'd agree, to keep up good relations between the Darkspear and the Zandalari.
Firebeard's Patrol: Firebeard's Patrol is a Wildhammer town located in the Devouring Breach of the Twilight Highlands. It is the home of the Firebeard clan of dwarves led by Keegan Firebeard. The nearby Firebeard Cemetery is located to the west.
Firebough Nook:
Firebough Nook was a small pandaren settlement nestled in the shadow of the Serpent's Spine in the southwest corner of Kun-Lai Summit. The Sha of Anger has come through, infesting nearby yaungol under the command of Kobai, leaving behind Blind Rage, and utterly destroying the village.
The sha-infested yaungol are also attacking the Shado-Pan Fallback of the Serpent's Spine, which is where Shado-Master Chong is trying to rally a desperate defense of the position, looking for help from the Shado-Pan Monastery which has not been coming.
Firegut:
The Firegut ogres of the Burning Steppes are allies of the Blackrock orcs. They work closely with those orcs, keeping the mineral rich Dreadmaul Rock guarded and the supply lines open at all times.
For a short time they were led by Gor'tesh until he was killed. Gorlop leads the clan currently... until he fell into lava.
All Firegut ogre mobs have  [Flamestrike] as a racial ability.
Firelands: The Firelands (referred to as the Elemental Plane of Fire or just Plane of Fire) is one of the four interlinked domains within the Elemental Plane. It was created eons ago by the titan-forged for the purpose of imprisoning most of Azeroth's fire elementals.
Firewalker Ruins: The Firewalker Ruins  are on the first rise of the Firewalkers' Path on the southeastern side of Timeless Isle. The ruins are above the Red Stone Run to the north and the Croaking Hollow to the east.
Firewing Point:
Firewing Point is an outpost maintained by Kael'thas Sunstrider's blood elves in northeastern Terokkar Forest.  In the courtyard of this outpost is a mana bomb similar to one found at the nearby Cenarion Thicket and set off by Kael's forces at Kirin'Var Village in what is now Netherstorm. The final code to set off the bomb is held by a Blood Knight named Sharth Voldoun, who resides at the top of the tower high above the courtyard.
The Blood Elves at Firewing Point wear Firewing Signets which allies of the Scryers in nearby Shattrath City can collect to enhance their reputation.
First Legion Forward Camp:
The First Legion Forward Camp is located south of the Bombardment in Icecrown.
The camp is a former base of Arthas and his men of the 1st Legion, prior to his corruption. This base may be the first time he openly fought and killed his own men.
The Forward Camp was a small base, consisting of a unit of Lordaeron Footsoldiers, their captain and several ballistae.
First Ones:
The First Ones (also known as the Progenitors) are enigmatic godlike beings who shaped the cosmos and the fabric of all realities. They conceived and put in place the six governing forces of reality—Light, Void, Order, Disorder, Life, and Death—as well as the pantheons that embody them—such as the Pantheon of Order and Pantheon of Death—and the realms that they inhabit. According to one interpretation, the First Ones and the cosmic forces themselves are to some extent synonymous.
The First Ones are shrouded in mystery, and very little is known for certain about them: it is unknown when they first walked the cosmos, whether they still do, or if their existence ended ages ago. They have long been absent even from Zereth Mortis, their workshop realm in the Shadowlands; the broker Firim believes that perhaps they are interred in the Sepulcher of the First Ones, or perhaps they simply went "elsewhere".
The First Ones' magic and architecture are so advanced that they resemble mathematics, and are characterized by geometric fractals and patterns. They and their servants—the automa—speak a complex runic language that is incomprehensible to most mortals. One of their recurring symbols is that of a coiled serpent, which is believed by broker scholars to be a representation of "their infinite cycle".
Fissure:
The Fissure is the seedy underbelly of Dornogal, found in the eastern corner of the city. Various types of trade appear to take place here, from barbershop services to the illicit dealings of Steelvein. A few outsiders have also established themselves, including Madam Goya of the Black Market Auction House and Griftah. Several displaced rogues from Dalaran have gathered near the back of the Fissure with some of their remaining possessions.
The Forgegrounds lie to the southwest, and there's an entrance to the Corridors leading north to the Stoneshaper's Atrium. After  [78-80] Uniting Severed Threads is completed, a tunnel to the Weaver's Lair becomes available at the back of the Fissure.
Fizzcrank Airstrip: Fizzcrank Airstrip is a gnome base in northern Borean Tundra, which overlooks the Geyser Fields. The airstrip rings with the sounds of hammer on anvil morning through night, though half the time one can barely hear them over the gnomish flying machines taking off. A hydrothermal system underlies the area around the airstrip, which connects it to the geyser fields to the southeast, where the gnomes built the Fizzcrank Pumping Station, an oil platform used to make fuel for their flying machines, until the mechagnomes took control of it. Several gnomish bombers and flying machines are stationed there.
Fizzle & Pozzik's Speedbarge:
Fizzle & Pozzik's Speedbarge looks like a massive, city-sized ship and an artificial island located on the Shimmering Deep in Thousand Needles. Although the barge is named after its leaders, Fizzle Brassbolts and Pozzik, Jinky Twizzlefixxit and Razzeric separately believe that the ship should have been named after themselves: after all, they built it.
Lorewise, a ship leaves for Gadgetzan every day.
It is a place where goblin and gnome engineers compete, free of the tensions abroad.
Flame Crest: Flame Crest is a Horde outpost in the Burning Steppes. It is located on a small outcropping of rock, only accessible by crossing a crude bridge. There is a small cave in the back where Kibler lives with the talkative parrot Opus. Eitrigg and Ariok used the outpost as their base of operations when planning an attack against the Blackrock clan. Before the Cataclysm, the outpost was neutral.
Flamestar Post:
Flamestar Post is located immediately south of the bridge leading to Blackrock Mountain in the Burning Steppes.  It is a small camp run by the Thorium Brotherhood and serves as the first quest hub for those entering the Burning Steppes.  While here, adventurers help start a plan to fight back against the Blackrock orcs.  
It contains a flight path and an Adventure Board leading Horde players into Blackrock Depths.
Fleshwerks:
The Fleshwerks is a large facility of the Scourge which is dedicated to the creation of abominations and flesh giants. It is located high above the Avalanche that rumbled down into Sholazar Basin. Even for a place controlled by the Scourge it is disgusting, with poison and plague bubbles everywhere, and undead fleshripper birds circle. The Fleshwerks consists of several different areas, a flesh giant lab named the Sanctum of Reanimation, and an abomination lab with a cauldron area and a summoning area.
The Blackwatch is the quest hub of this area, used by both the Knights of the Ebon Blade and the Argent Crusade as a base of operations to shut down the Fleshwerks, in order to deprive the Lich King of a large component of his armies.
Fletcher's Hollow: Fletcher's Hollow is a village in eastern Drustvar. It features several buildings, including the Rusty Bucket Tavern, Ladd's Boat Rental, and Deals for Wheels.
Flotsam Shoal: Flotsam Shoal is the makeshift base of operations for the expedition from Khaz Algar consisting of the Hallowfall Arathi, Dornogal earthen, and Gazlowe's Greasemonkeys found in the eastern part of Siren Isle.
Fordragon Hold: Fordragon Hold is an Alliance fortress at the base of Angrathar the Wrathgate, the gate to Icecrown Citadel, in the northern regions of the Dragonblight. The hold is made up of several cannon towers and a guard tower. Highlord Bolvar Fordragon once commanded the Alliance forces from this fortress. Its Horde equivalent is the Kor'kron Vanguard.
Forest Hozen: The Grookin tribe, also known as the Forest Hozen, are a group of hozen living in the Jade Forest. They find themselves allied with the Horde after the Horde gains their favor by rescuing some of their members, sating their appetite for fish, and killing some of their most fearsome enemies. They are enemies of the Pearlfin Jinyu.
Forest Song: Forest Song is an ancient night elf ruin located in northeastern Ashenvale, just northeast of Satyrnaar, north of the Warsong Lumber Camp, and southwest of Bough Shadow. Once almost abandoned, Forest Song is currently inhabited by night elves and draenei from the Exodar, who are building an outpost there to help the Silverwing Sentinels defend the forests from the Warsong clan and the Burning Legion remnants.
Forge of Afterlives: The Forge of Afterlives is a massive structure floating at the center of Zereth Mortis. As the name implies, it is responsible for creating new realms of the Shadowlands. When Maw Walkers arrive to Zereth Mortis, the Forge is in the process of putting together one such new afterlife.
Forgefire Outpost: Forgefire Outpost is located next to Nemea's Retreat in the Golden Pasture in Bastion. It is the workshop of Pelodis. A Discarded Centurion Core can be found here.
Forgegrounds:
The Forgegrounds  serves as the profession quarter of Dornogal, found in the southeastern corner of the city. The Coreway lies to the west, the Fissure to the northeast, and Foundation Hall is found to the north.
The Trading Post, Catalyst, Stable Master, and Rostrum of Transformation are found within, and the city's flight master is just to the north.
Forgotten Vault (Siren Isle):
The Forgotten Vault is accessed by interacting with the Singing Tablet at  in the Sacred Hollow of Siren Isle.
In the normal phase, two rares spawn: Gunnlod the Sea-Drinker and Shardsong.
In the  [Seafury Tempest] phase, Ksvir the Forgotten spawns, who drops the  [Whirling Runekey]. Also in the storm phase is the corpse of Thrayir, Eyes of the Siren and five runestones, which reward the  [Thrayir, Eyes of the Siren] mount.
Forkriver Crossing: Forkriver Crossing is a small Maruuk Centaur trading village in south eastern Ohn'ahran Plains.
Forlorn Hut: The Forlorn Hut is a pandaren crafted hut built in the Pei-Wu Forest by Wei Palerage. Many of the Horde survivors from the Skyseeker crash ended up here. Several crewmen are injured, while others are quickly gathering up bamboos in order to craft crude weapons. Horde druids are also trying to heal the wounded.
Forlorn Ruins: Forlorn Ruins is a set of ruins taken over by the Gob Squad in Nazmir.
Forsaken:
The undead Forsaken (or simply the Forsaken or Undead) are a race and a faction of intelligent undead who broke away from the Scourge after the Third War. Under the command of Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, these free-willed undead took control of much of the ruins of Lordaeron, and founded their own kingdom in the royal catacombs of the Undercity beneath the ruins of Capital City. Convinced that the races of the Horde could help them accomplish their objectives, the Forsaken entered an alliance of convenience to achieve victory over the Lich King Arthas Menethil in Northrend.
Although the Forsaken ranks consist of undead individuals from different races, they have all assumed their racial identity as "Forsaken," due to their shared goals and loyalties.
During the Fourth War, Sylvanas Windrunner unleashed the plague upon the Undercity rather than allow the Alliance to capture it, before ultimately abandoning the Horde. In the aftermath, Lilian Voss assumed the role of the Forsaken's representative on the Horde Council. She later joined other surviving Forsaken leaders to establish the Desolate Council and reclaim the Ruins of Lordaeron for their people.
Forsaken (kingdom):
The Forsaken kingdom is an undead nation, also referred to as an undead empire, founded by the Forsaken in the ruins of the fallen human kingdom of Lordaeron. Under the command of the Banshee Queen Sylvanas Windrunner, the Forsaken freed themselves of the Lich King's control after the Third War and settled in the Undercity, where they founded a powerful society devoted to the Dark Lady. Knowing that no human nation would offer them shelter or aid against the Scourge, now their most hated enemy, they turned to the Horde of Kalimdor for assistance in exchange for an invaluable foothold in the Eastern Kingdoms.
Though the Forsaken finally took vengeance upon Arthas Menethil in Northrend, the betrayal of Grand Apothecary Putress at the Wrathgate and the coup d'état of Varimathras in the Undercity proved costly for the kingdom, leaving them mistrusted by the other members of the Horde. In order to prove their loyalty to the cause and redeem themselves from their supposed treachery, the Banshee Queen launched a military campaign to secure the Forsaken's hold over Lordaeron and pledged her forces to support Warchief Garrosh Hellscream in his intercontinental war against the Alliance.
During the Fourth War, the Undercity was plagued to prevent its capture by the Alliance in the battle for Lordaeron, while the refugees were evacuated to Orgrimmar. After Sylvanas abandoned the Horde, Lilian Voss and several figures of the Forsaken gathered in the Tirisfal Glades to reclaim the Ruins of Lordaeron, then united as the Desolate Council, ready to lead their people towards their new destiny.
Forsaken Forward Command: Forsaken Forward Command was the main Horde outpost in the Ruins of Gilneas, located right along the Greymane Wall in the Northern Headlands, extending from the gate in all directions into the peninsula.
Forsaken Front: The Forsaken Front is an outpost and front lines to the Battlefront in southern Silverpine Forest. It's here Lady Sylvanas commands the attack on the Gilneas Liberation Front and where she had Lord Godfrey, Walden, and Baron Ashbury raised into her service.
Forsaken High Command:
Forsaken High Command, part of the Forsaken Front, is a subzone of Silverpine Forest and is the first quest hub players will run across after their adventures in Tirisfal Glades. The entire series of phased quests for the zone begins here with none other than Lady Sylvanas Windrunner personally overseeing the effort to rekindle the Forsaken as a race.
During  [5-30] The Warchief Cometh, Garrosh Hellscream and High Warlord Cromush make an appearance here. You will need to complete this in order to make the flightmaster and other vendors appear.
On the way here from Tirisfal Glades, players will witness Dreadguards marching up and down the zone as well as pass by Forsaken Troopers and Forsaken Apothecaries preparing for battle with Gilneas. After Garrosh and his troops leave, the area is phased, with Cromush left behind, the Forsaken troops battling Worgen Renegades, and the rest of the NPCs (flight master, quest givers, etc.) appearing in the zone.
Forsaken Rear Guard:
Forsaken Rear Guard is a Forsaken base located between Forsaken High Command and the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. A large contingent of Orgrimmar sea forces has recently arrived here, and they appear to enjoy their alcohol. Orc Sea Dogs can be found throughout the area.
Before the Shattering the area was known as the Dead Field.
Forsworn: The Forsworn, also known as the Dark Kyrian, are Kyrian Aspirants that failed to complete a rite of passage. These once-bright aspirants darken and become lost, wandering the plains of Bastion to lament. Containing the Forsworn is the key, for if left unchecked, doubt can spread like a disease.
Fort Daelin:
Fort Daelin is a star fort in western Stormsong Valley, named after Daelin Proudmoore and home to the Proudmoore Battalion. 
It was under siege by the naga, with brutes pummeling the stone walls as harpoons drove further into the walls.
Fort Livingston:
Fort Livingston is a new Alliance camp in Northern Stranglethorn.
During the war against the Zandalari, the place was attacked by Jungle Serpents, and its inhabitants were poisoned.
Fort Triumph: Fort Triumph was an Alliance military stronghold located in the central Southern Barrens. It stood on the eastern side of the Battlescar, and was in constant conflict with the Horde outpost at Desolation Hold across the gorge. Fort Triumph was vital to the Alliance's continued expansion into the Barrens during the Cataclysm, and represented their most fortified presence in the region outside Northwatch Hold. The fort was eventually looted and razed in the lead-up to the Battle of Theramore by a massive Horde army, though recent efforts have been made to re-establish the position.
Fort Victory: Fort Victory was an Alliance outpost founded in the swamps of Nazmir during the Fourth War.
Fort Wildervar: Fort Wildervar is the Alliance's northernmost outpost in Howling Fjord. Founded by the Valiance Expedition at the base of Frostblade Peak, on the banks of Caldemere Lake, Its purpose was to provide the necessary equipment and resources for Alliance expeditions advancing toward the Grizzly Hills. It also acts as an arrival point for human colonists intending to settle across Northrend.
Fort Wrynn:
Fort Wrynn is the main Alliance base in Talador, located in the northeastern part of the region, north of Vol'jin's Pride.
The only major building in this outpost is decided by the commander, which is either Wrynn Artillery Tower or an Arcane Sanctum. Before a choice is made, the space is occupied by Fort Wrynn Worksite. There is a command table in these buildings for completing and starting new garrison missions.
The units of the Fort Wrynn garrison were first encountered when they assisted the draenei to fight the orcs that invaded Karabor.
Forward Camp:
The Forward Camp is a small Devoted sethrak camp directly northeast of the Terrace of the Devoted in Vol'dun. Some of the Devoted from the terrace tried to get ahead of the Faithless siege by attacking the Faithless' nearby Temple Incursion in the dead of night. However, the Faithless knew that they were coming, and many of the defenders were captured.
During Faction Assaults on Vol'dun, a portion of the camp becomes a battlefield between the Horde and the Alliance from which Lasan Skyhorn sends Aviash and the Horde adventurer to the Alliance Airship.
Forward Command:
Forward Command is an Alliance outpost in eastern part of the Fields of Blood in the Southern Barrens under the command of General Hawthorne. 
When the Horde began their march against the Northwatch Hold, Kalecgos noticed that the command was abandoned, presumably having gone to help Northwatch. Those who survived in Northwatch would eventually regroup in Fort Triumph. Later on, however, Fort Triumph also fell, so it is unknown whether there are any survivors or not.
Foundation Hall: Foundation Hall  is the capitol building of Dornogal, located in the northwestern corner of the city. Thraegar Rest is to the southwest, Keepers Terrace is to the northwest, Stoneshaper's Atrium is to the east, and Stoneward's Rise is to the northeast. Portals to Stormwind and Orgrimmar can be found here, there is also a teleporter on the ground floor that leads to the top of the tower.
Fray Island: Fray Island is a small arid island located off the eastern shore of the Northern Barrens. A small sewer stretches the length of the island and players diving into it will be able to find several hostile fish.
Frazzlecraz Motherlode: Frazzlecraz Motherlode is a Horde goblin mining operation found near the quilboar in the Southern Barrens, just west of Bael Modan. After discovering his son's death, destruction of his keep, and a goblin corpse at the scene of the crime, General Twinbraid believed that the Horde was responsible for Bael Modan's destruction. As the new military leader in the Southern Barrens, he plans to destroy the mine and annihilate its workers to get revenge.
Freehold: Freehold is pirate port town located in southern Tiragarde Sound. Unlike the Kul Tiran capital of Boralus, Freehold is a "free people's port": it has no rules or regulations about what vessels are allowed to dock. It is a lawless haven for local pirates, criminals, privateers, and mercenaries. One can get anything they want in Freehold, provided that they pay for it, in gold or steel.
Freewind Post:
Freewind Post is a Horde town located high on a mesa in Thousand Needles. Tauren settlements in Thousand Needles are constructed atop the tall mesas in the region, staying out of reach of the centaur warbands that have several camps in the area. The village on the mesa's top is accessible by the employment of the ingenious wooden lifts of the tauren, although there is a series of rope bridges spanning amongst the adjacent pinnacles, gradually working their way to the top.
The tauren of Freewind Post work to stop the activity of the Galak tribe centaur in Thousand Needles. Screeching harpies pose a less dire threat to the stability of the region as well. Another large aspect of the society of Freewind Post deals with the wyverns of Highperch, where young tauren are sent to study the wyverns and to cull eggs from their ancestral nesting grounds to be raised as mounts for the Horde.
The Horde-aligned tauren of Freewind Post grew continually more wary of the activities of the Grimtotem tribe situated atop Darkcloud Pinnacle to the northwest. The Grimtotems had been suspected to be involved in murder, kidnappings of Freewind tauren, and visits from agents of unknown (but reportedly dark) origins. The chieftain of Darkcloud Pinnacle, Arnak Grimtotem, was largely held to be responsible for these heinous transgressions. A Freewind Post tauren, Lakota Windsong, was taken against her will when she refused Arnak's advances. Her brother was slain when he came to her defense. She is also apparently close friends with Thalia Amberhide.
Closely related to the problems with the Grimtotem was the concern surrounding a so-called "Alien Egg" that was rumored to have appeared near the nests of the Needles' resident wind serpents. The Grimtotem had given supplication to the creature that hatched from the egg, Arikara, Serpent of Vengeance, in hopes that it would aid them in their mission to depose Cairne Bloodhoof as punishment for his changes to tauren culture and tradition.
A blood elf presence appeared in Freewind Post in the form of Magistrix Elosai, who was effectively an exile of Silvermoon. Her controversial quest to seek a natural cure to the blood elves' racial addiction to the arcane led her to Freewind seeking reagents to use in her remedies, along with help from her associate, Wizlo Bearingshiner at Whitereach Post.
By the time Cairne died, the Grimtotem attacked the post, but the attack was repelled. Its warriors aided Baine in retaking Thunder Bluff.
Freewind Post was taken by the Grimtotem tribe during the Cataclysm. At the base of the Post is a small group of tauren and night elves who are apparently are working in conjunction to drive away the Grimtotems.
At some point, Freewind has been liberated once more by tauren and quilboar alike, who've united against the Grimtotem to retake their home. The town is currently populated by both races, who are very friendly to outsiders and open to trading, while Elmarine keeps the peace. Unfortunately, Freewind suffers from frequent harpy attacks after sundown, occurring once every three or four nights.
During the Burning Legion's third invasion, the bridge connecting Freewind Post and Darkcloud Pinnacle was barricaded with fel spikes by demons.
After the Fourth War, Zekhan reported that the Horde controls Freewind Post. Whether the quilboar and Elmarine remain in the town is unknown.
Frenzyheart Hill:
Frenzyheart Hill is the village of the Frenzyheart Tribe of wolvar in Sholazar Basin. It is a village of their typical low, round dwellings atop a hill that's been named after them. They founded it in the region after being driven from their lands by the Scourge, prior to the war against the Lich King.
Following the war against the Jailer, the brothers Bronzebeard visited Frenzyheart Hill and the wolvar there were happy to see Brann among them, as they welcomed him like a long-lost friend, and even more remarkable, they joked with him about also being friends with their sworn enemies, the Oracles. They welcomed the group to their fire and told them about their story over a delicious meal of roast crocolisk.
Frenzyheart Tribe: The Frenzyheart Tribe faction is a primitive tribe of wolvars located in Sholazar Basin.
Freywold Village:
Freywold Village  is the home of the Unbound earthen located in the southwestern part of the Isle of Dorn. The Earthcrawl Mines delve is at  just to the west, the Orecreg is northwest, the Opalcreg is northeast, Boskroot Basin is to the east, the Glimmering Shore lies to the southeast, and Dhar Durgaz is atop the mountain to the south.
Players are initially directed here for  [70-73] The Fourth Seat in the Isle of Dorn storyline.
Frigid Breach: Frigid Breach is area filled with Drakkari trolls in Zul'Drak. It's located north-east of Voltarus and is a new Drakkari front against the scourge. Following orders from the Ebon Blade, adventurers infiltrated the Scourge, and Drakuru asked to use abominations to kill Drakkari warriors and capture chieftains.[citation needed]
Frostborn:
The Frostborn (also spelled the frostborn, sometimes spelled frostborne and also known as frost dwarves, and Frostborn dwarves) are a race and a faction of dwarves native to the Storm Peaks. They have recently befriended members of the Explorers' League, and although they have differences with their dwarven brethren, they welcome Alliance members within their settlements.
They were led by Yorg Stormheart, "King of the Frostborn", who ruled over them from the mighty Frosthold in the Storm Peaks. This changed when Yorg recovered his memories, which he had lost some years back, and remembered that he was Muradin Bronzebeard, a dwarf from the Bronzebeard clan of Ironforge. After the war against the Lich King, Muradin decided to return home with his brothers, so he left Velog Icebellow in charge of the leadership of the frostborn in his absence.
Frosthold:
Frosthold is an Alliance town aligned with the Frostborn in southwestern Storm Peaks, south of the Temple of Storms and northwest of K3, on the same mountain as Stormcrest. It is home to the whole frost dwarf race. The settlement is located in and around a large pit of ice atop a massive mountain. There is no accessible method of reaching Frosthold from foot; requiring one to fly. From depictions within World of Warcraft: Exploring Azeroth: Northrend, and the fact that none of the buildings are accessible in game, it appears there is a larger city present within the mountain that is simply inaccessible to players; similar to Aerie Peak.
Following the war against the Jailer, the brothers Bronzebeard came to Frosthold, where the Frostborn were glad to see Muradin Bronzebeard. After the presentations and a feast, they spent the night drinking and sharing stories. During the night, Muradin told Velog that he had no doubt he left the Frostborn in the right hands, and with the help of the historian of Frosthold, he learned the story of the meeting between Mina Stormsmith and the Frostborn, 500 years ago.
Frostmane Hold:
Frostmane Hold was once the base camp of the Frostmane ice trolls located in the western edge of the cold mountains of Dun Morogh south of Gnomeregan and New Tinkertown. The hold is comprised of a few buildings and a cave system. The Cataclysm tore open deep caves beneath the Hold and as such allowed Rockjaw troggs to drive out the ice trolls, ruled by Boss Bruggor. The trolls who once resided here have fallen back to Frostmane Retreat.
Prior to the Cataclysm, young dwarves and gnomes were tasked to explore the caves and report back to Kharanos, in order to determine just how big a threat the trolls were. The area was heavily guarded by troll headhunters and hideskinners.
Now, Kharmarn Palegrip sends adventurers to deal with the troggs, including rescuing a number of captured gnomes. In   [1-30] Finishin' the Job, he orders to detonate explosives intended to collapse the tunnel through which the troggs arrived in order to stop their advance.
Frostmane Hovel: Frostmane Hovel is a cave located in the south of Coldridge Valley in Dun Morogh. Frostmane trolls have been present in the cave since the Cataclysm, with Grik'nir the Cold at their head. The adventurer is sent by Grelin Whitebeard to kill Grik'nir and a Wayward Fire Elemental who helps the trolls.
Frostmane Retreat:
Frostmane Retreat is an ice troll village found in Dun Morogh, located between Kharanos and the Tundrid Hills.
During the Cataclysm, dwarves of Ironforge with the aid of Gnomeregan Covert Ops managed to push toward the Retreat, preparing to attack it. Alliance forces consisting of adventurers and flying machines entered the area, fought Battok the Berserker and his warriors, and shrunk builders working on the construction of the village. Eventually, the Alliance mission was successful, with trolls's numbers being lowered.

 This section concerns content related to Legion.
During the Legion Invasions, the area was invaded by the demons.
Frostmane tribe: The Frostmane tribe (or clan) are a tribe of ice trolls that inhabit Dun Morogh and constantly fight a guerrilla war against the dwarves of Ironforge. In recent times, they have welcomed the trogg invasion of the dwarven lands, and are content to let the two sides fight it out whilst they sit and wait for an opportunistic moment to take back their lands. They can be found throughout Dun Morogh, notably in Shimmer Ridge, Frostmane Retreat and Frostmane Hovel. Their former capital, Frostmane Hold, was recently taken over by the troggs.
Frostwall:
Frostwall is the Horde Garrison, located in Frostfire Ridge. A fully-upgraded Frostwall garrison is considered to be a fortress.
The Alliance counterpart is Lunarfall, located in Shadowmoon Valley.
Following the end of the war in Draenor, the garrison was abandoned.
Frostwolf Orcs:
The Frostwolf Orcs, or Frostwolf clan, are renowned for their prowess as one-on-one combatants. Once led by Chieftain Durotan in alternate Draenor, they are a strong, close-knit clan whose bond with wolves only adds to their strength—though their numbers remain smaller than most clans. Though the clan spends much of their time in Frostfire Ridge, they migrate to Nagrand with the seasons.
They have since joined the Mag'har Clans and pledged their loyalty to the Horde after their arrival on Azeroth.
Fungal Rock: Fungal Rock is a large cavern in the northeastern wall of Un'Goro Crater. The cavern is filled with gorillas, which have made their home, and Ghost Mushrooms. Outside the entrance is a small pool of water with a waterfall, this is where A-Me 01, Karna Remtravel's mechanical ape can be found.
Furbolg:
Furbolgs are a hulking, simple-minded race of bear-men who live in the northern regions of Kalimdor, in the continent of Northrend, in the Broken Isles, in the Dragon Isles, and in the Verdant Wilds island.
Though they have no special love for war or murder, their tribes have become increasingly hostile as of late, many tribes have fallen to multiple forms of corruption, including but not limited to the corruptions of the Burning Legion, the Old Gods and the Primalists. Some tribes and individuals aren't hostile and are tolerant of outsiders, with tribes such as the Timbermaw, Stillpine, and Longclaw.
In northern Kalimdor, the furbolgs were old allies of the night elves. The night elves, concerned by the once peaceful race's condition, have attempted to help the furbolgs settle their tensions, but the mighty bear-men retreat ever further into their territories and fall deeper into the rage that is overtaking their race, they turned into fearsome new enemies of the night elves.
Furlbrow's Pumpkin Farm:
The Furlbrow's Pumpkin Farm (formerly known as Furlbrow's Pumpkin Patch) was one of the many farms in Westfall taken over by the Defias Brotherhood and their mechanical harvest golems. The killing machines used to patrol the fields before the Cataclysm, with the Defias taking up residence in the farm buildings. Farmer Furlbrow and his wife Verna fled during that time to the road near the Jansen Stead in northern Westfall.
After the Cataclysm, the Furlbrows have apparently met an untimely demise near the Jansen Stead, their deaths currently under investigation. Their farm was claimed by the Homeless Stormwind Citizens, Transients and similar individuals who can be found throughout the area. The farm also gained a flight path.
During the Burning Legion's invasion, the area falls under the Legion's control. Its residents are enslaved by nathrezim and are later killed by the defenders.
G'huun:
G'huun (/ɡə.ˈhuːn/ gə-HOON) was an Old God inadvertently created by the Pantheon of Order during their experiments on the other imprisoned Old Gods, as the titans tried to find a solution to the problem that they posed. Worshiped by the blood trolls of Nazmir as a loa, G'huun was known as the Blood God. Though it was quite less powerful than the other Old Gods, the threat it posed was still world-ending. G'huun's corruption was called "underrot". It sought to spread its rot, pestilence and decay across the world and beyond, and to consume Azeroth in the process.
G'huun is one of the main antagonists on Zandalar in Battle for Azeroth, and serves as the final boss of the Uldir raid.
Gadgetzan:
Rising out of the northern Tanaris desert, Gadgetzan is the capital city of the Steamwheedle Cartel, the largest of the goblin cartels. The city was once surrounded by desert, but since the Cataclysm Gadgetzan was converted from a busy goblin city into a busy beachfront capital.
Some of the best goblin engineers, miners, and alchemists ply their trade here. The goblins believe in profit above loyalty, thus Gadgetzan is considered neutral territory in any Horde-Alliance conflict. Anyone with a fat wallet or services to offer is welcomed in Gadgetzan. Both governments officially recognize goblin neutrality, and for those who don't, the streets are heavily patrolled by goblin bruisers ready to pound to a pulp anyone disrupting their trade by instigating conflict.
The city boasts many features including a port for all factions, but also with a blanket of black fumes hanging over the city.
Gahrron's Withering:
Gahrron's Withering is an abandoned farmstead located at the eastern end of the Western Plaguelands. Formerly known as Gahrron's Quickening, the farm has been taken over by the Scourge. They have placed a large cauldron in the middle of the field which constantly spews disease-filled vapors into the air. The cauldron is guarded by Cauldron Lord Soulwrath and other Scourge officers. Haunting Visions and many Wailing Deaths and Hungering Wraiths. Gahrron's Withering is a popular place for grinding Argent Dawn reputation, as the quest involving the Scourge Cauldron located here provides the best reputation of the four Cauldron quests.
Gahrron's Withering is the only farm of the four Target: Plague Cauldron quests given by High Priestess MacDonnell at Chillwind Camp that does not have additional quest givers in the area. It was once owned by Del Gahrron before the Scourge arrived. At the farm, the Alliance forces killed the corrupted Joseph Redpath. His shield remained there.
Galak tribe: The Galak centaur inhabit Thousand Needles. Their founding leader, or Khan, was Khan Veng, the fifth of the alleged offspring of Zaetar and Princess Theradras. They are currently ruled by no definitive Khan. The Galak hold no alliance with their brother tribes, but have been known to act both hostile and passive towards members of the Alliance and Horde.
Galen's Fall: Galen's Fall was a Forsaken camp along Thoradin's Wall near the entrance into the Hillsbrad Foothills from the Arathi Highlands.
Gallywix Docks:
Gallywix Docks is a port located in the northwest on the largest of the Lost Isles. These docks were taken from the Town-In-A-Box by the Trade Prince and placed in their current location on the island. By the time players reach the docks Gallywix has already had a new yacht built and ready to go.
This is where the final confrontation with Gallywix takes place.
Gammoth: Gammoth is area within the Bloodspore Plains in the Borean Tundra. It is the home of the magnataur Gammothra the Tormentor.
Gao-Ran Battlefront:
The Gao-Ran Battlefront comprises the eastern half of the southern border of Townlong Steppes with the Dread Wastes. Gao-Ran the Tempered has set up camp underneath the boughs of one of the great trees, which provides two natural choke points for mantid streaming north from the Dread Wastes: the battlefront itself and the Shallowstep Pass to the east. However, the constant streaming of mantid pouring in towards the chokepoints have been tiring the pandaren defenders both day and night and need the help of adventurers to push them back.  Immediately to the north is the Dampsoil Burrow, while further to the northeast is Hatred's Vice. The battlefront overlooks the Ambermarsh to the southwest, while the Dusklight Hollow is further along the path to the west.
Krik'thik Limbpincers are swarming up the actual battlefront, only to be blown up by dragon cannons used by cannoneers, shot by marksmen, frozen by magi, or killed by blackguards.
Garden Shrine: Garden Shrine is a drakonid and dragonspawn inhabited outpost in the south-west of Thaldraszus. It was originally a tea house for those traveling to Valdrakken but became a triage camp.
Garden of the Loa:
The Garden of the Loa is located in Zuldazar just west of Zanchul. It houses shrines dedicated to different loa. It was attacked by the followers of Zul who intended to kill the loa.
 [Tales of de Loa: Gonk] is found on the north bank of the river outside the main area of the garden. The Gift of the Brokenhearted can be found on a cliff to the east of the flight master by first lighting the incense found in the same location.
Garm herd: The Garm herd is a group that consists of a pride of magnataur led by Tormar Frostgut and their snobold servants found in and around Garm in the Storm Peaks. They are in conflict with the goblin town of K3.
Garrosh'ar Point:
Garrosh'ar Point was a Horde landing site in the Jade Forest led by Ga'trul. The outpost came under heavy assault from Alliance military led by the mighty airship The Skyfire when on a mission to search for Admiral Taylor and Anduin Wrynn.
By 40 ADP, the outpost was still found in ruins and abandoned, much to the relief of the local pandaren.
Garrosh's Landing:
Garrosh's Landing is a dock area on the western shore of Borean Tundra near Warsong Hold, where an orcish destroyer ship is moored, and the remains of a second ship can be seen nearby. There is a great hall and a watch tower, while the goblin Mobu once had a hut here. One part of the beach was made into a kennel.
Before they built up Warsong Hold, the Horde had Garrosh's Landing, named after Garrosh Hellscream since he led the fleet of Orcish destroyers that landed at the coast. They used it as their main port after they decided to build their fortress inland. About the time they marched the bulk of their forces off for the assault on Icecrown, the kvaldir attacked and nearly razed the buildings.
Around the time of Lich King's fall, the landing was retaken temporarily by the Horde, but when Cairne Bloodhoof and Garrosh Hellscream were taking some of their people back to Kalimdor, the kvaldir attacked again.
Following the war against the Jailer, the brothers Bronzebeard reported that the port still under the control of the kvaldir, and all they could see from a distance was mist and more mist.
Gate of the Setting Sun: The Gate of the Setting Sun is a dungeon in World of Warcraft: Mists of Pandaria. This is the gate of the Serpent's Spine, the great wall that is meant to isolate the mantid from the rest of Pandaria. Guarded by the Shado-Pan for the last 10,000 years, to their surprise the swarm of the mantid occurs ten years earlier than it is supposed to. The mantid have mustered an enormous army to lay siege to the Gate. If the Gates fall, the mantid will swarm through Pandaria, causing death and destruction. The dungeon is located within the Spine boundary between the Dread Wastes and the Vale of Eternal Blossoms.
Gates of Orgrimmar:
The Gates of Orgrimmar (or Orgrimmar Main Gate) is quite simply the main gateway into Orgrimmar. The area leads from the Dranosh'ar Blockade in Durotar to the Valley of Strength.
During the Siege of Orgrimmar one Blind Blademaster can be found guarding the tunnel, while Aysa Cloudsinger sneaks around behind him towards the Valley of Strength.
Following the Battle for Lordaeron, a sizable group of Forsaken refugees set up a camp on the upper portion of the Gates.
With patch 8.1.5, a new room known as the Pathfinder's Den was added to the gates housing all the portals to various parts of the world that had previously been scattered throughout Orgrimmar.
Sylvanas Windrunner-loyal Horde warriors gathered on the gate when Varok Saurfang, his rebels, and the Alliance, arrived at Dranosh'ar Blockade to breach them. They observed the mak'gora duel between Varok and Sylvanas. After the Banshee Queen killed the High Overlord and fled, the Forsaken banner-carriers stomped their banners in unison and respect as Thrall, Zekhan, and King Anduin Wrynn brought the body inside.
Gates of Sothann:
The Gates of Sothann is an area within the new Darkwhisper Gorge (it is technically just outside the borders of the original pre-Cataclysm gorge) that belonged to the Burning Legion, but was taken by force by the Twilight's Hammer. The cult then began to alter the landscape and build their structures when Garnoth, Fist of the Legion and his army slaughtered the cultist and took back which was theirs.
There is a lake with a small island that contains a gateway. This island is a quest hub and the gateway is a door to the Emerald Dream. Once opened, the defending forces (but not players) can "freely move between Moonglade, Nordrassil, and even Wyrmrest."  After completing  [30-35] Twilight Riot, Commander Jarod Shadowsong, Ysera, and Cenarius can be found here. The lake seems to be the source of the Southfury River.
After completing  [30-35] Slash and Burn, a cut scene will happen and the Guardians of Hyjal will appear and make the small island a forward outpost. The following NPCs will then appear.
Gazlowe's Greasemonkeys:
Gazlowe's Greasemonkeys are a Horde team that can be encountered on Island Expeditions as well as a group that goes to Mechagon Island. They can also be found idling in the Port of Zandalar along with the other teams.
Gazlowe created the Greasemonkeys to act in his stead when he is too busy to look into something himself.

 This section concerns content related to The War Within.
The Greasemonkeys were part of the expedition to the Siren Isle.
Gelikyr Post: Gelikyr Post is a drakonid and dragonspawn inhabited town in Thaldraszus. Across the bridge Primalists have taken over Gelikyr Overlook and are now trying to push into the town.
General Steelstrike: General Vaelisia Steelstrike is the leader of the Hallowfall Arathi and commander of their army. Having been placed in charge of the Hallowfall Expedition by the Emperor of the Arathi, her unyielding will has seen her people through the darkest of times.
Genn Greymane:
Genn Greymane (sometimes spelled as "Graymane") is the former reigning King of Gilneas, and one of the original founders of the Alliance of Lordaeron. He is a large bearish man, a brawny warrior with thick features, a heavy beard, and black and gray armor. Greymane has also been noted for being stubborn, proud, strong-willed, cunning, and arrogant.
During the Second War, Greymane met with the kings of the Seven Kingdoms at Capital City to hear of Stormwind's fall at the hands of the orcish Horde. Reluctantly, Greymane joined the other human leaders in forming the Alliance of Lordaeron to counter the invaders, but due to his pride, and for political and economic interests, he offered only token support. After the conclusion of the Second War, Greymane chafed at using Gilnean taxes to help pay for the orc internment camps and Nethergarde Keep. Following the liberation of the orcs from internment camps by the New Horde, Greymane decided that Gilneas could not and would not pay for the wars of other nations, so he withdrew Gilneas from the Alliance, ordered the construction of the Greymane Wall and isolated Gilneas from the rest of the world.
Around the time of the Third War, Greymane instructed Archmage Arugal, a Dalaran wizard loyal to Gilneas, to summon feral worgen to protect Gilneas from the Scourge threat. The plan backfired, and the worgen curse would eventually run rampant among the Gilnean population. In the following years, the number of people affected by the curse only increased, to the extent that they attacked Gilneas City a few days before the Cataclysm. At the head of the Gilnean Army, Greymane defended the capital until he ordered the evacuation of the citizens to Duskhaven. In the aftermath, Greymane faced the dual threats of the Shattering and the Forsaken invasion, culminating in the battle to retake Gilneas City, where he witnessed the death of his son and heir, Prince Liam, at the hands of Sylvanas Windrunner.
Humbled by his son's death and the devastation of his kingdom, Greymane accepted the aid of the night elves, who had offered to relocate Gilnean survivors to Darnassus. In a fit of stubbornness, Greymane was against formally rejoining the Alliance until he had almost lost his wife and daughter during the crossing. Following the formal establishment of diplomatic ties with King Varian Wrynn, Greymane became a staunch supporter of the Alliance, adding the ferocity of the Gilneans to the considerable might of the Alliance, and intending one day to reclaim his lost kingdom.
While Greymane himself became a close friend of Varian, his death during the assault on the Broken Shore, partly a consequence of the actions of Sylvanas, only intensified Greymane's burning hate for the new Warchief of the Horde. Their rivalry would come to define the brewing animosity between the Alliance and the Horde during the Broken Isles campaign and the third invasion of the Burning Legion as a whole. During the Fourth War, Greymane became an advisor to King Anduin Wrynn and assisted him in leading Alliance forces to the liberation of Lordaeron, as well as rallying his people to a new strength, going on the offensive to reclaim their homeland from their perennial foes. This goal was achieved under Genn's rule at last during the events of Dragonflight, in the aftermath of which he abdicated rule to his daughter, Tess Greymane. Despite this, he remains an active leader in the Grand Alliance, where his expertise is needed.
Ghost Walker Post: Ghost Walker Post is a small tauren outpost established in central Desolace directly adjacent to the Kodo Graveyard. It is one of two Horde outposts in the region, though Ghost Walker Post is much more exposed to danger compared to Shadowprey Village and its relatively secure location. It is from Ghost Walker Post that the Horde wages its war on the Burning Blade and their servants in Desolace as well as the various centaur tribes. The leader of Ghost Walker Post is Gurda Wildmane, a tauren shaman. Gurda and the other shamans ease the nearby kodo into their next lives and sometimes communicate with the spirits of dead kodo. There is also a contingent of orcs here, sent by Thrall. Ghost Walker Post is home to only the bare necessities of adventuring in Desolace, lacking so much as an inn or a wind rider master. The village has become part of the Cenarion Wildlands.
Gilneas (kingdom):
The kingdom of Gilneas (pronounced "Gil-NEIGH-uhs"), or the Gilnean kingdom, is one of the seven human nations in the Eastern Kingdoms, and is located in the peninsula of Gilneas, situated southwest of Silverpine Forest on the continent of Lordaeron. Originally an Arathorian city-state founded after the Troll Wars, it became an independent kingdom after the empire split apart. The nation's colors are described as a red design consisting of a circle with three vertical lines, akin to lances, and another line bisecting the circle itself, all set within a field of gray.
Led by King Genn of the Greymane family, the proud citizens of Gilneas once stood with the Alliance of Lordaeron against the Orcish Horde that sought to conquer all of Lordaeron. When King Greymane severed ties with the Alliance following the Second War, the kingdom became independent from all other nations after the Greymane Wall was erected at the borders of its land. Unbeknownst to the rest of the world, darkness fell on Gilneas after the wall's gates had been closed during the Third War. Before long, Gilneans were fighting among themselves in a bloody civil war that left the nation in tatters. At the same time, a terrible curse transformed many citizens into savage lupine beasts known as the worgen, until the night elves taught them how to control their inner beast through the Ritual of Balance.
Following the Cataclysm, and the destruction of the Wall, Sylvanas Windrunner and the Forsaken started the Invasion of Gilneas on the orders of Warchief Garrosh Hellscream, who sought the land as a strategic port for his war's efforts against the Alliance. In their hour of greatest need, Gilneas called out for their old allies' aid and accepted Tyrande Whisperwind's offer to relocate the survivors to Darnassus. After the formal establishment of diplomatic ties with King Varian Wrynn, Gilneas added the ferocity of the worgen to the considerable might of the Alliance, intending one day to reclaim their lost kingdom.
Over a decade after their exile, King Genn and his people finally returned to Gilneas. With the support of the Alliance and the Desolate Council, they faced the forces of the Scarlet Crusade to regain control of their kingdom. In the aftermath of their victory, King Genn abdicated his throne to his daughter, Tess Greymane, whom he deemed ready to lead their people to a better future as the Queen of Gilneas.
Gilneas City:
Gilneas City (formerly known as the Ruins of Gilneas City) is the capital city of the kingdom of Gilneas located in the peninsula of the same name. It is a dark and foreboding place of narrow cobblestone streets and crowded, Gothic houses, divided into four districts, centered around the Light's Dawn Cathedral. Shortly before the Cataclysm, the city was struck by a worgen assault led by the Wolf Cult, which was followed by an invasion of the Forsaken. After many conflicts and its abandonment by the Gilneans, the Alliance initially managed to retake the city, although it was ultimately left ruined and abandoned.
Over a decade after their exile, King Genn Greymane and his people finally returned to Gilneas. However, in their absence, the Scarlet Crusade had moved into the capital and used it as their stronghold for their operations in Lordaeron. With the help of the Alliance and the Desolate Council, the Gilneans defeated the zealots and returned to their homeland, where they began the rebuilding of their city.
The Gilneas City Guard are the law enforcement and protectors of Gilneas City, keeping the peace within the city's walls. Following the reclamation, the Greyguard manned the city defense.
Glimmerogg:
Glimmerogg  is the home of the friendly drogbar of Zaralek Cavern in the southwestern corner of the zone. Led by Brogg the Beast, the drogbar are all about lifting and snail racing, hosting the Glimmerogg Games.
The town is bordered by the Warder's Teeth to the southwest and west, Viridian Throne and Dragonscale Camp to the northwest and north, and Cascades Column to the northeast and east.
Loamm is sending shipments to Glimmerogg. Traveling Snailsmen from the village can also be found in the City of Threads.
