Gloom Hollow: Gloom Hollow is a settlement located in eastern Nazmir near the Frogmarsh and Nazwatha. The camp is inhabited by Tortollan Seekers with Darkspears guarding the perimeter.
Gloomshade Grove:
Gloomshade Grove is the place inhabited by neutral Podlings. They kill nearby creatures and haul the meat to piles in their lairs. They did something to the local squirrels, making them cannibals. Phlox has been leading Alliance Lumberjacks here in order to kill and presumably feed on them. After confronting Phlox in Gloomshade Grotto, the podlings turn hostile.
Leaf-Reader Kurri preaches the glories of the nearby fungus.
Glopgut: The Glopgut is a group of ogres at Glopgut's Hollow within the Twilight Highlands. They are led by Brogg Glopgut and Thog.
Glopgut's Hollow: The Glopgut's Hollow is a subzone of the Twilight Highlands. It is a sizable ogre fortress under control of the Glopgut, complete with a mound, several towers and a wall surrounding the area.
Gnarlpine Hold:
Gnarlpine Hold lies in the far southwest corner of Teldrassil.  It was formally home to the Gnarlpine furbolgs. Recently, corruption has taken over the area and many demons are now present. A steady stream of demons flow out of the area to the north where Tarindrella and Teldrassil ancients meet for battle.
During the Burning of Teldrassil, the conflagration spread to Gnarlpine Hold.
Gnarlpine tribe:
The Gnarlpine tribe was a corrupted furbolg tribe that dwelled atop the great world tree of Teldrassil. Though originally peaceful, the insidious effects of  [Fel Moss] caused the Gnarlpines to go berserk and attack their former allies, the night elves. Apart from living in Gnarlpine Hold and their other traditional villages in the south and west of Teldrassil, the Gnarlpines also invaded Ban'ethil Barrow Den and Starbreeze Village, driving out or slaying the local inhabitants.
The most dangerous of these corrupted feral beasts included Ferocitas the Dream Eater, Ursal the Mauler, and Uruson. They were led by Ursal and Ferocitas.
After the Cataclysm, their corruption returned. As the tribe made their home exclusively on Teldrassil, assuming they were not already wiped out by the night elves, the destruction of the world tree would have seen the tribe's end.
Gnomeregan:
Gnomeregan (/noʊmɹəˈɡɑːn/ NOHM-rə-gahn) is the subterranean capital city of the eponymous kingdom of Gnomeregan and the wrought-iron evidence of gnomish brilliance, ambition, and ingenuity.
During the Third War, a trogg invasion led to its tragic downfall, pulled from their sleep by the upheaval of titan sites. In a desperate attempt to kill the invaders, the gnomish ruler, High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque, on the advice of his advisor Sicco Thermaplugg, ordered his people to open the pressure valves of their giant, grinding machines and released toxic radiation throughout the city. Though the radiation killed some of the troggs, it empowered others, while nearly eighty percent of gnomekind died within days. The survivors fled to the protection of Ironforge, while others were transformed into horrific, mindless, evil-doing leper gnomes, who still live there. Driven completely mad by the radiation, Thermaplugg declared himself "King of Gnomeregan" and took control of the city, leading an army of troggs and leper gnomes.
After the Northrend campaign, Mekkatorque launched Operation: Gnomeregan with the support of the Alliance, allowing the gnomes to reclaim both the surface and the upper floors of Gnomeregan. Since then, the S.A.F.E. forces have been responsible for cleaning up the radiation, as well as saving the survivors inside the capital, using New Tinkertown as their base of operations at the surface.
The city is currently a mid-level dungeon.
Gnomeregan (faction): Gnomeregan (formerly known as Gnomeregan Exiles) is the faction associated with the playable gnome of the Alliance. They have recently their capital of Gnomeregan in western Dun Morogh.
Gnomeregan (kingdom):
The kingdom of Gnomeregan, formerly known as the Gnomeregan Exiles, is the gnomish nation on the continent of Khaz Modan and a member state of the Alliance. After King Mechagon's exodus four hundred years ago, the gnomes have resorted to democratically electing their High Tinkers. Under the leadership of High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque, the gnomes lost their capital city of Gnomeregan during the Third War and sought refuge within the neighboring allied dwarven city of Ironforge, where they have remained until the launch of Operation: Gnomeregan. Still in the process of retaking their ancient home from the troggs, they are now based in New Tinkertown while still engaging in major Alliance operations across Azeroth and beyond.
During the Fourth War, the nation reunited with their brethren, the mechagnomes of Mechagon, after Prince Erazmin aided in saving Mekkatorque's life. Electing to merge societies, rather than work as partners, Erazmin ceded leadership of Mechagon City and its people to Gelbin, dubbing him the true successor of King Mechagon as the first King of the gnomes since the now-defeated tyrant.
Go'Shek Farm:
Go'Shek Farm is a farmstead in the eastern part of the Arathi Highlands, near Witherbark Village. The farm is protected by Hammerfall Grunts.
The rare armored boar Swee can be found in the stables of the farm.
Golden Lotus:
The Golden Lotus are a mysterious society of pandaren who are guardians of the Vale of Eternal Blossoms. Their members are handpicked by the August Celestials themselves to help them keep an eye on the vale, and the pandaren see it as an immense honor to be chosen as a member of the sacred order. The Golden Lotus have recently noticed mogu trespassers sneaking into the Vale and have called upon the Shado-Pan and adventurers from the Horde and Alliance to help solve the mystery of their resurgence.
When the Vale was desecrated by the Heart of Y'Shaarj, many members of the Golden Lotus were killed. The rest of the order remained and worked to repair the Vale.
Golden Pagoda:
The Golden Pagoda is a subzone of the Vale of Eternal Blossoms. Found between the two gigantic mogu statues overlooking the western half of the vale, this place once housed the Golden Pagoda itself. When the mogu invaded the vale, the pagoda became a meeting place for the Golden Lotus to enlist adventurers from the Horde and Alliance to aid them. Several important members of the Lotus were stationed here, including Leven Dawnblade, Rook Stonetoe, Sun Tenderheart, and Kun and Anji Autumnlight. 
When Garrosh Hellscream awakened the Sha of Pride, feedback from the event destroyed the Golden Pagoda and surrounding areas, killing many of the residents there. All Golden Lotus quests were relocated to the Setting Sun Garrison on the western side of the zone. The area is now a desecrated crater, home only to the sha that now haunt the vale.
After the Vale of Eternal Blossoms was restored, the pagoda was also reconstructed.
Goldenmist Village: Goldenmist Village is located in the northwestern area of the Ghostlands. Originally a high elven village, the Salonar sisters lived here, and Sylvanas Windrunner had friends here. Its inhabitants were slain during the coming of the Scourge, and for many years haunted the village ruins as ghosts.
Goldshire: Goldshire is a human town centrally located in Elwynn Forest, just southwest of Northshire Valley. It has roads that lead to Stormwind City to the northwest, Northshire Abbey to the northeast, Westfall to the west, and Redridge Mountains to the east. It is the second settlement that most human heroes visit at the beginning of their journey. Marshal Dughan of the Stormwind Guard is in charge of the security. Many travelers are seen enjoying the hospitality of the Lion's Pride Inn, one of the most respectable ale houses in Azeroth.
Goldtusk Inn:
The Goldtusk Inn is an inn owned by Rhan'ka and staffed by the Goldtusk Gang inside a cave on the northeast side of Whistlebloom Oasis in Vol'dun. According to Rhan'ka, "All exiles are welcome to rest at de Goldtusk Inn, de only luxury lodge in dese harsh dunes". Guests at the inn need to earn their keep. The inn offers several excursion activities and packages, such as the "Warlord Package" (which is required for access to excursions to Dead Man's Pass), the "Scorpid King Package" (unlimited all-day access to Rhan'ka's famous scorpid blood drinks), and the "Giant Deadly Unstoppable Killer Cobra Experience" (an activity which challenges guests to travel to the dunes north of the inn and try not to be killed by Sevriss).
When adventurers first arrive at the inn, it offers no commodities and the visitors are only able to see the seemingly insane Rhan'ka talking to skulls. After Rhan'ka sends the adventurers to Dead Man's Pass, Sandfury raiders led by Gozda'kun the Slaver thrash the inn and kidnap the Goldtusk Gang (leading Rhan'ka to officially ban the tribe from the inn). After adventurers rescue the skulls, Rhan'ka conducts a ritual to initiate them into the Goldtusk Gang and allow them to see what the gang sees, revealing that most of the Goldtusk Gang members are actually ghosts that were previously invisible. After adventurers help the various gang members with tasks around the inn — specifically by helping Man'zul create and plant a "gold tusk" above the inn's entrance, clearing the oasis of predators for Volni, and gathering fruit for Zulsan's all-you-can-eat breakfast buffet — the place receives its first guest in the form of the injured Bladeguard Tarkaj, who is offered food, drink, bandages, and bedding by the adventurer. Afterward, Rhan'ka declares that the inn is officially open.
Goodgrub Smoking Pit:
The Goodgrub Smoking Pit is a small quest hub located northeast of Starfall Village in Winterspring. The residents at this location encourage adventurers to slay the nearby wildlife to provide great food for them. It was set up by Jez Goodgrub.
After the Fourth War, Zekhan and Rexxar visited the place.
Gor'vosh: The Gor'vosh are an ogre group who appear to have made their home at Ashmaul Burial Grounds on Ashran, in alternate Draenor. They are notable for their necromancers, who have raised a substantial number of undead at Ashmaul Burial Grounds. They are hostile to both Alliance and Horde.
Gordal Fortress: Gordal Fortress is located in Talador.
Gordunni: The Gordunni (or the Dire Maul Gordunni clan, the Gordunni Ogres, and the Gordunni clan of ancient Draenor) is an ogre tribe or clan based in central Feralas. They are despoiling the forest and its wildlife. Many have taken residency in the Ruins of Isildien in the High Wilderness as well as the foothills north of Camp Mojache, while the "upper class" is found in Dire Maul. Like most of their kind, Gordunni ogres are remarkably bloodthirsty and are comprised of both melee warriors and spell casters. In the ruins of an ancient night elven city, the Gordunni have established Dire Maul, a stronghold of some potency and power.
Gorian Empire: The Gorian Empire (also known as the Gorian ogre imperium or simply the Ogre Empire) was the nation-state of the ogres on Draenor. The ogres of Highmaul were referred to as high ogres.
Gorian Falls: Gorian Falls is a sub-zone in eastern Ashran, on Draenor. This damp, winding zone features marauding saberon, swarms of podlings, and some very large flying insects, as well as a series of caves. Notably, the  [Star Root Tuber] can be looted here.
Gorian Proving Grounds: The Gorian Proving Grounds are located in Nagrand.
Gorilla Gorge: Gorilla Gorge is a subzone of Zuldazar on Zandalar. It is full of intelligent Da'kani gorillas that are empowered by the chunks of Kaja'mite that are erupting from the steam vents.
Gorloc Shore: The Gorloc Shore is an area located in the Azure Span. It is the home of the Brinetooth gorlocs.
Gorshak War Camp: Gorshak War Camp is located on the Devouring Breach's eastern side, southeast of Bloodgulch and northeast of Firebeard's Patrol. It was once a sizable Dragonmaw clan base, made up of a great hall, a kennel, a forge and protected by several watch towers and blade throwers.
Grangol'var Village: Grangol'var Village is a ruined village located just north of the Bone Wastes, Terokkar Forest. It is occupied by numerous Shadow Council warlocks of diabolical intent, all led by Shadowmaster Grieve. Adventurers, at first, do not know what group controls Grangol'var Village, but after infiltrating the village with disguises during the quest Who Are They?, they find its true purpose. Grangol'var Village is an Orc archaeology dig site and contains a ruined barracks.
Grassy Cline:
The Grassy Cline can be found along the northern edge of the Valley of the Four Winds. It is bordered by Thunderfoot Ranch to the east, the Sunsoaked Meadow to the south, and the Pools of Purity on the cliffs above to the west.
Adolescent Mushan are found grazing and fighting with each other here, while the Wyrmhorn Turtles are found at the pond at the bottom of the hill.
Greasy Eel: The Greasy Eel is a goblin submarine captained by Captain Krooz. Thanks to Ricket, it came to Dazar'alor and was used by Gazlowe's Greasemonkeys to get to Mechagon Island.
Great Forge:
The Great Forge (situated in the Great Forge District) is the heart and namesake of the dwarf capital of Ironforge. It was the first part of the city to be built by the early dwarves who first settled under Ironforge Mountain. The rest of the city grew around it and was consequently named "Ironforge" in its honor.
The Great Forge never shuts down. It's a loud, hot, and cheerful place, serving not only as the physical center of the city, but also the central part of city life. Most citizens regularly pass through the forge, while visitors come to admire what is happening there. The current keeper of the Great Forge is Myolor Sunderfury. At its center is the famed Great Anvil, where most of the best dwarven blacksmithing trainers can be found. Ringed around the Great Forge are several foundries pouring molten slag and a great deal of shops and guild offices, including trainers for cooking, mining, first aid, tailoring and leatherworking, as well as the High Seat, the court of the Council of Three Hammers. Ironforge's gryphon master Gryth Thurden is also located here. 
Two bells were created here. As a token of friendship, the dwarves sent one to Lordaeron and the other to Stormwind City. It was also here, upon the Great Anvil itself, that the legendary blade Ashbringer was forged by King Magni Bronzebeard.
According to Mathias Shaw, the Great Forge is a fine spot for eavesdropping and hearing news from across the Alliance.
Green dragonflight:
The green dragonflight (or the Emerald Dragonflight) is a draconic organization led by the eponymous green dragons to uphold their creed of preserving nature. During the ordering of Azeroth, the titan Eonar charged Ysera and her flight with the protection of the natural world and the Emerald Dream, a pristine realm of nature and magic. Like the red dragonflight, green dragons are generally more approachable than those of other flights, occasionally seeking the help of druids to aid in this task, thus becoming very involved with the Cenarion Circle.
Tragically, the green dragons are susceptible to corruption of nature, making them a primary target of the Emerald Nightmare. The corruption was stemmed after the end of the war Against the Nightmare; though Nightmare Lord Xavius did eventually return during the third invasion of the Burning Legion, corrupting Ysera, who had to be slain. The flight eventually rallied behind Merithra, the daughter of Ysera, though the process was arduous. With the return of the Dragon Isles, the flight returned to one of their ancestral homes in the Ancient Bough, confronting the Primalist threat with the help of Ysera, who had temporarily returned from the Ardenweald. After the death of Fyrakk and the blooming of Amirdrassil, Merithra was empowered as the Green Aspect by Azeroth herself.
Greenpaw Village: Greenpaw Village is located in central Ashenvale, south of Raynewood Retreat, northeast of Silverwind Refuge, and northwest of the southern moonwell. It is the home of the Foulweald tribe, led by Chief Murgut and the shaman Oakpaw. Both Horde and Alliance adventurers frequently come to Greenpaw to battle the corrupted bearmen. The village has been partially destroyed by the Horde, with the furbolg inhabiting the conquered areas taken prisoner.
Greenstone Village:
Greenstone Village is a pandaren village found in east-central Jade Forest between Dawn's Blossom, the Arboretum, and the Emperor's Omen.
The pandaren still hold the village, as compared to the Mason's Quarter just north of town, which has been lost to Puckish Sprites.
Graceful Swan runs the Greenstone Inn on the north side of the village.
Greenwarden's Grove:
Greenwarden's Grove is a night elven outpost and quest hub, complete with a flight path.
After they learned of Rethiel the Greenwarden from a local dwarven legend, which told of a plant-man acting as protector of the region, the night elves came to the Wetlands just to find him, and after they succeeded they ended up settling down. They founded a whole grove near him to watch over the Greenwarden. Ferilon Leafborn is the head druid there.
There are a tower and an inn. There's also a moonwell which, at some point, was visited by Arwis Blackstone.
Greymane Manor: Greymane Manor is a palatial estate high in the hills of western Gilneas, owned by King Genn Greymane and his family. The king's observatory is located in the tower behind the manor.
Greywatch:
Greywatch is a Gilneas Brigade encampment found in eastern Stormheim. It is led by King Genn Greymane, who appears within the camp itself, and is the center of the Brigade's movements within Stormheim.
The Forsaken are attempting to blight bomb the encampment from the nearby Bronzeleaf Thicket, but are thwarted by heroes upon Greymane's orders.
Grimfrost Hill: Grimfrost Hill is a Grimfrost ogre village in eastern Frostfire Ridge. From here these ogres worship a creature at the Pit of the Devourer and have been capturing frostwolves from the Frostwolf clan.
Grimrail Depot: Grimrail Depot is a dungeon introduced in Warlords of Draenor, set in Gorgrond.
Grimtotem Post: Grimtotem Post is the base of Grimtotem tribe operations in Stonetalon Mountains. Many different types, such as Brutes, Ruffians, Sorcerers, and Mercenaries patrol the post and nearby areas. The Grimtotem here are led by the fierce Grundig Darkcloud.
Grimtotem tribe:
The Grimtotem tribe (also known as the Grimtotem clan, or simply the Grimtotem tauren) is one of the mightiest tauren tribes. They stand as an aggressive extreme of the usually pacifistic tauren, wishing to eradicate the "lesser races" from Kalimdor and retake the tauren's long lost ancestral holdings. The Grimtotem tribe fights to eliminate the enemies of the tauren; to the Grimtotem, almost all races are enemies of the tauren. They are known for unprovoked attacks, slaughter and mayhem, in great contrast to the peaceful, spiritual nature of the other tauren clans.
From early childhood, while other tauren their age learn the rites of the Great Hunt and to be in harmony with nature, the Grimtotem are taught how to fight each other. They learn to kill quickly and cleanly with hands, horns, and whatever weapon they can get their hands on. In any given conflict, the odds are with a Grimtotem to emerge victorious. They do not fight honorably; they fight to win.
The Grimtotem are currently split into two main camps: those led by the powerful shaman Magatha Grimtotem, who gained leadership after marrying the previous leader, who had died shortly after in an "unforeseen climbing accident"; and those led by Jevan Grimtotem, who are loyal to the Horde and renounced Magatha after the part she played in Cairne Bloodhoof's death. Jevan's Horde Grimtotem are about a quarter of the pre-split Grimtotem population.
Instead of learning to respect the land and elements, the Grimtotem do nothing but take land, power, and lives. They are skilled and relentless, and believe that no others have a right to be here, even the tauren who disagree with them.
Grishnath: Grishnath is an arakkoa settlement in Raven's Wood in northwestern Blade's Edge Mountains.
Grizzlemaw:
Grizzlemaw is a furbolg city located in the center of the Grizzly Hills of Northrend, built within the stump of the failed World Tree Vordrassil.
The furbolgs of Grizzlemaw are all hostile, and are part of the Redfang and Frostpaw tribes, which are constantly at war. Killing furbolgs from one side can make you temporarily neutral with the other for five minutes (unless you kill more of the opposition, in which case you may remain so as long as you're nearby).
Grol'dom Farm:
Grol'dom Farm  is one of the many orcish pig farms that have sprung up in the years after the founding of Orgrimmar. 
It was originally inhabited by only Kranal Fiss and his children, but since the Cataclysm it has grown into a stopping point for caravans traveling between Orgrimmar and Crossroads. The farm is under constant attack from Razormane Pillagers. The farm serves as a quest hub, with an innkeeper, stable master, and repairs.
Here, adventurers will first meet Mankrik and can pay their respects at the Humble Monument, a memorial to Mankrik's deceased wife, Olgra.

 This section concerns content related to Legion.
During the Burning Legion's invasions, the farm was assaulted by the Legion, leaving the area in turmoil. The swines specifically were targeted by imps.
Grom'arsh Crash-Site:
The Grom'arsh Crash-Site can be found to the east of the Temple of Storms, southeast of the Snowdrift Plains, west of the Terrace of the Makers, and north of the Engine of the Makers within the Storm Peaks.  It is an encampment made of the wreck of a goblin zeppelin, utilized by the Horde when events were heating up in Ulduar.
Following the war against the Jailer, the brothers Bronzebeard reported that camp is fully abandoned, though the wreckage of the airship can still be seen, peeping out of the ice.
Grom'gar:
Grom'gar is the ancestral home of the Thunderlord orc clan located in Frostfire Ridge. According to legend, Grom'gar was built in the skeletal remains of the last colossal, which was supposedly killed by the Thunderlords many generations ago.
After the Thunderlords attacked the Frostwolf clan, the Frostwolf orcs retaliated with the help of the Horde and invaded Grom'gar. The attack led to the death of the Thunderlord chieftain, Fenris.
Grom'gol Base Camp:
Grom'gol Base Camp (or Grom'Gol) is an orcish camp on the southwestern coast of Northern Stranglethorn. Led by Commander Aggro'gosh, the outpost provides a safe chain of supply to Stonard in the Swamp of Sorrows. This fort is heavily strengthened to be able to guard against jungle trolls, naga, and the many members of the Alliance who arrive from Booty Bay and Duskwood. The Savage Coast Raptor Fields are just to the north.
During the war against the Zandalari, the camp was attacked by the Gurubashi trolls led by Bloodlord Mandokir. The attack was successfully repelled.
Grommash Hold: Grommash Hold is an enormous fortress located in the Valley of Strength in the orc capital of Orgrimmar. It is named after the orcish hero Grommash Hellscream, it is the former seat of the Warchief of the Horde, and now it is the seat of the Horde Council. Delegations from Silvermoon and the Undercity reside within, including paladin and priest trainers, as well as the trainer for archaeology.
Grommashar:
Grommashar is the base of the Warsong clan on Draenor, located on the south-east coast of Nagrand, between Telaar and Mar'gok's Overwatch. It is a well-defended fortress, from which the Warsong clan dominate the eastern half of Nagrand. It is named for Grommash Hellscream, chieftain of the Warsong clan. The entrance is called the Gates of Grommashar.
There is a throne area where a tree, the one Grommash had been tied to may years ago, was moved. On the tree is the skull of a former Imperator.
Grookin Hill:
Grookin Hill is a hozen village found just west of Tigers' Wood, past the Slicky Stream in western Jade Forest. This is the main village of the Forest Hozen, where the big chief resides.
After gaining favor with the hozen, by killing the mean wikkets (the Alliance who were killing them), killing a hozen-killing tiger, and gathering bait to catch fish, the chief decides to fight alongside the good wikkets (the Horde). When the signal flare is lit by the adventurer, the surviving Horde attack force make their way from the Strongarm Airstrip to here as their new temporary base of operations.
Grosh'gok Compound: The Grosh'gok Compound is an ogre mound located in the Vice inhabited by the Deadwind ogres. It is the southernmost and largest of the multiple caves in the Vice.
Grove of Aessina: The Grove of Aessina is a small grove with night elven ruins, devoted to the greater wilderness spirit of Aessina. It is located in the northwest corner of Mount Hyjal. Ysera also refers to this place as the "Shrine of Aessina".
Grove of the Ancients: The Grove of the Ancients is a sacred ruin of an old night elven temple, where Onu, an Ancient of Lore, resides together with a pair of merchants and a sleeping druid. The grove lies in the southeastern part of Darkshore, nestled near the mountains, and is built around the surging Wildbend River. The Circle of Ancients meets here.
Growling Hollow:
Growling Hollow  is an area in northeast Hallowfall.
The entrance to the Mycomancer Cavern delve is at  on the eastern wall.
The area is bordered by the Fungal Fields to the west, Shadowgrove Vineyards and Whirring Field to the northwest, Stillstone Pond to the north, and Dunelle's Kindness to the south.
Grumbol's Hammers: Grumbol's Hammers are an Alliance group led by Grumbol Grimhammer. They can be found on Mechagon Island.
Gruul the Dragonkiller: Gruul the Dragonkiller was the gronn overlord of the ogres of Outland, ruling with an iron fist. He earned his "nom de guerre" (and the emnity of Sabellian) after slaughtering many members of the black dragonflight who had come to Outland in order to aid the Horde of Draenor. Gruul was worshiped as a deity by the ogres of the Blade's Edge Mountains, and his powerful sons ravaged both the Blade's Edge Mountains and the plains of Nagrand. Gruul's unparalleled strength and experience in battle would have posed a serious threat if he ever chose to attack the Horde or Alliance forces in Outland. Gruul was also allied with the Illidari, though to what extent is unclear.
Gruul's Lair:
Gruul's Lair is located north of Ruuan Weald in the Blade's Edge Mountains of Outland. Here, Gruul the Dragonkiller, the merciless gronn overlord, rules over the ogres of Blade's Edge.
This raid contains two bosses, Gruul the Dragonkiller and High King Maulgar, and requires no attunement. The player must be at least level 65 and in a raid to enter.
Guardians of Hyjal: The Guardians of Hyjal are a new faction that appeared in World of Warcraft: Cataclysm, whose job is to protect Mount Hyjal and Nordrassil. They are worshippers of the Ancients, such as Aessina and Tortolla, and wish to repopulate the region with animal life. Much like the Cenarion Circle, they are Neutral and made up mainly of druids.
Gul'rok: Gul'rok is a large orc village found in southwestern Talador where the Shadow Council is preparing for another assault on Auchindoun.
Gul'var: Gul'var is named after Gul'dan and is his main base of operation in Shadowmoon Valley. It is led by Razuun.
Gundargaz:
Gundargaz  is the quest hub and largest settlement of the Ringing Deeps, found in the west-central part of the zone. It also serves as the Assembly of the Deeps renown headquarters.
Players are initially directed here during  [73-75] Pomp and Dire Circumstance early in the Ringing Deeps storyline.
The area is bordered by Ironhaul Station to the west, the Hallowfall Gate to the northwest, the Earthenworks to the north, the Lost Mines to the east, Brunwin's Terrace to the east and south, and the Waterworks and Shimmermist Falls to the southwest.
Gundrak:
Gundrak (also spelled as Gun'Drak) is the capital of the ice troll Drakkari Empire in Zul'Drak in eastern Northrend. The Drakkari tribe rule Zul'Drak from here, constantly battling the mighty forces of the Scourge.
Gundrak is an instance which acts as the final bastion of the Drakkari Empire. These trolls, much like other troll tribes, worship various animal gods called the loa. With their backs against the wall due to their impending doom at the hands of the Scourge, the Drakkari have begun sacrificing their gods in a desperate attempt to survive.
Gunstan's Dig: Gunstan's Dig is a small dwarven camp setup by the Explorer's League south of the Southmoon Ruins, just east of the Valley of the Watchers, in Tanaris. Unlike the Horde equivalent, Dawnrise Expedition, this Alliance camp is not an actual subzone.
Guo-Lai Halls:
The Guo-Lai Halls lie beneath the Ruins of Guo-Lai in northwest Vale of Eternal Blossoms. The Halls' entrance can be found in the northwest corner of the ruins. Inside the halls are the Guo-Lai Ritual Chamber, the Guo-Lai Vault, the Hall of Statues, the Hall of the Serpent, and the Hall of Tiles. The Shao-Tien have occupied the Halls and are using that as well as the Golden Stair as a base from which to continue their assaults on the western and eastern vale.
Since the end of Garrosh Hellscream's Pandaren Campaign, it's been haunted, and the pandaren locals were terrified of this place. The shaman of the Earthen Ring and Rehgar Earthfury entered the halls in search of edicts for Xuen during the third invasion of the Burning Legion. They also cleansed the area by slaying mogu spirits.
Gurubashi Arena:
The Gurubashi Arena (or The Great Arena) is an arena located on the northwestern section of the Cape of Stranglethorn, just north of Booty Bay. The Arena is an old relic of the mighty Gurubashi Empire, which once controlled vast tracts of land in the southern regions of the Eastern Kingdoms.
The Gurubashi Arena provides ruffians a shot at competition, fame, and treasure. It is said that in ancient times, fights were to the death, and the sand of the area was muddy with troll blood. Short John Mithril is the overseer of the less-lethal matches. Old stories say that if one finds a blood-red amulet at midnight, a demon will devour their soul by daybreak. Once a generation, the greatest trolls from all over Azeroth come to this arena to challenge one another in combat. This is an ancient rite long presided over by the Zandalari troll king, Rastakhan. They fight for the glory of the loa. To win is one of the greatest honors to which a troll can aspire. With Rastakhan's death, it is unknown if the rite will continue.
Gurubashi Empire:
The Gurubashi Empire was once one of the most powerful forces of Azeroth, controlling much of the southern part of the eastern continents. It took its name from the strongest tribe of jungle trolls at the time, the Gurubashi. Their former capital of Zul'Gurub is located in Stranglethorn Vale. Eventually, this great nation splintered into separate tribes such as the Darkspear tribe.
At the height of the Gurubashi Empire, the jungle trolls ruled over lands from Stranglethorn Vale to the Echo Isles.
Gurubashi tribe: The Gurubashi tribe (/ˈɡʊ.ruˌbɑː.ʃi/ GOO-roo-BAH-shee) is the remnant of the Gurubashi Empire and is the strongest tribe of jungle trolls. They reside in their capital of Zul'Gurub.
Gutterville: Gutterville is located in the Verdant Gutters in the Ringing Deeps.
Halfhill:
Halfhill is the center of commerce in the Valley of the Four Winds, found more or less in the dead-center of the zone. It is a large community built onto a hill, several roads crisscrossing between houses on the hillsides. It is also the headquarters of the Tillers, a faction dedicated to farming. The outskirts of the town near the bottom of the hill hold granaries, a boat builder's workshop, Sunsong Ranch, and the all-important Halfhill Market. The town's tavern, the Lazy Turnip, lies about halfway up the hill, next to a flattened plaza. The upper levels of the hill hold several more houses. Among them is the headquarters of the Tillers Union where Nana Mudclaw stays, where once stood Shen-zin's Sundries which supplied Liu Lang with his trademark umbrella, causing Liu Lang to name his sea turtle after the shop's owner. The peak of the hill is partially hollow and used as a storage facility for historical records and seeds. This storage area is accessible through a cave entrance, next to the headquarters.
The town has had many visitors pass through from far away locales, often stopping by the marketplace. Farmers bring their wheat to Halfhill to be processed and distributed to breweries, traded, or made into food.
Halfhill is bordered clockwise from the north by the Verdant Belt, the Gilded Fan, the Gilding Stream, the Imperial Granary, and the Heartland.
Once, the citizens of Halfhill defeat attacking hozen by flinging the hozen's excrement back at them. The tortollan Toki was visiting the town when it happened.
Halgrind:
Halgrind was a vrykul town found in Howling Fjord. During the war against the Lich King, Halgrind was exposed to the New Plague, serving as a testing ground for the Royal Apothecary Society. When the Forsaken took control of the town, the chieftain Thorvald fled. The remaining vrykul, while not dropping dead from exposure, found themselves trapped and slowly killed.
After the war against the Jailer, the brothers Bronzebeard mentioned that the village was still in ruins and a patch of blighted land.
Hall of Holding: The Hall of Holding  is the location of the bank, guild bank, and Great Vault (weekly chest) of Oribos.
Hallowfall Arathi: The Hallowfall Arathi are the third Major Faction of The War Within, based out of Mereldar in Hallowfall. They represent the Hallowfall Expedition of the Arathi Empire.
Halls of Atonement:
The Halls of Atonement is a cathedral and area located in eastern Revendreth. They were once a pinnacle of redemption for the most prideful of souls. However, due to recent events they've fallen into darkness and succumbed to forbidden magics.
The members of the Halls of Atonement perform rituals of inquisition, of absolution, and of Judgment. The Ritual of Absolution, also called the ritual of extraction, requires a venthyr robe, dagger, and tome, and is usually be performed at a reliquary where four souls may be absolved at a time. The Ritual of Judgment requires four venthyr to pass judgment upon a soul, either recognizing its redemption, upon which the soul would either choose to become a venthyr or to be re-judged by the Arbiter, or the venthyr may condemn it to the Maw. For a soul to become a venthyr, another venthyr must choose to sire them, which can present a weakness for the sire in question. Inquisitors are seen to oversee the Rituals, serving under the Harvesters of Pride. The ritual of inquisition allows venthyr to see every sin by peering directly into a soul.
After a Ritual of Absolution, souls are placed in Atonement Crypts where they are sealed away for an extended period of time to contemplate on their lives after being unburdened of their pride. Cryptkeeper Kassir watches over the Atonement Crypts. The most stubborn souls are also forced to endure the Bell of Rebuke, one of the most punitive tools of the venthyr. When you ring the bell, you first rebuke yourself, but you also make yourself more vulnerable to rebuke from others. Each bell demands something from the soul who rings it.
The Halls of Atonement also contain the Sinstone Archive, the collection of every sinstone of every formerly-mortal venthyr that passes through the Halls and the rituals, however, sinstones of powerful venthyr tend to go "missing" and their owners hide them. They are overseen by Archivist Fane. This is important as sinstones contain a venthyr's true name as well as their sins, which gives you power over them. Archivam in the Catacombs Ward to the north, where the Harvester of Avarice normally resides, also contains the Sinstone Archives. The Catacombs hold souls until they are less arrogant and they are sent to the Halls of Atonement. Likewise the Forest Ward puts their souls on the Penitent Hunt until they are defenseless toward the process.
Since the dawn of Revendreth, the small stoneborn Temel has been charged with proclaiming the sins of souls for all to hear.
When the adventurer arrives in Revendreth, The Accuser is the Harvester of Pride.
The northeastern elevator that connects to the Trench of the Enders also contains a Venthyr Covenant Transportation Network mirror. The southern elevator connects with the Edge of Sin.
Halls of Valor:
The Halls of Valor (sometimes called the Hall of Valor, known as Valhalas or Valhallas in Vrykul) are said to be located high up in the clouds above Stormheim, however, they are also mentioned to be above Helya's realm of Helheim. This is where the greatest warriors of the vrykul are called to serve Keeper Odyn as their eternal reward for being the worthiest.
As you are seeking out the Pillar of Creation in Stormheim, you are contending with the Burning Legion cooperating leader of the vrykul in Stormheim, the God-King Skovald. As you race against him through the region, both of your paths lead you to this dungeon, which is the location of the Pillar. You must prove yourself worthy in battle so that you can claim it. We also learn more about the origin of the Val'kyr here. These aren't the undead Val'kyr from Northrend, but the pure warrior of the Light. Its polar opposite is Helheim. The Skyhold is a section of the Halls, which are entered through the Gates of Valor.
Hallvalor: Hallvalor is the ancestral home of the Burning Blade clan, located in eastern Nagrand.
Hand of Argus:
The Hand of Argus is an order of draenei paladins and vindicators that serve as the primary military and police force of the Exodar draenei. They are considered elite among their people. Under the command of the Triumvirate of the Hand — formed by the vindicators Boros, Kuros, and Aesom — the organization is based in the Exodar, with their forces stationed in both Azure Watch and Blood Watch.
At the start of the Legion's third invasion of Azeroth, the Triumvirate pledged its forces to the reformed Order of the Silver Hand, and remained affiliated even after the Argus Campaign. When Xal'atath and the Devouring Host launched their invasion of Quel'Danas, the Hand of Argus answered the call of the Light and have since joined the Vanguard of the Light to defend the Sunwell.
Hand of the Prophet: The Hand of the Prophet is the main Alliance force in Tanaan Jungle on alternate Draenor.
Haohan Mudclaw: Haohan Mudclaw is the pandaren head of the Tillers Union in Valley of the Four Winds.
Har'alnor: Har'alnor is a haranir village in southwestern Harandar. It is the closest settlement to the roots of Shaladrassil.
Har'athir: Har'athir is a haranir village in southeastern Harandar. It is the closest settlement to the roots of Amirdrassil.
Har'kuai: Har'kuai is a haranir village in northeastern Harandar. It is the closest settlement to the roots of Nordrassil. The roots of Nordrassil carry water from the Well of Eternity to Har'kuai. From Har'kuai, it then flows into the Vale of Mists and then the Rift of Aln.
Har'mara:
Har'mara is a haranir village in northwestern Harandar. It is the closest settlement to the roots of Teldrassil, whose roots still smolder after it was burned during the Fourth War.
Har'mara is the starting location for new haranir characters.
Haranir: The haranir are a reclusive humanoid race that resides in Harandar, a primordial jungle that lies where the roots of the World Trees converge. The haranir have been described as subterranean guardians of sacred and hidden lands. Ancient and ferocious hunters, they were first encountered during the war against Xal'atath in parts of Azj-Kahet where they live in secrecy and protect the great roots growing into the area. They were described as "not really elves, not really trolls"—with tapered, bat-like ears, small tusks, clawed feet with four digits in the front, and one protruding from the heel, and grayish-purple skin partially covered in dark fur and quills. The haranir wear clothing made out of leaves and thorns and can shapeshift into bats.
Harborage: The Harborage is a base of Broken who managed to stay sane after crossing over to the world of Azeroth from Draenor. It is located in the northern part of the Swamp of Sorrows. The Broken here were until recently led by Magtoor.
Hardwrench Hideaway:
Hardwrench Hideaway is a Horde goblin port town located behind Gurubashi Arena and along the coast in the Cape of Stranglethorn. It is named after Sassy Hardwrench, who appears here after the goblins evacuate the Lost Isles. It is a combination resort and resource salvaging plant. The resort offers attractions such as nature hikes and an oil rig day trip.
During the war against the Zandalari, Zanzil the Outcast aided the Gurubashi tribe by turning the inhabitants of Hardwrench Hideaway into voodoo zombies by poisoning the food in the town. Adventurers saved the town.
Harpy:
Harpies are vicious, flying creatures that resemble a cross between a night elf female and a hunting bird, with long talons for feet and large graceful wings for arms. Despite the similarity, they have little in common with the elves. Harpies employ nature-based magic like night elves, but they destroy the environments in which they settle, killing every creature they encounter and despoiling the land to build nests noted for their noxious odor. Harpies originally hail from the Stonetalon Mountains, but have since spread out across Kalimdor, Northrend, the Broken Isles, Alterac Valley, and the Exile's Reach island. The harpies in Thaldraszus only arrived recently, flying in from Kalimdor when the Dragon Isles awakened.
The cackling bird-women are capable of powerful elemental storm magic. Little is known about the source of their power, as they attack invaders on sight, few can discern any meaning behind their shrill cries, and none can tolerate the smell of their nests. They only get more beautiful as they age.
Harvesting Pits: The Harvesting Pits are located in the Spires of Arak.
Hatchery Observatory: The Hatchery Observatory is a tower located in the south of the Waking Shores. It overlooks the Ruby Lifeshrine to the north.
Hatchet Hills:
The Hatchet Hills is an area leading to the Amani Pass just southwest of Zul'Aman in the Ghostlands. The hills were once full of roaming forest trolls until Budd Nedreck's expedition came in and killed many of them, taking over the area. However, many of the expedition members were captured. The remaining ones stayed outside and requested the assistance of heroes to aid them.
After the Amani forest trolls were defeated and the expedition left, the area remained quiet for a time. Until the Zandalari came forth to aid the Amani. It was then that the hills were occupied by the Darkspear tribe, Farstriders, and even the Silver Covenant to prevent them from growing in power.
Haven:
Haven is the main quest hub in Zereth Mortis. It is the home of the Enlightened and was created out of Progenitor ruins. During the last stages of the war against the Jailer, the settlement came under attack by the Mawsworn, but it was protected by a protective shield and reinforced by Maw Walkers and Covenant armies. Cartel Xy also tried to sabotage Haven.
Located in western Zereth Mortis, it is surrounded by Felicitous Glade and the Great Veldt. The Slumbering Vault is located inside Haven, and just outside Haven's walls is the Geometric Cavern.
Hayward Fishery: Hayward Fishery was formerly a small single island prior to the Cataclysm. It is now a tiny archipelago off the coast of southwestern Gilneas which houses a fishing business run by the Hayward brothers: Sebastian, Ron, and Walt Hayward (formerly counting Trent and Tim before their death). The brothers have been running the Fishery for years and didn't make it to Duskhaven very often, except to trade their fish.
Healing Wings:
The Healing Wings is a dracthyr weyrn. This weyrn shall be the face and symbol for hope among all those who would call the Aspects their allies, this weyrn are charged with mastering the arts of Preservation and healing. Wield the powers of time and the Emerald Dream to return those who are wounded to their full might. Where there are injured, the Healing Wings will be there to tend them. Led by Scalecommander Viridia, the Healing Wings shall embody the resilience and fortitude of the Earth-Warder.
After Raszageth's attack, this weyrn was forced to evacuate the Forbidden Reach with the help of Wrathion, Ebyssian, and Nozdormu. Several blue dragonflight members who had been guarding the slumbering dracthyr joined them, now that their job of protecting the Forbidden Reach is done.
Heart of Fear:
Heart of Fear is one of the three launch raids that opened in World of Warcraft: Mists of Pandaria. This is the seat of the mantid dominion, and a place where the queen of the mantid currently resides, possessed by the Sha of Fear.
The entrance to this raid dungeon is in the base of a large rotting tree structure in the west of the Dread Wastes.
Normal mode opened October 30, 2012, first Raid Finder part and Heroic modes opened on November 6, 2012, and second Raid Finder part opened on November 13, 2012. Raid Finder difficulty requires an average item level of 470.
Heart of the Forest: The Heart of the Forest, also known as the celestial tree Tirna Achiad, the Forest's Heart, or the Heart of Ardenweald, in central Ardenweald is from where the Winter Queen and her Court of Night rule over the realm. The interior of the tree is the Covenant Sanctum for the Night Fae Covenant.
Hearthstone (game):
Hearthstone, originally subtitled Heroes of Warcraft, is a free-to-play, digital card game set in the Warcraft universe. It was announced on 22 March 2013 at PAX East 2013, and entered closed beta in the Americas region on 16 August 2013, and in the European region on 4 September 2013. The game entered open beta worldwide on 21 January 2014, and was fully released 11 March 2014.
Hearthstone is available on macOS and Microsoft Windows operating systems, Windows 8 devices, as well as on Android phones and tablets, and iOS devices supporting iPads and iPhones running iOS 12.0 or later with at least 3GB of RAM.
In Hearthstone, players can choose to play as one of eleven legendary Warcraft heroes, taking turns to play cards from their customizable decks to cast potent spells, use heroic weapons or abilities, or summon powerful minions to crush their opponent. 
Players can compete for glory and standing in the game's Ranked Play mode, battle legendary bosses from World of Warcraft's history in adventure mode, or forge a unique deck of randomly selected cards in the Arena, and can complete quests and earn prizes to gain gold and powerful new cards for their collection, constructing formidable decks with which to do battle. Hearthstone is designed to be a quick and accessible card game, that nonetheless features substantial strategic depth for more serious players.
Heartsbane Coven: The Heartsbane Coven is a coven of witches who appeared in Kul Tiras and terrorized the people of Drustvar during the Fourth War. They are humans whose bodies have been contorted by the ancient Drust magic that they wield. When a witch grows powerful enough, they slit their own throats to ascend. Witchcraft has long been a superstition of the people of Drustvar, but only recently did some of these superstitions become a reality.
Helarjar:
The Helarjar is an order created by Helya as a mockery of Odyn's Valarjar. It is composed primarily of Kvaldir, but also includes other undead forces such as Val'kyr. The Helarjar are powerful undead tasked with hunting down heroic warriors and taking their souls to Helheim before Odyn's val'kyr can bring them to the Halls of Valor. The rotting ruins of Tideskorn Harbor are their primary Port of Call outside of Helheim, and it is here where the Maw of Souls can be entered.
Not all kvaldir are made into Helarjar. It is a potential reward for their service.
Living mystic vrykul also serve her as a part of the Helarjar.
They use helhounds and helsquids as attack animals.
Hellfire Citadel: Hellfire Citadel is the headquarters of the fel orcs of Outland, a nearly impenetrable bastion that once served as the base of operations for the orcs of the Old Horde throughout the First and Second Wars. By the time of the Invasion of Draenor, it fell under the control of the Horde of Draenor until the forces of the Alliance Expedition assaulted the citadel to find Ner'zhul. Following the destruction of Draenor, Warchief Kargath Bladefist and his Fel Horde made their home in the citadel, where they were eventually defeated by the forces of the Alliance and Horde during the Invasion of Outland.
Hellscream's Reach: Hellscream's Reach is the Horde faction on Tol Barad that fought the Alliance-aligned Baradin's Wardens for control of the prison island. When in control of the zone of Tol Barad, Hellscream's Reach will offer additional daily quests.
Hellscream's Watch: Hellscream's Watch is a Horde encampment in Ashenvale, located just across the waters from the embattled Astranaar. It is one of the Horde's most contentious fronts in Ashenvale.
Hellsreach Citadel:
Hellsreach Citadel was the main base of the Mag'har Clans on Draenor. It appears to be connected to the Blackrock Foundry and Grimrail Depot, as train tracks run through it, as well as stationed trains.
It was attacked by the Lightbound armies led by High Exarch Yrel while Geya'rah and her forces teleported to Azeroth. Grommash Hellscream stayed back to defend the Citadel, and it is unknown how the battle ended, but the Lightbound forces were much more numerous.
Hero's Rest:
Hero's Rest is located in the center of Bastion. It is overseen by Kalisthene. The area contains the Beacon of Invocation that is able to directly draw the attention of the Polemarch of Bastion, who is the Archon's direct servant. Being a crossroads of Bastion on a rise, it offers breathtaking views, unparalleled steward service, and all manner of training and repair facilities. It is a place of respite for the aspirants of Bastion. It is also the resting place of the Spear of Kalliope.
During the war against the Jailer, Kleia and the Maw Walker arrived here to ask Kalisthene for help getting to the Archon.
High Chieftain Cliffwalker:
High Chieftain Cliffwalker is the leader of Cliffwalker Post in the Stonetalon Mountains. He is vehemently opposed to the efforts of Overlord Krom'gar and General Grebo to destroy Thal'darah Grove (the two orc commanders both believe that the Alliance is hoarding some kind of secret weapon to use against the Horde troops), and is accused of treason against the Horde.
Cliffwalker had sent his son Orthus, who has friends among the night elf druids, to find proof that the Alliance was not hiding a weapon there, and sends the Horde player (holding the rank of Champion in Krom'gar's army at this point) to find him and bring back the proof. Upon arriving, however, Orthus and his druid friends are dead, and Orthus clutches a Krom'gar general's insignia in his dead hand - identifying his killer as General Grebo, who is himself killed by Cliffwalker and the player.
Krom'gar, learning of Grebo's demise (though not the player's role in it), names the player as his new General and journeys to Cliffwalker Post, where he proceeds to burn it to the ground, killing Cliffwalker's wife Masha in the process. The Overlord forces Cliffwalker to watch as a goblin hot-air balloon, carrying a bomb specifically intended for wiping out Thal'darah Grove, completes its ghastly mission; the grove is left as little more than a smoking crater.
At that point, Warchief Garrosh Hellscream arrives from Orgrimmar, having learned of Krom'gar's dishonorable tactics. Sickened by the Overlord's actions, Garrosh "dismisses" Krom'gar from service by dropping him from the edge of Cliffwalker Post to his death. When the Warchief turns to the player, preparing to do the same, Cliffwalker intercedes, setting the facts straight on the player's involvement and begs the Warchief to show mercy. Garrosh, surprised that the chieftain would ask for such a thing after the murder of his mate and son and the destruction of his home, relents, and spares the player's life.
Cliffwalker then proclaimed that he will lay Masha to rest and stay by the crater to begin its healing.
High Rise:
The High Rise (or the high rise) is the top of Thunder Bluff's central mesa and contains the home of High Chieftain Baine Bloodhoof. Outside of the High Chieftain's quarters, Thunder Bluff's populace can witness important decisions and fateful events in an open-air auditorium.
It contains a crude amphitheater around a bonfire. Professional trainers for cooking and fishing can also be found here. It connects to the middle rise and lower rise through the wind rider roost, and to Hunter Rise and Elder Rise by separate rope bridges. This is the only one of the three central rises to not contain a lift to the plains of Mulgore below.
Highborne:
The Highborne (or quel'dorei, meaning "children of noble birth" in Darnassian), were the upper class and a sect of the ancient night elf civilization composed of the favored servitors of Queen Azshara. They had an aptitude for magic. The Highborne were largely responsible for the War of the Ancients, and most of those Highborne who had allied with the demons and survived the war were turned into satyrs or naga. Those who allied with the Kaldorei Resistance before the last battle of the war found themselves exiled from Kalimdor, and eventually became the high elves of the Eastern Kingdoms.
Although to this day there are surviving Highborne, they are not treated as nobility by modern night elf society, and in practical terms the caste ceased to exist over ten millennia ago. One notable exception are the Shen'dralar, a holdout group against the Burning Legion during the War of the Ancients. They were able to defend Eldre'Thalas (now known as Dire Maul) but in doing so became isolated from the rest of night elven society throughout the Long Vigil. However, after the Cataclysm, the Shen'dralar under the leadership of archmage Mordent Evenshade negotiated successfully to rejoin their kaldorei brethren in Teldrassil.
According to Brann Bronzebeard, there is little physical difference between the Highborne and the rest of the kaldorei (save perhaps being slightly pastier), but they consider themselves different enough.
Highmaul: Highmaul is the capital of the Gorian Empire and a raid instance introduced in Warlords of Draenor which opened on December 2, 2014. It features 7 bosses, and serves as the first raid of the expansion. The entrance is in western Nagrand. It is ogre-themed, showing them at the height of their civilization. The layout of the instance is nonlinear, allowing groups to select their own path of progression.
Highmountain Tribe: The Highmountain Tribe is the dominant tribe of the Highmountain tauren of the Broken Isles, currently led by High Chieftain Mayla Highmountain.
Highpass:
Highpass is a small outpost built in the center of Gorgrond and serves as a temporary base for the Rangari draenei and the Alliance led by the commander and Vindicator Maraad. The only major building in this outpost is decided by the commander, which is either the Highpass Logging Camp or the Highpass Sparring Ring.
There is a command table here for completing and starting new garrison missions.
Highvale: The Highvale are a group of high elves that dwell at the Quel'Danil Lodge in the Hinterlands. They are part of the Alliance and have ties of friendship with the Wildhammer dwarves.
Hiri'watha Research Station: Hiri'watha Research Station is a subzone of Hinterlands.  It was formerly known just as Hiri'watha, populated by Witherbark trolls before the Horde took it over during the Cataclysm.
Honeydew Village:
Honeydew Village is a pandaren village in northwestern Jade Forest. The village is made up of brewers and farmers, run by the Honeydews, however, the real heart of the village is the brewery, which is run by the Honeypaws. They make the best Honeybrew anywhere.
The village's usual calm was first disturbed by the Alliance troops, who set up camp in the nearby Thunder Hold and recruited some volunteers to build the Strongarm Airstrip, and later when the Horde gunship Hellscream's Fist reached the land too: in the ensuing battle (that ended with the Alliance forces eradicated and the Horde gunship crashed behind the village) the farms of the village were accidentally bombarded and some barrels of brew were lost too.
Mayor Honeydew agreed to let the Horde stay in the village to care for the wounded and regroup the survivors, but declared that the town had to remain neutral (despite its inhabitants being in fact all affiliated with the Horde).
Honor Hold: Honor Hold is the primary Alliance town on Hellfire Peninsula. A refuge of human, elven, draenei, and dwarven explorers, Honor Hold is the first major town Alliance explorers will encounter while traversing Outland. The town holds a flight path, inn, keep, destroyed barracks, mage tower, stables, blacksmith and a variety of profession trainers and vendors. Vestiges of the Sons of Lothar, veterans of the Alliance that first came into Draenor, have steadfastly held on to this Hellfire outpost. They are now joined by the armies from Nethergarde Keep, Stormwind City, and Ironforge.
Honor's Stand: Guarding the west road between Sun Rock Retreat and the Crossroads, Honor's Stand once consisted of a number of burrows, some badly damaged, as well as watch towers. In the past, it had been the location for many great battles between the Horde and its enemies. The orcs stationed here, including peons tasked with repairing the buildings, were very much conscious of the outpost's illustrious, if short, history, though recently they had been beset by attacks mounted by the Kolkar centaur.
Hope's Landing: Hope's Landing is the initial beachead of the Army of the Light in the Antoran Wastes. It is unlocked during  [45] Securing a Foothold.
Horde:
The Horde (also called the New Horde or Thrall's Horde) is one of the two major political factions of the mortal races in Azeroth, its counterpart being the Alliance which the Horde has traditionally been at war with. Driven by unity, the Horde consists of a coalition of disparate races and cultures loosely joined in an alliance of convenience against a hostile world that would see them destroyed. A faction led by off-worlders and composed of outsiders, the Horde has survived the obstacles of Azeroth by bonding together, fighting as family, comrades, or even uneasy allies. Focused, ferocious, and sometimes monstrous, the Horde values strength and honor and is relentlessly opposed to any who threaten the ideals of freedom and hope, but struggles to keep aggression in check.
During Garrosh Hellscream's reign, the faction was plunged into a state of civil war, divided between Hellscream's pan-orc government he referred to as the "True Horde" and the Darkspear Rebellion, comprised of the remaining Horde races, as well as orcs that have decided to oppose Garrosh, under leadership of Vol'jin. After the Siege of Orgrimmar upon the defeat of Garrosh, Vol'jin was chosen as the new Warchief of the Horde with every leader supporting the choice, even Thrall himself. This also marks the first time, when the Warchief's position was held by a person that isn't an orc, signifying a sense of unity between all the member races of the faction, in Vol'jin's own words - The Horde is a family. Following the disastrous Battle for Broken Shore at the start of the third invasion of the Burning Legion, Sylvanas Windrunner was named the new Warchief by a dying Vol'jin, who with his last breath said she must step out of the shadows to lead.
The Horde has throughout the Warcraft story remained the only force that can match up to the Alliance. These two factions have warred several times with their predecessors (Old Horde, Alliance of Lordaeron) having clashed together in the First, Second, and Third Wars. In the Fourth War, the last major conflict as of Battle for Azeroth, the controversial acts by the Horde Warchief Sylvanas Windrunner eventually caused a Horde rebellion led by Varok Saurfang. This led to a temporary unity between the two factions when Varok asked Anduin Wrynn, High King of the Alliance, for aid in assaulting Orgrimmar to end both the reign of Sylvanas and the enmity between the Horde and Alliance. Ultimately, the rebellion caused the Horde to lose its top leadership when Sylvanas killed Varok and abandoned the Horde. With his death and her abandonment, the Fourth War was considered over, and the Horde discarded the position of Warchief ruling the Horde in favor of a council style leadership, while the two factions began talks of peace, though many surmise it may not last or cannot forgive the atrocities of the past. Currently the Horde and Alliance are in an "uneasy armistice".
The Horde is one of the two factions that player characters belong to―the Alliance being the other―as determined by a given character's race (with the exception of Pandaren which can be both). Besides race, being a member of the Horde or Alliance affects gameplay through what settlements, NPCs, quests, reputation factions and in some cases items and encounters the player may access. Faction mechanics also prevent Horde and Alliance players from talking with each other or making groups together, and most PvP gameplay involves Horde players fighting against Alliance players. The divide between the Horde and Alliance—in regard to gameplay mechanics, story elements, and sometimes in social aspects like faction pride—acts as the core element of the World of Warcraft experience.
Horde Base Camp:
Horde Base Camp is a small camp setup by the Orc Survivors led by Aggra on the Lost Isles. It overlooks the wreckage of the Draka's Fury and ancient night elf ruins. Chawg, a vendor, can also be found here.
Occasionally SI:7 Infiltrators attack the camp.
Horde Council: The Horde Council is the ruling body of the Horde acting in the place of the retired position of Warchief. Each member is considered a representative of their people, if not the racial leader in some cases.
Horde Expedition:
The Horde Expedition is a coalition overseeing the Horde forces established throughout Northrend. Spearheaded by the Warsong Offensive, it consists of the following factions: 

Warsong Offensive - The main army of the Horde in Northrend, unified under Garrosh Hellscream command.
Hand of Vengeance - An expedition of Forsaken sent by Sylvanas Windrunner to eradicate the Scourge with the use of the New Plague.
The Taunka - The unified force of taunka tribes of Northrend under the leadership of high chieftain Roanauk Icemist.
The Sunreavers - An organization of blood elven mages that seek closer cooperation with the Kirin Tor.
Their Alliance counterpart is the Alliance Vanguard.
Horde Runners: The Horde Runners are a group of three elite Horde NPCs that roam the eastern side of the Loch in Loch Modan. They have a tendency to gank unsuspecting Alliance players, and these victims usually return to gank them at a higher level in return.
House Ashvane:
House Ashvane of Bridgeport is one of the four ruling houses of Kul Tiras, which was known for managing the wealth of the archipelago. They also control the Ashvane Trading Company.
Their holdings include the Ashvane Company Yards and Ashvane Docks in Boralus, as well as the town of Bridgeport and the Ashvane Foundry.
House Proudmoore: House Proudmoore is one of four noble houses that rule Kul Tiras. Masters of the sea and commanders of Azeroth's finest navy, the distinguished Proudmoore family has led Kul Tiras for decades from their seat of power in Boralus. Their seat is Proudmoore Keep, located in the city of Boralus. House Proudmoore rules the archipelago of Kul Tiras, commanding both the military and the guard in the form of the Proudmoore Admiralty and the Proudmoore Guard.
House Stormsong:
House Stormsong is one of the four noble houses that rule Kul Tiras. Their seat is the Shrine of the Storm, in the region of Stormsong Valley. It takes a role in the construction of the country's navy.
The Tidesages serve House Stormsong. Following the downfall of Lord Colm Stormsong, the family appears to be led by his nephew, Lord Brannon, who is working arm in arm with the Storm's Wake and deferring to Brother Pike.
House Waycrest: House Waycrest is one of four noble houses that rule Kul Tiras. Their seat is the Waycrest Manor in the region of Drustvar. Before rising as a noble house, the Waycrest family led the war against the Drust, when humans first settled Kul Tiras thousands of years ago. Providing most of the nation's ore and some of its toughest warriors, House Waycrest has been a loyal supporter of House Proudmoore's rule for centuries.
House of Constructs:
The House of Constructs is one of the five houses that rule Maldraxxus. The purpose of this House is the creation of necrotic constructs -- abominations and their ilk, to populate Maldraxxus's armies. However, as of late, Margrave Gharmal has been serving a very different master.  It is the origin of all the abomination constructs of the necrolords and their fleshcrafters, who depend on the art of fleshcrafting embued within their Margrave and used by the Primus in creating Maldraxxus.
The house is not just abominations. Liches are present, such as Faldo Iscar in the Amputory, as well as aranakk in the Thread House, such as Thread Mistress Leeda. The process of creating a construct involves gathering flesh and parts to construct the body, where different types of flesh can provide different effects (such as making the construct impervious or obedience and dexterity as with Kyrian flesh), pulled apart at the Separation Chamber, let liquify and congeal in the central pool, and requiring the flesh be purged of its memories and soul before assembly in order to insert a Maldraxxian soul by a necromancer, such as Faldo Iscar. Alternatively, an existing construct may be separated body and soul by a necromancer. Souls of constructs are kept within and around the Etheric Vault. Bones needed for the constructs are generated from the Ossein Foundry and infused with anima. Stitching the flesh together requires Pristine Fleshstitcher Needles, carved from the bones of Maldraxxus itself, and Razorthread Spool (likely from the Razorthread Spiders seen around the House of Eyes and around the Thread House). Once the body is constructed, the body is pumped full of ascerbic bile and mucilaginous enzymes and then fitted with a heart. Bringing the construct together requires an Abominable Stitching table and anima. The weapons of the constructs are created at the Ossein Foundry.
Each House of Maldraxxus has two Barons, with Baroness Antolyte leading the House's invasion of Bastion and Baron Halis staying in the House of Constructs. The Stitchmasters are elements of the House that resisted Gharmal's warmongering orders, instead remaining true to the vision of the Primus. Most of them were punished for standing against him by having their crafted forms taken from them, reducing them to useless souls. They later joined with the Necrolord Covenant, regaining their forms and helped to take down their former leader.
House of Eyes:
The House of Eyes is one of the five houses that rule Maldraxxus, whose members are called the Eyes. Filled with those who fought, lived, and died by their wits and cunning, it was a tenacious and cunning force in Maldraxxus. As befit its name, it was the intelligence arm of Maldraxxus, gathering intel in the worlds of the living and the dead. The Eyes have developed ways to extract information without words, extracting the memory directly from their mind. Some members are expert marksmen assassins. While regrowing, they've established a method for spying on the other realms, using eyes placed at the House of Rituals, the Eonian Archives, Tirna Vaal and Castle Nathria.
Every House of Maldraxxus has two Barons. Draka and Lady Vashj were the two Baronesses of the House of Eyes, but Draka changed Houses, so only Vashj remains such. Draka, an orc warrior who changed herself from a sickly young woman, into a warrior, is one of its few surviving members, and is now a member of the House of the Chosen.
It was destroyed at some point before the events of Shadowlands, but after the events of Wrath of the Lich King. The House was once protected by the surrounding insects as a first defense, but the spiders have grown increasingly hostile since their fall.
House of Rituals:
The House of Rituals is one of the five houses that rule Maldraxxus. Filled with sorcerers, necromancers, and liches, referred to generally as the Ritualists, the House of Rituals is the afterlife for those of a magical bent, who thrived in war, including the lich Kel'Thuzad. The house is constantly innovating and advancing the art of necromancy with new incantations and formulae. As such, their key advantage in battle is their endless army of risen fighters. Maldracite is used both as a conduit for anima and to drawn runes when in the form of a finely ground dust.
The liches have a very selective application process for entry, and prefer applicants with magical aptitude and will not lower their standards due to the drought or civil war. Acolytes to the house must be tested for the privilege to wear the ritualist's mantle by summoning an elder spirit of Maldraxxus at the Prime Arcanum through the Grimoire of Ancient Summoning. The House of Rituals is known to be unforgiving when it comes to betrayal. As such, the House of Eyes states that loyal Ritualists will not speak about the secrets they know.
Every House in Maldraxxus has two Barons, and the barons of the House of Rituals are, at first, Kel'Thuzad and Baroness Ninadar, but both barons betray Sin'dane in pursuit of power. Ninadar falls subservient to Kel'Thuzad, who aims to become the new Margrave; though she is ultimately slain by the Maw Walker. Kel'Thuzad's alliance to the Jailer revealed, he escapes; abandoning the House of Rituals. Margrave Sin'dane sides with the adventurer after she is saved from an attempt at Kel'thuzad consuming her power, appointing Balmedar as the new Baron of Rituals. One of the duties of one of the Barons is to maintain the libraries of the Grimorium.
Howling Oak:
The Howling Oak was an area in the north of the night elven capital city of Darnassus, centered around large Gilnean oak tree. It was the new home of the refugees who fled Gilneas with the aid of the night elves following the Cataclysm and the Forsaken invasion. The tree itself was a "worgen tree", very similar to Tal'doren in the Blackwald. The area was accessible from the Craftsmen's Terrace and Cenarion Enclave from the southeast and southwest respectively. It was a place where both worgen and night elf druids trained.
The Howling Oak was originally grown through the aid of the night elven druids from a seed taken from Gilneas. It stood for all the Gilneans have endured since the ruin of their kingdom, and all that their people have since accomplished. Shortly after the Gilneans' arrival in Darnassus, King Genn Greymane made an appearance here, as he and his people were greeted personally by Tyrande Whisperwind.
During the War of the Thorns, the Howling Oak was ultimately destroyed alongside Darnassus in the Burning of Teldrassil. However, all the Gilnean refugees were evacuated before the fire started and moved to Stormwind City, where they settled in the area around Olivia's Pond. It was Queen Mia Greymane, as a respected authority figure and the most suitable person available, who appeased the Gilnean people in the area and organized their evacuation with the help of the Highborne mage Maelir.
Hrothgar's Landing:
Hrothgar's Landing is a small island located off the northern coast of Icecrown, in Northrend. The Sea Reaver's Run is the strait between Hrothgar's Landing and the continent.
The adventurers who have risen in the ranks of the Argent Tournament, and were awarded with the title of <Crusader> by the Argent Crusade, were directed to the island with a new series of quests surrounding the kvaldir's taking of the island from the tuskarr.
Hrydshal: Hrydshal is a vrykul city located in southern Stormheim. It serves as the traditional home for the Tideskorn clan, and specifically the Drekirjar, notorious for their taming of the local storm drakes. As the largest settlement in Stormheim, Hrydshal is a major feature in the region and contains one of the largest concentrations of vrykul on the Broken Isles.
Huojin Landing:
Huojin Landing  is the Horde's beachhead on the Timeless Isle, maintained by the Huojin Pandaren. Situated at the northern end of the Timeless Shore, the Misty Strand is found immediately to the northeast, the Celestial Court is inland to the southeast, and the Tushui Landing is found at the southern end of the shore to the south.
The camp and the pandaren are still active as of the discovery of the awakening of the Dragon Isles, and Chen Stormstout, Li Li Stormstout, and Catelyn the Blade passed through it.
Hyjal Barrow Dens:
The Hyjal Barrow Dens is a large and ornate barrow den located northeast of Ruins of Lar'donir in the Verdant Thicket atop Mount Hyjal.
The barrow dens are defended by Barrow Deeps Watchers, affiliated with the Guardians of Hyjal. They are fighting Twilight Assassins who are trying to free Fandral Staghelm, who is held prisoner deep inside. At Alysra's behest, adventurers move Fandral out of the den through the Emerald Dream (evading Nightmare Terrors along the way) and hand him over to Alysra for transport to Moonglade, though in reality Alysra is a traitor and subsequently turns Fandral over to the Twilight's Hammer.
The entrance hallway leads into an area with some small living quarters carved into the sides of the hall. This, in turn, leads to a larger room divided by a small, shallow pond, with a gazebo-covered path going across it. From this room, one can look across a deep lake from a balcony and see that the barrow dens extend far beyond the accessible area. From the room/platform with the pond, one can go through a door to a bridge that goes over deep chasm or underground river. This bridge leads to a room with more small living quarters carved around its circumference, and a small pond with a platform in its center. On that platform stands Captain Saynna Stormrunner, watching over the captive Fandral.
Grotto Voles, Bats, and Schools of Fish can be found here.
Icecrown Citadel:
Icecrown Citadel is the greatest fortress of the Scourge and the last bastion of the dread Lich King. Located in the frozen wastes of Icecrown on the continent of Northrend, the Citadel rises up from the Icecrown Glacier, a cathedral of blades and claws made entirely of saronite. It is a fortress as big as a city, its halls crawling with the most vile and loyal of the Scourge - a great army of the living dead standing between their dark master and those who once sought to destroy him. The fortress is, itself, layer after protective layer of cursed metal wrapped around the Frozen Throne that once held the spirit of Ner'zhul, until he joined with Arthas Menethil to become the new Lich King.
The citadel's southern entrance, Angrathar the Wrathgate, is surrounded by the Court of Skulls, while the fortified northern entrance is surrounded by the Court of Bones. The sole way for any kind of force to invade Icecrown Citadel would be to breach the gates that encompass Icecrown, respectively named Mord'rethar: The Death Gate; then Aldur'thar: The Desolation Gate; and last Corp'rethar: The Horror Gate. Each gate and its wall is made almost entirely of saronite, near indestructible, and manned by massive Scourge constructs.
Icemist Village:
Icemist Village is located on the edge of Lake Wintergrasp within the Dragonblight.
The ravaged settlement was destroyed by undead nerubians and is currently controlled by the Scourge forces out of Azjol Nerub. The Scourge forces here were once led by Under-King Anub'et'kan, who captured the taunka chieftain Roanauk Icemist during the attack. Adventurers of the Horde were later sent to save Roanauk and kill Anub'et'kan.
Ihgaluk Crag:
Ihgaluk Crag  is the home of the Skumblade tribe of saurok on the Isle of Thunder. Situated between Shaol'mara / Violet Rise to the northeast, Za'Tual to the west and the Diremoor to the north, the crag has a commanding view of the southern portion of the isle. The Skumblade practice a particularly nasty way of life, by spreading disease far and wide to weaken their enemies.
The  [Shoulder of the Chamberlain] can be found at one of several locations in the crag for  [32-35W] The Crumbled Chamberlain. There is additionally a cave off on the southeast side of the crag along the shore which houses a Primal Ritual Stone.
Illidari:
The Illidari (also known as Illidan's Forces, or Illidan's forces, and Illidan's army) are the faction of Illidan Stormrage, representing his servants and a specific, elite faction of his demon hunters. Under the Slayer's leadership, it changed to include Broken, naga, shivarra forces. They wield the forbidden powers of the demons they slay to fight the forces of chaos - at any cost.
During the invasion of Outland, the Illidari were one of the prime enemies of the Alliance and Horde, the other being the Burning Legion. From the Black Temple, Illidan commanded vast armies throughout Outland, organizing his forces in their war to end the Burning Crusade. After his defeat, the demon hunter survivors were imprisoned by Maiev Shadowsong in the Vault of the Wardens, along with the corpse of their master.
Years later, during the third invasion of the Burning Legion, the freed Illidari regathered with the forces left behind on Mardum, and seized control of the Fel Hammer, which became their order hall. Under the leadership of the Slayer, Illidan's right arm in his absence, the Illidari fought against the Burning Legion alongside the other class orders, united as the Armies of Legionfall.
Imbu: Imbu is a tuskarr town located in southeastern Azure Span, southwest of Camp Nowhere. The town was attacked by the Primalists and renegade furbolg, and now the tuskarr of the Imbu tribe are fighting to take it back.
Independent: The terms independent or neutral are used for individuals, organizations and factions that are aligned with neither the Alliance nor the Horde.
Indu'le Village: Indu'le Village was a tuskarr village found northwest of Moa'ki Harbor in the Dragonblight. The village along with the villages were destroyed by arcane energies that poured out from the ley line. The Kalu'ak that were not immediately killed, becoming ghosts, by the chaotic magic coming from Lake Indu'le still suffered and become deranged.
Infused Ruby: Infused Rubies are a currency unlocked after completing  [10-60] The Endmire.
Inkgill Mere:
Inkgill Mere is the name of the large lake in southeastern Kun-Lai Summit and also the jinyu village on the eastern bank of the lake. Binan Village can be found on the southwest side of the lake, which feeds the Ancient Passage of the Veiled Stair. Furthermore, this lake is the source of the Yan-Zhe River, coming to an end in the valley at Krasari Falls, pouring into the lake below. In the center of Inkgill Mere is the Inkgill Ritual Island.
The sha have corrupted the mere and the jinyu within it.
Inkgill tribe: The Inkgill are a tribe of jinyu based at Inkgill Mere in Kun-Lai Summit.
