A large graveyard called Seafarer's Rest can be found here as well, along with a hill with Galestorm on it.
Larger battleships are built at Port Fogtide across the water, connected to this strand by the bridge at Tidecross.
Marshal Expeditions: Marshal Expeditions is a non-aligned expedition troupe that is led by the human Marshal siblings: Williden and Hol'anyee.
Marshal's Refuge: Marshal's Refuge was a neutral camp at the northern edge of Un'Goro Crater set up by Marshal Expeditions.
Marshal's Stand:
Marshal's Stand is a fortified base near the road leading from the Marshlands in Un'Goro Crater. To the north is Fire Plume Ridge, a volcano in the center of the crater. After leaving Marshal's Refuge, Marshal Expeditions made their way here and built this small base, making sure they won't be run off so easily again.
By the time of the end of the Fourth War, the camp was reinforced with sturdy walls and watchtowers. After the war, the base was visited by Zekhan and Rexxar.
Marshtide Watch:
Marshtide Watch is an Alliance port outpost north of the Temple of Atal'Hakkar in the Swamp of Sorrows. It is made up of several cannon towers, stables, and a blacksmith.
According to Joanna Blueheart, the commander of the settlement, the regions of Redridge Mountains, Duskwood, and Elwynn Forest are all a day's march from here.
Master Li: Master Li runs the Celestial Tournament from the Celestial Court on the Timeless Isle.
Master's Cellar:
The Master's Cellar is an area riddled with ghosts in the southernmost portion of the Deadwind Pass, just south of Karazhan. It is below the ruins of a small village, probably the former home of servants that worked in the nearby tower of Karazhan. Its lower section is called Lower Cellar.
There are two separate entrances to the Master's Cellar. One leads into a vast wine cellar, filled to the brim with Unliving Residents, Unliving Caretakers, Damned Souls, Restless Shades, and Wailing Spectres. The other leads into a similar cellar, but here the floor has collapsed into a cave system leading deep underground. The second cellar and cave system are also filled with the same type of undead, but there are no named or rare undead of any type to be found.

 This section concerns content related to Cataclysm.
Shortly before the death of Deathwing, Nalice and her followers inhabited the place. The place was infiltrated and Nalice killed by the adventurers on the orders of Wrathion.

 This section concerns content related to Legion.
During the third invasion of Azeroth, the Burning Legion forces took over the cellar during their invasion of Karazhan, and the entrances were guarded by Archmage Leryda and Archmage Alturus.
Mawsworn:
The Mawsworn are minions who serve Zovaal the Jailer in the Maw. They bring pain and punishment to the most wicked of souls. These soldiers are the very worst the damned have to offer: the result of the Jailer torturing mortal souls until only a mere shade of their former glory remains and they willingly serve their tormentor for eternity, all begin as empty suits of armor forged at Zovaal's Cauldron, and then are infused with a decrepit shade to be brought to "life".
The size of the Mawsworn army rivals that of the Burning Legion, and with the soul-river Gorgoa overflowing, their ranks continue to swell. The Mawsworn's weapons and armor were designed by the Runecarver against his will.
Mazthoril: Mazthoril is a huge and deep icy cavern — populated by blue dragons — located near the central part of Winterspring, not far from Lake Kel'Theril or Everlook.
Mechagon City: Mechagon City (commonly referred to as the lost city of Mechagon) is an old gnomish city located on a formerly unexplored island in the Great Sea called Mechagon Island. The Robodrome is located in the entrance to Mechagon. The city can be entered via a Mechagon City Teleporter in Rustbolt or Stormwind Embassy by both factions.
Menagerie of the Master:
Menagerie of the Master is found in the northmost part of the Castle Ward in Revendreth. It connects to Dominance Gate to the west, Redelav District to the east, and to The Eternal Terrace through the Bridge of Temptations, and contains the entrance to the Sanguine Depths. 
Part of the Menagerie of the Master is visibly being pulled into the Maw; off in the distance to the north, you see the tower and some bridge segments falling into the Maw.
Mereldar:
Mereldar  is the capital of the Hallowfall Arathi, located in the western half of Hallowfall, near Beledar. It is named in honor of the priestess Mereldar, one of the first human priests to come into contact with the Holy Light. Players are directed here in  [75-78] To Mereldar, the start of the final chapter of the Hallowfall storyline, though there are optional quests that are available the instant players can fly into Hallowfall.
The instance line to the Priory of the Sacred Flame is located at  in the northwestern part of town.
The area is bordered by the Priory of the Sacred Flame across the river to the north, Lorel's Crossing to the northeast, the Hungering Pool to the east, Dayspring Fields and Beledar's Bounty to the southeast, Light's Redoubt to the south, and the Veneration Grounds (and the Nightfall Sanctum delve) to the west.
Merithra:
Merithra, known as Merithra of the Dream, is the Aspect of the green dragonflight and a child of the former Dragon Aspect Ysera. Following her mother's death, she became the de facto leader of the green dragonflight, until her ascension to Aspect on the Dragon Isles.
During the War of the Ancients, Merithra led the green flight in the Ohn'ahran Plains of the Dragon Isles and forged a pact with Teera, the matriarch of the centaur clans. Millennia later, Merithra played a major role in the War of the Shifting Sands, but was taken captive by the qiraji and trapped in Ahn'Qiraj alongside the red Caelestrasz and the blue Arygos. She remained trapped there for a thousand years before she was freed by adventurers.
During the Fourth War, following Ysera's death, Merithra stepped forward to represent the green dragonflight and worked with a mortal hero to help save the Emerald Dream from an infestation of the Void. While not confident she could live up to her mother's legacy, she decided she would do her best to fulfill the task ahead. When the Dragon Isles reawakened, Merithra led efforts to re-empower her flight's oathstone, and renewed her pact with the centaur clans in order to defend the Emerald Dream from the Primalists.
Mezzamere: Mezzamere is the base of the Waveblade Ankoan in Nazjatar, sitting on a rise in the Hanging Reef. The camp was established by the ankoan when they moved into the region to make war on Queen Azshara's naga forces after they killed the Waveblade leader. Mezzamere is centered around a cluster of ancient kaldorei ruins. Since the waters around Nazjatar were parted during the Nazjatar Campaign, Mezzamere and the surrounding area have become dry land, and now accommodate a large Alliance presence, new allies of the ankoan.
Millstone Hamlet:
Millstone Hamlet is a settlement found in the west of Stormsong Valley and its allegiance is to House Stormsong. Davenport Residence and Netley Inn can be found here.
It is being besieged by the ettins of Sprucewood. Just around and outside of the hamlet, Kickers and Poacher Zane lurk.
Mirror Lake Orchard:
Mirror Lake Orchard is situated in western Elwynn Forest, on the southern banks of Mirror Lake. At some point, Defias bandits had taken possession of the orchard as well as the nearby cottage.

 This section concerns content related to Cataclysm.
During the Elemental Unrest, the area was commandeered by Twilight's Hammer cultists, led by Overseer Sylandra. Alliance adventurers were tasked to infiltrate the cultists' activities.
Since the Cataclysm, the Twilight cultists have left, and three humans - Ian Jolly, Joanna Jolly, and Samantha Cleland - have appeared behind the previously deserted cottage. It is possible they are the original residents of the Orchard.
Mistblade Den: Mistblade Den is a cave found at the south-eastern edge of the Lake of Stars in the Dread Wastes. It serves as a base of operations for the Mistblade tribe.
Mistcaller's Cave: Mistcaller's Cave is a cave on the western side of Hrothgar's Landing.  Mistcaller Yngvar has taken up residence here and from this cave he manipulates the mists to conceal the Kvaldir and the sea beasts they command.
Mistfall Village: Mistfall Village can be found in southwestern Vale of Eternal Blossoms, below the Tu Shen Burial Ground to the east, and across the river from the Setting Sun Garrison to the west.
Mists of Tirna Scithe: Mists of Tirna Scithe is a dungeon in Shadowlands located in Ardenweald. Cursed to exist outside the cycle of Life and Death, the Drust seek to circumvent their fate using Ardenweald's mechanisms of Rebirth. Their would-be conquest has found its way to Tirna Scithe, where Ingra Maloch and his followers use foul magic to subjugate the local inhabitants.
Mistwhisper Refuge: Mistwhisper Refuge is an outpost of the Oracles clan of gorlocs in northwest Sholazar Basin. It is bordered by the Bittertide Lake to the south, Dorian's Outpost to the northwest, the Savage Thicket to the north, and the Glimmering Pillar to the east. The nearest Frenzyheart Tribe of wolvar is located just to the northwest of Dorian's at Spearborn Encampment.
Misty Reed Farm:
Misty Reed Farm is a farm in the Swamp of Sorrows. It used to be Misty Reed Post.
During the Fourth War, it was used by Varok Saurfang as a hideout after he escaped from Stormwind City. Dark Ranger Lyana and Deathguard Elites arrived here to kill Varok on orders of Sylvanas Windrunner. Lyana threatened to burn it like Teldrassil was burnt. Varok was defended by Zekhan and the Horde champion and the attackers killed. Afterwards, Varok left the farm and Zekhan returned to Orgrimmar.
Mmarl:
Mmarl is a niffen settlement found in Azj-Kahet. Mmarl has been around for a long time, longer than Loamm. The niffen there have managed to set up trade with the nerubians of Azj-Kahet and some of them are even able to trade in the City of Threads. In the past, the nerubians tried to forcibly "conscript" the Mmarl niffen to work for them in Rak-Ush, but they failed and now the nerubians are banned from the town.
In recent times the niffen came into contact with a group of Venture Company goblins, led by Jenni Boombuckle, who excavated their way into Azj-Kahet and set up camp at the edge of Mmarl. The goblins also built a robot fighting arena in what is now called the Grudge Grotto. When they arrived, the goblins replaced the incense the niffen used to keep nerubian flyers away, because of its bad smell. This eventually caused the flyers to emerge again and start preying on the goblins. Monte Gazlowe and adventurers helped the niffen and the goblins solve this bug infestation.
Later, the adventurers also helped the nerubians in Rak-Ush to contact the niffen again and recruit some of their arachnologists to help tend to the swarmbeasts.
When a group of niffen were captured by kobyss in Tak-Rethan Abyss, Vetiverian asked Brann Bronzebeard and adventurers to help rescue them.
Mo'grosh: The Mo'grosh are a group of ogres that have taken up residence to the northeast of Loch Modan.
Mo'grosh Stronghold: Mo'grosh Stronghold is a set of ogre-infested caves located in northeastern Loch Modan. The Mo'grosh ogres number several darkmaulers and earthbenders, and serve the Twilight's Hammer. They are in progress of defiling the land with the elementium spikes, just as their neighbors did at the camp on the drained Loch, and must be stopped. The ogres are led by the disciple of Cho'gall himself, Gor'kresh.
Mogu empire:
The mogu empire (or Mogu Dynasty) possessed immense size and strength. The mogu built it based on might, in which the weak — other races — were subjugated, and the strong — always mogu — ascended to power. So brutal was their regime that its name is never uttered aloud: pandaren call it either the "Old Kingdom" or "First Dynasty". The mogu empire was a meritocracy, where the previous regime and/or dynasty must be overpowered and executed. 
The mogu empire was founded by Lei Shen, "The Thunder King." He united the mogu, defeated the other pandaren races, and built an empire that would last for thousands of years.
Mogu'shan Palace:
Mogu'shan Palace is a dungeon added in World of Warcraft: Mists of Pandaria, located within the Palace structure at the eastern edge of the Vale of Eternal Blossoms. During the mogu reign over Pandaria, this palace served as the seat of power and capital of their immense empire.

 This section concerns content related to Battle for Azeroth.
During the Assault in the Vale of Eternal Blossoms, Magni Bronzebeard and an adventurer entered the palace following Ra-den's advice, seeking to activate the Engine of Nalak'sha. The areas they visited were devoid of mogu, leaving behind only a few terracotta warriors, traps, and Trapped Saurok in the tunnels below. The pair took one of the tunnels that led to the Mogu'shan Vaults.
Mok'gol Watchpost: Mok'gol Watchpost is a Warsong clan fortification overseen by Packleader Vor'gash located in Nagrand. More recently, raiders from Mok'gol have been terrorizing travelers in Nagrand. Loot from these raids can be found in chests throughout the camp, which typically contain a few gold and some poor equipment.
Molsen Farm:
The Molsen Farm is one of the many farms of Westfall that have once been taken over by the Defias Brotherhood. Since the fall of the organization, only the deadly mechanical Harvest Watchers roam the fields. Private Molsen of the Westfall Brigade may have a family connection with the farm.

 This section concerns content related to Legion.
During the Burning Legion's invasion, the area fell under the Burning Legion's control. Its residents were enslaved by nathrezim and were later killed by the defenders.
Moon Guard:
The Moon Guard (also spelled the Moonguard or simply the Guard) are an elite group of night elf sorcerers who served as protectors and peace-keepers of Ancient Kalimdor. The order was established long before even the War of the Ancients and its members included talented spell-casters who dedicated themselves to upholding the peace and security of the Kaldorei Empire and its capital, Zin-Azshari. Owing allegiance to no noble or lord, save for Queen Azshara herself, the Moon Guard played an active role in the War of the Ancients, operating from the city of Suramar.
In more recent times, during the third invasion of the Burning Legion, the Moon Guard became active once again and was involved in a brutal conflict with the Nightborne on the Broken Isles. Following the Nightfallen rebellion, the surviving members restored the organization under the leadership of Lothrius Mooncaller.
Moon Guard Stronghold: Moon Guard Stronghold is a large fortress in northern Suramar. The Moon Guard there have been recently killed by the nightborne armed forces.
Moonbrook:
Moonbrook is a small town located southwest of Sentinel Hill, which once served as a mining town and the focal point of the farmlands in Westfall. After being razed by the orcs during the First War, then rebuilt following the Second War, the rampant corruption in the kingdom brought the town under the control of the Defias Brotherhood. Without the Stormwind Army to protect them, the Defias drove out the citizens and used the Deadmines as their headquarters. After years of tyranny, the People's militia and the adventurers liberated Moonbrook after they killed the Brotherhood's leader, Edwin VanCleef.
However, the war against the Lich King caused a financial crisis in the kingdom, and a high population of the homeless came to settle in Moonbrook. Following the Cataclysm, the Defias Brotherhood made a resurgence, and its leader Vanessa VanCleef encouraged the anti-Stormwind sentiment among the people of Moonbrook. After the attack on Sentinel Hill, the Alliance heroes entered the Deadmines once again, where they wiped out all the new Defias leadership. In the following years, the town was once more supported by Stormwind, which protected it from bandits, the Riverpaw pack gnolls, and even demonic invasions. After his coronation, King Anduin Wrynn's reforms and aid to Westfall extinguished the spark of the revolution in the town.
Although the town itself is devoid of vendors, the nearby camp of the Westfall Brigade to the northwest has a flight path and a few vendors.
Mor'shan Base Camp: Mor'shan Base Camp, one of the more sizable Horde settlements in the Northern Barrens, is located just south of the Ashenvale-Barrens border, near the Mor'shan Rampart. It is the base of the Warsong Outriders and also the location of the Horde entrance to the Warsong Gulch battleground.
Mor'shan Rampart:
The Mor'shan Rampart lies at the northern terminus of the Gold Road in Northern Barrens. This makeshift defensive post was built to withstand the push of Alliance forces into the region from Ashenvale to the north. The rampart and its watch towers still serve as a makeshift launching point for raids on the night elven town of Astranaar.
Following the Cataclysm the rampart has come under attack by the Alliance. Ashenvale Skirmishers regularly charge the rampart and engage in combat with the Mor'shan Defenders, while Ashenvale Bowmen shoot arrows at them.
Following the Siege of Orgrimmar, the ramparts were abandoned by the Horde and taken by the night elves. During the War of the Thorns, the elves were killed by two Horde rogues.
Although originally a strong and reinforced bulwark of the Horde, the chaos of the Cataclysm and unending military pushes saw the Alliance claim the Mor'shan Rampart at long last. The area was changing hands between the Alliance and Mor'shan defenders since then. As of the end of the Fourth War, the area is held by the Alliance's troops.
Morgan's Plot:
Morgan's Plot is a small decrepit church with a graveyard and crypt located in Deadwind Pass. It can be found just behind Karazhan, and its graveyard serves as the respawn and spirit healer point for adventurers who die within the actual Karazhan instance. Lydia Accoste is found here.
The chapel itself was once inhabited by two Unliving Residents, and there was a third patrolling just down the hill.
Aegwynn and Cook are buried here, and Moroes and Medivh were before they were revived.

 This section concerns content related to Legion.
Since the third invasion of the Burning Legion, the place is now inhabited by Restless Spirits.
Morning Breeze Village: Morning Breeze Village is a pandaren village found west of the Temple of Five Dawns on the Wandering Isle.
Morqut Islet:
Morqut Islet  is an island found off the western shore of the Forbidden Reach. Morqut Village is on the eastern side of the islet, and the Zskera Vaults are on the north.
The islet is bordered by the Tempest Cove to the north, the Tempest Coast to Caldera of the Menders to the northeast, Aerie Chasm to the east, Sharpscale Coast of the Old Weyrn Grounds to the southeast, Talon's Watch to the south, and Sylvern's Roost to the west.
The Irontide Raiders have set up a beachhead on the northern shore.
The Morqut Ascent dragonriding race starts at  just south of the village, and there's a Dormant Waygate at  in the tower overlooking the village from the south.
Inside the cave with a mouth at  halfway up the eastern face of the mountain at  can be the rare Loot Specialist.
Morqut Village:
Morqut Village  serves as the quest hub and sanctuary of the max-level Forbidden Reach.
Situated on the eastern shore of Morqut Islet, itself off the western shore of the greater Forbidden Reach, the village is bordered by the Tempest Cove to the north, the Tempest Coast of the Caldera of the Menders to the northeast, the Aerie Chasm to the east, and the Sharpscale Coast of the Old Weyrn Grounds to the southeast. On the islet itself, Zskera Vaults is northwest of the village.
Renpiaq, the flight master, has connections to Wingrest Embassy in the Waking Shores, and the Veiled Ossuary in Thaldraszus.
Mortwake's Tower: Mortwake's Tower, formerly Klaven's Tower (named after its rogue Defias master Klaven Mortwake) lies at the southeastern edge of Westfall near the river and north of the Dagger Hills.
Mosh'Ogg:
The Mosh'Ogg tribe of ogres live in the jungles of Stranglethorn Vale. They are rumored to be in possession of a powerful stone that may be of use to the Horde.
During the war against the Zandalari, both the Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound and Mizjah Ruins were overrun by Jungle Serpents and all the ogres were killed.
Following the war against the Primalists, the Mosh'Ogg were revealed to have returned to the Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound. As Rokhan and Kevo ya Siti looked for Lukou, they discovered her within the mound. Realizing that Mai'Zoth was holding the loa, Rokhan sent the Darkspear champion to kill Mai'Zoth and free Lukou.
Mosshide tribe: The Mosshide tribe is a gnoll tribe native to Wetlands. After the Cataclysm, the tribe also moved into Loch Modan, where they took control of the Tunnel Rat kobolds and planned to take over the region by forming an alliance with the Bluegill murlocs.
Mosswalker Village:
Mosswalker Village is the ravaged village of the gorloc Mosswalker tribe, located in the Lost Lands and south of The Avalanche in Sholazar Basin.
During the war against the Lich King, all its residents fled or were killed by the undead Scourge when the Lifeblood Pillar fell, which allowed the Scourge to invade the region from Icecrown.
Following the war against the Jailer, the brothers Bronzebeard reported that the village is still in ruins.
Mossy Pile: Mossy Pile is a small fortified camp located just northwest of Fire Plume Ridge in Un'Goro Crater. It's here that a few goblins from Gadgetzan, while working with Marshal Expeditions, exploit the area for profit.
Mount Kajaro:
Mount Kajaro is a still-active volcano on the Isle of Kezan. According to Al'tabim the All-Seeing, Kajaro is an area plagued by volatility - marked by violent and oftentimes magical volcanic eruptions. Kaja'mite was mined underneath it. The Undermine is believed to be situated deep in the bowels of the mountain.
During the Cataclysm, Deathwing attacked Mount Kajaro, setting it alight, causing it to become active again and later erupt, destroying Bilgewater Port and possibly other parts of the island.
Jastor Gallywix considers it a possibility that his cartel's deep digging into Kezan may have contributed to the volcano's eruption.
Mourning Rise:
Mourning Rise  is a graveyard overtaken by the Candlelit kobolds in northeastern Isle of Dorn. The Kriegval's Rest delve is found at  on the lowest level.
The rise is bordered by the Fallside Outpost to the west, the Oath Gate and Stoneward's Rise of Dornogal to the northwest, Rambleshire to the north-northwest, the Cinderwold to the northeast, the Ironwold to the east and southeast, and Durgaz Cabin immediately to the southeast.
The Wold Ways skyriding race is at  just to the southwest.
Mudsprocket: Mudsprocket is a goblin town in the south-west of Dustwallow Marsh. It is a quest hub with a flight master, inn, graveyard, anvil, forge and mailbox. This town's faction is tied with Gadgetzan and it contains a goblin laboratory.
Mulgore:
The green, verdant plains of Mulgore are home to the noble tauren. Mulgore is nestled in the foothills of the Stonetalon Mountains to the north, and protected by a natural wall of mountains on all sides. The only pass through these mountains is currently closed off by the Great Gate, which leads into the Southern Barrens to the east. 
Mulgore provides bounty for the hunt, as a diversity of wild beasts roam the rolling plains and climb the foothills of the surrounding range. In the northern section of Mulgore, the new Camp Sungraze sits in the shadows of the mesas of Thunder Bluff, a tauren city which towers above the plains. Bloodhoof Village is centrally located and surrounded by the clear waters of Stonebull Lake, while further south on Red Cloud Mesa, Camp Narache stands as the principal training camp for all young tauren.
Despite the serene landscape and the pine-scented breeze, Mulgore is fraught with trouble. Brambleblade Ravine and the sacred Red Rocks are overrun by quilboars, and they continue to spread into the rest of Red Cloud Mesa. The goblin-run Venture Company infests the Venture Co. Mine in the eastern mountain face, while the Grimtotem tribe try to take vengeance against the other tauren by poisoning their water wells. The Windfury harpy tribe lay claim to the extreme northern reaches of Mulgore and the southeast mountain face. A tribe of gnolls known as the Palemane make their home at the cave called Palemane Rock, as well in scattered camps along the southern mountains.
Naga:
The serpentine naga (/ˈnɑːɡə/ NAH-gə) (sometimes pluralized as nagas) are some of the most formidable villains of Azeroth. Masters of sorcery, the naga were formerly Highborne night elves, members of Queen Azshara's court during the age of the Kaldorei Empire. Following the War of the Ancients, and the Great Sundering caused by the destruction of the Well of Eternity, they were transformed into naga by the Old God N'Zoth after Azshara pledged herself to his cause, dedicating her people to become his army and recreate the Black Empire on Azeroth. Since their transformation, they haunted the seas of Azeroth, building a great civilization on the ocean floor in the name of their queen.
They have since stayed out of major world affairs for over 10,000 years, until the Third War, when they have been rising up to the surface for nefarious purposes. An expedition led by Lady Vashj notably answered the call of Illidan Stormrage after the Battle of Mount Hyjal, they joined the ranks of the Illidari to confront the Lich King in Northrend and the Burning Legion in Outland, in order to further the plans of their dark masters. Many tribes of naga also appeared to invade the coasts and beaches of all continents, beginning a campaign against the land dwellers. During the Cataclysm, N'Zoth ordered the naga to go to war against Neptulon, the Elemental Lord of water, in order to become the masters of the seas.
Nal ks'kol:
Nal ks'kol  is a titan facility in southeastern Zaralek Cavern. Players visit the facility for the duration of the second chapter of the Embers of Neltharion campaign, "Sundered Legacy", starting with  [70] Future Aspects.
The area is surrounded by the Crystal Fields to the north and northwest, and bordered by the Sundered Flame Camp to the west.
The area is occupied by Nal ks'kol Defense Orbs, Redolent Whelks, and the occasional Sundered Defender pushing out from their camp.
Outside is a large stone called Binding Oaths, one of the  [Ancient Stones of Zaralek] criteria:

Binding Oaths
When at last we breached these hidden halls, the master was wroth.
He murmured angry words about Tyr's many secrets. I judged it unwise to press him further.
But when we presented the artifact we'd found, his mood brightened.
"The ideal soldier never questions orders," he told us.
The glove fit as though it had been made for him. Before long, the master returned to his experiments, heartened that he would soon succeed.
Inside are a number of Informational Plaques in front of objects of note. Clockwise from the entrance, they read:

Galakrond boulder
A fragment of the boulder that killed Galakrond.
Let this serve as a reminder to always adapt when faced with seemingly insurmountable problems.
Proto-drake egg shell
A protodrake egg shell.
A reminder to never forget how far we have come and what we as dragons have achieved.
Nozdormu trinket
A trinket favored by Nozdormu.
We have lost track of when it is as well as where.
Galakrond's claw
A fragment of Galakrond's claw.
Nath'raxas Hold:
Nath'raxas Hold is a fortified city in Krokuun. Nath'raxas Spire and the Court of the Avenger make up the inner keep.
It is one of the Legion's chief military fortifications on Argus. The Army of the Light attacked it, but was defeated, and their ruined camp can be found alongside ruined batteries and a draenei bunker, which is inspected by Vagath the Betrayed. The Lightforged armaments were eventually retrieved.
There is an infernal production pit on the grounds of the hold.
Natha'vor:
Natha'vor is a blood troll village in Nazmir.
The women of the tribe are cannibals that eat the men and refer to their witch doctors as "corpse mongers". Root-Hexxer Ib'aka uses their sacrifices to feed Bloodlasher Seedlings.
A treasure chest can be found in a building on the east side of the area.
Natha'vor tribe: The Natha'vor tribe is a tribe of blood trolls located in a village of the same name. The tribe is known for its heavy ritualistic practice of cannibalism, the women eating the males of the tribe and anything they capture believing that the practice grants them greater power. In addition to the eating of their own tribe and captured individuals, the tribe sacrifices some of the unfortunate souls to serve as food for the monstrous mawfiends they train and raise to aid the tribe in combat.
Nazjatar Empire:
The Nazjatar Empire is the naga civilization beneath the Great Sea, formed by Queen Azshara and her followers in the wake of the Great Sundering and the birth of the naga race.
The naga of Nazjatar are masters of sorcery and natural dwellers of the ocean deeps.
Nazmani tribe:
The Nazmani tribe is a tribe of blood trolls inhabiting Zul'Nazman in Nazmir.
The Alliance also dealt with them. They seemed to be originally friendly and open to trade and fight against the Horde. Captain Conrad established a trust with the tribe, having been believed to be a messenger of G'huun.
It was formerly a Zandalari tribe.
Nazzivian: Nazzivian is a satyr encampment located in southwestern Bloodmyst Isle. It serves as the base of operation for the Nazzivus sect.
Nazzivus: Nazzivus (or the Nazzivian) is a sect of satyrs based in the camp of Nazzivian in Bloodmyst Isle.
Necrolord Covenant:
The warlike necrolords of Maldraxxus, also called the Maldraxxi, are one of the Covenants in the Shadowlands. They forge the undead armies that serve as the first line of defense for the Shadowlands and honor those who seek power and glory in battle. All Necrolords receive a portion of the Primus' power in order to carry out their duty.
Warlike souls who never yield or bow—and are willing to strive against one another for greatness—will find a home in Maldraxxus. While Maldraxxus is home to wicked beings like necromancers and abominations, not everyone here is evil. The Necrolords welcome all who are mighty and driven, such as the indomitable Warlord Draka. They follow the creed of "survival of the fittest".
Necropolis (Nazmir):
The Necropolis is the temple of Bwonsamdi in Nazmir. The spirits of departed trolls can be seen approaching it. Being in the area when you are dead allows you to see numerous troll spirits going toward the Necropolis, which can also be seen in reality but much more transparent.
The Offering to Bwonsamdi chest is found in a ruined building on the northeast side of area. Treasure chestscan be found in the northwest and the building in the east.
Needlerock Slag:
Needlerock Slag is the home of the stone trogg within Deepholm. The town is located just north of the Fractured Front and Stonehearth. 
The Earthen, which has been warring with the troggs for thousands of years, have brought the battle into their home after the troggs invaded Stonehearth and captured the Stonefather. The stone trogg mystics have control over the fungal giants that sprouted below and send them to attack the Earthen.
Neferset City:
Neferset City is the capital of the Neferset tribe, a faction of tol'vir, found in southern Uldum. The Neferset have sworn allegiance to Deathwing in exchange for returning to their immortal stone selves, which many tol'vir lost to the Curse of Flesh. The people of Neferset are in conflict with the people of Ramkahen and now kill their tol'vir brethren, looting tombs and searching for a powerful artifact for their master. The city and its people are ruled by Dark Pharaoh Tekahn. Neferset City is the seat of their power, and the Ramkahen have assembled their troops within the Neferset City Outskirts to the north in order to make a final, destructive assault against their brethren in an attempt to stop them and thwart Deathwing's plans. With the help of adventurers, the Ramkahen are able to defeat Dark Pharaoh Tekahn and take control of Neferset City.
What survivors remained of the Neferset headed for the Lost City where they made their new seat of power, with the help of Siamat.

 This section concerns content related to Battle for Azeroth.
By the time of the events of the Black Empire Campaign, the city was under the control of the Ramkahen and Uldum Accord.
Nek'mani Wellspring: The Nek'mani Wellspring is a sacred spring located high in the cliffs overlooking the Southern Savage Coast on the west side of the Cape of Stranglethorn. Its Holy Spring dispenses the only clean freshwater south of Duskwood. The spring is the subject of great conflict among religious scholars, since every race in Azeroth claims that the waters were made divine for their people. An expedition of naga explorers have recently advanced on the spring and guard it ferociously.
Neltharaku: Neltharaku is the the patriarch of Netherwing dragonflight, the faction of nether drakes of Outland, and the mate of Karynaku.
Neltharion's Lair:
Neltharion's Lair is the cavern located in Highmountain, southeast of Thunder Totem. It was here where Neltharion lived before he became Deathwing. Class leaders ventured inside to recover the  [Hammer of Khaz'goroth] stolen by Dargrul the Underking. The entrance is at Snowblind Mesa  - a short walk East up the hill from the cliffs behind Thunder Totem. The dragon-sized entrance is Neltharion's Vault.
The exit (up a path to the right of the last boss, Dargul, marked by torches) takes you to The Bartering Cave behind Spiritwatch Point. A fake portal that Dargrul destroys can be found at Understone Breach. Note that this is the only exit route for Mythic dungeons, other than leaving the group and then being re-invited, to get repairs done without an  [Auto-Hammer] or  [Jeeves].
Neptulon: Neptulon the Tidehunter is the Elemental Lord of water and the master of the Abyssal Maw. In past ages, Neptulon was one of the Old Gods' lieutenants and was defeated by the Pantheon of Order and their titan-forged, who imprisoned him and his water elementals within the Elemental Plane. During the Cataclysm, the Tidehunter refused to ally himself with Deathwing, and as a result, N'Zoth sent his naga and faceless ones to capture him. After breaking free from his captor, the kraken Ozumat, Neptulon returned to the Throne of the Tides, from where he has since assisted the adventurers on multiple occasions. He notably agreed to defend Azeroth during the third invasion of the Burning Legion and later sent his forces to oppose Queen Azshara's armies during the Nazjatar Campaign.
Nesingwary Base Camp:
The Nesingwary Base Camp is Hemet Nesingwary's new location in Northrend. The base camp is located in western Sholazar Basin, just north of the Seabreach Flow, inside the Path of the Lifewarden, southwest of the Suntouched Pillar and west of the Wildgrowth Mangal. It serves as a full-fledged camp with a quest givers, an innkeeper, and a flight path.
This is basically where his ship ended up after crashing through the river's entrance from the North Sea, thinking the Seabreach Flow might be a good river inland and finding too late he was wrong. After the war against the Lich King, the Nesingwary's Safari moved on to other hunting grounds.
Following the war against the Jailer, the brothers Bronzebeard visited the grounds of the former camp, thinking to see if the jungle had fully reclaimed it. However, they were surprised to find tents and Hemet Nesingwary himself. The greatest hunter of Azeroth explained that he'd been passing through and wanted to take a look at Sholazar for a few days. He then showed them what bits of rotted wood remained of the ship he crashed in here so many years ago, and all of them did a bit of target shooting for fun in the camp.
Nesingwary Safari (group): The Nesingwary Safari, also known as the Nesingwary Expedition or Hemet's Hunting Party, are the various adventurers and big game hunters who accompany the legendary dwarven hunter and Alliance war hero Hemet Nesingwary in his travels around Azeroth and beyond. Only those with exceptional hunting skills are allowed to join Hemet's hunting parties.
Nesingwary's Safari: Nesingwary's Safari, latest location of legendary hunters Hemet Nesingwary and his son, Hemet Nesingwary Jr., can be found in the southwest corner of the Valley of the Four Winds. Bordered to the west by the Dustback Gorge, the north by the Torjari Pit, and to the east by the Wild Plains, plenty of wildlife roam the area to meet their untimely demise by the father-son duo.
Netherwing:
The Netherwing, sometimes called the Netherwing dragonflight, are the main faction of the nether dragons in Outland and Azeroth.
Although generally hostile to most humanoids based on their treatment by the Dragonmaw clan of orcs in Shadowmoon Valley, they can be swayed to change their attitude if tasks to aid them are completed. After joining the Valdrakken Accord, they came to be represented by Vyranoth as their aspect, serving as the newly dubbed Aspect of Storms; who also represents the Thorignir.
New Agamand:
New Agamand is a Forsaken town in the Howling Fjord. The town is presumably named after the Agamand family and their haunted mills, a symbol of the prosperity of Tirisfal Glades before the Plague of Undeath. Unlike other towns controlled by the Forsaken — which are actually ruined villages in northern Lordaeron, for the most part — it was built in the distinctive Forsaken architectural style, which can be described as dark, gothic, and spindly.
During the war against the Lich King, New Agamand was at the front line of the Forsaken efforts against the Scourge. Since Sylvanas Windrunner's rise to power, the Royal Apothecary Society in the Undercity have been developing a "New Plague" intended to wipe out the Scourge. After several years of research, the Forsaken were ready to unleash their ultimate weapon against Arthas' forces, and it was tested at New Agamand, turning the land around the town dead and brown in the otherwise verdant landscape.
After the war against the Jailer, the brothers Bronzebeard reported that the town was still active and run by the Forsaken.
New Cifera:
New Cifera is a small pandaren village found at the base of the Pools of Purity in north-central Valley of the Four Winds. Once the special lotuses from the Pools of Purity arrive in the village, they are sorted out and sent around all of Pandaria by the Traveling Traders.
This village appears to have been a jinyu village before it was abandoned for unknown reasons. What ever structures that might have been here, have since been removed and pandaren structures built in their place.
New Thalanaar:
New Thalanaar is a night elf outpost located in the far east of Feralas, and was built after the original Thalanaar was flooded. It is currently under siege by Grimtotem forces. As a result, Alliance players are quickly asked to make their way out of the war zone to the dock where a boat awaits to take them to Fizzle and Pozzik's Speedbarge. New Thalanaar remained under siege by the Grimtotem for several months.
There is a one-way trip here from Shadebough via the quest  [15-30] To New Thalanaar from Falfindel Waywarder, a refugee from Thalanaar.
Newhome: Newhome is the settlement of the Unshackled in Nazjatar. After the Horde crashed into the Queen Azshara's realm, Neri Sharpfin found the Horde heroes and invited them to make Newhome their refuge.
Nifflevar:
Nifflevar is a vrykul town belonging to the Dragonflayer clan, located high atop the cliffs surrounding Daggercap Bay in Howling Fjord. Sitting in the shadow of Utgarde Keep itself, it is much larger than Wyrmskull Village and high on the cliffs.
Many of the wooden vrykul houses are built over the edge of the cliff, with naught but a walkway between a person and a long fall followed by a final splash. The village boasts a number of harpoon guns of different sizes, all of them trained on Daggercap Bay below. A large portion of Nifflevar's structures is built onto the cliff face.
During the war against the Lich King, Nifflevar was one of several vrykul strongholds in the area targeted by the Horde and Alliance as they pushed further into Northrend. In particular, the Forsaken of Vengeance Landing would assail the town's defenses to beat the Alliance to the prize. Thoralius the Wise here learned about the origin of humans.
Night Fae Covenant:
The mystic night fae of Ardenweald fiercely defend the spirits of nature from those who would deprive them of rebirth. They tend those who pass on with a deep connection to nature, retrieving anima from mortal souls and infusing it into slumbering spirits, rejuvenating their lives with the remnants of the old. They are led by the Winter Queen.
The demigod Cenarius spent time recovering in Ardenweald so that he could return to Azeroth during the events of the Cataclysm. It is a beautiful, yet deceptively dangerous land.
Joining the Night Fae makes you a hunter of the Wild Hunt, a champion of the Court of Night and protector of Ardenweald.
Night Watch: The Night Watch is a policing militia created to defend Darkshire from the dangers plaguing Duskwood. The most prominent dangers they face are the undead of Raven Hill Cemetery and Tranquil Gardens Cemetery, and the worgen of Brightwood Grove and Roland's Doom. For at least twenty years, the Night Watch did what it could to keep the region safe, often relying on the recruitment of citizens and passersby to aid in their defense. Individual members are referred to as Watchers, Night Watchers, or Watchmen. They have their own office in Darkshire.
Nightbane pack:
The Nightbane pack (or simply the Nightbane) are a pack of worgen in Duskwood. The Nightbane consists of former humans of Duskwood, transformed by the worgen curse. Their most prominent presence is in Brightwood Grove, west of Darkshire, but they are said to have come from Roland's Doom, a cave to the south. There, Jitters found a mysterious scythe jutting from the cave wall. When he pulled it free, the worgen spontaneously began to appear, and have since grown in number.
Once led by Gervase, the Nightbane pack also served Alpha Prime, with Revil Kost referring to them as the Wolf Cult. After the death of Gervase at the hand of the adventurers, Marus succeeded him as the new leader of the Nightbane pack.
Nightfallen (faction):
The Nightfallen (also called Dusk Lily rebels  or simply the Dusk Lily) are a dissident nightfallen and nightborne faction that led a rebellion to overthrow Grand Magistrix Elisande and her demonic allies. Under the leadership of First Arcanist Thalyssra, the Nightfallen successfully took control of Suramar City, then supported the defenders of Azeroth in their wider fight against the Burning Legion.
For most of the rebellion, their main headquarters were located in the underground complex of Shal'Aran, though they maintained bases and safehouses throughout Suramar. Having come to power in the city, they are now based in the Nighthold palace, seeking to forge a new future for their people. They eventually pledged the loyalty of the kingdom of Suramar to the Horde prior to the Fourth War.
Nighthaven:
Nighthaven is the main settlement in the Moonglade. It is a primarily night elven village that is the home to the druids of the Cenarion Circle.
The village is located on the shores of Lake Elune'ara. It features night elvish architecture, some of it with stone walls. It also has a pair of moonwells. Nighthaven's location is considered remote and the village is usually sequestered to outsiders. It caters mostly to druids, who have an ability to teleport here and have access to exclusive flight masters. There are trainers for druidism and herbalism in the town, as well as a number of unique vendors, such as a specialty dressmaker, Geenia Sunshadow. The village is also home to the Nighthaven Inn, which can be visited during the Kirin Tor Tavern Crawl.
The town is the center of the Lunar Festival, and for this holiday it opens up to outsiders. The druids welcome members of both the Alliance and Horde to celebrate and shoot fireworks - a symbol of Elune's power. During the event, non-druids can also teleport here with a  [Lunar Festival Invitation]. For the duration of the festival, a number of special vendors and quests can be accessed here.
Nijel's Point: Nijel's Point is an Alliance and Cenarion Circle outpost located in the northern mountains of Desolace. It holds flight paths to Feathermoon Stronghold, Theramore Isle, and Lor'danel.
Niuzao: Niuzao the Black Ox (/njuːˈzaʊ/ nyoo-ZOW) is one of the four creatures known as the August Celestials who watch over Pandaria. Niuzao watches over the Townlong Steppes and Dread Wastes and is sometimes referred to as the Western Celestial. He is the spirit of fortitude. He has been referred to as the strength of the west and protector of the weak. As such, he is served by the Niuzao Sentinels.
Niuzao Temple:
Niuzao Temple is a temple dedicated to the August Celestial Niuzao, serving as the headquarters of the Niuzao Sentinels. It is accessible just off the western coast of Townlong Steppes via a bridge from the Shado-Pan Garrison. To the northeast of the temple is the Fields of Niuzao, and the Niuzao Catacombs are under the temple, accessible via a cave entrance on the western edge of the island.
Atop the temple on the same terrace as Commanders Lo Ping and Oxheart, the justice and valor quartermasters, is The Emperor's Burden - Part 5, one of the objectives of  [The Seven Burdens of Shaohao], a Pandaria exploration achievement.
Nordrassil:
Nordrassil, meaning the "Crown of the Heavens" in Darnassian, is the original World Tree of the night elves, located on the new Well of Eternity, atop Mount Hyjal, in the mountain's summit. It granted the elves immortality and allowed the druids to enter the Emerald Dream with ease, until the Battle of Mount Hyjal in the Third War, which severely wounded the tree and where the night elves lost its powers. Nordrassil's roots grow deep into the earth, spreading life-giving energy across the world. This is similar to what the first Well of Eternity did before it was destroyed.
Originally, Nordrassil had served two purposes - not only had it been designed to keep others from abusing the magic of the new Well, but also to prevent the second fount's power from growing too great over time.
North Gate Outpost:
North Gate Outpost is the northeasternmost settlement of the dwarves built in Dun Morogh. It lies in the middle of North Gate Pass, which links Dun Morogh in the west with Loch Modan in the east. 
The mountaineers stationed at the outpost are busily defending it from encroaching wildlife, and some dwarves have gone missing in the mountains in search of the more ferocious beasts. Young dwarves and gnomes are tasked with exploring the area and looking for any signs of the lost mountaineers and the animals which killed them.
Northsea Freebooters: The Northsea Freebooters are a group of pirates that arrived in the Howling Fjord and set up a port at Scalawag Point. They have a severe dislike of the Southsea Freebooters, from which they most likely branched off. The Northsea Freebooters are making up for being fewer in number by being worse criminals and murderers.
Northshire Abbey: Northshire Abbey is the seat of the Brotherhood of Northshire, a religious order of clerics affiliated to the kingdom of Stormwind. It is located in Northshire Valley, in the foothills of Elwynn Forest, with the town of Goldshire lying to the southwest. The abbey is comprised of three sections: the Main Hall, Hall of Arms, and Library Wing. It holds trainers for mages, priests, warriors, monks, and paladins, as well as a couple of quest givers. The warlock trainers haunt the small graveyard to the east of the main doors, while the rogue and hunter trainers can be found at the abbey's stable.
Northshire Vineyards:
The Northshire Vineyards are located just east of the abbey in Northshire Valley.
The vineyards were originally taken over by the agents of the Defias Brotherhood and their leader, Garrick Padfoot. It was here that human players had their first encounter with the Brotherhood, fighting their minions and retrieving the stolen property of Milly Osworth. Since the Cataclysm, the vineyards are under attack by the forces of the Blackrock clan, who are burning them to the ground.
Northwatch Expeditionary Unit: The Northwatch Expeditionary Unit is a group of sailors and soldiers sent from Northwatch Hold and Theramore to attempt to gain a further stronghold into Kalimdor. Recognizable by their Theramore Tabards, their troops have been operating since the Cataclysm for the interests of the Alliance, notably across the regions of Durotar, the Barrens, Azshara and the Stonetalon Mountains.
Northwatch Foothold: Northwatch Foothold, once known as the Kolkar Crag, is a valley located west of Sen'jin Village in Durotar. The humans of Northwatch Hold have begun to gain a foothold into Durotar and with the orcs of Razor Hill having their own problems to deal with it is up to the Darkspear Trolls to prevent this from happening. The humans are transferring large crates of supplies from two icebreakers docked at the nearby Darkspear Strand.
Norwington Estate:
The Norwington Estate (or Norwington Manor) is the property belonging to Lord Aldrius Norwington and Lady Elena Norwington in Tiragarde Sound. They host the annual Norwington Equestrian and Hunt Festival for equestrian riders and hunters from all over Kul Tiras, attracting nobles and the Roughneck riders. The land the estate was built on was originally inhabited by the Grimestone troggs, but Lord Aldrius' grandfather drove them out and forced them to settle in the nearby Mistfall Cleft.
Lord Stormsong ordered his cronies to steal the horse Goldenmane from the estate.
Later, the Alliance chose to use the estate as a testing ground for their Azerite weaponry. As part of the War Campaign, Horde forces led by Rexxar attacked the estate in order to collect its caches of Azerite and Azerite weapons. Aside from the Kul Tirans, it was protected by the footsoldiers from the Stormwind Army, the Lightforged draenei paladins and their warframes. The Horde slaughtered the defenders and gathered the Azerite in front of the manor in order to be transported. However, the Alliance reinforcement came and surrounded the Horde force. The Horde retaliated, and the adventurer started shooting at the Alliance soldiers with Azerite munition from a gyrocopter while the rest of the Horde successfully escaped with the Azerite.
Afterward, Lord Admiral Jaina Proudmoore asked SI:7 to investigate the incident, and a final report was delivered to her by the Alliance emissary from Master Mathias Shaw.
Nozdormu:
Nozdormu the Timeless One, aspect of the bronze dragonflight and guardian of time, is one of the Dragon Aspects empowered by the titans to watch over Azeroth. Blessed with mastery over time by Aman'Thul, the Highfather of the Pantheon of Order, Nozdormu once spent most of his time in seclusion, immersing himself in his duties to protect the timeways, and intervening only very rarely in mortal affairs. He notably intervened during the War of the Scaleborn, the War of the Ancients, and a few millennia later, to fight Deathwing during the Battle of Grim Batol.
With the threat of the infinite dragonflight and the advent of the Shattering, Nozdormu found himself less able to ignore the needs of his fellow Aspects and their allies. After aiding in the defeat of Deathwing's abominable creation, Chromatus, and his own insane potential future self, the Aspect of Time sacrificed his powers and immortality to destroy once and for all his corrupted brother.
After the return of the Dragon Isles, Nozdormu played an instrumental part in reintroducing the dracthyr to the world, and joined the leadership of the Valdrakken Accord; seeking to restore their aspectral powers to defeat the Primal Incarnates. With the help of his brood and their mortal allies, he had to face the resurgent infinite dragonflight, which sought to subvert him into his dark alternate self, Murozond. Their dark magic clouded his visions of the future, until the heroes and Chronormu stopped the Dawn of the Infinite, freeing the Lord of Time from his melancholy and restoring his ability to peer into the timeways. Following the blooming of Amirdrassil, and the defeat of Fyrakk, Nozdormu and the Aspects were once again empowered, this time by Azeroth herself.
O'ros: O'ros was a naaru who journeyed from Draenor to Azeroth with Velen and his followers aboard the dimensional ship called the Exodar. He could be found at the core of the ship, at the Seat of the Naaru. O'ros was the last of the prime naaru Xe'ra's line.
Oasis:
The Oasis  is the primary eco-dome located on K'aresh, at the northern end of the eastern island. Within this, Project Eco-Dome is carried out by Ve'nari and Cartel Om with the backing of the K'aresh Trust. Most of the  [Ecological Succession] storyline plays out here.
The area dynamically changes based on how far along the player is in the Ecological Succession campaign, adding more activities for the world quest version as well as new characters and animals that inhabit the area.
Obsidian Brood:
The Obsidian Brood, also known as the Outland brood, refers to the group of black dragons that were shepherded and cared for by Sabellian in Outland. Having been originally placed on Draenor by Deathwing, the clutch was abandoned after the mad aspect's plans went awry and the planet later exploded. Having bent Blade's Edge to their will, the Obsidian Brood returned to Azeroth upon the re-awakening of the Dragon Isles. They supported the endeavors of their leader to become the next Aspect of the black dragonflight. With Sabellian's withdrawal from Aspect, however, they still serve him as their general under his brother and new Aspect, Ebyssian.
By unknown means, they have been purged of their Old God corruption, and have also ensured the return of their flight to the world by caretaking a plethora of eggs and whelps.
Obsidian Bulwark: The Obsidian Bulwark  is a ruined outpost inhabited by Wrathion's Blacktalon forces. It is located near the center of the Waking Shores, on a hill overlooking the Emberflow and providing a view of the Obsidian Citadel. During the war against the Primalists, it was used as a base to launch an attack against the djaradin in the citadel.
Obsidian Citadel:
The Obsidian Citadel is the ancient home of the black dragonflight, located in western Waking Shores. It is here that the Obsidian Oathstone and Obsidian Throne can be found. The citadel was constructed so that the black flight might defend the entire Dragon Isles. It was conquered by the djaradin during the War against the Primalists, but the unified forces of the black dragonflight were able to reclaim the citadel and prevent further invasions.
It is a large fortress set into a volcano, featuring multiple towers, lava pools, and underground passages. Its underground vaults stretch for miles, where many powerful weapons and artifacts were locked away for safekeeping. Alongside the dragon architecture, one can see clear signs of the djaradin occupation, with large piles of supplies and trophy bones scattered across the lower fortress.
Obsidian Hollow:
Obsidian Hollow  is a max-level shadow-filled corner of the Ringing Deeps, located centrally on the eastern wall of the zone.
The area is bordered by the Chittering Den to the northwest, Shadowvein Point to the west, and the Rumbling Wastes to the southwest.
With War Mode enabled, the area is a Free For All and  [80WQ] Foggy Faceoff is sometimes available.
Obsidian Rest:
Obsidian Rest  is the forward post of the Valdrakken Accord and Wrathion's Blacktalon on the way to Aberrus in northern Zaralek Cavern.
The accord has set up in a ruined tower, bordered by Brimstone Garrison to the north and west, and Slitherdrake Roost to the south.
Keskos, the flight master, has connections to the Dragonscale Camp and Loamm.
Uphill to the east of the rest at , a Bronze Timekeeper starts the Brimstone Scramble dragonriding race.
Obsidian Warders: The Obsidian Warders is a weyrn once charged with defending the allies of the black dragonflight and protecting its strongholds. Whether it is deployed to reinforce draconic legions or guard the skies alongside dragons, this weyrn is the embodiment of the Earth-Warder's aegis. Put into a slumber that lasted for 20 000 years, the Primalists' return caused the Obsidian Warders to stir and forge their own path in Azeroth by joining the Alliance. Currently under the authority of the Scalecommander Azurathel, the Warders trained to be the bulwark that enemy forces will break upon. Azurathel believes that given time, the Alliance can be molded into a more unified and dignified fighting force, as he values order and discipline above all—and the Alliance has both in spades.
Odesyus' Landing:
Odesyus' Landing is a Alliance outpost located on the southern coast of Azuremyst Isle. It is little more than a campfire with a two-story log wall, along with two ships moored near the shore.
Several loggers and axemen can be found working near the forest, while Stormwind Marines have been tasked to guard the outpost.
Ogre Mine:
Ogre Mine is a sub-zone in Molten Quarry in southeastern Ashran, alternate Draenor. 
The mine features a sizeable population of mobs, including goren and a large number of the neutral Power Geodes. At the far end of the mine a large and very powerful rare mob can be found.
Old Gods' forces: The forces of the Old Gods, known in ancient times as the Black Empire, are a vaguely united faction of all the entities and organizations that serve the Old Gods. Although they suffered a crushing defeat long ago at the hands of the Pantheon of Order, having been imprisoned with the majority of their minions by the titan-forged, the Old Gods' activities on Azeroth have been steadily increasing since the opening of the Dark Portal. Among their recent attempts to escape their prisons and restore the Black Empire, there are those of C'Thun during the Ahn'Qiraj War, followed by Yogg-Saron's corruption of Ulduar and its Keepers, and culminating in Deathwing's major offensive orchestrated by N'Zoth during the Cataclysm. Nevertheless, the Old Gods' forces were eventually being pushed back by Horde and Alliance repeatedly, until their final defeat in the aftermath of the Fourth War, with the death of N'Zoth and the destruction of Ny'alotha at the end of the Black Empire Campaign.
Old Horde:
The Old Horde (aka old Horde or the first Horde; known during the time of its existence simply as the Horde, the Orcish Horde, or the Orc Horde) is the name given to the faction of orcish clans of Draenor from its beginning prior to the First War until it was defeated by the Alliance of Lordaeron at the end of the Second War. The term "Old Horde" is used to differentiate the faction from the New Horde, founded by Thrall after the Old Horde's defeat.
Fundamental principles of the Old Horde included demon worship, the consumption of demon blood to become stronger, merciless killing and warfare, and victory in combat to prove one's worth. Their ranks consisted originally only of orcs, soon joined by ogres from Draenor and later during the Second War by forest trolls and goblins from Azeroth. The Old Horde was initially led by Warchief Blackhand from its creation until the later stages of the First War, and later by Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer from the end of the First War to the Horde's dissolution.
Old Ironforge:
Old Ironforge, also known as the Assembly of Thanes, is a chamber deep below the High Seat of the dwarven capital of Ironforge. In an effort to aid the troubled elementals that foreshadowed the Cataclysm and the return of Deathwing, King Magni Bronzebeard opened a part of the old city and attempted a titan ritual to commune with the earth but was turned into diamond. He stood rooted on what has become known as Magni's Dais. A long and winding path leads over the lava to the two doors of Aegrim's Study.
While Old Ironforge has always been present in-game, its entrance was originally closed off until Cataclysm.
Old Pi'jiu:
Old Pi'jiu  is a ruined pandaren fishing town on the southwestern part of Timeless Isle that used to have brewery. To the north is the Celestial Court, the Tushui Landing is to the northwest, and eastward is the Firewalkers' Path leading to the Firewalker Ruins and points northward.
The Really Skunky Beer event plays out here occasionally. Ten Skunky Brew Alementals will spawn, all with the standard alemental set of abilities. Once they have been defeated, Zhu-Gon the Sour spawns in the center of town by the well. Kill it for a decent amount of Timeless Coins.
At the dock, Fin Longpaw occasionally starts fishing. If interacted with, he will fish up the kraken Karkanos. Off the shore to the southeast is a sunken hozen ship, where there a number of cursed hozen swabbies guarding the Sunken Treasure.
On the Offensive (achievement):
On the Offensive is a meta-achievement awarded for completing 6 of the 9 secondary-objective achievements during the four covenant assaults in the Maw. Many achievements are tied to quests, not all of which are active every assault.
Completing this achievement is one of the requirements to purchase the a covenant-specific mount from Duchess Mynx in Keeper's Respite for 1000  [Stygia]:  [Battle-Hardened Aquilon],  [Battlefield Swarmer Harness],  [Pale Gravewing] or  [Winter Wilderling Harness].
Oomlot Village: Oomlot Village is a pygmy village located east of Town-In-A-Box and northeast of Ruins of Vashj'elan, located on Lost Isles. Inside, pygmy witch doctors are turning the Town-In-A-Box villagers into goblin zombies.
Oostan:
Oostan is large area of pygmy territory in the western part of Lost Peak's caldera, on the Lost Isles. Within the area there are three villages: Nord in the north, Sor in the west, and Ost in the south. It is from here that the pygmy witch doctors—Gaahl, Malmo, and Teloch—turn the goblin survivors into zombies and send them to attack the Town-In-A-Box.
Oostan and its surroundings are completely destroyed by the volcano's eruption.
Opalcreg:
The Opalcreg  is a nerubian-occupied mine on the north shore of Isle of Dorn, south of Dornogal.
Crossroads Plaza is to the northeast, Boulder Springs is to the east, Boskroot Basin is to the southeast, and Freywold Village is to the west.
Opportunity Point:
Opportunity Point  is the southernmost quest hub of the Ringing Deeps. The area (and elevator to the Orecreg up on the Isle of Dorn!) has been occupied by goblins of Opportunity Acquisitions, who work for Jastor Gallywix.
The Opportunity Point Spa and Resort is bordered by the Ancient Falls to the north, the Deepforge Golemworks to the northwest, the Abyssal Excavation to the west, and the Lightless Chasm to the south.
The Opportunity Point Amble skyriding race is located at  just north of town.
Oracles: The Oracles are a faction of several friendly gorloc tribes that inhabit Sholazar Basin. They see themselves as guardians of the titan technology that remains in the area, though they don't really have an understanding of the artifacts they are guarding. They find themselves in an escalating territorial war with the Frenzyheart Tribe of wolvar.
Orb of Translocation:
An Orb of Translocation is a swirling red orb of blood elven manufacture, a device used to teleport oneself either short or far distances within the world. They are common in Quel'Thalas.
There are five known connected pairs of orbs in Azeroth and Outland. The first and most often used connects Sunfury Spire in Silvermoon City to the Ruins of Lordaeron in the Undercity, which were implemented to allow blood elf players in Quel'Thalas to travel to the "mainlands" without having to venture through the Eastern Plaguelands. Alliance players cannot use this orb. This is probably to prevent easy raids on Silvermoon City.
The orbs are also used in single buildings to connect from the ground floor to the top. Such locations include Duskwither Spire in Eversong Woods, Falcon Watch in Hellfire Peninsula, the Sun's Reach Sanctum on the Isle of Quel'Danas, and the Kael'thas-controlled Firewing Point in Terokkar Forest.
There is also an orb behind Kael'thas Sunstrider, the final boss of Magisters' Terrace, that translocates players to Vindicator Xayann at the Shattered Sun Staging Area.
Order of the Broken Temple:
The Order of the Broken Temple (also referred to as the Broken Temple) is an order of monks founded after the destruction of the Peak of Serenity in Pandaria. Following the Legion's assault on their monastery, and the subsequent death of Master Hight, the survivors rallied on the Wandering Isle which happened to be traveling nearby at the time. Under the leadership of their Grandmaster, the monks set up their order hall within the Temple of Five Dawns and fought alongside the other class orders, united as the Armies of Legionfall, during the third invasion of Azeroth. They are the bringers of hope to a dim future.
Since the end of the Argus Campaign, the Order of the Broken Temple has remained active, training young monks in the ways of martial arts.
Order of the Cloud Serpent: The Order of the Cloud Serpent is an order of serpent riders sworn to defend the Jade Forest and the Temple of the Jade Serpent, dedicated to the August Celestial Yu'lon. They are mighty warriors who rode on the backs of the ferocious beasts, and are said to swoop into battle as swiftly as the wind itself, striking with the strength of storm and sky. They welcome and train all who wish to join them at the Arboretum.
Ordon: The Ordon are a large warlike tribe of yaungol found on the Timeless Isle. While the yaungol as a race are usually associated with fire, the Ordon base their entire culture around it. The Ordon worship and are led by Ordos, a yaungol shaman who sacrificed himself to the flame to become a demigod. As a threat to Pandaria, they are opposed by the recently awoken Emperor Shaohao and his allies. They offer rewards such as the  [Reins of the Ashhide Mushan Beast] to those who would kill their enemies (AKA, everyone else).
Ordon Sanctuary:
The Ordon Sanctuary  is the home of Ordos, the yaungol demigod of fire. Found on a rise high above the rest of the Timeless Isle, the sanctuary was originally accessed by the last bridge span of the Firewalkers' Path, but the bridge has been destroyed. 
After the discovery of the Dragon Isles, Chen Stormstout, Li Li Stormstout, and Catelyn the Blade flew over the sanctuary and spotted Ordos. Li Li noted that adventurers continue to come to fight the massive demigod.
Orgrimmar: Orgrimmar ['ɔɹgɹɪmɑɹ] is the capital city of the orcs and the Horde as a whole. Named in honor of the legendary Orgrim Doomhammer, and nestled into a system of valleys on the northern edge of Durotar, Orgrimmar stands as one of the mightiest warrior cities in the world. It is the seat of the Horde Council that governs the entire faction. It is the primary hub for player characters of the Horde and, as with all capital cities, has banks, class and profession trainers, and auction houses.
Orgrimmar Legion camp:
Orgrimmar Legion camp is the name of the Horde camp stationed near Hive'Regal in Silithus. It served as the Orgrimmar Legion's base of operations.

 This section concerns content related to Legion.
As of the end of the Burning Legion's third invasion, the camp was destroyed alongside the majority of Silithus by Sargeras and his sword. Several bodies of the Orgrimmar Legion were later found, but it is unclear if the other members managed to escape or perished as well.
Oribos:
Oribos, the Eternal City (/ˈɔːrəboʊs/ OR-ə-bohs, or sometimes /ˈoʊrɪbəs/ OH-rih-bəs), also known as the Undying City, is a very ancient city located at the heart of the Shadowlands. All souls who enter the Shadowlands are first sent here to be judged by the Arbiter before being sent off to their appropriate afterlives. Constructed by the First Ones and predating all memory, the Eternal City serves as a nexus between the various domains of the Shadowlands and is a gathering point for power brokers, wheelers, dealers, and anima traders. Oribos is the central player hub of the Shadowlands.
Oribos is the first destination of the departed. Oribos is the gateway to the afterlives of the Shadowlands, where souls begin their journey in the thereafter and the first sight a soul beholds with their newly unliving eyes after their arrival is the eternal city.
With the Arbiter having gone mysteriously dormant and with all incoming mortal souls being damned to the Maw, Oribos and its Attendant and Broker inhabitants welcome members of both the Alliance and the Horde to the citadel, but force them to set aside their differences while inside its walls as the city is considered sacred neutral ground.
Orsis:
Orsis is a tol'vir city located in west-central Uldum. When the tol'vir were afflicted by the Curse of Flesh, as many creations of the Titans were, they were offered to swear allegiance to the evil dragon Deathwing in order to regain their stone skin. But the people of Orsis refused... and so Deathwing's ally, the Elemental Lord Al'Akir, buried Orsis beneath the sands in a great windstorm as punishment and to serve as a warning to the other tribes.
King Phaoris of Ramkahen, who leads the tol'vir who oppose Deathwing and Al'Akir, sends any adventurers who are willing to give aid to the survivors of Orsis, buried beneath the choking sands. Powerful air elementals, minions of the Windlord, also inhabit the region making sure the tol'vir stay buried while they search for The Scepter of Orsis. The Orsis tribe has been bound by oath to protect this scepter from evil.

 This section concerns content related to Battle for Azeroth.
After N'Zoth was released, Orsis became a breeding ground for aqir.
A group of Alliance soldiers defended the place, and some perished.
Outriggers:
The Outriggers, or Stormriggers, are an organization of Kul Tiran monster hunters based in Tiragarde Sound. The group has dedicated itself to defending Kul Tiras and the Sound from external threats that might emerge, though they specialize in fighting monsters and creatures from the sea, centered around Anglepoint Bay. The group maintains a base at Krakenbane Cove.
Eventually, as the Fourth War progressed, the Outriggers would accept an offer to crew a new flagship constructed specifically for King Anduin Wrynn, with Rosaline Madison acting as first mate on board.
Overspark Expedition Camp: The Overspark Expedition Camp is located on Mechagon Island.
Ozumat: Ozumat is the patriarch of all kraken. It appears to be in the service of the Old Gods' forces, fighting alongside the naga and faceless ones during  [30-35] Final Judgment and  [30-35] Defending the Rift. He is the final boss of the Throne of the Tides in World of Warcraft: Cataclysm and makes several appearances during the Vashj'ir storyline.
Pale Roost:
The Pale Roost is an area on the upper shelf of northern Deepholm. It is here the stone dragons call home. Terrath the Steady is here in an attempt to bring the stone dragons back into the fold.

 This section concerns content related to Legion.
After Geth'xun fell into Deepholm, he corrupted the stone troggs that became known as the Felrock. They attacked the area, subduing drakes on the ground. Aeosera, however, refused to leave her eggs. Therazane sent the Farseer of the Earthen Ring to rescue the stone drakes, kill the corrupted troggs, and reassemble fallen Opalescent Guardians in order to carry Aeosera's eggs to safety. Opal Defenders were also throwing boulders onto the enemies.
Palemane Rock:
Palemane Rock is a cave in western Mulgore inhabited by gnolls of the Palemane tribe. They are aggressive creatures and will attack any who wander too close.
The gnolls live both inside the cave and in a camp outside, and the cave itself stretches fairly deep into the mountainside.
Pandaren Empire: The Pandaren Empire was the central government of the pandaren people in their homeland of Pandaria. It did not include lands west of the Serpent's Spine. The last Emperor of Pandaria was Shaohao. After he disappeared, the power in Pandaria shifted to the local level instead.
Pang's Stead:
Pang's Stead is the home of Pang Thunderfoot, owner of the Thunderfoot Fields in the Valley of the Four Winds. It can be found not far from the eastern border of the Valley of the Four Winds. This is also the location of Thunderfoot Inn, the only inn on the east side of the Valley.
Just to the southwest is the Thunderfoot Farm, and down the hill to the west is the Thunderfoot Ranch.
Pantheon of Order:
The Pantheon of Order, also known as the Titan Pantheon or simply the Pantheon, are a group of titans who shaped and ordered worlds while watching over the Great Dark Beyond and searching for others of their kind. They created the titan-forged, various races of Azeroth, and empowered the Dragon Aspects through the titanic keepers.
The entire Pantheon was defeated in a battle with their former brethren Sargeras who obliterated their physical forms. However, Norgannon cast a spell to protect their spirits and sent them hurtling towards Azeroth, where they tried to merge with the keepers. This failed as the keepers' bodies were unable to handle the titans' souls' entire might. Their spirits faded, and all that remained was a flash of memories and feelings that the keepers could not comprehend. The keepers tried to reach out to the Pantheon but received no answer in return. Eventually, Keeper Ra concluded that the Makers had died, and he fell into a deep state of depression. He left all civilization behind and retreated into the Mogu'shan Vaults, abandoning his kin and mogu followers.
As the armies of Azeroth and the Army of the Light launched their united assault on the Burning Legion's capital world of Argus, Magni Bronzebeard, Azeroth's Speaker, discovered that the ruined planet hosted a worldsoul within its core. The titan Argus was being tortured and twisted by Sargeras' servants and used to fuel the Legion's infinite army.
There, it was also discovered that at some point, the Legion had acquired the diminished forms of the Pantheon's spirits and had brought them to Antorus, the Burning Throne, where they were being tortured and brainwashed by The Coven of Shivarra in order to corrupt them into a Dark Pantheon. It was already too late for the noble Aggramar whose tortured spirit had been infused into an avatar to serve his dark master. After millennia spent hiding in isolation, Eonar's essence too was recently discovered on the world of Elunaria by the Legion who sent the Legion ship Paraxis to capture her.
Eventually, Eonar and Aggramar were restored and reunited along with the other members of the Pantheon, and with the help of Azeroth's champions, they eventually severed Argus's connection with the Legion, and after his defeat, they combined their powers with the last remnant of Argus to imprison Sargeras at the Seat of the Pantheon, ending the Burning Crusade.
Park:
The Park used to be the district located in the western corner of Stormwind City. It was once a place devoted to leisure activities for Stormwind's populace until it became a refuge for visiting night elves, who found the comforting presence of nature a welcome respite from the vast stone thoroughfares of Stormwind proper. It was the only place in the Eastern Kingdoms where druid trainers resided. The night elves created a Moonwell in the center of the park square.
To get to the Park, one would have headed southwest from Cathedral Square or northwest from the Mage Quarter.
During the invasion of Outland, Ros'eleth tried to send olemba seeds to the park.
The Park was destroyed by Deathwing's visit to Stormwind, during the Cataclysm. When he attacked the city, the druid trainer Sheldras Moontree, priest trainer Nara Meideros, and Argos Nightwhisper were the only ones known to escape alive, with the rest unaccounted for. They relocated down to Stormwind Harbor. The Old Barracks appeared to be all that remained of the Park, and before patch 7.0.3, the subzone name was displayed as "The Old Barracks" throughout the entire former Park. Lion's Rest was finally built on its ruins.
Patch 2.4.0: Patch 2.4.0, titled Fury of the Sunwell, was a content patch that released on 25 March 2008.
Patch 3.2.0: Patch 3.2.0: Call of the Crusade brought a host of new features for World of Warcraft: Wrath of the Lich King and went live on 4 August 2009.
Patch 7.2.0:
Patch 7.2.0: The Tomb of Sargeras is the first content patch of Legion, focusing on assaulting the Broken Shore once more and closing the portal within the Tomb of Sargeras.
The patch was deployed on the Public Test Realm on January 19, 2017. Its release date was announced on March 23, 2017 during a Live Developer Q&A with Senior Game Designer Ryan Shwayder.
Last patch notes update: 2017-03-27
Paw'don Village:
Paw'don Village is a pandaren village just north of Garrosh'ar Point, previously led by Mayor Sunke Khang. The village is divided into two parts, connected by a bridge.
Unlike the usual brews produced by the pandaren, Paw'don Village is known for their apple cider, which is prized throughout the Jade Forest.  They are thus dependent on their apple orchard; it not only provides the villagers' food supply, but the village's livelihood as well.
A direct portal to Paw'don Village, maintained by Tushui Magisters, exists in the Wizard's Sanctum in Stormwind.
By 40 ADP, Sunke Khang had retired as mayor and the replanted young apple trees were producing their first apples.
Perdition Hold:
Perdition Hold  is one of the two elite areas of the Maw. Before unlocking the area, players' Exposed Anima will leave them vulnerable to the locals:

 Exposed Anima — Anima patterns reveal the player's vulnerabilities, increasing damage taken by 200% while in Perdition Hold.
The mobs already hit hard, so the 200% buff can effectively one-shot most classes. Upon reaching Tentative standing with Ve'nari, she will provide the quest  [60] Rule 5: Be Audacious. This quest will shield the player's anima, allowing them to get around the area (and earn the achievement  [Prepare for Trouble!]).
Perdition Hold is accessed via the bridge from the north coming from the Cocyrus through the Face of Oblivion.
Pinchwhistle Gearworks: Pinchwhistle Gearworks is a neutral goblin settlement on the eastern coast of the Spires of Arak on Draenor, constructed after the inhabitants' previous town Pinchwhistle Point to the south was infested by spores from the local fungi. The new town also experiences problems with the encroaching fungi from the Sporemist Shallows, and request aid from the Horde and Alliance Commanders to deal with it.
Pinchwhistle Point:
Pinchwhistle Point was a Steamwheedle goblin settlement located at the cape of Arak. The town and the inhabitants were, however, infested by spores from the local fungi and were abandoned. It is now inhabited by infected goblins, fungal creatures, sludges, and a single uninfected goblin, Krixel Pinchwhistle, who was injured while trying to find a cure for the infection.
