Prior to the infestation, the goblins were harvesting many of the local resources with many lumberjacks and oil pumps found in the area. The Mother Lode zeppelin crashed after surveying the area.
After the arrival of Kimzee Pinchwhistle and the Commander, Krixel manages to finish his serum. After curing a number of goblins, he sets the town on fire with the help of the Commander and escapes to Pinchwhistle Gearworks.
Plump: The Plumps are a brood of virmen found in the Wandering Isle, in the Rows and at the Teeming Burrow.
Plunder Harbor:
Plunder Harbor is a town in eastern Tiragarde Sound under the control of the Fogsail Freebooters. The Maiden's Lament inn is located here.
During the Fourth War, the Fogsail Freebooters allowed the Honorbound Horde to use the harbor as a safe foothold in Kul Tiras after they helped Owings pull a mutiny on the previous captain Rhenik for wanting to sell the crew out to the Ashvane Trading Company. The Horde's actions led to the Proudmoore fleet attacking the harbor, sending the Siren's Daughter and Valorous Rose battleships to get Derek Proudmoore's body back.
Port Fogtide:
Port Fogtide is a shipyard for battleship-sized vessels in Stormsong Valley, in the shadow of the Sagehold. The tidesages and k'thir have taken over the port and The Abyssal Melody. The ettin, Dagrus the Scorned is captured here.
It was later retaken, and Dorian Atwater built a ship for King Anduin Wrynn here.
Port of Zem'lan:
The Port of Zem'lan, also known as Zem'lan's port or simply Zem'lan, is a large, ruined Zandalari port town on the southwestern coast of Vol'dun. It is a cursed place, ruled over by Pirate-King Zem'lan and his crew of the eternal damned. In ages past, the port was attacked by the Faithless sethrak. Pirate-King Zem'lan refused to allow Zandalari refugees onto his ships to escape the sethrak attack and ordered his crew to rally and defend the port with their lives. However, when it became clear that the sethrak were too many, Zem'lan instead gathered his crew on the Golden Isle and conducted a ritual with three magical idols to curse his crew into undead skeletons, forced to serve him for eternity.
Thus, in the present day, the port is almost entirely inhabited by Zem'lan's skeletal pirates. The corpses of souldrained refugees, Zem'lan's own defenders, and the Faithless invaders litter parts of the ruins. Pirate-King Zem'lan doesn't stay in the port with the rest of his crew and instead keeps to the forbidden Golden Isle to the southwest, hoarding the treasures his pirates have plundered over the years, so that only he can enjoy them.
Prepfoot Compound:
The Prepfoot Compound is a small Highmountain tauren village nestled in the seaside cliffs in northeastern Highmountain. It is the main base for the Prepfoot, a group of tauren who believe that Deathwing will soon return and that the end of the world is imminent.
A small storehouse where the Prepfoot store their supplies is found at the southeastern end of the compound. Below the eastern side of the village, there is a small lake with a graveyard on the eastern end.
Pridefall Hamlet: Pridefall Hamlet is the entry point of all souls that arrive in Revendreth from Oribos, assigned there by the Arbiter as a last chance to avoid the Maw. Upon arrival, each soul is given their sinstone.
Primalists:
The Primalists are the followers of the Primal Incarnates, ancient proto-dragons that chose to side against the titans and the Dragon Aspects. They recruit people by offering them elemental powers. The Primalists have been known to reshape the land, whether by lava or by ice, like at the Flashfrost Enclave. They also steal dragon and proto-dragon eggs in order to infuse them with elemental energies and turn them to their side. They have also been known to transform furbolgs by giving them bodies of hardened stone.
Besides their hatred for the titans and their dragon loyalists, they also oppose the Kirin Tor, thinking they deserve death for using arcane magic. The dragonspawn and drakonid who rejoined the Primalists did it because they felt displaced by the return of the dragons. To help with their war, they summoned various elementals from the Elemental Planes through elemental gateways.
The Primalist Future in Thaldraszus is an example of what they strive to achieve; a primal world of ice, earthquakes, and fire.
Primals:
Primals are various plant-like beings inhabiting Draenor, whose dominion is life and who intend to transform the entire planet into a lush jungle landscape. They are the children of the Sporemounds: some such as the genesaur fell off the Sporemounds' bodies during their fight with Grond and gained a life of their own, while others such as the botani and podlings arose from spores infused with the Spirit of Life that released from Botaan during its death and fell onto plantlife. They are locked in an eternal war with the Breakers, who seek to transform the entirety of Draenor into a barren desert wasteland.
The genesaur are revered by the lesser Primals as some kind of demigods. One of them has also managed to cross the portal to Azeroth, but met his demise at the hands of Kirin Tor and adventurers.
The Primals found in Ashran's Amphitheater of Annihilation are known as "the Shapers".
After the fall of the draenei and Shattrath City, Kilrogg Deadeye and his followers slaughtered the botani and genesaur in the name of the Horde.
Primus:
The Primus is the founder and ruler of Maldraxxus and the five houses of the Necrolord Covenant, whose charge is to defend the Shadowlands and the force of Death from external influences. The most tactical and long-thinking of the Eternal Ones, he is a master strategist who is nearly unbeatable on the field of battle and is notorious for always thinking far ahead of everyone else. The Primus embodies the five traits of the ideal Maldraxxi soldier, virtues he also instilled into the five houses: ambition, might, insight, guile, and relentlessness. In addition to his military might, he is also known as a legendary weaponsmith and the best armor crafter in the Shadowlands. He is the creator of Maldraxxi rune magic, which serves to manipulate necromantic energy, and its more powerful counterpart, Domination, which he made for the purpose of imprisoning his traitorous brother, Zovaal the Jailer. All necrolords receive a portion of the Primus' power in order to carry out their duty of defending the Shadowlands.
At some point, the Primus left his sanctum to investigate the schemes of the captive Zovaal. The Jailer defeated the Primus, took his memories from him, and confined him to the tower of Torghast as a prisoner called the Runecarver. In this form, the Primus was forced to create countless armaments for the Jailer—including Frostmourne and the Helm of Domination, which were later used by the succession of Lich Kings on Azeroth. The necrolords were unaware of their leader's fate, and in his absence, Maldraxxus fell into chaos: two of the houses were nearly destroyed, and the leaders of the remaining three ruthlessly fought to claim the Seat of the Primus and the position of commanding the realm's armies.
Before his disappearance, the Primus left behind cryptic messages and prophecies concerning the coming of one who would embody the might of Maldraxxus and save the realm from itself, prophecies that were fulfilled by mortal Maw Walkers. During the four covenants' campaign to waylay the Jailer's efforts in the city of Korthia, these same heroes recovered the Primus' sigil, which he had concealed before his journey to the Maw. When brought to Torghast, the sigil restored the Primus' memories and freed him from his existence as the Runecarver, allowing him to lend his tactical genius to the covenants as they fought to prevent the Jailer from achieving his goals. The Primus ultimately ensured his brother's defeat by reforging the shards of the Helm of Domination into the Crown of Wills, which granted the Maw Walkers the resistance they needed to counter the Jailer's Domination magic and save the Shadowlands.
Prince Farondis: Prince Farondis is a Highborne night elf and the ruler of Azsuna. During the War of the Ancients, Farondis was one of the few Highborne rulers who dared defy Queen Azshara, resulting in the destruction of his city Nar'thalas and most of Azsuna at her hands. Ten thousand years later, when the Legion invaded his lands yet again, Queen Azshara herself appeared before Farondis, offering to break her curse should he pledge his people's allegiance to her, but once again, Farondis rejected her, finally impressing and winning back the long-denied favor and support of his people.
Prince Renathal:
Prince Renathal is a venthyr who leads the rebellion from Sinfall in Revendreth against Sire Denathrius. Convinced that the Master is behind the anima drought, he rallied a formidable force to lead a rebellion to succeed Sire Denathrius and make the anima flow once more.
In contrast to his prideful father, Renathal is more humble and devoted to Revendreth's original mission. He also appears to enjoy taking chances on gambits that seemingly have very little chance to succeed. Despite his attacks on Castle Nathria and his attempts to unite the Court of Harvesters against Denathrius all initially ending in failure, he refuses to let the Venthyr and the Shadowlands go out without a fight. He describes the war against the Jailer as something that will inevitably end in failure, but claims that there is excitement to be had in battling the inevitable.
Prince Renathal personally refers to Denathrius as father. His blade Vorpalia is sentient like Denathrius's Remornia. He has a pet gargon named Vrednic. The dredger Breakfist was one of the last of Renathal's forces from his first rebellion left in Sinfall. His former home is Darkwall Tower.
Priory of the Sacred Flame: The Priory of the Sacred Flame is a dungeon in The War Within, located in western Hallowfall high on a rise, close to Beledar.
Prophet's Lesson: Prophet's Lesson is a short story by Marc Hutcheson featured on the official site. It is the twelfth and last in the Leaders of Azeroth series, released on April 23, 2012, and centers on the draenei's leader, the Prophet Velen.
Prophet's Reflection: Prophet's Reflection is a location in Eredath.
Protectorate: The Protectorate is a faction of ethereals formed in reaction to the obsessive search for vengeance of the Ethereum ruling class. They consider that the Ethereum are as great a threat to their existence as Dimensius the All-Devouring, the void lord who destroyed their homeworld of K'aresh. Commander Ameer appears to represent their interests in Outland at the Protectorate Watch Post in the Netherstorm.
Pygmy: Pygmies are a race of small, primitive humanoids found on the Lost Isles and in Uldum. According to Brann Bronzebeard, pygmies share an unknown common ancestor with goblins.
Pyrox Flats: Pyrox Flats is a level area north of The Cauldron in Searing Gorge. It is inhabited by camps of Dark Iron dwarves.
Qalashi tribe: The Qalashi tribe is a djaradin tribe found in the Waking Shores on the Dragon Isles. Formerly led by Warlord Sargha, they are the fiercest of dragon hunters. According to legend, a legendary Qalashi warlord conquered the weaker djaradin tribes and united their strongest members under the Qalashi banner.
Qiraji: The qiraji (/kiˈɹɑːʒ.i/ kee-RAHZH-ee) are a race of insectoid creatures based in southern Silithus. Different types of qiraji are referred to as castes, and it seems that every caste has a leader who is under the command of the Twin Emperors: Vek'nilash and Vek'lor. The three most notable castes are the battleguards led by Battleguard Sartura, the gladiators led by General Rajaxx, and the prophets led by the Prophet Skeram.
Quel'Thalas (kingdom):
The kingdom of Quel'Thalas (meaning High Home in Thalassian) is the realm of the blood elves, led by Regent Lord Lor'themar Theron since the fall of the Sunstrider dynasty. Nestled in the eponymous region of Quel'Thalas in northern Lordaeron, its capital is Silvermoon City and its borders stretch from the northernmost tip of the Eastern Kingdoms to the Thalassian Pass, including the Eversong Forest, once comprised of the Eversong Woods and the Ghostlands before its restoration, and the Isle of Quel'Danas where the Sunwell is located.
The kingdom was founded by the exiled Highborne under Dath'Remar Sunstrider, who wrested the land from the Amani Empire, and proclaimed themselves the high elves. A council of lords called the Convocation of Silvermoon was raised to assist King Dath'Remar in his governance, and with their aid the Sunstrider dynasty ruled for generations. The kingdom's military is commanded by the Ranger-general of Silvermoon, and the leader of the elven magi is known as the Grand Magister of Quel'Thalas. Silvermoon remained unconquered for 7,000 years under the protection of the Sunwell.
During the Third War, however, Arthas Menethil led the undead Scourge in a devastating rampage through Quel'Thalas on his quest to claim the fount of power, resulting in the deaths of roughly 90% of the elven population and its leadership. The corrupted Sunwell was later destroyed by Prince Kael'thas Sunstrider, who renamed the survivors the blood elves in honor of their perished brethren. The prince then named Lor'themar Theron as Regent Lord of Quel'Thalas to defend the kingdom in his stead, and traveled far beyond his homeland to seek salvation for his people, ultimately meeting a tragic end. The blood elves eventually reclaimed and rebuilt much of Quel'Thalas, and the Sunwell was restored, heralding a brighter future after some of the kingdom's darkest days.
Ragefeather wildkin:
The Ragefeather wildkin are a group of wildkin that inhabits Ragefeather Ridge on Bloodmyst Isle. They have been corrupted by the Exodar's crystals, while the Royal Blue Flutterers helped spread it even further.
Though they had lived in harmony with the land for thousands of year, the Ragefeather eventually traveled to Wyrmscar Island for unknown reasons, where they stole the bones of fallen dragons, causing the spirits of the brood to grow restless due to this sacrilege. The ghost of Prince Toreth later sent Alliance adventurers to recover the bones in Ragefeather Ridge.
Rainspeaker Canopy:
Rainspeaker Canopy is a village wich sits northeast of River's Heart, within the Wildgrowth Mangal of the Sholazar Basin. It is home to the Oracles, a gorloc tribe. They live in little elevated houses, open-sided to encourage cool breezes and thatched with leaves to keep off the rain. They keep many crystals about too, from the pillars, and the Oracles build wind chimes tipped with crystal fragments that they hang from their trees.
Following the war against the Jailer, the brothers Bronzebeard visited the village, where they were well received, just like the Frenzyheart tribe at their village, thanks to the diplomatic relations that Brann Bronzebeard maintained with them.
Rak-Ahat: Rak-Ahat is an area found in Azj-Kahet. Most of the silk in Azj-Kahet is produced here, from the finest veils to the strongest warsilk. The Severed Threads also uses the facility to smuggle military secrets woven into the silks. Teth took control of the facility after she pitted Grand Overspinner Antourix and Ren'khat against each other.
Rak-Ush: Rak-Ush, also known as Rak-Ush Ranch, is an area found in Azj-Kahet.
Ramkahen: Ramkahen is the capital city of the Ramkahen tribe of tol'vir, located in the center of Uldum on the fork of the Vir'naal River.
Ramkahen (faction): The Ramkahen tribe is a faction of tol'vir that control the territory of northern Uldum. They have lived in peace with the other tol'vir tribes for a long time, until the Neferset tribe made relations with Deathwing and the elemental lord Al'Akir. The Ramkahen were given the same choice but refused, they however have taken steps to insure their safety after seeing the aftermath of the attack on Orsis.
Rangari Refuge:
Rangari Refuge is a Rangari outpost located in southwestern Tanaan Jungle, near the Iron Front. Besides the Rangari, it also houses several Laughing Skull refugees.
Occasionally, Terrorfist will spawn and attack the Refuge.
Ravel: The Ravel (/ˈrævəl/ RAV-əl) was an organization made of the brightest minds in K'aresh who sought to save their world from Dimensius during the Devouring War. Most K'areshi believe the void lord was responsible for their planet's destruction. In truth, the Ravel attempted to preemptively kill Dimensius before he could consume K'aresh, knowing there was no other way to stop him, and shattered the planet in the process.
Raven Hill: Raven Hill is an abandoned town located in western Duskwood, north of Addle's Stead and south of the Raven Hill Cemetery. Though once all but empty, several worgen have taken up residence here in their search for a cure to the worgen curse.
Razorfen Downs:
Razorfen Downs (or simply Razorfen or the Downs) are the ancestral burial grounds of the quilboar, nestled amid huge brambles in the Thousand Needles.
It is said that the entrance to the Downs is made from Agamaggan's maw. The entry to the outside dome is an arched gap, nearly invisible to any who didn't know where to look.
Red dragonflight:
The red dragonflight is a draconic organization primarily led by the eponymous red dragons to uphold their creed to the world. They are led by Alexstrasza the Life-Binder, whom the titan Eonar charged with protecting life. The red dragonflight wishes to protect all life on Azeroth as their queen does, and does not hesitate to fight anyone who wishes to harm the world, notably the Burning Legion. The flight is made up not only of the red dragons, but also of their mortal followers and dragonkin as well—the majority of whom share scale colors with the flight.
Following the betrayal of Deathwing during the War of the Ancients, they held a deep-seated rivalry with the corrupted black dragonflight, as they found their cruel ways profane against life. For centuries, the red dragonflight slowly recovered from its losses and continued to fulfill its duty of protecting the world. However, during the Second War, Alexstrasza and the majority of her flight were enslaved by the Black Aspect with the Demon Soul, and were reduced to become living weapons for the orcs of the Old Horde against the Alliance of Lordaeron. During the Battle of Grim Batol, the Dragon Queen and her flight were finally freed from slavery by the Alliance, and after taking revenge on their tormentors, they disappeared to recover after years of suffering.
During the war against the Lich King, all the dragonflights founded the Wyrmrest Accord after Malygos's declaration of the Nexus War, and had to eliminate the Aspect of Magic before he doomed Azeroth and all its magic users. Following the Cataclysm, and the return of Deathwing, the red dragonflight once again allied with the other flights and the mortal races of Azeroth to confront the black and twilight dragonflights, and their masters in the shadows. During the final battle, Alexstrasza and the other Dragon Aspects sacrificed their titanic powers to defeat their fallen brother, losing their immortality in the process and condemning their flight to no longer being able to reproduce. With all the dragonflights weakened, the Dragon Queen announced the beginning of the Age of Mortals.
For years, the red dragonflight continued to help the mortal races against the enemies of Azeroth. When the Dragon Isles were uncovered, Alexstrasza and her flight felt its call and returned to their home after ten thousand years. However, a new conflict began against their ancient enemies, the Primalists, and Alexstrasza seeks to regain her powers to protect the flights from the Primal Incarnates. Following the defeat of Fyrakk and the blooming of Amirdrassil, the Dragonqueen was once again empowered as the Red Aspect, but this time by Azeroth herself.
Redridge pack: The Redridge pack is a tribe or clan of gnolls found in almost every spot of the Redridge Mountains.
Redrock Harbor: Redrock Harbor is a bay near the southwestern edge of Vol'dun, currently occupied by Ashvane Trading Company forces that have arrived to launch an Azerite-mining operation at the nearby Redrock Mines. The ship The Siren's Call is docked in the bay. Pathways lead up the cliffs, with one road splitting off to the northeast (to the Ashvane Encampment and the Redrock Mines) and northwest, while another winds its way up to a series of hovels and small buildings high up on the harbor's southern cliffs.
Reliquary Restoration: Reliquary Restoration is awarded to players who complete all twenty relics for Archivist Roh-Suir at Keeper's Respite in Korthia. Most of the relics are gated behind standing with the Archivists' Codex reputation faction. This achievement is required for the meta:  [Breaking the Chains].
Remulos: Keeper Remulos is a keeper of the grove and one of the sons of Cenarius. He is described as being immortal. As the ruler of Moonglade, Remulos, Fandral Staghelm, and Hamuul Runetotem led the Cenarion Circle for several years in the absence of Cenarius and Archdruid Malfurion Stormrage. He later led the battle against the corrupted green dragon Eranikus and participated in the War Against the Nightmare.
Render's Camp: Render's Camp is a Blackrock orc outpost in the northwestern Redridge Mountains, near the entrance to the Burning Steppes.
Render's Valley:
Render's Valley  is a Blackrock orc outpost in the southeastern Redridge Mountains. The orcs here were originally not as powerful as their counterparts to the northwest, but their strength has increased dramatically since Deathwing's return.
The Blackrock orcs have since established a firmer hold here with a larger camp, towers, and elite mobs. Dragon riders now guard their camp.
Rensai's Watchpost: Rensai's Watchpost is a Shado-Pan base in southwestern Townlong Steppes under the command of Rensai Oakhide. To the east is Dusklight Bridge, the Widening Deep can be found far below to the south, and Farwatch Overlook is just to the southwest, which is where most of Rensai's forces can be found. Further southwest is Sik'vess, and just up the path to the northwest is the Shado-Pan Garrison.
Revantusk Sedge:
The Revantusk Sedge was the home of the Revantusk tribe, who lived in Zul'Aman.
When the Twilight's Blade invaded Zul'Aman, they destroyed the Revantusk Sedge, which caused the Revantusk to suffer heavy casualties, with their elders and chieftain amongst them. As his granddaughter Lilaju rose to the position of chieftain and led her people away, the Twilight's Blade desecrated the area as they seized it as their own.
Lilaju later asked the hash'ura to infiltrate the Revantusk Sedge and recover the body of Idago, who had sacrificed himself to ensure her survival when the village was destroyed by the Twilight's Blade. As she sought to reclaim Idago's belongings, she also called upon them to strike back at the Twilight's Blade for defiling her home, which she vowed to reclaim. During the effort, however, she was surprised to learn that Idago still lived, having been taken by the cult to their crypts. At her command, Idago was ultimately rescued and resumed his duties as one of her honor guard.
Lilaju later called upon the hash'ura to recover priceless relics of the Revantusk tribe from the ruins of the Revantusk Sedge.
Rikkitun Village: Rikkitun Village is nestled on the northwest side of Kor'vess along the northern border of Dread Wastes with Townlong Steppes. Chief Rikkitun leads the Rikkitun sprite village.
Riverbend:
Riverbend is the home village of the Rivermane tribe of Highmountain tauren, found in southwestern Highmountain.
During  [10-45] The Underking Comes, Dargrul the Underking uses the  [Hammer of Khaz'goroth] to destroy most of the village, forcing most of its inhabitants to flee to Thunder Totem.
Riverpaw pack: The Riverpaw Pack is a clan of gnolls indigenous to Westfall and Elwynn Forest.
Riverside Post: Riverside Post is a Horde outpost in western Nagrand, located between Mok'gol Watchpost, the Ancestral Grounds, Spirit Woods and Lok-rath.
Rooksguard:
The Rooksguard was an elite force of night elf soldiers who served the House of Ravencrest during the time of the Kaldorei Empire. Based in the Ravencrest ancestral seat of Black Rook Hold, the Rooksguard acted as a personal army to the masters of the hold.
The force has likely been in existence since the first members of House Ravencrest began carving out the fortress that would become Black Rook Hold, and since then have taken an active role in both the hold's and family's protection. This notably included the defense of Black Rook Hold when it was attacked by the demonic Burning Legion during the War of the Ancients. Outside this, the Rooksguard also fought as part of the Kaldorei Resistance throughout the same war to thwart the Legion's invasion.
Rotting Orchard:
The Rotting Orchard is located in southern Duskwood—east of the Yorgen Farmstead, west of the Tranquil Gardens Cemetery, and southwest of Darkshire. The orchard has become home to many ravenous worgen of the Nightbane pack, who now occupy the orchard's dilapidated buildings and make camps, where the Nightbane Shadow Weavers practice their magic and Nightbane Stalkers keep watch in the shadows. The current packleader, Marus, patrols the area between the orchard and his den.
A version of the orchard also exists within the Emerald Dream. Here, Nightmare-corrupted worgen protect the  [Shadowscythe] under the command of Amokarok.
Ruby Lifeshrine:
The Ruby Lifeshrine  is the seat of the red dragonflight and location of the Ruby Oathstone in southeastern Waking Shores. It is surrounded by the Ruby Life Pools from west to northeast, Valdrakken to the southeast across the chasm, and the Flashfrost Assault (and entrance to the Ruby Life Pools instance proper) to the southwest.
The shrine is under the protection of the Shrineguard led by Commander Lethanak.
Two Dragonriding races start here, the Flashfrost Flyover at , and the Ruby Lifeshrine Loop at .
The flight master, Vaknai, has connections to Dragonscale Basecamp, Obsidian Bulwark, and Life Vault Ruins in the Waking Shores, Algeth'era and Valdrakken in Thaldraszus, and Timberstep Outpost in the Ohn'ahran Plains.
Rubyscale Outpost:
Rubyscale Outpost is a small outpost of the red dragonflight located on the eastern part of the border between the Waking Shores and the Ohn'ahran Plains.
A ruined tower here contains an Etched Ancient Monolith. A Dragon Glyph required for  [Ohn'ahran Plains Glyph Hunter] is floating above a bridge on the north side of the ruins.
Ruins of Deatholme: The Ruins of Deatholme are all that remain of the Scourge citadel of Deatholme in Eversong Woods, at the southern end of the Tranquil Repose (formerly the Dead Scar). The Twilight's Blade have established themselves here, particularly within the Shadow Enclave beneath.
Ruins of Kra'nak: The Ruins of Kra'nak is an area in north-western Tanaan Jungle. Once housing Sethekk Arakkoa, its denizens have since joined the Shadow Council with the help of Shadow-Lord Iskar. Adventurers venture here to combat their forces during  [40 Daily] Assault on the Ruins of Kra'nak, and can tackle the elite members in Farlight Terrace.
Ruins of Lordaeron:
The Ruins of Lordaeron (or Lordaeron Keep, also called Ruins of Capital City and Capital City Ruins, and sometimes referred to as Lordaeron City) is the remains of the city of Lordaeron, the great capital city of the fallen kingdom of Lordaeron. It was destroyed by the Scourge after Arthas Menethil betrayed his people and set on the path to become the Lich King. The area is literally haunted by the final tragic events that led to the death of King Terenas and the city's destruction. Lordaeron's palace still stands, and once served as an entrance into the Forsaken capital of the Undercity.
After the Battle for Lordaeron, the Forsaken lost control of the ruins, and the city was further devastated and completely blighted. With the help of adventurers, the Forsaken later applied techniques learned in Maldraxxus to purge the blight from the ruins. Afterward, the city became their new capital, watched over by the new Desolate Council. The city holds a translocation orb that links to Silvermoon City, and has also several portals that lead to Orgrimmar, Vengeance Landing, and Grom'gol Base Camp; in lieu of the still ruined zeppelin towers that once led to these locations.
Ruins of Nar'thalas:
Ruins of Nar'thalas (/ˈnɑɹ.θə.lɑːs/ NAHR-thə-lahs) is a subzone found in Azsuna. The city is built around Nar'thalas Academy and the El'dranil Shallows that surround it. The Crumbled Palace and its Drowned Gardens are at the western edge of the area. The city was protected by the Nightwatchers.
The great city of Nar'thalas was destroyed an eon ago by Queen Azshara. The city's ruler, Prince Farondis, fell with the city. The elves that lived there were cursed to wander the land for all eternity in the form of ghosts. They had in their possession the Pillar of Creation known as the  [Tidestone of Golganneth].
The Hatecoil naga have stirred up the Salteye murlocs, who are now threatening the Ruins of Nar'thalas.
Ruins of Shandaral: The Ruins of Shandaral are the remnants of an ancient kaldorei city located in the eastern part of Crystalsong Forest, in the center of the Unbound Thicket.
Rut'theran Village:
Rut'theran Village was a village port for the night elven city of Darnassus, located at the very bottom of the World Tree Teldrassil. There is a portal here that goes directly into Darnassus, as well as three docks with regular boats going to the Exodar and Stormwind City. There is also a hippogryph roost that goes, for free, to both Darkshore and, for druids, Moonglade in Northern Kalimdor. The Midsummer Fire Festival braziers are lit here.
The first settlement by this name was destroyed by the sea during the Cataclysm, but the second one was quickly built. It was humble by night elf standards but with an exceedingly fresh appearance. In the hippogryph breeding area, hippogryph eggs were meticulously cared for and the young were raised. The kaldorei living in the village worked to support their capital above, but they also hosted all kinds of celebrations, like the Midsummer.
Saltheril's Haven:
Saltheril's Haven is a small enclave found in Eversong Woods hosted by Lord Saltheril, a blood elf who likes to throw elaborate parties in spite of the imminent threat of the Scourge. He is always happy to give invitations to his party table for those who can help him get supplies for his parties. Many years before the Great Wars, Saltheril's Haven hosted parties where Lirath Windrunner performed.
Magistrix Eredania can be found here instructing newcomers to the mystical world of enchanting, while Botanist Tyniarrel shows off his knowledge of native flora. Also present are Sempstress Ambershine, artful with needle and thread, and Arcanist Sheynathren, handy with bubbling liquids.
Years later, Saltheril's Soiree was taking place here.
Sanctuary of Malorne:
The Sanctuary of Malorne is an ancient shrine to the demigod Malorne that was destroyed by the invading fire elementals. It is located just south of Ashen Lake and northwest of Sulfuron Spire in Mount Hyjal.
After completing the quest  [30-35] Aessina's Miracle the area known as the Flamewake becomes part of the Regrowth and the shrine is rebuilt.
Sanctuary of the Mad: The Sanctuary of the Mad is an area in central Ember Ward and contains the elevator to Sinfall. It also contains a mirror in the crypt to the Shrouded Asylum.
Sanctum of the Moon:
The Sanctum of the Moon is an arcane sanctum located just to the west of Tranquillien. It has been overrun with arcane elementals and mana wyrms and has been partially destroyed.
According to Alleria Windrunner, this was once a testament of the mastery of the arcane. Magister Umbric left his notes about Void experiments here, which were later found by Alleria.

 This section concerns content related to Midnight.
The sanctum has been rebuilt and was being used to make new runestones, but is now taken over by the Twilight's Blade.
Sargeron:
Sargeron was once a night elven city, but has lain in ruins since the War of the Ancients. The town's original name has been lost to time, but its ruins are now home to numerous Hatefury satyr who have redubbed it Sargeron — after their demonic master Sargeras.
The ruins were home to many holy sites of Elune, including Elune's Cathedral, Elune's Temple and Elune's Sanctuary. Several relics can still be found there, namely Elune's Brazier, Elune's Handmaiden, the Cup of Elune and the Ancient Vortex Runestone.
Sashj'tar Ruins: Sashj'tar Ruins is an ancient elven research community now in ruins on the Azuregale Bay of Suramar. Elite Sashj'tar naga have claimed the ruins.
Scalecracker Keep:
Scalecracker Keep is a subzone of the Waking Shores on the Dragon Isles, located along the northern coast. It is a large djaradin settlement and the home of the Qalashi.
During the War of the Scaleborn, it was utilized as a base by the djaradin seeking to conquer the Obsidian Citadel while their enemies were distracted. However, the red and black dragonflights led a devastating assault against the keep, eventually forcing them to flee. Like other djaradin strongholds, it went empty after the Great Sundering, with its inhabitants going into hibernation until the reawakening of the Dragon Isles.
During the war against the Primalists, it was once again used as a base to launch attacks against the nearby dragon settlements, including the Obsidian Citadel. Wrathion, adventurers, and his Blacktalon agents struck back at the keep and were able to defeat their leader, Gragza the Dragon-Breaker.
Schnottz's crew:
Schnottz's crew (simply referred to as troopers and employees) is an organization led by Commander Schnottz operating in Uldum. The group is at least partially funded by private businessmen. They are referred to as over-aggressive pillagers.
The crew has a strict policy, one that is taken most seriously: the troops are to dress in official uniform at all times. This helps with organization, friendly fire incidents are reduced, and it keeps the troops looking wonderful. This that what they call "Fashionism".
Schnottz's operatives are digging all over Uldum in order to find relics. The crew is however dissatisfied, and dissensions are appearing within its ranks.
Following the events in Uldum, the remnants of the crew regrouped at the Maker's Ascent, though ultimately the group was disbanded by the time of the Assault in Uldum, where it is noted that all of the former holdings have either been abandoned or taken over by the Wastewanders, along with a significant amount of their abandoned equipment.
Scourge:
The Scourge (sometimes called the Undead Scourge or Scourge Army) is a faction of undead created by the Burning Legion as the precursor for their Second invasion of Azeroth. After the Third War, the Scourge broke free from their demonic masters and — under the iron rule of the dread Lich King — have built up their power base on the arctic continent of Northrend. Their influence spreads throughout the icy continent, as well as the Plaguelands in northern Lordaeron and southern Quel'Thalas, and even Kalimdor to a small degree. Consisting of thousands of walking corpses, disembodied spirits, beasts of the north, and damned mortal men, the Scourge is a terrifying and insidious enemy which, before its downfall, was perhaps the most dangerous threat to the world of Azeroth.
After the Scourgewar, the Scourge became relatively quiet, controlled by the new Lich King Bolvar Fordragon with the Helm of Domination. After the Fourth War, the helm was shattered by Sylvanas Windrunner, destroying the Veil between Azeroth and the Shadowlands. Since then, the Scourge became leaderless and is now an aimless mass of undead rather than an organized force aimed at the hearts of all living things.
Scryers:
The Scryers are a faction of blood elves led by Voren'thal the Seer. The group broke away from Prince Kael'thas Sunstrider, heir to the throne of Quel'Thalas and ruler of the blood elven race, and offered to assist the naaru in rebuilding Shattrath City. They are at odds with the Aldor, and compete with them for power within Shattrath and for the naaru's favor. Nowadays, the Scryers are notable for having the largest library out there, housing the "greatest repository of lore in Outland".
Characters may join the Scryers by completing the quest  [15-30] Allegiance to the Scryers, thereby becoming friendly with the Scryers and hostile with the Aldor.
As of the events of Warlords of Draenor, Scryers still answer to the naaru first and foremost.
Sea Reaver's Run:
The Sea Reaver's Run is the strait north of Icecrown, between the Northrend and an island called Hrothgar's Landing. Halfway the strait are The Wavecrest and The Firehawk, fending off the Kvaldir Harpooners, Kvaldir Berserkers, and the North Sea Kraken. At the southern end of the run are The Silver Blade and The Crimson Dawn, waiting to strike. Between The Wavecrest and The Firehawk is an unnamed kvaldir raiding vessel manned by Kvaldir Deepcallers, which control the kraken.
During the war against the Lich King, Kvaldir Deepcallers brought up krakens to attack any ship that tried to pass through the strait, while he Sunreavers and Silver Covenant both sailed their ships in these waters, they fought the kvaldir back from Icecrown's main shore and had to slay the kraken they kept summoning, with the help of adventurers.
Following the war against the Jailer, the brothers Bronzebeard reported that the kvaldir are still bringing up krakens to attack any ship that tries to pass through the strait.
Seat of the Aspects: The Seat of the Aspects  is the primary tower of Valdrakken and the seat of power of the Dragon Aspects, where Alexstrasza, Kalecgos, Merithra, Ebyssian, Nozdormu, Vyranoth, and their advisors are present. At the bottom of the tower, players have access to portals to Stormwind and Orgrimmar, as well as Unatos, the Keeper of Renown of the Valdrakken Accord major faction.
Seat of the Primus: Seat of the Primus (or Seat of Primus) in Maldraxxus is the Covenant Sanctum available only to members of the Necrolord Covenant. It's the seat of power of the Necrolords. The Necrolords Anima Conductor, Travel Network, and more found here.
Seat of the Triumvirate: The Seat of the Triumvirate is a long-abandoned building in the center of Eredath that was once the center of eredar ruling power. It has been overtaken by the presence of the Void and its Shadowguard, seeking the darkened naaru L'ura. It was a site of miracles and marvels.
Second War:
The Second War, also known as the second Great War, was a major conflict that took place in the Eastern Kingdoms between the Orcish Horde and the Alliance of Lordaeron, beginning five years following the opening of the Dark Portal and lasting until year 6 ADP. The conflict immediately succeeded the First War and involved nearly all major races of the Eastern Kingdoms, which aligned themselves with one of the two factions battling for control of the entire continent.
After the fall of Stormwind, the new orc Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer set out to conquer the rest of Azeroth so that the orcs could secure a homeworld of their own. Doomhammer instigated a renewed campaign to seize control of the other lands north of Stormwind, certain that the human kingdoms would eventually seek to avenge Stormwind if the orcs did not strike first. At the same time, Anduin Lothar, the new Regent of Stormwind, led his surviving people across the Great Sea to the shores of Lordaeron. He met with Terenas Menethil II and warned him of the orcish victory. A meeting with the leaders of the other human nations was called and led to the formation of the Alliance of Lordaeron, which would eventually grow to encompass allies such as the Bronzebeard and Wildhammer dwarves, the gnomes of Gnomeregan, and the high elves of Quel'Thalas, with Lothar as Supreme Allied Commander. Meanwhile, the Horde secured new allies to strengthen their effort against the Alliance, including the continent's various forest troll tribes, the goblins of the Steamwheedle Cartel, and the unwilling participation of the captive red dragonflight.
The Horde led two major offensives. The southern offensive was through the dwarven lands of Khaz Modan which the Horde conquered, except for the dwarven capital city of Ironforge and gnomish capital of Gnomeregan. The northern offensive involved maritime landings via the Great Sea and culminated with a failed invasion of Quel'Thalas. Though the Horde achieved early success by using enslaved red dragons, and almost took the Capital City of Lordaeron after Alterac betrayed its comrades, the war began to turn in favor of the Alliance due to a number of factors, most notably the founding of the Knights of the Order of the Silver Hand and the betrayal of the orc warlock Gul'dan. Outmaneuvered and outmatched, the Horde was ultimately forced to retreat south to its previous holdings. The Alliance armies pushed the Horde back to the bridges of the Thandol Span and eventually liberated Khaz Modan during this pursuit, then caught up and did battle with Doomhammer's forces in the Burning Steppes, the outcome of which proved a decisive victory for the Alliance. However, Lothar had fallen in the battle, and leadership was taken up by his second in command, Turalyon.
The war soon came to an end after a final battle at the Dark Portal, which was subsequently destroyed. The conflict had raged on for over a year, and had seen the destruction of villages and populations across the continent on an unprecedented scale, leaving entire kingdoms devastated in its wake. The war's continent-wide scale saw the races of Azeroth pursue closer ties, with the Alliance enduring for many years afterward. Though the Horde found itself thoroughly defeated, the conflict did not secure long-term peace on the continent. Two years later, a new war would once again break out, culminating in the Invasion of Draenor.
Sepulcher of the First Ones:
Not to be confused with the Sepulcher (a town in Silverpine Forest) or the Sepulcher of Knowledge (a library in Maldraxxus).

The Sepulcher of the First Ones is the final raid instance of the Shadowlands expansion, located east of Zereth Mortis. It is an ancient place of power, containing secrets of the eponymous First Ones that the Jailer seeks to use to rewrite the rules of the universe.
Serpent's Spine:
The Serpent's Spine (or the Pandaren Wall and the Great Wall) is the great wall that separates the mantid territories - the Townlong Steppes and the Dread Wastes - from the Pandaren Empire. The wall is guarded by many Shado-Pan wallwatchers and has several garrisons.
 [30-35 Daily] Roll Club: Serpent's Spine occurs here.
Severed Threads:
The Severed Threads is the fourth Major Faction of The War Within. They represent the conspiracy aimed at dethroning Queen Ansurek and restoring Azj-Kahet to its former glory.
It has three sub-factions, based on favor gained with Anub'azal (The General), Executor Nizrek (The Vizier), and Widow Arak'nai (The Weaver).
Sha'tar:
The Sha'tar, meaning "Born from Light" in Draenei, are a faction of powerful naaru led by A'dal, and a part of the Army of the Light. They rule over a rebuilt Shattrath City, and with the help of the Aldor and the Scryers, they led the battle against Illidan Stormrage and the Burning Legion during the course of the invasion of Outland.
The Sha'tari Skyguard are an air wing of the Sha'tar defending the capital from attackers in the hills, as well as battling against the arakkoa of Terokk in the peaks of Skettis.
Shackle's Den: Shackle's Den is a small camp controlled by Mr. Shackle just north of the Temple of a Thousand Lights in Azsuna.
Shado-Pan Garrison:
Shado-Pan Garrison is the crossroads of Rensai's Watchpost, Sik'vess, and Niuzao Temple in southwest Townlong Steppes. The Underbough and Kri'vess are to the northeast.
Most of the major Shado-Pan players in Townlong wind up at the garrison, including Rushi the Fox, the Shado-Pan quartermaster.
Shadow Fracture: Shadow Fracture is a Legion camp covered in Void energies where eredar are enslaving voidwalkers.
Shadowbreak Ravine: Shadowbreak Ravine is a well-hidden haven for Burning Blade cultists found in the mountains southeast of Shok'Thokar in Desolace. It holds several structures including giant mushrooms and a summoning circle with giant chains. The Burning Blade and demon army, which has invaded Magram Village and pushed the centaur from the area, are commanded by Agogridon. They have begun burning the structures and renamed the area to Shok'Thokar. After the quest  [10-30] Death to Agogridon, the area will only have the corpses of Burning Blade cultists and demons.
Shadowguard: The Shadowguard are a faction of ethereals who have heeded the call of the Void and become void ethereals. They serve as Nexus-King Salhadaar's military division.
Shadowguard Incursion: Shadowguard Incursion is a location in Eredath.
Shadowmoon Burial Grounds:
Shadowmoon Burial Grounds is a dungeon introduced in Warlords of Draenor, set in Shadowmoon Valley within Anguish Fortress. It features Ner'zhul as its end boss.
Following the defeat of the Dark Star, Ner'zhul and his followers retreated here.
Shal'Aran:
Shal'Aran (/ˈʃɑːləˌrɑːn/ SHAHL-ə-rahn) is an underground ruin in Meredil in Suramar.
Withered avoid it, which makes it a good refuge for First Arcanist Thalyssra and a class leader when fleeing from a swarm of Withered crawling around Meredil. It is initially occupied by the banshee Keeper Selentia; after clearing Shal'Aran on  [45] Arcane Thirst, it becomes the staging ground for the fledging nightfallen rebellion against Grand Magistrix Elisande, led by Thalyssra.
Occupied by the resistance, Shal'Aran slowly comes to life, gradually filling with resistance sympathizers and refugees from all over Suramar, who also clear the debris and fill the chamber with their belongings, supplies, and decorations. Notably, Valewalker Farodin plants an arcan'dor on the central platform of Shal'Aran, which eventually grows to the point of bearing magical fruit capable of curing the nightborne's addiction to the Nightwell.
After the liberation of Suramar, Shal'Aran became a stronghold of the reformed Moon Guard. Thalyssra was pleased to garrison them in Shal'Aran, for their forces offer the arcan'dor additional protection. Even after returning to power in Suramar City, Thalyssra considers Shal'Aran her second home.
Shaladrassil:
Shaladrassil (/ʃəˈlæ.drə.sɪl/ shə-LA-drə-sil) is a World Tree situated in northern Val'sharah that was once responsible for protecting the land, but it was corrupted by the Emerald Nightmare during the Burning Legion's third invasion of Azeroth.
The ruined town of Shala'nir was built around it. The Emerald Nightmare raid can be entered through the base of the tree, and Darkheart Thicket, which is underneath it, can be entered from a nearby cave. Inside the raid, the Clutch of Corruption occupies the trunk, while the Emerald Nightmare proper can be entered through the Core of the Nightmare located simultaneously atop the tree and inside the Nightmare itself.
Shalewind Canyon: Shalewind Canyon is an area in the eastern part of Redridge Mountains, near Stonewatch Falls, with a small human encampment.
Shan'ze Dao:
Shan'ze Dao is the northernmost island in the Westersea off the northwest coast of Townlong Steppes. The Shado-Pan from the Shado-Pan Garrison have staked a claim on the southeastern corner of the island, setting up a small camp, and a portal back to the garrison. With the rise of the Thunder King, the majority of the Shan'ze mogu on the island have gone to the Throne of Thunder to prepare for the final assault on Pandaria. Despite the majority leaving, Lei Shen still maintains a firm grip on the island, keeping it under mogu occupation.
Upon completing the quest  [25-35] Through the Portal, players will be able to teleport between Shan'ze Dao and Shado-Pan Garrison.
Even though the Isle of Thunder is just north of Shan'ze Dao, it is located in a separate instance and is not reachable by flying or swimming north. Players attempting to do so will find their way blocked by an impenetrable fog.
Shang Xi Training Grounds:
The Shang Xi Training Grounds is the initial spawning location for newly-created pandaren. Located on the northeast portion of Shen-zin Su, the Wandering Isle, adventurers learn under the tutelage of Master Shang Xi. The place is a monastery and has its own small temple.
Every adventurer that leaves these training grounds must be ready to take up arms in defense of their fellow pandaren.
Shang Xi's Academy:
Shang Xi's Academy is the in-game faction of starting playable pandaren, who start their adventure on the Wandering Isle of Shen-zin Su.
For nearly three generations, the esteemed Shang Xi has prepared pandaren heroes for lives of adventure.
Shaper's Terrace: The Shaper's Terrace is the name of two titan-related areas found in Un'Goro Crater, referring to Khaz'goroth "The Shaper". One section, on the bluffs above and east of Marshal's Refuge, contains a Waygate connecting to Sholazar Basin. Another in the cliffs on the eastern wall of Un'Goro houses the titanic watcher Nablya, who continues Khaz'gorith's experiments on life in the crater.
Shattered Rise: Shattered Rise is a subzone in the Spires of Arak on Draenor. It is a Shattered Hand clan area.
Shattered Sun Offensive: The Shattered Sun Offensive (abbreviated as SSO) is an army rallied by the Sha'tar naaru to prevent Prince Kael'thas Sunstrider's mad bid to use the Sunwell as a portal to summon his master, Kil'jaeden. The Offensive marks the union between the draenei priests of the Aldor and the blood elf wizards of the Scryers in an effort to avert the Burning Legion's invasion of the Isle of Quel'Danas. Their main base of operations is the port town of Sun's Reach, located on the northwest edge of the island, where they used its arcane sanctum, armory, and harbor to supply their troops during the Battle for Quel'Danas.
Shimmering Expanse: Shimmering Expanse is the second zone in the undersea region known as Vashj'ir. It is the stronghold of the naga empire within the area. Besides the wide variety of plant and marine life there are also many mysterious wonders such as Nespirah. This zone is home to the ancient Ruins of Vashj'ir. Players will learn about the ruins, and what befell them, as well as interesting factoids about Queen Azshara and Lady Vashj's mother.
Shipwreck Shore: Shipwreck Shore is the appropriately named beach shore on which the goblins wash ashore on the Lost Isles after the Alliance ships attacked Gallywix's Yacht carrying the Kezanian evacuees and slaves. The forward section of the ship has been made into a shelter. Several problems have arisen from the foliage to the north.
Sholazar Basin:
Sholazar Basin (/ˈʃoʊləzɑːr/ SHOL-ə-zarh) is a tropical jungle basin in the midst of Northrend. It is found between Borean Tundra and Icecrown. The region's climate and safety from the Scourge is maintained by pylons, erected by the titans. The whole history of Sholazar is that of a cradle of life, with at least some of the titan keepers taking an interest in the development of creatures great and small.
During the war against the Lich King, one pylon in the east has fallen, and the Scourge took this opportunity to invade from Icecrown to the north.
In Sholazar Basin, adventurers can take part in a faction war between the wolvar Frenzyheart Tribe and the gorlocs, arctic cousins of murlocs. The various gorloc tribes have gathered together to form the group called the Oracles. Adventurers are only able to choose one side at a time, but are allowed to easily change to whichever faction they wish to be allied with.
Silver Covenant:
The Silver Covenant was a militant faction of high elves founded and led by Ranger-General Vereesa Windrunner. They rejected the admission of the blood elves into the Kirin Tor, and took it upon themselves to serve as a military deterrent for any potential Horde uprising in Dalaran City. The Horde equivalent of the Silver Covenant were the Sunreavers.
During the war against the Lich King, they joined the ranks of the Alliance Vanguard and the 7th Legion, as part of the Valiance Expedition in Northrend. The Silver Covenant later answered the call of Quel'Thalas to halt the growing threat of the Amani Empire. After Jaina Proudmoore succeeded Rhonin, the Covenant managed to temporarily expel the Sunreavers from the city during the Purge of Dalaran; however, the latter ended up being reinstated during the third invasion of the Burning Legion. The Silver Covenant then pledged itself to the cause of the Unseen Path to repel the demonic invaders.
A few years later, the Silver Covenant defended Dalaran from the Kaheti nerubians' attack, until they had to be evacuated on the Isle of Dorn when Xal'atath destroyed the magical city. When Xal'atath turned her eye to Quel'Thalas, the Silver Covenant brokered a measure of peace with the Sunreavers and reinforced the blood elves against the Void. In the wake of Dalaran's loss and the threats posed to Silvermoon, Vereesa and Aethas Sunreaver agreed that conflict between their wounded factions was no longer tenable, and disbanded the Silver Covenant and the Sunreavers to unite their people in the Silversun Compact.
Silvermoon City:
Silvermoon City (or the City of Silvermoon and just Silvermoon) is the crown jewel of the blood elves, once the high elves, and the capital city of the kingdom of Quel'Thalas. It is nestled in the northern reaches of the Eversong Woods (at the northernmost tip of the Eastern Kingdoms) in their ancestral homeland of Quel'Thalas. The city guards the way to the Sunwell, and as such is of strategic importance to the kingdom. The beauty of its spires and thoroughfares stand in stark contrast to the Dead Scar, the tainted path that the Scourge tore through the city during the Third War. Though nearly destroyed by Arthas Menethil's attack on the Sunwell, Silvermoon was rebuilt by the Magisters and became once again a thriving city, while the western half of it remained in ruins since the Scourge invasion.
The rebirth of the Sunwell at the climax of the Battle for Quel'Danas lifted spirits among the sin'dorei, who continued to heal Silvermoon's scars in the hope of returning their beloved capital to its former glory, and eventually succeeded. Risen from the ruin inflicted by Arthas, the gleaming capital of the sin'dorei, fully restored, now stands as a testament to reclamation and resurrection.
According to the sin'dorei themselves, Silvermoon City is unrivaled in beauty or grandeur. Its majestic spires reflect their boundless elegance, creativity, and craftsmanship.
The Silvermoon Guard are the law enforcement and protectors of the capital, keeping the peace within its walls and across the Eversong Woods.
Silvermoon City Guardian: Silvermoon City Guardians are max level guards located throughout the blood elf capital of Silvermoon City. They give directions to various locations within the city. They also appear in Eversong Woods.
Sinfall: Sinfall is the Sanctum of the Venthyr Covenant. It is located in the central part of the Ember Ward, in western Revendreth. A valued possesion of Denathrius in the past, the structure is now used as a base of operations for Prince Renathal and his rebellion.
Skitter: Skitter is a kobold located in the Ringing Deeps. She is the leader of the Quickwick tribe of kobolds.
Skold-Ashil:
Skold-Ashil is a large vrykul town on Ashil's Bay in central Stormheim. It is built around the Vault of Eyir and contains both Tideskorn shield-maidens and Valkyra aspirants loyal to Eyir.
It was likely named after Ashildir.
Skumblade tribe:
The Skumblade tribe of saurok are led by the Skumblade Saur-Priests, who promote the idea that the saurok were not created by the mogu, but instead were created by Kros, the invisible devilsaur in the sky. Kroshik is held to be a gift from Kros and a glimpse at the Skumblade's future.
Several members were taken as prisoners by Garrosh Hellscream and the True Horde.
Skyhorn: Skyhorn is a Highmountain tauren village found in eastern Highmountain. As the name suggests, it is the home of the Skyhorn tribe. It is currently under attack by the Crawliac harpies.
Skytop Observatory: Skytop Observatory is a ruined dragon settlement located atop a mountain in the southwestern Waking Shores, east of the Ruby Lifeshrine. Recently, several dragons and dragon-riders from the Valdrakken Accord made the area their home and now teach others about dragonriding. Skyriding facilities, such as the Rostrum of Transformation, are found here.
Slagworks: The Slagworks is a foundry southeast of Baradin Hold on Tol Barad. Horde and Alliance forces will battle over it to gain control of the island.
Slain Tualiq Villager: Slain Tualiq Villagers are tuskarr found slain everywhere on Hrothgar's Landing. Freeing their spirits with the  [Confessor's Prayer Book] is the objective of the daily quest  [25-30 Daily] The Light's Mercy.
Slave Pits: The Slave Pits is a Southsea mercenary camp found on the northwestern shores of the Lost Isles. It's here that the recaptured goblins, class trainers included, have been taken. The goblin Candy Cane is overseeing the area in Trade Prince Gallywixs name.
Soggy's Gamble:
Soggy's Gamble is a town on the southeastern coast of the Dread Wastes founded by the shipwrecked crew of the Mist-Hopper, an Anglers vessel under the command of Captain "Soggy" Su-Dao. The Chittering Coast overlooks the cove to the northeast, the Lonesome Cove is southeast, and Mazu's Overlook is the high bluff to the immediate west. The Anglers here make most of their money by fishing emperor crabs,  but they send all kinds of goods from the sea back around the Serpent's Spine, including oils, plants, shark teeth, and rare minerals.
San the Sea Calmer runs an inn here named the Chum Bucket.
Sorrowmurk:
The Sorrowmurk is the area of the Swamp of Sorrows located just east of the Pool of Tears and the Sunken Temple.  The area was once crawling with green dragonspawn as well as a large green drake that patrolled the region, making it inhospitable for all but the most adventurous traveler.
A neutral band of goblins led by Crazy Larry has since established a camp on the shore of the Sorrowmurk. While the tide of dragonkin has subsided, the area has now come under attack from gilblins.
Southsea Freebooters: The Southsea Freebooters (or Southseas Freebooters and the Southsea Pirates) are a group of pirates. Prior to the Cataclysm, they could be found along the coast of the Barrens and Tanaris, and have even recently appeared in the flooded Thousand Needles. Their connection with the Northsea Freebooters is unclear, but the Northsea pirates seem to have a severe dislike towards their Southsea counterparts.
Southsea Holdfast:
The Southsea Holdfast is a Southsea Pirates outpost located on a shelf above the Shimmering Deep in Thousand Needles. They've built ramps from the top to the waters down below where they have three vessels awaiting orders. This group of pirates is led by Tony Two-Tusk, which can be found in the nearby cavern named the Admiral's Den.
A goblin and his gnome companion from the speedbarge came to this location to barter with the pirate, however, they were captured and since then the pirate have begun attacking the ship.
During the Thousand Boat Bash, the ships anchored here are raided for grog.
After the Fourth War, the area is still occupied by the Southsea pirates.
Southwind Village: Southwind Village was once a night elven base of operation in Silithus, but was destroyed by the qiraji during the War of the Shifting Sands. Following the devastation of Silithus by Sargeras, its ruins now serve as a Horde base for the goblin mining operation for Azerite in the Wound.
Sparktouched Haven: Sparktouched Haven is an outpost of the Oracles, located just west of The Mosslight Pillar in south-west Sholazar Basin. It is the home of the Sparktouched tribe who are at constant war with the wolvar of the Frenzyheart Tribe at Kartak's Hold.
Spearborn Encampment: Spearborn Encampment is a Frenzyheart outpost in northwest Sholazar Basin. It is bordered by the Savage Thicket to the east, the Glimmering Pillar to the southeast, and Dorian's Outpost to the south. The nearest Oracle camp of gorlocs is to the southeast at Mistwhisper Refuge.
Splinter Fist:
The Splinter Fist, also known as the Stone Fist Clan, are a group of ogres found in Vul'Gol Ogre Mound. The leader and champion of this group is Zzarc'Vul, whom can be found inside the cave.
According to Watcher Dodds, they usually keep to themselves, but they've got a bad habit of attacking travelers. As the Night Watch wanted to only risk its few members in the defense of more immediate threats, they engaged adventurers to kill some of the ogres in exchange for rewards.
At some point, Abercrombie was attacked by the ogres, and after they chased him off, they wagered back to their mound and brought his "crate of precious tools and herbs" with them. The necromancer thus sent an Alliance adventurer to recover the crate. Viktori Prism'Antras also needed the monocle of Zzarc'Vul to use for his research and sent an adventurer in the cave to defeat the ogre leader.
In Season of Discovery, a group of Splinter Fist ogres crossed into the Emerald Dream and got corrupted by the Nightmare.
Splinterspear Junction: Splinterspear Junction is where the main road into the Swamp of Sorrows splits. The north branch will take you past the Harborage and to the Fallow Sanctuary, while the southern branch will take you to Stonard and the path to the Blasted Lands. An old orcish watch tower sits there and the area is regularly patrolled by Horde guards, so Alliance adventurers are advised to keep their eyes open when traveling the roads. The guards are PvP tagged.
Splithoof Heights:
Splithoof Heights is the Galak centaur village, on the large shelf to the north of the Shimmering Deep in Thousand Needles. It's here that the Galak retreated to from Splithoof Hold, Splithoof Crag, and Camp E'thok to survive the flooding caused by the Cataclysm.
The land contains many oil pools and likely has a huge pocket of oil under them. Both the goblins and gnomes are trying to make a deal with the centaur in order to gain the drilling rights to the oil.
The centaur here worship an air elemental and a lord within the Skywall,  named Whrrrl, who has become the supposed leader of the tribe.
Starbreeze Village:
Starbreeze Village lies southeast of Shadowglen and east of Dolanaar in Teldrassil. Once a night elven village, Starbreeze became overrun by corrupted furbolgs of the Gnarlpine tribe. The village consists of a few small houses. Ferocitas the Dream Eater can be found in its outskirts and Uruson can be seen patrolling the village.
During the Burning of Teldrassil, the conflagration spread to Starbreeze Village before it reached Darnassus.
Starlit Overlook: Starlit Overlook is an area of the celestial tree of Tirna Rowen, located on a plateau above the Shrouded Mire. It is the highest point of all of Ardenweald, and the first part of the forest you see when you enter from Oribos. Lady Moonberry and Featherlight sent the adventurer from here to tell Droman Krelnor that his grove was to be culled.
Steamwheedle Cartel: The Steamwheedle Cartel is one of the largest and most successful of the goblin cartels in the Undermine. It is a neutral organization that controls several cities and towns around Azeroth. They have made a great deal of profit from maintaining neutrality in the conflict between the Horde and the Alliance. Their services are always available to the highest bidder, employing anyone regardless of their affiliation if they can produce results. In Undermine, they are known for being the oldest and largest cartel in town, with their hands in every industry across Azeroth and beyond, currently specializing in premium-grade alchemy. In the Undermine, their color scheme is green.
Steamwheedle Cartel (faction): Steamwheedle Cartel is a faction of The War Within, based out of Steamwheedle Laboratories in Undermine.
Stillpine Hold:
Stillpine Hold is a furbolg settlement on the northern side of Azuremyst Isle and home to the Stillpine tribe. The hold within the cave itself is occupied by corrupted moonkin.
In Year 26 ADP, after the Oomooroo wildkin succumbed to madness caused by the Bloodmyst Radiation, they invaded the hold with the help of The Kurken. Through some digging, the draenei adventurer found a Blood Crystal stationed deep in the cave, confirming the source of their corruption. With no other choice, Stillpine the Younger tasked heroes to kill Chieftain Oomooroo, then sent a squad to clear the hold.
At some point, the Siltfin murlocs attacked Stillpine Hold and stole the tribe's food stores, leading Gurf to recruit draenei heroes to recover the stolen grain at the Silting Shore.
Stillpine tribe: The Stillpine tribe is a tribe of furbolgs inhabiting Stillpine Hold in Azuremyst Isle. Led by High Chief Stillpine, they allied themselves with the draenei after the Exodar crashed on the island.
Stonehearth:
Stonehearth is the home of the Earthen within Deepholm. The town is located on the upper shelf in the far southwest.
The town has been overtaken by the stone troggs, the earthen fight to retake it, and then move onto the stone troggs home for revenge.

 This section concerns content related to Legion.
Stormcaller Mylra came here and asked the earthen about Thrall's weapon, the Doomhammer. They didn't know anything about the weapon, but they were missing several prospectors. The prospectors were found dead in the Crumbling Depths by the Earthen Ring.
Stoneplow:
Stoneplow is a small farming village found just east of the wall separating the Valley of the Four Winds from the Dread Wastes to the west. The Blacksoil, Greentill, Marlfur, and Spadepaw families of farmers tend to its fields.
Stoneplow has come under attack from the mantid, and the Shado-Pan have come to help fend off the invasion. Had the mantid taken the village, they would be able to take the entire valley as there is nothing beyond this point that could stop them. The village sent Han and Len in search of help.
Stonewatch: Stonewatch is the common name of the military stronghold in central Redridge Mountains. This human fortress serves as a defensive base against the orcish raids coming from the nearby Burning Steppes. It includes both the easily defensible Stonewatch Keep and the armored Stonewatch Tower, with the Stonewatch Falls cascading down a cliff face below it.
Stormrage:
Stormrage is the name of a World of Warcraft novel by Richard A. Knaak.
The novel centers around Malfurion Stormrage; Christie Golden confirmed it was definitely not about Illidan at BlizzCon 2008, and Chris Metzen and Micky Neilson said Malfurion would play a major role at New York Comic Con 2009.
The storyline explores the corruption of the Emerald Dream. The story takes place after the War against the Lich King as evidenced by Sylvanas' nightmare, where she notes that Arthas has already been defeated.
An audiobook version read by Richard Ferrone was released in February, 2010.
Stormrage Barrow Dens:
The Stormrage Barrow Dens are the sacred barrow dens of the Moonglade where many of the nightelven druids slumber in the Emerald Dream. The great druid Malfurion Stormrage, for whom the barrow dens are named, used to slumber deep within the dens. Clintar Dreamwalker now sleeps here.
Directly north of the barrow dens are Minions of Omen, high level wolf-like creatures. They only come out at night during the Lunar Festival. A part of the Moonkin Festival also occurs here.
Stormreaver clan:
The Stormreaver clan was a small but powerful orcish clan created by Gul'dan at the onset of the Second War. Most of the clan was destroyed when Gul'dan ventured to the Tomb of Sargeras in search of the power therein, being either torn apart by the demons dwelling in the Tomb or slaughtered by the Black Tooth Grin forces sent to exact vengeance on Gul'dan for abandoning the Horde during its critical time. Some remnants of the clan remained, scattered in various covens of their own making or as hermits.
Its clan color was blue.
Stormspire:
The Stormspire is a neutral Consortium-run town located in Netherstorm. It is located beneath the interconnected eco-domes of Sutheron and Skyperch. Lush jungle vegetation grows within the settlement creating a sharp contrast with the purple, arcane-channeled sky.
The town itself is of draenei architecture, however there are no draenei to be seen here now. Nexus-Prince Haramad, leader of the Consortium, is found in his chambers at the uppermost part of the Spire. He oversees the town through a holographic image. Haramad deals with Prince Kael'thas and the forces of Azeroth alike. The Consortium uses this base to engage in activities such as excavation, mining and trading throughout the Netherstorm.
The Stormspire is under constant threat by the forces of the Burning Legion from their forge bases Gehenna and Oblivion. Nether-Stalker Nauthis leads the defense efforts. The Protectorate also has a small presence at the Stormspire.
The town is accessible in two ways; via a flight path with the goblin Flight Master Grennik and by an elevator . Located here is a Grand Master jewelcrafting trainer, an ethereal named Jazdalaad, and a Grand Master enchanting trainer, an ethereal named Asarnan. Karaaz, the Consortium Quartermaster reputation vendor, is also based here. Dealer Jadyan offers exotic weapons. Dealer Rashaad sells rare pets, including the unique brown rabbit. Numerous other vendors and quest givers are also here. Many of the goods are smuggled, avoiding naaru prohibitions and goblin taxation alike.
A small goblin contingent is present at the Stormspire, looking for ways to steal parts of the Ethereals' eco-dome technology. This is causing critical problems to the sustainability of the domes. Because of this, the Consortium has even considered locking down the Stormspire to outsiders.
Stormstout Brewery:
The Stormstout Brewery was the third announced 5-man dungeon of World of Warcraft: Mists of Pandaria.
The brewery has been overrun by virmen, hozen, and alementals. Players are tasked with clearing out the brewery to reclaim Chen Stormstout's family heritage... and his beer.
Stormsunder Crater:
Stormsunder Crater  is the eastern anchor of the Forbidden Reach. The entrance to the Siege Creche is just northeast of the elementalist spire, and the Burrow of the Faithful cave is to the southeast.
The area is bordered by the Stormsunder Mountain to the north, Ebon Landing offshore to the east, Darksand Hollow to the southeast, Talonlords' Perch and the Old Weyrn Grounds to the southwest, and the Hornswog Grounds to the northwest.
Two dragonriding races start near the crater: the Stormsunder Crater Circuit at  to the southeast, and the Aerie Chasm Cruise at  to the northwest. There's also a Dragon Glyph and a Dragonscale Expedition Flag north of the crater proper on the Stormsunder Mountain peak.
Two rares are present: Volcanakk at  /  in the Siege Creche, and Veltrax at  in the Burrow of the Faithful.
A Forbidden Hoard chest spawns at  south of the crater on a small island guarded by two Farscale Raiders.
Stormsunder Mountain:
Stormsunder Mountain  overlooks Stormsunder Crater in eastern Forbidden Reach.
The area is bordered by Dragonskull Island to the north, Ebon Landing offshore to the southeast, Stormsunder Crater to the south, and the Hornswog Grounds to the west.
Atop the mountain are a Dragonscale Expedition Flag, a Dragon Glyph, and an engineering teleporter target.
Stormwind (kingdom):
The Kingdom of Stormwind (also called Kingdom of Azeroth) is one of the seven human nations in the Eastern Kingdoms, which controls much of the southern continent of Azeroth, from Elwynn Forest and Westfall to Duskwood and the Redridge Mountains. Originally settled by descendants of the Arathi after the Empire of Arathor split apart, Stormwind flourished until the First War when it was conquered and laid waste by the Orcish Horde from Draenor. The survivors of that conflict, led by Anduin Lothar, sought refuge in Lordaeron and were able to reclaim their homeland at the end of the Second War with the aid of the Alliance of Lordaeron. Since the fall of the kingdom of Lordaeron to the Scourge during the Third War, the kingdom of Stormwind has become the strongest bastion of humanity and the most powerful force in the Grand Alliance. From its capital, Stormwind City, its citizens hold fast to the principles of honor and justice as they defend their settlements, and the Alliance, against any aggressors.
Stormwind is ruled by the House of Wrynn from their court in Stormwind Keep. The throne is presently occupied by King Anduin Wrynn, succeeding his father King Varian Wrynn who died at the Broken Shore. Also aiding in the governing of Stormwind is the House of Nobles: the bureaucracy of Stormwind's government that currently aids the king in the running of the kingdom's day-to-day affairs. After Anduin vacated his throne temporarily, Turalyon became lord regent with the support of the House of Nobles, and in turn, has on numerous occasions called upon Genn Greymane to watch over the kingdom when he is needed on the field.
Stormwind City:
Stormwind City, also known as New Stormwind or simply Stormwind, is the capital city of the eponymous kingdom of Stormwind and the largest human city on Azeroth. Located north of Elwynn Forest on Azeroth region's northwest coast, it has become one of the last great human cities after the Third War, and embodies the heart of the Alliance. Stormwind's willingness to work with others to find diplomatic solutions stands out as one of its true strengths. Its citizens hold fast to the principles of honor and justice as they defend their settlements and the Alliance against any aggressors.
No city better demonstrates human determination than Stormwind. Destroyed by the Orcish Horde during the First War, the capital was painstakingly reconstructed by the Stonemasons' Guild after the Second War. Parts of the city were eventually razed again when the Dragon Aspect Deathwing provoked the Cataclysm that shattered the world. From the magnificent Cathedral of Light, which serves as a major spiritual hub, to the awe-inspiring Valley of Heroes, which commemorates the sacrifices of Stormwind's loyal champions, the city truly represents the courageous heart of humanity, and serves as a bastion of the Holy Light.
The Stormwind City Guard are the law enforcement and protectors of Stormwind City, keeping the peace within the city's walls.
Stormwind Harbor:
Stormwind Harbor is a large port and shipyard, consisting of a series of wharfs, dry docks, and fortifications located in the northwestern area of Stormwind City, with the access point set between Lion's Rest and Cathedral Square. The harbor serves as a major strategic base for both the kingdom of Stormwind and the Alliance navy. Here, many Alliance warships are constructed and fleets assembled; it is likely the largest and most important Alliance naval base in the Great Sea and potentially beyond. From a civilian perspective, transport ships regularly sail from the harbor to numerous other destinations across Azeroth, such as Boralus in Kul Tiras, and Valiance Keep in Northrend.
The harbor has been expanded in recent years and is much safer to enter than in the past. It is heavily fortified to protect against attack, presumably by the Horde, whose navy is also known to operate off the western coast of the Eastern Kingdoms. To this end, there are numerous tiered plateaus leading to the city proper, upon which are stationed articles of heavy artillery in the form of cannons (whether on the ground or mounted in towers). Additionally, on the lower tiers, numerous ballistae and steam tanks can be found aimed out to sea.
The Stormwind Harbor Guards is a military subgroup of the Stormwind City Guard, operating and patrolling the Stormwind Harbor. It is necessary for a crew to have regulatory papers to moor at Stormwind Harbor. While pirates are usually killed on sight by the Stormwind Army, in very rare cases, they may obtain a royal pardon for past crimes if they manage to accomplish a mission of great importance to the kingdom. If successful, they will be allowed to moor at the kingdom's harbor.
Stormwind Keep:
The mighty Stormwind Keep (also called Stonewind Keep, Castle Stormwind, stronghold of Stormwind, Stormwind Castle, and after its reconstruction sometimes referred as Castle of New Stormwind) is the seat of power of the human kingdom of Stormwind. This keep is the residence of the Stormwindian kings, currently King Anduin Wrynn. The royal court as well as some of the nobles of the kingdom are also here.
The Keep offers a view of the whole city, so that the king can watch over the masses, and provide a powerful reminder of what deserves to be defended. Citizens make good use of the garden and the Royal Library, strolling the grounds and reading, and it has private areas - the king's rooms, guest quarters for prominent visitors, and a small royal armory for extremely rare pieces. The keep has its own personal contingent of fiercely devoted guards but also a considerable number of agents, posing as lesser noblemen or servants to the crown. There are also multiple secret passages.
Sun's Reach: Sun's Reach is a blood elven town and the staging area for the Shattered Sun Offensive on the Isle of Quel'Danas.
Sunfury:
The Sunfury (also referred to as Kael'thas' forces and Kael'thas' army) were the armies under Prince Kael'thas Sunstrider's command after he departed from Azeroth and joined Illidan's forces in Outland. The army consisted mostly of blood elves, but also included some fel orcs and demons, numbering in the thousands. Pilgrims from Quel'Thalas also voluntarily joined their ranks after crossing the Dark Portal. The bulk of their forces were established in the Netherstorm and Shadowmoon Valley, while several members left the main contingent to pursue other goals—most notably, the Scryers and the blood elven forces loyal to Illidan Stormrage.
Although Kael'thas was allied with Illidan, he eventually betrayed him to join the Burning Legion, manipulated by Kil'jaeden to bring "salvation" to his people. According to various discussions between Dawnblade agents, however, it seems that the rank-and-file soldiers were not truly loyal to the Legion or its goals. They were more interested in saving the sin'dorei from the addiction that bound them, or in monetary gain, believing themselves the true masters of the demons. Kael'thas was eventually killed by Horde adventurers in Tempest Keep, only to be resurrected by his demonic master as a pawn to invade Azeroth.
During the battle for Quel'Danas, the prince recalled his loyal servitors from Outland to his side at Quel'Danas. Though some remnants of his army heeded this call and became known as the Dawnblade at the Sunwell Plateau, others did not. A number of the Sunfury forces broke away from the prince's increasingly damning path and instead reaffirmed their loyalty to their homeland of Quel'Thalas and its acting regent, Lor'themar Theron. Though little is known of the organization's current status, their presence has helped ease the burden on the Farstriders in protecting the nation's borders.
