Sunfury Spire: Sunfury Spire is Silvermoon City's royal palace located in the Court of the Sun. It contains the Inner Sanctum, the council room, the Artists' Quarters, and the private royal quarters.
Sunhawk: The Sunhawks were a group of blood elves loyal to Prince Kael'thas Sunstrider who commandeered the Exodar before the draenei, led by Prophet Velen, reclaimed it. On Bloodmyst Isle, a small group of Sunhawks was led by Sironas, who had begun using the remains of the ship's Vector Coil to create a Sun Gate, a dimensional rift which allowed for a steady supply of reinforcements to be shipped from Outland. They wished to reclaim the Exodar and attempted to turn draenei into man'ari eredar. They have since been disbanded by Alliance adventurers sent by the Hand of Argus.
Sunreaver Onslaught:
The Sunreaver Onslaught is the Horde reputation faction introduced in patch 5.2. It is personally led by Lor'themar Theron, Regent Lord of Quel'Thalas, and bears the namesake of the Sunreavers. Its base camp is named the Dawnseeker Promontory. Their main goals are to prevent the Kirin Tor Offensive, allied to the Alliance, from obtaining powerful artifacts from Emperor Lei Shen and to also fight the coalition of Zandalari and mogu threatening Pandaria.
Daily quests for the Sunreaver Onslaught are divided into two categories, only one of which can be chosen per day: PvE-oriented tasks, or PvP-based missions. The former involves assisting Grand Magister Rommath, Halduron Brightwing and Aethas Sunreaver in dealing with the local threats (primarily the saurok, the Zandalari and the mogu), while the latter is focused on attacking the Kirin Tor forces and defending the promontory.
Sunreaver's Command:
Sunreaver's Command is a Sunreaver outpost opposite to Windrunner's Overlook north of the Unbound Thicket in northeast Crystalsong Forest.
Following the war against the Jailer, the brothers Bronzebeard reported that while most of the Sunreavers remained with Dalaran as it moved, Sunreaver's Command is still their outpost in Northrend.
Sunreavers:
The Sunreavers were a faction of blood elves who represented the Horde in Dalaran. Led by Archmage Aethas Sunreaver, they joined the Horde Expedition in Northrend and sought to have their people readmitted into the Kirin Tor, a plight they were successful in. The Sunreavers were eventually expelled from the city some time after Jaina Proudmoore came into power. Their Alliance equivalent was the Silver Covenant.
Following their return to Quel'Thalas, Aethas and the Sunreavers began collaborating with the Magisters under Grand Magister Rommath,and later took up arms in the name of the Sunreaver Onslaught under Lor'themar Theron's direct leadership. The organization eventually rejoined the Kirin Tor during the third invasion of the Burning Legion, with several members pledging themselves to the cause of the Tirisgarde.
A few years later, the Sunreavers defended Dalaran from the Kaheti nerubians' attack, until they had to be evacuated on the Isle of Dorn when Xal'atath destroyed the magical city. When Xal'atath turned her eye to Quel'Thalas, the Sunreavers returned to their homeland to join the War of Light and Shadow, and accepted overtures of peace from the Silver Covenant to prevent its fall. In the wake of Dalaran's loss and the threats posed to Silvermoon, Aethas and Vereesa Windrunner agreed that conflict between their wounded factions was no longer tenable, and disbanded the Sunreavers and the Silver Covenant to unite their people in the Silversun Compact.
Sunset Brewgarden: The Sunset Brewgarden can be found immediately southeast of the Dusklight Bridge on the northern border of Dread Wastes from Townlong Steppes. Nestled in an unnamed kypari tree, the Amber Vault can also be found inside, accessed via the south side of the tree on the Horrid March. Just west, immediately south of the Dusklight bridge, is Kor'vess.
Sunstrider Isle: Sunstrider Isle is a small island located in northwestern Eversong Woods. It is the starting area for blood elven players.
Sunsworn Camp: Sunsworn Camp is a small Blood Knight camp found in southeastern Talador. Its from here Lady Liadrin can sense more of the demonic taint in the area.
Sunwell:
The Sunwell is a fount of mystical power located within the Sunwell Plateau, on the Sunwell Grove of Quel'Danas. While its waters, holy to the high elves, were originally pure arcane power, it has since been restored as a fount of both arcane and Light energy. It was originally created by Dath'Remar Sunstrider who used a stolen vial of water from the Well of Eternity at a nexus of ley lines within the northern forests of the Eastern Kingdoms. His Highborne followers named the Sunwell after their leader, in honor of his bold quest to reignite their culture, as magic had been outlawed in their ancestral homeland. Now calling themselves the high elves, they embraced the Sunwell as the very heart of their culture, since the kingdom of Quel'Thalas was only made possible because of it.
The Sunwell was destroyed during the Scourge invasion of Quel'Thalas, when the death knight Arthas Menethil used its power to resurrect Kel'Thuzad. The ritual tainted its energies and threatened to kill the elven survivors of the onslaught; in response, Prince Kael'thas Sunstrider, last of Dath'Remar's bloodline, destroyed the corrupted Sunwell. This act saved his people from destruction but also cut them off from their source of power completely. Now calling themselves the blood elves in honor of their fallen people, the survivors were left with an insatiable hunger for magic.
Created by the red dragon Korialstrasz, the Sunwell's remaining power manifested itself as Anveena Teague, who was put under the protection of Quel'Thalas. However, after he was defeated on Outland and twisted by fel energies, Kael'thas returned to the ruins of the Sunwell and openly sided with the Burning Legion, seeking to usher his new master Kil'jaeden into Azeroth through the fountain's exhausted mystical depths. Leeching the powers of Anveena and the naaru M'uru, and fortified by arcane energy harvested in Netherstorm, the Sun King restored the Sunwell.
During the Battle for Quel'Danas, the Shattered Sun Offensive succeeded in defeating the Legion, while Prophet Velen of the draenei sanctified the corrupted Sunwell using the holy spark of M'uru. The Sunwell shone once again, now a fount of both arcane power and Light -- bringing about the gradual "rebirth of a nation's soul". Almost immediately after its restoration, the addiction pangs of both the blood elves and their high elven kin were considerably relieved.
After Xal'atath usurped the power of Dimensius, she unleashed the Devouring Host and the Voidstorm upon Quel'Danas, intent on claiming the Sunwell. The Vanguard of the Light was summoned to defend it, and in their hour of need, beseeched the Light to empower the Sunwell to keep the storm at bay. Xal'atath defeated the Vanguard at the Voidspire and tore the dark naaru L'ura from Alleria Windrunner to corrupt the Sunwell into the Darkwell. The elves of Azeroth united to retake Quel'Danas and cleansed the Darkwell, anointing it as the Dawnwell.
Sunwell Plateau: The Sunwell Plateau is a raid instance located on the Isle of Quel'Danas north of Silvermoon City.
Sylvanas Windrunner:
Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, formerly styled "the Dark Lady" and "the Banshee Queen" (/sɪlˈvɑːnəs/ sil-VAH-nəs), is the former Warchief of the Horde and former supreme ruler of the Forsaken, a faction of undead who broke away from the the control of the Lich King. In life, Sylvanas was the ranger-general of Silvermoon and bravely defended Quel'Thalas from the Scourge invasion led by the death knight Arthas Menethil in the Third War. Rather than honor the ranger-general with a quick death, Arthas ripped out her soul and transformed it into a banshee: a cunning and vengeful agent of the Scourge empowered by hate.
When the Lich King's control over his minions weakened, Sylvanas broke away from her tyrannical master's control and reclaimed her body. In her quest for revenge, she gathered other renegade undead as the Forsaken, leading them as the Banshee Queen in their war against the Scourge. Convinced that the Horde could help them accomplish their objectives, Sylvanas pledged her people to Warchief Thrall against the Alliance, and later during the war for Northrend. However, after an uprising within her ranks leading to the Battle for the Undercity, the Banshee Queen became mistrusted by many of her allies. Following the fall of Arthas, she sought a higher purpose for a people who had already died once. As Sylvanas began fortifying their territory within the Tirisfal Glades in order to establish a proper kingdom for her followers, she maintained that her loyalty to the Horde was undiminished, however, some of the faction's members were uncertain about her true intentions.
It was later revealed that after the Lich King's defeat, Sylvanas came to the shocking realization that she, like Arthas before her, was damned to an eternity of darkness and torture in the afterlife. Yet she also found a new purpose when she met the ancient evil controlling this realm, an entity known only as the Jailer. She formed an alliance with him, and shortly after entered into a pact with the Val'kyr, allowing Sylvanas to regain her place in the realm of the living for as long as her Val'kyr survive. Sylvanas would initially claim that she considered her people a bulwark against the horrifying darkness that awaited her in the end. Though the truth of this matter was that she needed them to create as much war and death as possible to deliver souls to her new ally. To this end, she subsequently launched an aggressive attack into the regions of Lordaeron and the greater Eastern Kingdoms not directly under her control, in an attempt to conquer the continent and secure it for the Forsaken, while securing all souls lost for the Jailer.
Mortally wounded during the battle for the Broken Shore, Warchief Vol'jin declared Sylvanas as his successor with his dying breath, leaving her to lead the Horde against the third invasion of the Burning Legion. In the aftermath of the Argus Campaign, Sylvanas led the Horde against the Alliance in the Fourth War, which spanned all of Azeroth. Upon being challenged to mak'gora by the defector Varok Saurfang, Sylvanas defeated him with the help of her newfound powers, revealing to both factions that these matters meant nothing to her, implying that she was dealing with matters of a much grander scale. Ultimately, Sylvanas left everyone behind, flying away from Orgrimmar in the form of dark smoke. Despite her duplicity against her own faction and people, there were those who were still loyal to her cause.
After defeating Bolvar Fordragon and shattering the Helm of Domination, Sylvanas opened a doorway into the Maw and worked side by side with the Jailer, under the belief they would shatter the systems of Death. However, upon discovering that she had been lied to and that her ally intended to have everyone (herself included) serve him, she declared that she'd never do so. The Jailer responded by returning the fragment of her soul she'd long been missing, rendering her unconscious and abandoning her to her enemies. Uther the Lightbringer helped the two disparate parts of Sylvanas' soul reunite, and a remorseful Sylvanas subsequently set about making amends for her sins by aiding the heroes of Azeroth in working against the Jailer and freeing Anduin Wrynn from his control. After the Jailer's defeat, Sylvanas submitted to the judgment of her archenemy Tyrande Whisperwind, who sentenced her to freeing all of the souls trapped in the Maw as the first step toward penance for her crimes. As she carried out her punishment, Sylvanas discovered something was amiss about the Shadowlands and worked on uncovering the truth.
Sylvanas serves as one of the main characters in Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos, Warcraft III: The Frozen Throne, and World of Warcraft. Sylvanas eventually becomes more antagonistic, serving as one of the main antagonists alongside N'Zoth in Battle for Azeroth, and a main antagonist and raid encounter in Shadowlands.
Taelloch Mine:
Taelloch Mine  is a lost mine in southeastern Ringing Deeps, accessed from either side of Camp Murroch.
The mine area is the southern half of Taelloch, and the Taelloch Twist skyriding race is at  in the southwestern corner.
Tazavesh, the Veiled Market: Tazavesh, the Veiled Market (/tæˈzəvɛʃ/ TAZZ-ə-vesh) is a broker city located at  to the southern end of K'aresh. Once one of the K'areshi city-states built across the arid planet, it was relocated to the In-Between within the Shadowlands following the Devouring War. After Ve'nari became the leader of Tazavesh, the city was relocated back to the broken world, where it now serves as the primary base of operations for the K'aresh Trust. It also functioned as the primary player hub for the zone during patch 11.2.0.
Telaar (alternate universe): Telaar is a former draenei town located in southern Nagrand. It has recently been captured by the Iron Horde. The Rangari led by Ogir are monitoring the situation from Rangari Overlook.
Telaari Station:
Telaari Station is the main Alliance base in Nagrand, located in the central part of the region, south of Yrel's Watch and north of Telaar.
The only major building in this outpost is decided by the commander, which is either the Rangari Corral or the Telaari Tankworks. Before a choice is made, the space is occupied by Telaari Worksite. There is a command table in these buildings for completing and starting new garrison missions.
Teldrassil:
Teldrassil (meaning "Crown of the Earth" in Darnassian) (/ˈtɛl.drə.sɪl/ TELL-druh-sill) was a World Tree situated on the eponymous island off Kalimdor's northwestern coast. Created shortly after the Third War by the night elves, Teldrassil served as their home and primary base of operations, its thick crown housing the capital city of Darnassus. Other major settlements on the tree included Rut'theran Village, Dolanaar and Shadowglen. Owing to its size, Teldrassil possessed its own unique ecosystem with a variety of flora, fauna, and vast twilit forests.
According to Broll Bearmantle, as a World Tree, Teldrassil was linked to the very health of Azeroth, affecting not merely its immediate surroudings, but those lands beyond the island, and a Teldrassil that was not well could not properly maintain the balance between nature and decay. The new tree was not blessed by the Dragon Aspects at its birth, unlike its predecessor Nordrassil, which would ultimately leave it vulnerable to corruption from the Emerald Nightmare. After the War Against the Nightmare, it eventually received the blessings of Alexstrasza and Ysera, while all known lingering corruption was purged during the Cataclysm.
Teldrassil served as the largest bastion of Alliance power in Kalimdor, and maintained naval connections to the mainland, the nearby Azuremyst Isles, and the distant Eastern Kingdoms. Many young and ambitious night elves began their journey out into the world from the verdant shelter of the World Tree. During the War of the Thorns—roughly a decade after its creation—Teldrassil was burned down by the Horde under the orders of Warchief Sylvanas Windrunner, killing many of the night elves dwelling in it.
Temple of Courage:
The Temple of Courage, located in the west of Bastion, is one of the region's major holy sites, each of which represents one of the virtues of the Kyrian Ascended. Its purpose is training the Kyrians in combat. It is overseen by the Paragon of Courage, Xandria. It is the base of the Bearers.
On arrival, the temple is under attack by the Maldraxxi House of Constructs. The entrance to Necrotic Wake, the zenith of the incursion, is located here, in Xandria's Vigil.
Temple of Earth:
The Temple of Earth is a temple in the center and lower shelf of Deepholm. It was here, in the Stonecore, that the Twilight's Hammer brought Deathwing back to full health and forged him new armor. A titan-made stone called the World Pillar was kept inside. This item bore the weight of all the elemental and magnetic forces in Deepholm. When Deathwing became fully healed, it was he who destroyed the pillar, causing the Shattering. Now, the Earthen Ring work in desperation to recover the fragments of the pillar and restore the temple. All of Deepholm would collapse into Azeroth if the World Pillar is not put back together.

 This section concerns content related to Legion.
Shaman of the Earthen Ring were still stationed in the Temple of Earth during the Burning Legion's third invasion. Thrall came here and asked them if they saw his weapon, the Doomhammer.
Temple of Purity:
The Temple of Purity is one of Bastion's major holy sites that represent one of the virtues of the kyrian Ascended, located in the southeast of the region. The temple is an important spot for aspirants on their path to ascension as they work to rid themselves of any doubts they carry, thus becoming pure according to the kyrian path. The area is overseen by the Paragon of Purity, Vesiphone, and her followers.
It is the base of the Watchers.
Temple of a Thousand Lights: Temple of a Thousand Lights is a large temple dedicated to Queen Azshara found south of Shackle's Den in southeastern Azsuna. Perhaps symbolically, it towers over the Garden of Elune.
Temple of the Moon:
The Temple of the Moon (or the Temple of Elune) in Darnassus was a major temple dedicated to the goddess Elune, the dwelling and moonlit sanctum of the Sisters of Elune, and the center of all night elven spiritual life. The temple also served as the seat of government in Darnassus and Teldrassil, with the night elven leaders High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind and Archdruid Malfurion Stormrage residing here. Incidentally, it was one of the largest artificial structures in the region.
The building itself was built in Darnassus following the Battle of Mount Hyjal that ended the Third War. In its center was the statue of Haidene placed in the middle of a moonwell which was used for bathing and recuperating. The waters of the temple are known to be blessed, being described as the water of Elune herself.
The temple was destroyed alongside Darnassus during the War of the Thorns after the Horde burned Teldrassil.
Tenir's Ascent:
Tenir's Ascent  is the main airship dock of the Hallowfall Arathi, located in south-central Hallowfall. A dawntower stands at the northwestern end, and the Dawnbreaker is permanently docked here. Players are initially directed here in  [75-78] Rally on the Dawnbreaker, midway through the first chapter of the Hallowfall storyline, to help fight off a continuous Kaheti assault.
The entry portal to the dungeon the Dawnbreaker is at  at the northwestern end of the airdocks, and the Tenir's Traversal skyriding race is at  to the southeast. The area is bordered by the Fangs to the north, the Stagnant Mire to the northeast, the Whispering Pool and Sanguine Grasps to the east, Beledar's Bounty to the west, and Lightspark to the northwest.
The name "Tenir's Ascent" derives from an idiom that means victory, especially an armada victory or one that involves a risky adventure, in turn derived from a character from an Arathi play.
Terminus:
Terminus is a massive port for Legion ships in the Antoran Wastes. A massive portal spire looms over the area that which may start summoning the Paraxis initiating an event for the entire zone. It is protected with the artillery at Felfire Armory.
The vessels docked at Terminus were taking on soldiers and supplies for the Legion's assaults against Azeroth. Champions of Class Orders were sent to bring the vessels down.
Thaldraszus:
Thaldraszus on the Dragon Isles is the seat of power of the Dragon Aspects and their flights. It stands as a shining beacon of the dragons' kingdom. It is also here that the bronze dragonflight watches over the timeways. The main city hub of the expansion, Valdrakken, is here.
After spending time seeing the many dragon-building ruins in the previous three zones, Thaldraszus offers something more pristine with beautifully intact buildings in the seat of power for all five of the dragonflights and the home of the dragons. Vertical lofty mountains and great cave systems.
Built by the Titan keeper Tyr, Tyrhold can be found in Thaldraszus. This ten-thousand-year-old Titan technological marvel houses great aqueducts that reach across the valley. It was Tyr who helped the Aspects fight Galakrond and when they came to settle in the Dragon Isles, it was he who built this facility. Even though Tyr is long gone, the dragons still hold him in reverence. The Titan keepers have continued to maintain Tyrhold while the dragonflights have gone on to take part in an incredible amount of history as the defenders of Azeroth.
The Fold: The Fold is a small Horde encampment located near the Talondeep Pass in Stonetalon Mountains. It is the first stop for Horde soldiers entering from Ashenvale.
Theater of Pain:
The Theater of Pain is a location found in central Maldraxxus.
One event that frequently takes place here is the Contest of Conquest, a competition between the strongest champions of every Maldraxxus house. Gunn Gorgebone, Scrapper Minoire, and Rencissa the Dynamo are competitors in the Contest.
It is surrounded by the Valley of a Thousand Legs and Challenger's Promenade to the southeast, the Forgotten Wounds below Scalpian Ridge to the northeast, the Sepulcher of Knowledge and Blackhound Outpost to the northwest, and the Stabbing Wastes, Wrangler Pit, and Iron Trench to the southwest. The anima conductor point for the Theater is to the northeast.
The theater has one entrance for each house: the Constructs entrance comes from the Stabbing Wastes, the Chosen entrance comes from the Iron Trench, the Eyes and Rituals entrance comes from the Forgotten Wounds, and the Plagues entrance comes from the Valley of a Thousand Legs.
Therazane: Therazane the Stonemother is the Elemental Lord of earth, and formerly one of the Old Gods' lieutenants. As the ruler of Deepholm and mother of the mighty Stone Lords, she is the master of all earth elementals. She takes the form of a massive female figure made of brown rocks and violet gemstones that are always seen floating just above the ground. Despite her general disinterest in mortal affairs, Therazane has worked with the adventurers to protect Azeroth, having shown nothing but contempt for her former masters and their servants. She also rallied her forces to aid the Earthen Ring during the third invasion of the Burning Legion.
Therazane's Throne:
Therazane's Throne is a large area and throne for the earth lord Therazane found in northern Deepholm on the upper shelf. The throne is filled with the most polished and reflective crystals in all of Deepholm, to which they continue to collect in exchange for gold they often pay to those able to collect.

 This section concerns content related to Legion.
After Therazane met the Stone Lords and the new Farseer of the Earthen Ring, Aeosara with her eggs moved here as they were attacked by Felrock troggs.
Third War:
The Third War (also known as the Third Great War, the Chaos War, and the Reign of Chaos) was a global conflict that took place between the mortal races of Azeroth and the demons of the Burning Legion from 20 to 21 ADP. Unlike the First and Second Wars, which primarily pitted the Horde against the Alliance, the Third War was a multi-factional conflict involving nearly every race on Azeroth. Major factions included the Alliance of Lordaeron, the New Horde under Warchief Thrall, the night elves of Kalimdor, the Burning Legion, and their undead allies the Scourge. The war spanned three continents—the Eastern Kingdoms, Kalimdor, and Northrend—and resulted in some of the most destructive battles in Azeroth's history. It marked the Burning Legion's second invasion of Azeroth.
The conflict began in earnest when the Plague of Undeath, created by the Lich King Ner'zhul under the direction of the Burning Legion, spread through the Kingdom of Lordaeron. The plague resulted in the fall of the kingdom to the Scourge army, led by the corrupted death knight Arthas Menethil, and the death of King Terenas Menethil II, Arthas' father. Following Lordaeron's fall, Arthas led the Scourge in a devastating invasion of Quel'Thalas, which resulted in the death of King Anasterian Sunstrider and nearly 90% of the high elven population. The Eastern Kingdoms campaign concluded with the Siege of Dalaran, where the demon commander Archimonde was summoned to Azeroth and the city was razed.
Heeding the warnings of the redeemed Guardian Medivh, the Horde and Alliance refugees fled across the sea to Kalimdor, where they soon came into conflict with each other as well as the night elves. The fighting in Kalimdor claimed the lives of several notable figures, including Warsong Clan chieftain Grommash Hellscream, the demigod Cenarius, and the demon pit lord Mannoroth. With the Burning Legion's arrival on Kalimdor, the Alliance, Horde, and night elves temporarily united to defend the World Tree Nordrassil against the Legion. In the resulting Battle of Mount Hyjal, the Alliance, Horde, and night elves together decisively defeated the Legion and the Scourge, killing Archimonde and ending the war.
The Third War transformed Azeroth and set the stage for its modern era. The conflict devastated kingdoms and populations, particularly in Lordaeron, where the Scourge's onslaught led to the near-total collapse of civilization across much of the continent. Large swathes of the Eastern Kingdoms and some areas of Kalimdor remained corrupted by the influence of the Scourge and the Legion for decades. The war also reshaped political alliances: the Horde expanded its ranks and consolidated power by settling new territory in Kalimdor, Stormwind emerged as a new leader of the Alliance in the wake of Lordaeron's fall, the night elves abandoned centuries of isolation to take a more active role in world affairs, and the Forsaken and the blood elves rose from the ashes of Lordaeron's destroyed kingdoms. Although the Burning Legion was defeated, its threat endured: the demons would later return to launch further invasions of Azeroth, while the Scourge under Arthas' rule remained a major power for years to come.
Thorignir:
The Thorignir are a brood of storm dragons residing on the mountain of Thorim's Peak in Stormheim and led by Thrymjaris. They are the oldest and wisest dragons in Stormheim, and to fly with them is to sail amongst the gods themselves. Unlike the storm dragons loyal to Nithogg to the north, the Thorignir swear fealty to the titan keepers and Odyn. They have also traditionally maintained a pact with the Drekirjar, allowing these vrykul to ride the Thorignir into battle as mounts. Recently, however, an alliance with the Burning Legion has set the vrykul against their former allies.
After joining the Valdrakken Accord, they came to be represented by Vyranoth as their aspect, serving as the newly dubbed Aspect of Storms, who also represents the Netherwing.
Thorium Advance: Thorium Advance is a camp headed by the Thorium Brotherhood. It is situated along the road in the Searing Gorge that leads to the Badlands.
Thorium Brotherhood:
The Thorium Brotherhood (TB Ltd.) is a group of Dark Iron dwarves who have left the Dark Iron clan. On the cliffs overlooking the region called the Cauldron, in the far north of the Searing Gorge, the dwarves of the Thorium Brotherhood have established a base of operations, Thorium Point. From here, they keep a close eye on the Dark Iron dwarves' activities in the Searing Gorge and beyond. Adventurers seeking out Thorium Point will find that the dwarves of the Thorium Brotherhood hold great rewards for those who aid them in their never ending struggle against their former brethren.
The Thorium Brotherhood comprises many exceptionally talented craftsmen, and the blacksmiths of the Brotherhood are rumored to be among the finest Azeroth has ever seen. They possess the knowledge required to make the arms and armaments of Ragnaros, the Fire Lord, but lack the manpower to obtain the materials required for the crafting. It is rumored that one member of the Thorium Brotherhood has been empowered to trade the dwarves' fabled recipes and plans with those who can prove their loyalty to the Brotherhood. Of course, proving one's loyalty at some point may include venturing to the heart of the Molten Core, the domain of Ragnaros, the Fire Lord himself, to supply the dwarves with the rare raw materials found there. A daunting task, no doubt, but gaining access to the Thorium Brotherhood's secrets should prove to be a reward well worth the effort.
Thorium Point:
Thorium Point is a small, neutral town in northern Searing Gorge inhabited by the Thorium Brotherhood.  
It has a flight path and the majority of the quests in the Searing Gorge as well as a couple of vendors. It is located northeast of Firewatch Ridge and is populated mostly by neutral Dark Iron dwarves. It is a critical hub for farming Thorium Brotherhood reputation.
There is a forge and anvil at this location.
Thraegar Rest: Thraegar Rest  is located between Foundation Hall and Keepers Terrace in northwestern Dornogal.
Three Shields: The Three Shields  is a set of three islands off the northeastern shore of Isle of Dorn. A Dragon Glyph is found at  atop the highest peak of the middle island. It is home to the Shimmerfin gorlocs and a flock of cloudrooks. It was also home to Olbarig, where he lived as a hermit after he left the Stormriders.
Throne of Thunder:
Throne of Thunder is the patch 5.2 raid instance. Emperor Lei Shen, the Thunder King, has returned to wreak his vengeance on Pandaria. It falls to the heroes of the Alliance and the Horde to stop the newly resurrected tyrant and his Zandalari allies in the Throne of Thunder. The Throne of Thunder is a sprawling citadel housing 12 raid encounters, and players that defeat Emperor Lei Shen in Heroic mode can earn the opportunity to face an additional 13th foe, Ra-den.
The Raid Finder version of the Throne of Thunder is divided into 4 different wings, and each wing opened a week (or two) after the previous. The instance opened on 5 March 2013, Heroic mode and "Last Stand of the Zandalari" LFR opened on 12 March, "Forgotten Depths" LFR opened on 19 March, "Halls of Flesh-Shaping" LFR opened on 2 April, and "Pinnacle of Storms" LFR opened on 16 April.
Join the Shado-Pan Assault in their singular drive to see Lei Shen, The Thunder King defeated once and for all, and gain access to impressive Valor reward items. Reputation with this faction can be earned only within the Throne of Thunder raid dungeon.
Thunder Bluff:
Thunder Bluff (sometimes spelled as Thunderbluff) is the tauren capital city located in the northern part of the region of Mulgore on the continent of Kalimdor. The entire city is built on bluffs several hundred feet above the surrounding landscape and is accessible by elevators on the southwestern and northeastern sides. Established by the wise chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof and his stalwart tribe, Thunder Bluff overlooks the verdant land of Mulgore from atop a series of windswept mesas. Prior to the construction of the capital, the tauren had lived as nomads for countless generations, often under attack by marauding bands of centaur. With Thunder Bluff’s founding, however, the proud and good-spirited race was finally granted a permanent home.
The city of many tribes is a hub for tauren, welcoming tradesfolk and artisans of every kind.
Thunder Bluff (faction): Thunder Bluff is the faction associated with the playable tauren of the Horde. The capital city of Thunder Bluff is located in the northern part of the region of Mulgore.
Thunderfoot Fields:
The Thunderfoot Fields can be found in the easternmost reaches of the Valley of the Four Winds north of the Yan-Zhe River. It comprises Pang's Stead, Shang's Stead, Thunderfoot Farm, Thunderfoot Ranch, and Shang's sheep farm.
The fields are controlled by the Thunderfoot family and their employees. Snagtooth virmen have been rampaging through their fields stealing crops, tools, and just being a nuisance.
Thunderhead Peak:
Thunderhead Peak  is a mountain peak found in northern Isle of Dorn.
The Thunderhead Trail skyriding race is at .
Tides of Darkness: Tides of Darkness is a novel by Aaron Rosenberg focusing on the events of Warcraft II: Tides of Darkness.
Tideskorn:
The Tideskorn clan are the united vrykul tribes of Stormheim, led by a God-King. They include the Drekirjar, the Bonespeakers and the Valkyra. Both the leaders of the Drekirjar and the Bonespeakers thus have a claim to rule the Tideskorn. If female, the ruler is expected or assumed to be a member of the Valkyra.
Their largest settlement is the city of Hrydshal, home of the dragon-taming Drekirjar. Those among the Tideskorn who accepted the fel gift and turned felsworn became known as Felskorn. They remained the same tribe and shared the same banner.
Tillers: The Tillers (short for the Tiller's Union or Tillers Union) are a group of pandaren farmers who harvest and produce crops to feed their people. They were seemingly founded by a man only referred to as "the Tiller".
Timbermaw Hold: Timbermaw Hold is the capital of the Timbermaw tribe of furbolgs. It is located in north east Felwood and includes the tunnel that connects Felwood with Moonglade and Winterspring.
Timbermaw tribe:
The Timbermaw tribe is a tribe of uncorrupted furbolgs that inhabit Felwood. They could also be found in Azshara until the Cataclysm, which led to their separation from the Blackmaw tribe.
The Deadwood tribe are the sworn enemies of the Timbermaw. They are corrupted and have been driven mad by the taint of Felwood.
Tinkers' Union:
The Tinkers' Union is a goblin organization led by Director Riddlevox. Their headquarters is in the Undermine, but they also have workshops in Gadgetzan.
The Union was tasked (likely by the trade-princes) with dealing with the issue of Mogul Razdunk hiring a gnome, Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle, as overseer of Windshear Crag.
They have a saying: "out of the heat-applied metallic cooking container and into the oxydizing, energetic mixture of reacting gases and solids!"
Tirisfal Glades:
Tirisfal Glades (/ˈtɪrɪsfɑːl/ TEER-ihs-fahl), also known as the Tirisfal Glade or simply Tirisfal, is an eerie region found on the northern coast of Lordaeron. It was named after the Titan Keeper Tyr, as Tirisfal means "Tyr's Fall" in the vrykul tongue. Before receiving this name, the region was simply called the Eastern Glades. The lands of the Forsaken, the wooded hills are seeped through with the curse of the Lich King's plague. The sky over Tirisfal is eternally gloomy and tinted a blighted green, and the trees and other flora desperately cling to their last shreds of life.
Those who inhabit the area of Tirisfal used to feel two conflicting energies emanating from the earth: the remaining spiritual essence of Keeper Tyr, and that of his enemy Zakajz. Some tapped into Tyr's energy; others would become attuned with the C'Thrax's dark aura. Although tainted and melancholy, Tirisfal still very much has its own unique, haunting beauty, particularly in such areas as the stony North Coast, the town of Brill, and the deep atmosphere of the ruined Agamand Mills.
Tirisfal Glades is home not only to the Forsaken but to their enemies as well. The Scarlet Crusade has several outposts here, including the seat of their religious faith, the Scarlet Monastery. The minions of the Scourge are also ever-present, tainting the derelict farmsteads and dilapidated mills with their foul presence.
In the aftermath of the Battle for Lordaeron, Tirisfal Glades became a contested territory between the Alliance and the Horde, with the ruins of Capital City becoming heavily plagued and the central areas of Tirisfal itself being overrun with Blighted Soldiers risen by Sylvanas Windrunner, who attack anyone on sight.
Tirisfal once again belongs to the Forsaken after the end of the Fourth War, although the Undercity remains uninhabitable.
Titan: The titans (sometimes capitalized) are a race of colossal, planet-sized cosmic beings, composed of arcane magic and the primordial matter from which the universe was born. As the main manifestation of Order, they roamed across the cosmos like walking worlds, imbued with the raw power of creation itself. The titans used this incredible force to find and awaken others of their kind. Hailing from the far reaches of the cosmos, they shaped and brought life and order to countless worlds across the Great Dark Beyond. They were described as perfect and majestic beings who are akin to gods.
Tomb of Sargeras:
"Temple of Elune" redirects here. For other similar temples, see temples of Elune and the Temple of Elune (Val'sharah).

The Tomb of Sargeras (formerly the Temple of Elune, also spelled as the temple of Elune, and simply referred to as the Tomb) is a great structure situated on the island of Thal'dranath in the Broken Isles. The Guardian Aegwynn imprisoned the corpse of the Avatar of Sargeras in the deepest parts of the Temple, miles beneath its surface, after she defeated it 800 years ago. After centuries of having been submerged under the sea, the dark power of the Avatar worked its influence upon the halls of the Tomb, twisting it with fel energy.
The Tomb was raised back to the surface by the warlock Gul'dan during the Second War, but he was torn apart by the demonic guardians within before he could claim the power contained inside the Tomb. Later still, during the Third War, the structure was visited by Illidan Stormrage in search of the Eye of Sargeras. Following the defeat of the Burning Legion on the alternate Draenor, the Tomb was reopened by alternate Gul'dan to allow the Legion entry into Azeroth once more.
Torghast, Tower of the Damned: Torghast, Tower of the Damned is an infinite dungeon in World of Warcraft: Shadowlands that can be played by 1 to up to 5 players. It sits at the center of the Maw. Torghast is an endlessly replayable, ever-changing dungeon that can be challenged alone or in a group. Each run will differ, and adventurers will need to explore cautiously, as death comes at a terrible cost. Advance through Torghast's unpredictable challenges to unlock anima powers to enhance damage output or survivability. The goal is  [Soul Ash], used to craft the legendary weapons and armor that will help restore balance to the Shadowlands.
Townlong Steppes:
Only the bravest pandaren dare enter these highlands. Although the area remains uncorrupted by the Sha, only the nomadic yaungols and the mantid choose to make the region their home.
The Townlong Steppes is a relatively small zone located in northwestern Pandaria. The main story that is played out here involves aiding the Shado-Pan on their pursuit against the Sha of Hatred, and aiding them in fending off the Osul yaungol and the aggressive mantid coming from the south.
Trade Coalition: The Trade Coalition is the name of the goblins' merchant empire. The Venture Company is part of the coalition, as are presumably all goblin organizations and cartels, including the Trade Fleets.
Trade Fleets: The Trade Fleets are goblin fleets, led by Vice Admiral Grezzlik, which helped make Kezan a great technological wonder of Azeroth. Trade Prince Maldy had a trade fleet until Jastor Gallywix tricked him into destroying it. Despite how much money the trade princes invested into the fleets, Gazlowe was disappointed with Grezzlik's ability to ensure the safety of his own vessels.
Trade-prince:
Trade-princes (also written simply as Trade princes) and occasionally referred to as merchant princes or trade lords, are the main leaders of the Cartels of Undermine.
Before the trade princes, it was every goblin for themselves, with no one safe. The trade princes brought a form of order.
Trade princes are usually also leaders of a goblin cartel, but they aren't necessarily equivalent. The Venture Company is a cartel whose leader is not called trade prince, likely because they're always getting in trouble for mining or cutting where they shouldn't, or for trying to keep what they promised to someone else.
Some goblins such as Ziz Fizziks of the Tinkers' Union and Mogul Kebok seem to be the direct enforcers of their collective will.
Treasures of Korthia: Treasures of Korthia is awarded to players who find all 10 treasures scattered about Korthia and Desmotaeron in the Maw. This achievement is one of many for the meta-achievement  [Breaking the Chains].
Tremaculum:
The Tremaculum  is the northwestern corner of the Maw. Bordered to the east and south by the Planes of Torment, and the southwest by the Ruin's Cradle, the Tremaculum holds some of the Jailer's more important prisoners before they get transferred to Torghast, Tower of the Damned. Anduin Wrynn was imprisoned in this place after he got kidnapped by the mawsworn and sent to the Maw.
A Chaotic Riftstone to the Crucible of the Damned is available once players unlock it with the  [Encased Riftwalker Essence].
Here souls are tormented, twisted into wretched shades.
True Horde: The True Horde (or the true Horde, Hellscream's Horde, and the Orcish Horde) was the organization formed by those members of the Horde who remained loyal to Warchief Garrosh Hellscream after Vol'jin led a rebellion against him. They were devoted to the conquest of Azeroth and orcish supremacy, and as such there were very few other races in it. It was the main antagonistic faction of the final story arc in Mists of Pandaria. After their defeat in Orgrimmar, they were led by Zaela and entered an alliance with Kairoz and the Infinite dragonflight in order to free Garrosh from custody (or rather buy time in order to transport him to alternate Draenor of the past). Many later joined the Iron Horde formed by Grommash Hellscream in the alternate universe.
Tushui Landing: Tushui Landing  is the Alliance beachhead of Timeless Isle. Located on the southern end of the Timeless Shore, the landing is northwest of Old Pi'jiu, southwest of the Celestial Court, and due south of the Huojin Landing, the Horde's beachhead.
Twilight Throne:
The Twilight Throne is located in Deepholm. It is the stronghold of the Twilight's Hammer in Deepholm at the time of the third invasion of the Burning Legion.
The entrance to the Twilight Depths is found here.
Twilight's Hammer:
The Twilight's Hammer, also known as the Twilight's Hammer clan, Hammer clan, Twilight's Hammer cult, Twilight Cult, Cult of Twilight's Hammer or simply the Hammer, is a nihilist quasi-religious sect active across Azeroth that fanatically serves and worships the Old Gods and seeks to bring about the end of the world. Originally founded by Cho'gall as a clan of pale orcs, the cult has been active since before the First War but became a major worldwide threat to both the Alliance and the Horde after Deathwing's return and the great Cataclysm shattered Azeroth.
After many defeats and setbacks, the Twilight's Hammer reformed into the Twilight's Blade following the war on K'aresh, now serving Xal'atath.
Tyrande Whisperwind:
Tyrande Whisperwind (/təˈɹɑːn.də/ tə-RAHN-də) is the chosen high priestess of the goddess Elune, the former general of the night elf Sentinels and the current head of the Sisterhood of Elune. Together with her lifelong mate, the archdruid Malfurion Stormrage, she has represented the highest leadership of the night elves since the fall of Queen Azshara and the Highborne caste ten thousand years ago. Since the middle of the Fourth War, Tyrande was the most recent incarnation of the Night Warrior, the embodiment of Elune's wrath.
In the years prior to the Burning Legion's first invasion, Tyrande was the object of both Malfurion and his brother Illidan's affections. In the end, the priestess chose the druid over the sorcerer. After playing a pivotal role in the War of the Ancients, Tyrande was promoted to General of the Sentinels and would protect Kalimdor for over 10,000 years during the Long Vigil, while her lover and the druids slept in the Emerald Dream. Tyrande and Malfurion then led the night elves in the Third War, defeating the Burning Legion as they had done in ages past at the Battle of Mount Hyjal. She subsequently stepped down as general, handing the reins to her adoptive daughter Shandris Feathermoon, to devote herself fully as the leader of her people.
After Malfurion had become trapped within the Emerald Dream for a prolonged period of time, Tyrande journeyed into the dream to rescue him. In the wake of the Shattering, Tyrande and Malfurion were wed and began to lead their people as one. Together they supported the worgen of Gilneas in their return into the Alliance. Tyrande also restored complete night elf control over Ashenvale as a result of the Alliance-Horde war. However, following the burning of Teldrassil, Tyrande became the Night Warrior in response to the Horde's invasion of night elven territory and to claim justice against Sylvanas Windrunner and the Horde.
After killing Nathanos Blightcaller, Tyrande pursued Sylvanas into the Shadowlands. Though she eventually caught her quarry, Elune interfered at the last second, and the Night Warrior's powers became nearly fatal to Tyrande. In the end, Tyrande chose peace over vengeance, saving herself, and instead sentenced Sylvanas to atone for her crimes by collecting the souls of the night elves who had died because of her. Years later, Tyrande helped to restore Ysera to life, which came at the expense of her husband taking the Green Aspect's place in the Shadowlands, in order to help the Dragon Aspects defeat the Primal Incarnates. Following the defeat of Fyrakk and the blooming of Amirdrassil, Malfurion and Tyrande reunited and chose to step aside, leaving the leadership of the kaldorei to their adopted daughter, Shandris.
Tyrande serves as one of the main protagonists in the Warcraft franchise.
Uldum Accord: The Uldum Accord is a reputation faction in Uldum that opposes the encroaching forces of N'Zoth as well as the Amathet tol'vir. It is comprised of various denizens of Uldum, including the Ramkahen, Explorers' League, and Wastewander nomads.
Underbelly:
The Underbelly (or the Dalaran Sewers) is the name of the Dalaran sewer system which has its own separate map. Many races, but mostly goblins, dwell in these sewers and they could be viewed as the slum of Dalaran. The central area of the sewers is the Circle of Wills, a large hall in which the arena vendors, some dueling circles, and a small, currently unused cluster of buildings stand. Southwest of here is a section called Cantrips & Crows which contains the inn, the tavern, and the bottom exit pipe of Dalaran. The northeastern corner goes unnamed, and has a few vendors but not much else notable. Finally, further northeast, there is a small chamber in which the rogues of Dalaran operate the Black Market where reagents and rogue supplies can be found, as well as the vicious sewer shark Segacedi.
Dalaran Arena, one of the two  arenas, is set here, the other being the Orgrimmar Arena in Orgrimmar.

 This section concerns content related to Legion.
In Legion, the Underbelly Guard patrols the area, led by the corrupt Guard Captain Raethan.
The southwestern section of the Underbelly has been transformed into the Hall of Shadows of the Uncrowned during the Burning Legion's third invasion of Azeroth. The transformation halved the accessible areas and removed access to the inn, bank, and tunnel out of Dalaran.
Undermine: The Undermine, or just Undermine, is the subterranean capital city of the goblins, located in the bowels of Mount Kajaro on the Isle of Kezan in the South Seas. Weaving through the heart of Kezan in a dizzying network of tunnels, vaults, and lava tubes, Undermine epitomizes the goblins' complex, unpredictable mindset. The city has many sluicetowns such as Pyrix, and its air is stale and oily. Troll slaves work in the city. The city of Bilgewater Port, located on the surface of Kezan, linked to the underground metropolis.
United tauren tribes: The united tauren tribes are a nation formed by the tauren tribes of Kalimdor and acting as a member state of the Horde. Once led by High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof, the nomadic tauren founded Thunder Bluff as their capital in the windswept mesa of Mulgore, where they united under a single banner to protect their new home. It was Cairne's vision of a peaceful home for all tauren tribes that led to the unification of the formerly disparate race. Currently under the leadership of High Chieftain Baine Bloodhoof, the tauren of Mulgore live honorable lives and value peace over the warmongering ways of their allies, striving to preserve the balance of nature and heed the will of their goddess, the Earth Mother.
Valdrakken Accord:
The Valdrakken Accord is a draconic organization led by the Dragon Aspects to represent the reunification of the dragonkin upon their home of the Dragon Isles. A spiritual successor to the Wyrmrest Accord, the Valdrakken Accord takes its name from the mighty draconic city of Valdrakken, where the Dragon Aspects lead their people from the Seat of the Aspects. Unlike the predecessor, the Valdrakken Accord contains representatives of all five major flights and several minor flights, and is led by the six Dragon Aspects, Alexstrasza, Nozdormu, Kalecgos, Merithra, Ebyssian, and Vyranoth.
The Scalesworn serves as the military wing of the [accord, but also as the city guard of Valdrakken, being led there by Captain Drine.
Vale of Eternal Blossoms:
The Vale of Eternal Blossoms is a region at the center of the continent of Pandaria, and has great cultural importance to both the pandaren and mogu, particularly due to the Mogu'shan Palace. Formerly known as a Cradle of Life and used as a place of experimentation by the titans similar to Sholazar Basin and Un'Goro Crater, this vale of golden flowers and trees served as the seat of power for the rulers of Pandaria, such as the mogu rulers following the death of Lei Shen.
After the Alliance and Horde came to Pandaria bringing their war with them, the August Celestials decided to reopen the gate after sealing it following the downfall of the mogu empire. The Alliance and Horde proved themselves in aiding the Golden Lotus in defeating the Shao-Tien mogu. Later, Warchief Garrosh Hellscream used the vale's power as a means to revive the Heart of Y'Shaarj. The Old God's power utterly destroyed the eastern half of the vale, causing some to refer to it as the Vale of Eternal Sorrows. Following the Siege of Orgrimmar, Emperor Shaohao's spirit planted a magical tree in the center of the destruction, providing hope that the vale will heal one day now that Pandaria need no longer fear the seven breaths of Y'Shaarj.
Valley of Honor: The Valley of Honor is the military district of Orgrimmar. It is home to both warrior and hunter trainers, various arms and armor vendors, and the Horde battlemasters. The Ring of Valor arena is located here. The Hall of the Brave houses the warrior guild, as well as all the city's battlemasters. Blacksmithing, mining, and fishing trainers and vendors are found in the valley.
Valley of Spirits: The Valley of Spirits is a long narrow valley that leads from the Valley of Strength to the Talon Gate in Orgrimmar. It is the long-standing seat of the Darkspear trolls.
Valley of Strength: The Valley of Strength is the main valley of Orgrimmar. The area is a bustling hive of activity for most of the day and night, with all manner of adventurers frequenting its shops and facilities. It is also the first area encountered after passing through the main gate.
Valley of Wisdom:
The Valley of Wisdom was once the location of Grommash Hold, where Warchief Thrall once resided in Orgrimmar. The valley connects to the Drag in the east, the Valley of Spirits to the west, and the Cleft of Shadow and Valley of Strength to the south. Like most of the districts of Orgrimmar, it contains access to an inn, banker, and auction house.
When the Cataclysm struck, much of the area changed as the land sank in some places creating spots for pools to form. A few remains of Grommash Hold can still be seen where the tauren were allowed to set up huts and take this valley for their own use. The armor of pit lord Mannoroth, which once rested on a tree here is now gone, and the tree was destroyed.
A towering waterfall casts a cool mist over the valley, making the tauren structures shine.
Vanguard of the Light: The Vanguard of the Light, often shortened as the Vanguard, is a coalition of champions summoned by Azeroth's worldsoul, united to oppose Xal'atath and the Devouring Host. When the Voidstorm appeared above the Isle of Quel'Danas, Lady Liadrin beseeched the Light to help them repel the Void invaders; in response, the worldsoul teleported most of the world's priests and paladins to protect the Sunwell.
Varok Saurfang:
High Overlord Varok Saurfang (/vɛɹ.ɑk ˈsaʊɚ.fæŋ/ VEHR-ock SAHur-fang) was a renowned orc warrior of the Blackrock clan, and the younger brother of Broxigar. A famed veteran of the First, Second, and Third Wars, he served as Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer's second-in-command during the Second War, and as Supreme Commander of the Might of Kalimdor during the second War of the Shifting Sands against the qiraji of Ahn'Qiraj.
He later led the Kor'kron against the Scourge in Northrend, and assisted Thrall during the Siege of Orgrimmar. Following the tragic battle on the Broken Shore and Sylvanas Windrunner's promotion to Warchief, Saurfang took up the position of leader of Orgrimmar and resided in Grommash Hold. Disgusted with Sylvanas' increasingly cruel and brutal reign, Saurfang turned against the Warchief and asked King Anduin Wrynn for assistance in removing her from power. Both the armies of the Alliance and the Horde-loyalists gathered by Saurfang and Zekhan's campaign gathered at the gates of Orgrimmar, where Saurfang challenged Sylvanas to mak'gora, which culminated in his death and in Sylvanas's departure, preventing massive bloodshed between the two factions.
He was one of the main protagonists in Battle for Azeroth.
Vault of the Wardens:
The Vault of the Wardens is the Warden maximum security facility holding among the greatest threats to Azeroth, which once included the body of Illidan Stormrage, his Illidari demon hunters, and other terrifying monsters. The door to the Vault is opened by the Darnassian phrase "Anu'dorini Talah", which translates to "Let my will be known."
The Vault is replete with magical safeguards, and powerful containment crystals are used to encase each prisoner in their cell. Aside from the demon hunters once imprisoned in the Illidari Ward, the most powerful prisoners of the Vault are sealed in the vaults of the Demon Ward. Being posted there was once considered prestigious.
Ve'nari:
Ve'nari (/vɛˈnɑːri/ veh-NAH-ree), originally named just Nari, is a broker who seeks to restore K'aresh. Once a K'areshi member of the Ravel, she served as an agent of then High Priest Salhadaar. Having brokered a friendship with Locus-Walker, they attempted to stop the destruction of their world by the void lord Dimensius. Though she was unable to prevent the destruction of K'aresh, she swore an oath to restore her homeworld. She would later join Cartel Ve as a Broker, though her goals remained illusively her own.
She was eventually assigned to the Maw alongside other members of her cartel, where she managed to survive somehow for years away from the eyes of Zovaal and his Mawsworn. She was first encountered by players within the Shadowlands expansion, located at her refuge within the Maw. There, she trades in Stygia for useful items in the Maw and Torghast, Tower of the Damned. The closest thing adventurers could find to a friendly face in the Maw, Ve'nari engaged in a number of lucrative deals with the Maw Walker during their war against the Jailer. Despite her own cartel attempting to waylay her, Ve'nari remained undeterred within the Maw and would ultimately traverse to Zereth Mortis. Though her findings there were limited, she was able to create a device that allowed her to explore the cosmos.
With her amassed fortune and connections from her time in the Shadowlands, Ve'nari created the K'aresh Trust, serving as its founder and leader. She also took control of a cartel of her own, Cartel Om. Purchasing the loyalty of several Cartels as well as the city of Tazavesh, Ve'nari led the charge to reclaim what was left of their world, as well as re-establishing Project Eco-Dome; the culmination of everything she had done. Alongside the ethereals from the Consortium, adventurers from Azeroth, and her once ally Locus-Walker -- they once more faced against the evil that was Dimensius. In the wake of his defeat, Ve'nari not only at last saw the fall of her ancient foe, but also secured the survival of her world by restoring the worldsoul of K'aresh, thus fulfilling her ancient oath.
Ve'nari's Refuge: Ve'nari's Refuge  at the eastern end of Cocyrus is, straightforwardly enough, home to Ve'nari in the Maw. Players use this as their base of operations, and while in the area are not subject to the Eye of the Jailer.
Veiled Den: The Veiled Den is one of the camps of the Illidari in the Antoran Wastes. It is a small foothold against the onslaught of the Burning Legion, and is perpetually under attack by demonic forces, including Vile Thrashers and Fel Shriekers. This location is unavailable on an alternating basis with the camp at Light's Purchase; whenever one is destroyed, the other camp and its Lightforged beacon become available for use.
Velen:
Velen has been the leader of the draenei people since their flight from Argus 13,000 years before the first orcish invasion of Azeroth. Known by his people as the Prophet, he has been granted the gift of the Sight, and — aided by the Light — rejected offers of dark power from Sargeras and has guided his people as they fled from, and later fought against, the Burning Legion and their former eredar brethren. He is first among the draenei and is the arch-nemesis (formerly best friend) of Kil'jaeden.
Following the draenei's flight to Azeroth, they made a new home on the Azuremyst Isles and, sensing great courage in the Alliance, Velen and his followers pledged themselves to this noble faction. The strengthened Alliance then helped the draenei reclaim their former holdings from the Legion. Most recently, Velen used the heart of the naaru M'uru to sanctify the blood elves' tainted Sunwell, transforming the sacred fount into a source of holy and arcane energies. He also managed with the aid of the Conclave to bring the void god Saraka the Lighteater back to the Light as the naaru Saa'ra.
Although the Legion's forces in Outland have been greatly diminished and the demonic invasion of Azeroth has been driven back, Velen remains fearful of an upcoming war between light and shadow. During the third invasion of the Burning Legion, Velen led the defense of the Exodar from a Legion attack led by his own son High General Rakeesh. After the deaths of both O'ros and Rakeesh, Velen declared that he was neither prophet nor pawn, and that the draenei were returning home to Argus. Following the defeat of Argus' corrupted world-soul and the containment of Sargeras, apparently ending the Legion and the Burning Crusade forever, Velen returned to Azeroth with his reunited people, offering his counsel to King Anduin Wrynn and the Alliance in the conflicts to come, and noting that perhaps it was time for each one of them to forge their own fate.
Vengeance Point: Vengeance Point is a small island off the northwestern coast of the Broken Shore. A flightpath can be found there.
Venthyr:
The venthyr of Revendreth are vampiric punishers of the unworthy, charged with rehabilitating the sinful souls sent to them by the Arbiter. Souls who are successfully rehabilitated can then choose to be sent to another realm to serve for eternity, or become a venthyr themselves and continue the cycle as an instrument of repentance.
The venthyr were created by Sire Denathrius in his own likeness. The first of them, Prince Renathal, and other members of the original Court of Harvesters such as the Curator and the first Harvester of Wrath were willed into being by Denathrius. Later venthyr—the first of which was the Stonewright—were (and are) created from redeemed souls who are given a new name and taught the ways of Revendreth by a venthyr, who endorse and sire them in turn. Their original names are still very important to them, for they could potentially let someone find their sinstones and compel the venthyr to their will. A venthyr is unable to act directly against someone with their sinstone.
Venthyr find exposure to the Light extremely painful. If a venthyr is exposed to the Light for too long, they're driven mad and eventually becomes an ash ghoul. The only preventative remedy after too much exposure is to quickly find a dark spot and to consume the anima that venthyr extract, referred to as liquid shadows. It is noted to taste bad to the dredgers. The Light is not normally lethal to venthyr, but if focused through mirrors, depending on the amount of concentrated Light a venthyr can be trapped in one spot, torturously unable to move, all the way up to instantly bursting into a cloud of ash.
The Venthyr Covenant is one of the four covenants ruling over the Shadowlands.
Venthyr Covenant:
The cunning venthyr of Revendreth are one of the Covenants in the Shadowlands. They feast on the souls of the prideful and vain in a gothic realm of opulence and torment. Joining this covenant means accepting the gift of the Court of Harvesters.
This is where flawed souls are sent who haven't been able to leave something behind, whether it's pride or some other failing. Souls sent here are not quite ready for service in one of the Shadowlands' other domains, and it is the duty of the vampiric Venthyr to prepare them—through unimaginable torment. It is much like a purgatory for souls who need to atone for past misdeeds and shed the burdens of their life. The journey is not an easy one, however. The former sin'dorei prince Kael'thas Sunstrider is one such soul who has found himself in Revendreth for his deeds in life.
Venture Co. Mine: The Venture Co. Mine (also spelled Venture Company Mine) is an enormous mine run by the Venture Company in the eastern cliffs of Mulgore. The mine has three entrance points. The first is the main entrance where Supervisor Fizsprocket resides—it is the only entrance accessible on foot. Fizsprocket is the goblin in charge of Venture Co. operations in the tauren homeland. The second entrance is a cliff, and the third entrance is a small lumber camp.
Venture Company: The Venture Company or Venture Trading Company, often shortened to simply Venture Co., is a goblin-run cartel notorious for plundering Azeroth's natural resources. Part of the Trade Coalition, the company specializes in gathering raw materials. If you can dig it up, chop it down, or blow it out of a mountain, they will. They also got some of the best heavy machines, miners, shredders, and drills out there. The Venture Company has had and continues to have operations throughout many parts of Azeroth. In addition to being known for their ruthless methods, the company has historically had dealings with various nefarious organizations, like the Defias Brotherhood, the Sunfury, and the Crown Chemical Company. Mogul Razdunk was the president of the company for many years, but he was never able to ascend to the position of Trade-prince. Grimla Fizzlecrank is the one who hands out the jobs these days. She is trying to push the Venture Co. in the right direction, but there's a whole parade of troublemakers pulling other strings. In the Undermine, their color scheme is yellow.
Venture Company (faction): Venture Company is a faction of The War Within, based out of Venture Plaza in Undermine.
Verlok Stand:
Verlok Stand, as called Verlok Village, is a stone trogg village just north of the Crimson Expanse on the upper shelf in Deepholm. With suspicion that the Verlok troggs are polluting the expanse with mushrooms and other growths the Stone Lord Gorsik the Tumultuous seek elementals to reek havoc on their village.
The entrance into the Fungal Deep cavern is found just past Ruberick on the bottom area of the village.
Vestibule of Eternity: The Vestibule of Eternity is an area in southern Bastion where all souls assigned to Bastion first enter. After being greeted by the Greeter Mnemis, they will be taken to four stations for brief general explanations and purification.
Vindicaar:
The Vindicaar (pronounced VIN-di-kar) is a space-faring vessel, similar in design to the naaru dimensional ships, created by the draenei of the Exodar in order to return to their homeworld of Argus. The vessel would go on to take part in the Argus Campaign against the Burning Legion, in which it acted as headquarters for the Azerothian forces. The ship can maintain instant connections to various nearby and distant locations at a given time through the use of Lightforged beacons. The Vindicaar is also equipped with powerful defensive shields, as well as offensive air-to-surface weaponry.
Currently, the Vindicaar has come under the control of the Army of the Light, who use the vessel as their primary base after the Xenedar's destruction, and have since joined the Alliance.
Violet Rise:
The Violet Rise  is the Kirin Tor Offensive toehold on a small island off to the southeast of the Isle of Thunder. After claiming Shaol'mara (and phasing in the Violet Rise), adventurers of the Alliance wishing to help the Kirin Tor Offensive claim the isle can teleport here from the Alliance camp at  north of the Shado-Pan Garrison in Townlong Steppes. Surrounded by the Whispering Inlet, to the west are the Shadewood Thicket and Diremoor, and Ihgaluk Crag is to the southwest. 
The  [Kirin Tor Beacon] can be used to return Alliance players directly to the Violet Rise every ten minutes, but it can only be used on the Isle of Thunder.
The Kirin Tor Offensive continued to maintain Violet Rise after the Alliance-Horde war. During the trial of Garrosh Hellscream, the base hosted Jaina Proudmoore, Varian Wrynn, his son Anduin, Vereesa Windrunner, Kalecgos, and several powerful magi after each day's court proceedings.
Violet Stand:
The Violet Stand is a Kirin Tor outpost located within night elf ruins. It is located just to the northwest of the Azure Front in southwest Crystalsong Forest. To the north is the Great Tree and the Decrepit Flow coming from Icecrown. The mages had a magical shield dome to protect themselves from the blue dragonflight during the Nexus War. Corpses of blue dragonspawn, presumably from the nearby Azure Front, litter the ruins. There are also burnt holes here, presumably from battle. It has a Teleport to Violet Stand Crystal from Teleport to Dalaran Crystal.
Following the war against the Jailer, the brothers Bronzebeard reported that the Kirin Tor left the ruins after the end of the war. There are now only the old ruins of tall towers still draped with vines and still-smoldering craters left by the blue dragonkin.
Vol'jin's Pride:
Vol'jin's Pride is the main Horde base in Talador, located in the northeastern part of the region, south of Fort Wrynn.
The only major building in this outpost is decided by the commander, which is either Vol'jin's Arsenal or an Arcane Sanctum. Before a choice is made, the space is occupied by Vol'jin's Pride Worksite. There is a command table in these buildings for completing and starting new garrison missions.
Vyranoth:
Vyranoth the Frozenheart is one of the four Primal Incarnates. Along with her brethren, she rejected the gift of the titans and turned to the elements instead, becoming an incarnation of frost. Before doing so, she was an old friend of Alexstrasza the Dragon Queen from the days before the titans uplifted the dragons. Having left her fellow Incarnates because of how far they were willing to go, after the events of Amirdrassil, the Dream's Hope Vyranoth was blessed by Azeroth and became the sixth Dragon Aspect. She has dubbed herself the Aspect of Storms, in reverence for her fallen sister, Raszageth, as well as the storms that were the homes of the two flights she represents, the Netherwing and the Thorignir.
Her visage form is an elemental.
War Quarter:
The War Quarter is located in the northwest corner of the Undercity. This is where the Forsaken military is based, and is also home to the city's priest and warrior guilds, as well as a few profession trainers.
The War Quarter contains an Altar of Darkness.
Facilities:

Hunter trainers 
Priest trainers
Warrior trainers
Weapon skill trainer
Blacksmithing trainers
Mining trainers
Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos:
Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos is a computer game released by Blizzard Entertainment in 3 July 2002. It is a real-time strategy computer game, the second sequel to Warcraft: Orcs & Humans and the third game set in the Warcraft universe. As such, it is usually referred to as Warcraft III, (often abbreviated to WC3, WCIII, or War3). Warcraft III is also considered to be one of Canada's national sports (along with hockey and lacrosse), due to the high level of top WCIII gamers that come from Canada and due to the occasional televised broadcast of the game, especially in British Columbia. The demo that was once available on Blizzard's website is no more; although the demo can still be downloaded from available third parties such as the Internet Archive.
Details the second invasion of the Burning Legion and the origins of the Scourge, along with the fall of Lordaeron and the awakening of the night elves are the plot of the story. In addition, the orcs leave the Eastern Kingdoms, and on their journey to Kalimdor, save the Darkspear trolls from destruction. When they arrive, they also assist the tauren and officially form the Horde as a collective of these races.
A demo version includes the tutorial and the prologue campaign.
At BlizzCon 2013, J. Allen Brack said they have several people working on a side project to update the old Warcraft games for modern computers. At BlizzCon 2018, the Classic Games team announced Warcraft III: Reforged, a full remaster of Reign of Chaos and its expansion, which released in early 2020.
Wardens (faction):
The Wardens are night elven wardens loyal to Maiev Shadowsong operating in the Broken Isles. They have worked from their base of operations, the Isle of the Watchers in Azsuna, to hunt down and neutralize major threats to Azeroth's inhabitants, through imprisonment or summary execution. Captured foes were interned in the Vault of the Wardens. 
They reward the heroes who help them deal with dangerous threats on the Broken Isles. The faction is known to possess Warden Towers across the Broken Isles, although in recent times they have been forced to abandon many of them. There are two in most Legion zones that serve as PvP targets.
Warlock:
The warlock is a damage-dealing spell-caster class, known for their wide range of debuffs and damage over time effects. They are magical practitioners that seek to understand darker magics, among other fel-based and destructive spells. While many warlocks willingly follow the Burning Legion, there are those who work against it, using their magic to fight against evil. They have proven themselves to be powerful allies, as well as powerful foes, and are known to be interested in seeking power in the darkest of places and making bargains most people in their right minds wouldn't make.
Warlocks burn and destroy weakened foes with a combination of crippling illnesses and dark magic. While their pets, which may be both demons and aberrations, protect and enhance them, they strike at their enemies from a distance. As physically weak spellcasters bereft of heavy armor, cunning warlocks allow their minions to take the brunt of enemy attacks in order to save their own skin. They deliver fire and shadow damage with their spells, and they're able to hurt others both instantly and with ongoing afflictions. Warlocks are adept at summoning their allies to their presence, whether said allies are other heroes or bloodthirsty demons. Warlocks bind demons to their will; these infernal denizens defend their masters with their lives or rain death upon their enemies. They also make use of debilitating curses to weaken and disable enemies, reducing their ability to fight back.
Warlock talents can improve the damage of their searing magics, increase the potency of their curses and persistent damaging spells, and empower their demonic servants:

Affliction warlocks are masters of shadow magic who specialize in drains and damage-over-time spells.
Demonology warlocks are commanders of demons who twist the souls of their army into devastating power.
Destruction warlocks are masters of chaos who call down fire to burn and demolish enemies.
Warrior's Terrace:
The Warrior's Terrace (also referred to as the Hall of Justice) is a major central district in the night elf capital city of Darnassus, serving as a base for the city's warrior trainers, battlemasters, and the Sentinels. Most night elves of military status utilized the training areas here to hone their skills. There they had the use of target ranges and dueling grounds. It occupies the easternmost section of Darnassus, located at the main gate leading out into the greater Teldrassil region.
The district protects Darnassus from violent incursions. Patrollers on nightsaber mounts guard the city's impressive gates.
The Warrior's Terrace is accessible from the Craftsmen's Terrace in the north, the Tradesmen's Terrace in the south, and the Temple Gardens in the west. In addition to the large military presence, the terrace also hosts a large number of low- and high-level training dummies, as well as blacksmithing training and supplies.
Wastelanders: The Wastelanders are a group of ethereals who have sworn an oath to Nexus-King Salhadaar to destroy the Ravel for what they did to K'aresh. Once known as the K'areshi Oracles prior to the Devouring War, they lead a harsh existence on the shattered planet of K'aresh where survival is a continuous struggle.
Waterworks:
The Waterworks  is a kobold-infested dam in west-central Ringing Deeps. It provides power to various machines across the cavern. The interior area is a delve, with the entrance found at  on the southern end of the exterior area.
The exterior area is bordered to the north by Shimmermist Falls, the northeast by Brunwin's Terrace, Pillarstone Spire to the east, and the Cataract River to the east and southeast.
During Operation: Floodgate, the Venture Company and Darkfuse Enforcement threatened to flood the Ringing Deeps after drawing too much power from the dam to power Gallywix's schemes. Renzik "The Shiv" led a covert operation to stop Gallywix's goons and returned control of the Waterworks to the earthen.
Wayfarer's Rest: Wayfarer's Rest (or the Wayfarer's Rest Tavern), located between the Walk of Elders and the Bazaar, is the larger of the two inns located inside the blood elf capital, Silvermoon City. Wayfarer's Rest Inn is host to Innkeeper Jovia; Sylann, a cooking trainer; Quelis, a cooking supplier; and Rarthein.
Weaver's Lair: The Weaver's Lair is found in Azj-Kahet. It is the headquarters of the Severed Threads and possesses a portal to Dornogal.
Wellspring Hovel: Wellspring Hovel is a small hamlet located in Teldrassil on the main road between Darnassus and Dolanaar.
Wenren Althal: Wenren Althal was an Arathi quest giver located at Beledar's Bounty in Hallowfall. The last surviving mage of the Hallowfall Arathi, he was working on a way to open a portal back to the Arathi Empire, and eventually asked adventurers to assist him in his experiments. With their help, he discovered a way to return his people to their homeland, and wondered if his pet cat Larky was still at home. However, Tefferty Ulreth, a grizzled member of the Hallowfall Expedition who assisted Wenren to reunite with his wife who stayed behind in the empire, turned out to be a member of the Order of Night. He ultimately assassinated Wenren and destroyed his research before the mage could put it into practice. General Steelstrike subsequently lamented the mage's death and regretted not offering him more protection.
Westfall Brigade: The Westfall Brigade, formerly known as the People's Militia, is Stormwindian military organization comprised of citizens of Westfall and veteran militiamen that fought back the Defias Brotherhood.
Wild God: Wild Gods are primal manifestations of life and nature found on both Azeroth and other planets. Many of them appear in the form of gargantuan animals, such as wolves, bears, tigers, or birds. Wild God, Ancient Guardian, Loa, and August Celestial are interchangeable when referring to great spirits aligned with nature destined to Ardenweald.
Wild Hunt:
The Wild Hunt is a reputation faction in Ardenweald.
The Wild Hunt is stationed at various groves, such as Guardian Molan at Hibernal Hollow, Guardian Kota at Tirna Vaal, and Sorcha at Glitterfall Basin. They are informed of what happens throughout Ardenweald by Watcher Vesperbloom. Their duties are to defend and protect the groves of Ardenweald from enemies, which would normally be gorm and spriggan suppression but now include a Drust invasion and Mueh'zala's forces as well. They are not a standing army, and assembly of the Wild Hunt is a rarity in the history of the eternal forest.
Wildcamp Or'lay: Wildcamp Or'lay is found in Azj-Kahet.
Wildcamp Ul'ar: Wildcamp Ul'ar is an area found in Azj-Kahet.
Winter Queen:
The Winter Queen is an Eternal One who rules the realm of Ardenweald and its inhabitants, the night fae, who defend the spirits of nature. She is charged with the sacred task of maintaining the cycle of rebirth: restoring perished Wild Gods, Ancients, loa, and other nature spirits and returning them to the mortal plane. She and the land are one; when the land thrives, so does she. Her sister and counterpart is Elune, who resides in the realms of Life. Together, they embody the balance of the great cycle of Death and Life.
Ardenweald has suffered more keenly from the anima drought than any other realm in the Shadowlands, and this has taken a bitter toll on the queen. For the first time in endless ages, she has been forced to choose which of the land's lush groves—and which souls—will be fed the last precious drops of anima and which will fade away forever, a task enacted by the Wild Hunt.
Wor'var:
Wor'var is the main Horde base in Nagrand, located in the eastern part of the region, northwest of Hallvalor.
The only major building in this outpost is decided on by the commander, which is either the Wor'var Corral or the Wor'var Tankworks. Before a choice is made, the space is occupied by Wor'var Worksite. There is a command table in these buildings for completing and starting new garrison missions.
World of Warcraft: Battle for Azeroth:
World of Warcraft: Battle for Azeroth (abbreviated as Battle or BfA) was the seventh expansion for World of Warcraft. It was announced at BlizzCon 2017 on 3 November 2017.
The idea of the expansion came up after recognizing the heroes of Azeroth have dealt with so many large, external threats like the Burning Legion. Alex Afrasiabi said, "So when we talk about what's the biggest threat in this world, is it the Titan or is it the Dwarf Paladin that put a hammer in that Titan's head"? As such, at the expansion's start, the enemy was the opposite faction; a "vast army of world-destroying forces".
On 30 January 2018 Battle for Azeroth was made available for preorder, and unlocked the four first allied races.
